The verse encourages believers to maintain their faith and cultivate a sense of reverence for Allah, acknowledging His absolute ownership and control over all existence.

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing sovereignty of God, indicating that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. It underscores the idea that God is sufficient as a guardian or trustee over all affairs, reassuring believers of His comprehensive care and providence.

translation: If He wills, He can eliminate you, O people, and bring others in your place. And Allah is Most Capable of that.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to humanity of their complete dependence on Allah's will. It underscores the transient nature of human existence and the fleeting presence of any particular generation. The capability of Allah to replace one people with another emphasizes His omnipotence and serves as a call to righteousness and obedience, lest one faces replacement or severe consequences. It highlights the concept that Allah's power is not limited by human history or the existence of current populations, and that He can bring about new creations or nations as He sees fit. This understanding is meant to instill a sense of accountability and to encourage people to adhere to the path of righteousness.

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights that those who seek worldly gain should recognize that true and lasting rewards for both this life and the hereafter are in the hands of Allah. It underscores the importance of seeking Allah's pleasure in all endeavors, as He is fully aware of our intentions and actions, and is capable of rewarding us accordingly. It encourages believers to align their goals with divine will, ensuring that their pursuit of worldly benefits is not at the expense of their spiritual well-being.

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing up for justice, as witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and fairness in testimony, even if it is against oneself or one's close relatives. It highlights that personal biases, whether due to the wealth or poverty of the individual involved, should not influence one's testimony. The verse warns against distorting or withholding the truth, as God is aware of all actions and intentions. It underscores the principle that justice should be upheld regardless of personal relationships or interests, and that one's testimony should be guided by a commitment to fairness and truthfulness.

translation: O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that He has sent down upon His Messenger and the Scripture which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having a firm and unwavering faith in God, His Messenger, and the scriptures revealed to him, as well as the previous scriptures. It warns that rejecting faith in these fundamental aspects of Islam, including belief in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Day of Judgment, leads to a profound and far-reaching deviation from the right path. The verse is urging believers to reaffirm their commitment to their faith and to be cautious of straying from it by disbelieving in any of its core components.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed then disbelieved then believed then disbelieved and then increased in disbelief - never will God forgive them nor guide them to a way.
interpretation: This verse is warning that those who repeatedly vacillate between faith and disbelief, ultimately hardening in their disbelief, are unlikely to receive God's forgiveness or guidance. It highlights the danger of persistent indecision and the hardening of one's heart against faith, suggesting that such a pattern can lead to a spiritual state from which it is difficult to return.

translation: And give tidings to the hypocrites that for them is a painful punishment
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who are hypocritical in their faith, indicating that their duplicity will not go unpunished. It signifies that those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor disbelief or doubt will face a severe and painful punishment. The verse underscores the importance of sincerity in one's beliefs and actions, suggesting that God is aware of the true intentions of individuals and will hold them accountable for their hypocrisy.

translation: Those who take the disbelievers as allies, instead of the believers. Do they seek 'izzah (power, honor, or prestige) with them? Indeed, 'izzah belongs entirely to Allah.
interpretation: This verse is cautioning against seeking power and prestige through alliances with non-believers, rather than with the community of believers. It emphasizes that true power and honor belong solely to Allah, and that seeking it elsewhere is misguided. The verse suggests that those who form alliances with non-believers are likely motivated by a desire for worldly gain or prestige, rather than a genuine commitment to their faith. By doing so, they are essentially seeking 'izzah (power, honor, or prestige) from the wrong source, as 'izzah ultimately belongs to Allah alone.

translation: And it has already come down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being disbelieved and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in a different conversation. Indeed, you would then be like them. Surely Allah will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell all together.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to believers against participating in gatherings where the signs of Allah are being denied or ridiculed. It emphasizes that sitting with such people until they divert to a different topic is tantamount to being like them, implying a shared culpability. The underlying message is about maintaining one's distinct identity as a believer and avoiding actions or situations that could assimilate one into the company of those who disbelieve or hypocritically behave, as all such individuals will face a collective reckoning in the hereafter.

translation: Those who wait [and watch] you. Then if you have a victory from Allah , they say, "Were we not with you?" And if the disbelievers have a share [of victory], they say [to them], "Did we not gain the upper hand over you, and did we not protect you from the believers?" Allah will judge between you [all] on the Day of Resurrection, and never will Allah give the disbelievers over the believers a [lasting] way [to overcome them].
interpretation: This verse is referring to the hypocrites who wait for the outcome of a battle to decide their allegiance. They claim to be with the believers when they are victorious and claim to have protected the disbelievers from the believers when the disbelievers have the upper hand. The verse is highlighting the duplicitous nature of the hypocrites and warning that God will judge between the believers and the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. It also reassures the believers that God will not give the disbelievers power over them, indicating that ultimately, the believers will be vindicated and the disbelievers will not prevail against them.

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites [think to] deceive Allah , but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who pretend to be believers but lack true faith. It indicates that their attempts to deceive Allah are futile, as He is aware of their true intentions. Their actions, such as performing prayer, are done half-heartedly and with the intention of impressing others rather than genuinely worshiping Allah. The verse suggests that their remembrance of Allah is minimal and superficial, revealing the hollowness of their faith.

translation: wavering between that [and that]; [belonging] neither to these nor to those. And whoever Allah sends astray - never will you find for him a way [of guidance].
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of attempting to find guidance or a path for those whom Allah has led astray. It underscores the idea that those who are confused or wavering between truth and falsehood, unable to commit to either, are a result of divine will. It emphasizes the sovereignty of Allah's guidance and misguidance, suggesting that human effort cannot correct or alter the path that Allah has chosen for an individual.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you want to give Allah against you a clear case?
interpretation: This verse warns the believers against taking disbelievers as allies or supporters at the expense of their relationships with other believers. It cautions that doing so would give Allah a clear proof or authority against them, implying a severe consequence or judgment for such actions, as it undermines the solidarity and loyalty that should characterize the community of believers.

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire; and never will you find for them a helper.
interpretation: This verse signifies that hypocrites will face the most severe punishment in the afterlife, being relegated to the lowest depths of Hell, and that they will be devoid of any helper or savior to intercede on their behalf or alleviate their suffering.

translation: Except those who repent, mend (their lives) and hold fast to Allah, and purify their religion for Allah; they are with the believers. And Allah shall grant to the believers a mighty reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and justice of Allah by emphasizing that individuals who repent, mend their ways, hold firmly to their faith in Allah, and sincerely dedicate their religion to Him alone will be counted among the believers. It underscores the principle that true faith and righteous actions are key to being considered part of the community of believers, and it promises that believers will be rewarded greatly by Allah.

translation: What concern is it of Allah to punish you if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is Ever-Appreciative, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that God's punishment is not arbitrary, but rather it is a response to human actions. If people are grateful and have faith, there is no need for punishment. The verse emphasizes God's appreciation and knowledge, suggesting that He values gratitude and is aware of the actions of His creation. It implies that punishment is not a default or a whim, but rather a consequence of human behavior, and that a righteous path can avoid it.

translation: Allah does not like the utterance of evil words except by one who has been wronged. And ever is Allah Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of maintaining decorum and refraining from speaking ill of others, except in cases where one has been wronged and is seeking justice or redress. It suggests that while generally, Allah does not approve of openly speaking evil or bad words, there is an exception for those who have been victims of injustice, implying that they are allowed to speak out against the wrong done to them. The verse underscores Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and hearing, indicating that He is fully aware of all that is said and done.

translation: If you disclose good or conceal it or pardon an evil, then surely Allah is ever Pardoning, Powerful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive nature of Allah's power and mercy, emphasizing that whether one openly does good, conceals it, or forgives an offense, Allah is capable of pardoning and has the power to do so. It underscores the virtue of forgiveness and the concealment of good deeds, suggesting that such actions are in line with Allah's attributes of being forgiving and powerful.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to discriminate between Allah and His messengers and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and wish to adopt a way in between
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to believe in certain aspects of faith while rejecting others, specifically in relation to God's messengers. It underscores the importance of having a unified and unwavering faith in all of God's messengers, as differentiating between them or believing in some while disbelieving in others is considered a form of disbelief. The verse emphasizes that true faith requires acceptance of all divine guidance and messengers without discrimination or selectivity.

translation: Those are the disbelievers, truly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who reject faith are truly disbelievers, and for such individuals, a humiliating punishment has been prepared, indicating a severe consequence for their disbelief.

translation: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not differentiate between any of them - those, He will give them their rewards. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of believing in all the prophets sent by God without making any distinction between them. It highlights that those who have faith in God and all His messengers, and do not differentiate or discriminate between any of them, will be rewarded. The verse underscores God's attributes of being forgiving and merciful, indicating that He will grant them their rewards. The underlying message is one of unity and inclusivity in faith, stressing that the belief in all prophets is a cornerstone of the faith, and that God's mercy and forgiveness are available to those who adhere to this belief.

translation: The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven. They had asked Moses for an even greater miracle, for they said, "Show us Allah manifestly," whereupon the thunderbolt struck them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf [for worship] even after clear proofs had come to them, but We pardoned that [transgression]. And We gave Moses clear authority.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the stubbornness and arrogance of the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) in demanding a miracle or sign from the Prophet Muhammad, similar to or even beyond what they had demanded from previous prophets like Moses. It serves as a warning that such demands are not driven by a genuine search for truth but rather by obstinacy and a tendency to test the limits of divine patience. The verse recalls the historical instances where the Israelites demanded to see God openly and later worshipped the calf despite clear evidence, only to be punished and later forgiven. It underscores the theme that true faith is not about demanding signs but about accepting the clear evidence and guidance provided by God.

translation: And We raised above them the Mount (Tur) over their covenant (with Us), and We said to them: "Enter the gate in prostration" and We said to them: "Do not transgress (the limits) on the Sabbath" and We took from them a firm covenant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the repeated disobedience and covenant-breaking nature of the Israelites. It mentions several instances where they were given clear instructions by God, such as entering a gate in prostration and not transgressing on the Sabbath, yet they failed to comply. The verse underscores the severity of their covenant with God, emphasizing the gravity of their violations and setting the stage for understanding their historical and spiritual context within the narrative of the Qur'an.

translation: So, for their breaking their covenant, and their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets unjustly, and their saying, "Our hearts are wrapped" - nay, Allah has set a seal upon them because of their disbelief, so they do not believe except a few.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of the persistent disobedience and disbelief of a people. Their actions, including breaking covenants, rejecting God's signs, unjustly killing prophets, and claiming ignorance or insincerity ("Our hearts are uncircumcised"), are met with God's sealing of their hearts due to their disbelief. This divine response results in their inability to believe, with only a few exceptions. It underscores the theme that persistent and willful rejection of faith can lead to a state where belief becomes unattainable, a condition brought about by their own actions and God's response to them.

translation: And [We cursed them] for their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of the slander committed by the detractors against Mary, the mother of Jesus. The phrase 'بكفرهم' (because of their disbelief) establishes a link between their disbelief and the slander, suggesting that their rejection of faith led them to spread false accusations against her. The term 'بهتانا عظيما' (a great slander) emphasizes the magnitude of their falsehood, indicating that the accusations were not only untrue but also severe and damaging. This interpretation underscores the idea that the act of slandering Mary is a manifestation of a deeper issue - their disbelief - and serves as a critique of those who spread falsehoods against righteous individuals.

translation: And [for] their saying, "Indeed, we have killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the messenger of Allah ." And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but [another] was made to resemble him to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him, for certain.
interpretation: This verse is addressing a fundamental theological dispute regarding the crucifixion of Jesus Christ. It asserts that the claim by certain groups, likely referring to the Jews, that they killed Jesus, the Messiah, son of Mary, who was a messenger of God, is incorrect. The verse clarifies that Jesus was not actually killed or crucified; instead, it was made to appear so to them. The verse further criticizes those who debate this matter, stating they are in doubt and lack certain knowledge, relying merely on conjecture. It reaffirms that Jesus was not killed with certainty, underscoring the ambiguity and lack of factual basis surrounding the event among those who dispute it. Theologically, this verse is often interpreted as suggesting that God saved Jesus from crucifixion, aligning with Islamic beliefs that reject the crucifixion as a means of Jesus' death, instead often positing alternative narratives such as the substitution of another person in Jesus' place. This interpretation reflects a broader Islamic theological perspective that seeks to correct what it perceives as inaccuracies or misconceptions in other religious narratives regarding Jesus' fate.

translation: But God raised him up to Himself. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the event involving Prophet Jesus (Isa ibn Maryam). The interpretation is that God elevated Jesus to His presence, saving him from the humiliation of being crucified, and this action is a demonstration of God's omnipotence (عزيزا, Aziz) and wise plan (حكيما, Hakim). It signifies that God took control of the situation, intervening in a manner that reflected His power and wisdom, thus protecting Jesus from an unjust fate.

translation: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness.
interpretation: This verse suggests that every person from among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) will come to believe in Jesus (referred to 'him') before their death. The verse is often interpreted to mean that Jesus, being referred to as 'him', will be acknowledged by the People of the Book as a true prophet or servant of God before they die, possibly indicating a universal recognition or belief in Jesus at some point before the Day of Judgment. On the Day of Judgment, Jesus will be a witness against or over them, testifying to their actions and beliefs during their lives.

translation: So, because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them good things which were made lawful for them and [We made unlawful for them good things which were made lawful for them] because of their hindering many [people] from the path of Allah.
interpretation: This verse suggests that due to the wrongdoing of those who were given the Torah (i.e., the Jews), certain previously lawful good things were forbidden to them as a punishment. Additionally, their deviation from the path of Allah was significant, implying that their actions not only harmed themselves but also led many others astray from the righteous path.

translation: And for their taking usury while they had been forbidden from it, and for their consuming the people's wealth unjustly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against two major financial transgressions: usury (riba) and consuming others' wealth unjustly. It signifies that those who engage in such practices, despite being forbidden from doing so, are considered among the disbelievers and are thus deserving of severe punishment. The verse underscores the gravity of these economic sins, equating them with a form of disbelief that warrants a painful retribution. It serves as a cautionary message, emphasizing the importance of ethical financial dealings and adherence to divine prohibitions.

translation: But those who are firmly grounded in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been sent down to you [Muhammad], and what was sent down before you. And the establishers of prayer [are] those who give the zakah and the believers in Allah and the Last Day. Those We will give a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who are rooted in knowledge and those who are not. The 'firmly rooted in knowledge' (الراسخون في العلم) and the believers are characterized by their unwavering faith in the revelations sent down to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and those sent before him. They are also distinguished by their commitment to establishing prayer (المقيمين الصلاة), giving charity (المؤتون الزكاة), and their faith in God and the Last Day. The verse promises that such individuals will be rewarded greatly, indicating that true faith, knowledge, and righteous actions are the keys to a substantial reward in the Hereafter.

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and to David We gave the Book [of Psalms].
interpretation: This verse establishes a connection between the Prophet Muhammad and a long line of prophets before him, emphasizing that the revelation he received is part of a continuous tradition of divine guidance. It underscores the unity of the prophetic message across different times and figures, suggesting that the Prophet Muhammad's experience is not isolated but is linked to a broader history of prophethood in Islam. By listing various prophets, it highlights the universality and consistency of the divine message, reinforcing the legitimacy and authenticity of Muhammad's prophethood by associating it with revered figures from the past.

translation: And messengers We have mentioned to you before and messengers We have not mentioned to you. And to Moses, Allah spoke directly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unique and direct nature of the communication between Allah and Prophet Musa (Moses). The phrase 'وكلم الله موسى تكليما' (And Allah spoke to Moses directly) emphasizes that Moses was honored with a direct conversation with Allah, without the mediation of an angel, underscoring the special status and prophetic role of Moses in Islamic theology.

translation: (We sent) messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners so that mankind may have no plea against Allah after the [sending of] messengers. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purpose of sending prophets by Allah, which is to establish clear proof and remove any potential excuse from humanity for not following the right path. It signifies that with the sending of messengers who give glad tidings to those who do good and warn those who do evil, Allah has made His message clear to humanity, leaving no room for argument or excuse on the Day of Judgment. The attributes of Allah being 'Aziz' (Mighty) and 'Hakim' (Wise) underscore that His actions, including the sending of prophets, are carried out with power and wisdom, reinforcing the idea that His justice and judgment are beyond human challenge or dispute.

translation: But God bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge; and the angels bear witness [as well]. And God is sufficient as a witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reliability and authenticity of the revelation received by the Prophet Muhammad. It asserts that despite potential denials or doubts from others, God bears witness to the truth of the revelation sent down to the Prophet, having done so with full knowledge. The angels too testify to this truth. The verse underscores God's sufficiency as a witness, highlighting His adequacy and reliability in validating the authenticity of the divine message.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the path of Allah have certainly strayed far astray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting faith and obstructing others from the path of righteousness, indicating that such actions lead to a profound and far-reaching deviation from the truth, underscoring the severity of the spiritual and moral delusion that results from such behavior.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and commit injustice, it is not for Allah to forgive them nor to guide them to a path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting faith (kufr) and committing injustice (zulm). It suggests that those who persist in disbelief and wrongdoing are unlikely to receive God's forgiveness or guidance, as their actions are in direct opposition to the path of righteousness. The verse implies that their rejection of faith and engagement in injustice have hardened their hearts, making it improbable for them to receive divine mercy or direction towards the right path.

translation: Except the path of Hell, abiding eternally therein; and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability and ease with which Allah can bring about a consequence or punishment for those who have chosen a path of disobedience, in this case, eternal dwelling in Hell. The phrase 'وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا' (and that is easy for Allah) underscores the omnipotence of Allah, suggesting that bringing about such a consequence is not a challenging or difficult task for Him, emphasizing His absolute power and authority.

translation: O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you. But if you disbelieve - then indeed, to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And ever is God Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of faith and submission to the divine message brought by the Prophet. It suggests that believing in the Prophet and his message is in the best interest of humanity. The verse also serves as a warning, stating that if people choose to reject the message, it will not harm God, as everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. The verse concludes by affirming God's omniscience and wisdom, implying that His plan and judgment are beyond human comprehension, and that faith is a response to His all-encompassing knowledge and wise decree.

translation: O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion or say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a soul [created at a command] from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And do not say, "Three"; desist - it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is but one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse is cautioning the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) against excesses in their faith, specifically the Christian doctrine of Trinity and the divinity of Jesus. It emphasizes that Jesus is a messenger of God and a creation of God, brought into being through God's word 'Be' and His spirit. The verse is urging Christians to abandon the concept of Trinity and recognize the oneness of God, affirming that God is the sole deity and has no offspring or partner, and that everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Him. It encourages faith in God and His messengers, and asserts that God is sufficient as a guardian and protector.

translation: The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels who are nearest [to Allah]. And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant - He will gather them to Himself all together.
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and devotion of the Messiah (Jesus Christ) and the angels closest to Allah, emphasizing their willingness to serve Allah without pride or arrogance. It serves as a warning to those who refuse to worship Allah or are too proud to do so, stating that they will all be gathered before Allah for judgment.

translation: As for those who have believed and done righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards and increase them out of His bounty. But as for those who have disdained and been arrogant, He will afflict them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the reward for the righteous and the punishment for the arrogant. It suggests that those who have faith and perform good deeds will not only receive their due reward but will also be blessed with additional bounty from God, underscoring God's generosity and grace. On the other hand, those who reject faith out of pride and arrogance will face a painful punishment, and in their time of need, they will find no protector or helper other than God, implying their isolation and helplessness. The verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of one's actions and attitudes towards faith and righteousness, emphasizing the importance of humility and good deeds.

translation: O mankind, there has come to you a conclusive proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a manifest light.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the message brought by the Prophet is a clear proof and evidence from God, and the Quran is a clear and manifest light that guides people to the truth. It emphasizes the importance of the revelation as a source of guidance and illumination for humanity.

translation: As for those who believe in God and hold fast to Him, He will admit them to a mercy from Him and bounty, and guide them to Himself on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who have faith in God and seek refuge in Him will be enveloped in His mercy and bounty, and will be guided on the straight path to Him. The 'straight path' is often understood to be a path of righteousness and guidance, and the verse implies that God's guidance is a gift to those who have faith and trust in Him.

translation: They ask you for a legal decision. Say: 'Allah directs (thus) about those who leave no descendants or ascendants as heirs.' If it is a man that dies, leaving a sister but no child, she shall have half his estate: and he shall be her heir if she has no child. If there are two sisters, they shall have two-thirds of the estate (between them): if there are brothers and sisters, the male shall have the share of two females. Allah makes clear to you (His law) lest you err. And Allah has knowledge of everything.
interpretation: This verse provides guidance on the distribution of inheritance when a person dies without leaving behind any children, a scenario referred to as 'kalalah' in Islamic law. It clarifies that if the deceased has a sister and no children, she is entitled to half of the inheritance. Conversely, if the deceased is a woman with no children and she has a brother, he inherits her entire estate. If there are two or more sisters, they collectively receive two-thirds of the inheritance. In cases where the deceased is survived by both brothers and sisters, the principle of distribution is that a male receives twice the share of a female. The verse underscores God's clarification of these rules to prevent confusion among people regarding the distribution of inheritance, highlighting God's omniscience in all matters.

translation: In the name of God, the most Compassionate, the most Merciful. O you who have believed, fulfill the contracts. Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock except for that which is recited to you [in this Qur'an] - hunting not being permitted while you are in the state of ihram. Indeed, Allah ordains what He intends.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling contractual obligations and highlights the permissibility of certain animals for consumption while prohibiting others, particularly during the state of Ihram for Hajj or Umrah, illustrating the balance between legal rulings and spiritual states in Islam.

translation: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah, nor the sacred month, nor the sacrificial animals, nor the garlanded, nor those on their way to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and [His] approval. And when you have come out of ihram, then [you may] hunt. And do not let the hatred of a people for having obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Haram lead you to transgress. And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting the sacred symbols and rituals ordained by Allah, such as the sacred months, the sacrificial animals, and the pilgrimage to the Holy House. It reminds believers that when they are in a state of ihram, they should refrain from hunting and other prohibited actions. The verse also cautions against allowing animosity towards others to lead to transgression, and instead encourages cooperation in righteousness and piety, while warning against collaboration in sin and aggression. Ultimately, it serves as a reminder of Allah's severe punishment for those who disobey His commands.

translation: Prohibited to you are: dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that on which hath been invoked the name of other than Allah; that which hath been killed by strangling, or by a violent blow, or by a headlong fall, or by being gored to death; that which hath been (partly) eaten by a wild animal; unless ye are able to slaughter it (in due form); that which is sacrificed on stone (altars); (forbidden) also is to seek to know your fate by divination arrows: that is impiety. This day those who reject faith have given up all hope of your religion: yet fear them not, but fear Me. This day have I perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and have chosen for you Islam as your religion. But if any is forced by hunger, with no inclination to transgression, Allah is indeed Oft-forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse signifies a pivotal moment in Islamic history where the faith was perfected and the believers were freed from the fear of their detractors, as the disbelievers had lost hope in undermining their religion. It outlines dietary restrictions, emphasizing God's mercy and forgiveness towards those who, under extreme necessity and without inclination towards sin, may consume otherwise forbidden foods.

translation: They ask you (O Muhammad) what is made lawful for them. Say: 'Lawful for you are the good things. And those beasts and birds of prey which you have trained as hounds, teaching them as God has taught you; so eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of God over it. And have fear of God, surely, God is swift in reckoning.'
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle that God has permitted certain good and lawful things for human consumption, and that humans can also train animals to hunt for them. The act of training these animals is seen as a form of imparting God's knowledge to them, and when they catch prey, the people are allowed to eat it as long as they invoke God's name and are mindful of their accountability to Him. The verse highlights the importance of acknowledging God's sovereignty over all aspects of life, including the way people obtain their sustenance. It also underscores the idea that God's reckoning is swift, emphasizing the need for people to be mindful of their actions and to adhere to the guidelines set forth by Him.

translation: This day [all] good foods have been made lawful, and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them. And [lawful in marriage are] chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their due dowries, desiring chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse or taking [secret] lovers. And whoever denies the faith - his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the permissibility of interfaith marriage and dietary practices between Muslims and the People of the Book (Jews and Christians), emphasizing the importance of maintaining faith and righteous actions. It underscores that while certain social and dietary interactions are permissible, faith in Islam is crucial, and apostasy leads to the nullification of one's deeds and loss in the Hereafter.

translation: O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows and wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles. And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves. But if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not want to place a burden on you, but He wants to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of purification in Islam, both physically and spiritually. It shows that God intends to ease the lives of believers by providing alternatives for purification when water is not available or when one is in a state that makes the use of water difficult, such as illness or travel. The act of purification is not just a physical act but is deeply connected to the completion of God's blessings upon the believers and their gratitude towards Him. It signifies that the rituals in Islam are designed to facilitate a believer's life while maintaining a strong connection with their Creator.

translation: And remember the favor of God upon you and His covenant which He bound you with when you said, 'We hear and we obey.' And fear God. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse is reminding the believers to be mindful of God's favor upon them and the covenant they made with Him when they pledged their obedience. It is cautioning them to maintain their fear of God, as He is aware of their innermost thoughts and intentions, implying that one's outward actions should be consistent with their inner beliefs and that God will judge them based on their true intentions.

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing up for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and fairness, even towards those one may dislike or be in conflict with. It warns against allowing personal biases or animosity towards a particular group or individual to influence one's judgment, and instead encourages believers to uphold justice and equity. The verse suggests that being just is closely related to being God-conscious (muttaqi) and that God is aware of all actions, thus implying that justice is not only a moral virtue but also a means of demonstrating one's devotion to God.

translation: God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's promise to believers who perform righteous deeds, assuring them of two great rewards: forgiveness for their past sins and a great recompense, likely referring to Paradise or a high status in the hereafter. It emphasizes the dual nature of God's mercy and reward, encouraging believers to maintain their faith and good actions.

translation: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those are the companions of the blazing fire.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the consequence of rejecting faith and denying the signs of God. It suggests that those who disbelieve and reject the truth will be companions of the blazing fire, or hell, implying a severe and eternal punishment for their actions.

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people intended to stretch out their hands against you, but He restrained their hands from you. And fear Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse is an exhortation to the believers to remain vigilant in their faith and trust in Allah's protection. It recalls a specific instance where a group of people had hostile intentions towards the believers, planning to attack them, but Allah intervened and restrained their hands. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's favor and protection towards the believers, encouraging them to be mindful of their duty to fear Allah (Taqwa) and to place their trust (Tawakkul) in Him alone. It underscores the importance of reliance on Allah's power and providence, especially in the face of adversity or potential harm, highlighting that true security and safety come from Him.

translation: And Allah had already taken a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We appointed from among them twelve leaders. And Allah said, "I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakat and believe in My messengers and support them and lend Allah a good loan, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever disbelieves after that among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way."
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the Muslim community of the solemn covenant that Allah took from the Children of Israel, emphasizing the importance of fulfilling their commitments to Allah, including establishing prayer, giving zakat, believing in His messengers, supporting them, and lending Allah a good loan. It highlights the consequences of faithfulness versus unfaithfulness, warning that those who turn away after having been guided will lose their way. The verse subtly cautions the Muslim community not to follow in the footsteps of the Children of Israel, who failed to uphold their covenant, by emphasizing the rewards for obedience and the punishment for disobedience, thereby encouraging steadfastness in their faith and actions.

translation: So, for their breaking their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They change the words from their (right) places and have forgotten a good part of the message that was given them. You will not cease to discover deceit in them, except a few of them. But forgive them, and overlook (their misdeeds). Indeed, God loves those who do good.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the behavior of a group, likely the Children of Israel or some other group from the People of the Book, for breaking their covenant, distorting the scripture, and forgetting parts of it. Despite their treachery, the verse advises the Prophet to pardon and forgive them, as God loves those who do good. The underlying message is one of advocating for mercy and benevolence towards others, even in the face of their wrongdoing, as long as one is acting with good intentions. It highlights the importance of moral character and the virtue of being benevolent, reflecting the broader Islamic values of compassion and forgiveness.

translation: And [We cursed] those who said, "We are Christians," - We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded. So We caused [enmity and hatred] to endure among them until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah is going to inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the consequences of the Christians forgetting a significant part of the message they were given. It suggests that as a result of this forgetfulness, God caused enmity and hatred to arise among them, a state that will persist until the Day of Judgment. The implication is that their internal divisions and conflicts are a direct consequence of their deviation from the original teachings they were entrusted with. The verse also foreshadows that God will inform them about their actions, implying a reckoning for their deeds.

translation: O People of the Scripture, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you much of what you used to hide of the Scripture and overlooking much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has come to clarify and reveal many of the truths and teachings that were previously hidden or distorted within the scripture of the People of the Book (Jews and Christians). It indicates a purification and correction of the religious understanding, guided by the light and clear guidance of the Qur'an, which is a source of illumination from God.

translation: With it God guides those who pursue His pleasure to the ways of peace and brings them out of darknesses into the light, by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of the Qur'an or divine guidance in leading those who seek God's pleasure to paths of peace and salvation. It signifies that by following divine guidance, individuals can transition from states of ignorance, confusion, or darkness to enlightenment and righteousness, ultimately being directed towards a straight and virtuous path, with the understanding that this process occurs under God's will and permission.

translation: Those who say, "Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary" have certainly fallen into disbelief. Say, "Who could prevent Allah from destroying the Messiah, son of Mary, his mother, and everyone else on earth?" To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and everything in between. He creates whatever He wills. And Allah is Most Capable of everything.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who believe that Jesus, the son of Mary, is God. It challenges their belief by questioning who can possibly stop God if He decides to destroy Jesus, his mother, and everyone else on earth, emphasizing God's omnipotence and sole authority over all creation. The verse underscores the Islamic belief in the oneness of God (Tawhid) and asserts that God is the creator and controller of the universe, capable of doing anything He wills.

translation: And the Jews and the Christians say, "We are the children of Allah and His beloved." Say, "Why then does He punish you for your sins?" Rather, you are human beings from among those He has created. He forgives whom He wills, and He punishes whom He wills. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse critiques the exclusivist claims of Jews and Christians who considered themselves to be the 'children and beloved ones of God'. The verse challenges this notion by questioning why, if they were indeed so privileged, God would punish them for their sins. It asserts that, like all other humans, they are subject to God's judgment and mercy, and that their status before God is not different from that of others. The verse underscores the universal sovereignty of God over all creation and emphasizes that accountability and judgment are based on individual actions, not on claims of special status or lineage. It serves as a reminder that divine mercy and punishment are not limited by ethnic or religious identity but are exercised according to God's will.

translation: O People of the Scripture, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and overlooking much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book. With it Allah guides whoever pursues His pleasure to ways of peace and brings them out from darknesses into the light, by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the advent of the Prophet Muhammad marked the end of a period where there was a gap in the succession of prophets, thereby fulfilling God's promise to never leave humanity without guidance. It emphasizes that with the arrival of the Prophet, the excuse of not having a warner or a bearer of good tidings is no longer valid, and it underscores God's omnipotence in being able to accomplish all things.

translation: And [mention] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you when He appointed among you prophets and made you possessors and gave you that which He had not given anyone among the worlds."
interpretation: This verse highlights the numerous blessings that Allah bestowed upon the Children of Israel, including the appointment of prophets among them, granting them kingship and dominion, and providing them with favors and bounties that were unparalleled among the nations of their time. The verse serves as a reminder to the Children of Israel to acknowledge and appreciate these divine favors, and it underscores the idea that such blessings come with the expectation of gratitude and righteous conduct.

translation: O my people, enter the holy land which Allah has written for you, and turn not back (in flight) for then ye will be turned back in loss.
interpretation: This verse is urging the Israelites to enter the sacred land that God has ordained for them, warning them not to turn back, lest they suffer a great loss. The verse is highlighting the importance of obedience to God's command and the consequences of disobedience. It is emphasizing that the Israelites should have faith and trust in God's promise and not let fear or doubt cause them to retreat. The verse is also underscoring the idea that turning back or retreating would result in a great loss, not just a physical loss, but also a spiritual one, as it would indicate a lack of faith and trust in God.

translation: They said, "O Moses, indeed within it is a people of giant stature, and indeed, we will not enter it until they exit from it; so if they exit from it then we will be enterers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological barrier that fear and perception of others' strength can create. The Israelites, despite being commanded by Moses to enter the sacred land, express their reluctance due to the presence of 'giants' or powerful people, indicating how the perception of others' power can deter one from fulfilling a divine command or achieving a goal, unless those perceived as powerful are removed or weakened.

translation: Two men of those who feared [God] and on whom Allah had bestowed favour said, 'Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, you will be victorious. And upon Allah put your trust, if you are indeed believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust in Allah and the inevitability of success when one puts their faith into action with the right strategy. The two men who were God-fearing and had been blessed with wisdom by Allah advised the believers to enter the gate with resolve, assuring them of victory upon doing so, but also reminded them to place their trust in Allah, a condition that underscores the Islamic principle that true faith is accompanied by reliance on God's will and support.

translation: They said, "O Moses, indeed we will not enter it, ever, as long as they are within it; so go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are remaining here, right here."
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological state of the Israelites, who, despite witnessing numerous miracles and being on the brink of entering the Promised Land, exhibit cowardice and disobedience. Their statement reflects a deep-seated lack of faith in God's promise and a misplaced fear of the inhabitants of the land. By saying "Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we will stay here," they not only refuse to follow Moses but also imply a rejection of God's command, showcasing their reluctance to take the necessary actions to fulfill God's covenant with them. This verse serves as a critique of their faithlessness and lack of trust in divine providence.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, I have control over none but myself and my brother, so distinguish between us and the defiantly disobedient people'
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of human capability and authority, as Prophet Musa (Moses) acknowledges that he and his brother Harun (Aaron) are the only ones he has influence over, and that the ultimate decision and power rest with Allah. It signifies the recognition of the boundaries of individual influence and the need to rely on divine guidance and intervention in the face of adversity or unrighteousness.

translation: He said, 'Then indeed it is forbidden to them for forty years [in which] they will wander throughout the land. So do not grieve over the people who are defiantly disobedient.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that due to their disobedience and lack of faith, the Israelites were condemned to wander aimlessly in the wilderness for forty years, being barred from entering the sacred land they yearned for. The directive to the Prophet not to grieve over the fate of the rebellious people underscores the inevitability of divine judgment upon those who defy God's commands, emphasizing the need for submission to God's will.

translation: And recite to them the story of Adam's two sons, [Abel and Cain] in truth, when they both offered a sacrifice [to Allah ], and it was accepted from one of them but was not accepted from the other. The latter said, 'I will surely kill you.' The former said, 'Indeed, Allah only accepts from the righteous [who fear Him].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of righteousness and piety in determining the acceptance of one's deeds by Allah. The story of the two sons of Adam serves as a warning that the mere act of performing a ritual or offering a sacrifice is not enough; what matters is the state of one's heart and the intention behind the action. The acceptance of one's deeds is contingent upon one's level of taqwa (piety or God-consciousness), underscoring the need for sincerity and righteousness in one's actions.

translation: If you stretch out your hand to kill me, I will not stretch out my hand to kill you, for I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral superiority of the righteous individual over the aggressor. The speaker is indicating that even when faced with the threat of violence, they will not resort to violence themselves, out of reverence for God and a commitment to moral principles, demonstrating a reliance on divine justice rather than taking matters into their own hands.

translation: Indeed, I want you to take on my sin and your sin, so you will be among the companions of the Fire; and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of wrongdoing and the burden of sin. By stating that the person will bear both their own sin and the sin of the speaker, it emphasizes the gravity of taking on the responsibility of another's wrongdoing. The verse serves as a warning that such actions will lead to severe punishment, as represented by being among the companions of the Fire. It underscores the principle that wrongdoers will face just retribution for their deeds.

translation: So his soul encouraged him and made him feel good the killing of his brother; he killed him and became among the losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the devastating consequences of succumbing to one's base desires, as embodied by the story of Cain and Abel. The fact that Cain's 'self' or 'soul' (nafs) 'embellished' or 'adorned' (zawwamat) the act of murder for him signifies the corrupting influence of one's inner, worldly desires, which can lead an individual astray from the path of righteousness and into committing grave injustices. It underscores the internal struggle between good and evil inclinations within a person and the tragic outcome when the baser inclinations prevail, resulting in loss and ruin, both spiritually and morally.

translation: Then Allah sent a raven digging into the earth to show him how to conceal the corpse of his brother. He said, 'Woe is me! Have I failed to be like this raven and conceal the corpse of my brother?' And he became one of the regretful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the theme of accountability and the consequences of one's actions. The story of Cain and Abel serves as a reminder that one's deeds, whether good or bad, have repercussions. The character of Cain, who is unable to hide his brother's corpse, is a symbol of the inescapable nature of guilt and the inevitability of being held accountable for one's actions. The raven sent by God serves as a catalyst for Cain's realization of his own shortcomings and his subsequent remorse, underscoring the idea that individuals must confront and atone for their wrongdoings.

translation: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption [done] in the land - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves one - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And certainly did Our messengers come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, [even] after that, throughout the land, were transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of taking a life unjustly and the value of saving one. It signifies that the act of unjustly killing one person is tantamount to killing all of humanity, emphasizing the sanctity of human life. Conversely, saving one life is as significant as saving all of humanity, underscoring the importance of preserving life. The verse also criticizes the Children of Israel for their historical transgressions and excesses despite being guided by clear signs from God's messengers, indicating a pattern of disobedience and moral decay.

translation: The punishment of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth [to cause] corruption is that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment
interpretation: This verse outlines the severe consequences for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger, and cause corruption on earth. The punishments mentioned - execution, crucifixion, mutilation, or exile - serve as a deterrent to those who would seek to undermine the social and religious order. The verse highlights the gravity of such actions, indicating that they are not merely criminal but are considered a rebellion against the divine authority. The dual punishment, both in this life and the next, underscores the seriousness with which Islam views such transgressions, emphasizing that the consequences of such actions are not limited to this world but extend into the hereafter.

translation: Except for those who repent before you have them in your power; for then know that God is Forgiving, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of the timing of repentance. It signifies that those who repent before being caught or brought to justice will be forgiven, emphasizing God's mercy and forgiveness for those who turn back to Him before being held accountable by others.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means [of nearness] to Him and strive in His cause that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving for spiritual proximity to God (wasila) as a means to attain success (falah). The concept of 'wasila' refers to the means or the way to get closer to God, which can be achieved through righteous deeds and acts of worship. The verse encourages believers to cultivate a strong relationship with God by seeking nearness to Him, and to exert their utmost efforts in His cause (jihad fi sabilihi), thereby implying that true success is contingent upon one's ability to draw closer to God and to dedicate themselves to His path.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - if they should have all that is in the earth and the like of it with it by which to ransom themselves from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it will not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of the punishment on the Day of Judgment for those who have rejected faith. It suggests that on that Day, the disbelievers will desperately wish they could ransom themselves from the torment by offering everything they could possibly give, even if it were to be double the wealth of the entire earth. However, their ransom will not be accepted, and they will face a painful punishment, indicating the hopelessness and irreversibility of their situation on the Day of Judgment.

translation: They will wish to come out of the Fire, but they will not be able to; and for them is an enduring punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futile aspirations of those who have been condemned to Hellfire. Despite their ardent desire to escape the torment, it is an impossibility for them. The verse serves as a stark reminder of the permanence of the punishment for those who have rejected faith and lived a life of disobedience to God's commandments. The 'persistent punishment' they are to endure signifies the eternal nature of their suffering, underscoring the gravity of their actions in the worldly life and the inescapable consequences that follow in the hereafter.

translation: And [as for] the thief, the male and the female, amputate their hands in recompense for what they committed as a deterrent [punishment] from Allah . And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse is often cited in discussions about punishment for theft in Islamic law. The interpretation here is that it emphasizes the severity of the punishment for theft, cutting off the hands of the thief, as a deterrent and a consequence of their actions. The phrase 'Nakal-an min Allah' suggests that this punishment is a form of divine deterrence, indicating that it is not merely a human-made law but a divinely ordained consequence. The attributes of Allah as 'Aziz' (Mighty) and 'Hakim' (Wise) underscore that the punishment is both a manifestation of His power and a wise legislative measure aimed at maintaining social order.

translation: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed, Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, emphasizing that those who repent and mend their ways after committing wrongdoing can be forgiven. It underscores the idea that true repentance, coupled with a genuine effort to correct one's actions, is met with divine mercy and pardon, reflecting Allah's attributes of being forgiving and merciful.

translation: Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and God is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's absolute sovereignty over the heavens and the earth, emphasizing His power to punish or forgive whomever He wills, illustrating His omnipotence and authority over all things.

translation: O Prophet, let not those who hurry into disbelief grieve you - those who say, "We believe" with their mouths, but their hearts do not believe, and [among] those who are Jews [there are those who are] attentive to falsehood, attentive to other people who have not come to you. They distort the meaning of the [revealed] words, [saying], "If you are given this, take it; but if you are not given it, then beware." And he whom God intends to test - you will not possess for him anything against God. Those are the ones whom God does not intend to purify their hearts. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to be disheartened by those who hasten to disbelieve, including those who claim to have faith but whose hearts are not truly committed to it. It also criticizes certain Jews who are prone to listening to falsehood and to the words of others who have not even come to the Prophet. They distort the scripture by altering the meaning of its words. The verse highlights God's control over the fate of individuals, stating that those whom God intends to test will not be protected by anyone else. It underscores that those whose hearts God does not intend to purify will face humiliation in this world and a severe punishment in the hereafter.

translation: Listeners to falsehood, eaters of the unlawful. If they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. If you turn away from them, they will not harm you in any way. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who are just.
interpretation: This verse is warning the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) about the hypocrites and those who are prone to falsehood and corruption. It is indicating that even if they come to him for judgment, he should either judge between them justly or turn away from them, and that turning away from them will not cause him any harm. The verse is emphasizing the importance of justice and fairness in judgment, and reminding that Allah loves those who are just and fair.

translation: And how do they make you a judge while they have the Torah, wherein is the judgment of Allah? Then they turn away after that, and those are not believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inconsistency and hypocrisy of those who claim to believe in the Torah, which contains God's judgment, yet they turn away from it and do not adhere to its rulings. It suggests that true faith requires not just having the scripture, but also following its guidance and judgments.

translation: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to Allah] judged by it for the Jews, as did the rabbis and scholars by that with which they were entrusted of the Scripture of Allah, and they were witnesses thereto. So do not fear the people but fear Me, and do not sell My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the divine law as revealed in the Torah. It highlights that the Prophets, Rabbis, and Scholars were entrusted with the responsibility of upholding and judging according to the Book of Allah, serving as witnesses to its teachings. The verse warns against fearing human disapproval over divine displeasure and cautions against compromising or trading away God's revelations for worldly gain. Ultimately, it declares that those who fail to rule according to God's revelations are considered disbelievers, underscoring the gravity of deviating from divine guidance in governance and judgment.

translation: And We ordained for them therein a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds is legal retribution. But whoever gives [up his right as] charity, it is an expiation for him. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of justice and retribution in a fair and proportional manner. The law of 'qisas' or retribution is prescribed, where the punishment matches the crime. However, it also introduces the concept of forgiveness and charity, suggesting that if one forgives the perpetrator, it can serve as an expiation for their own wrongdoing. The verse concludes by emphasizing that those who fail to rule according to God's revelations are considered wrongdoers, underscoring the divine origin of justice and the necessity of adhering to it.

translation: And We sent, following in their footsteps, Jesus, the son of Mary, confirming that which came before him in the Torah; and We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light and confirming that which preceded it of the Torah as guidance and instruction for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity and validation of divine revelation across different prophets and scriptures. It signifies that Jesus was sent as a confirmer of the Torah, which was revealed before him, and was given the Gospel, which contained guidance, light, and served as a confirmation of the Torah. The verse underscores the importance of the Gospel as a source of guidance and admonition specifically for those who are mindful of God, indicating that the message of Jesus was particularly relevant for the righteous among his people.

translation: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the teachings and laws revealed in the Injil (the Gospel revealed to Jesus) for those who claim to follow it. It warns that those who do not judge or live according to what God has revealed are considered 'fāsiqūn' (transgressors or disobedient ones), indicating a deviation from the right path and disobedience to God's commandments.

translation: And We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming what came before it of the Scripture and as a guardian over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations away from what has come to you of the truth. To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. And if Allah had willed, He would have made you one nation [united in religion], but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you; so race to [all that is] good. To Allah is your return all together, and He will [then] inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of adhering to the divine guidance revealed in the Qur'an, emphasizing its role as a confirmer and guardian over previous scriptures. It underscores the need for the Prophet to judge according to what Allah has revealed, rather than following the desires of others. The diversity in laws and paths among different communities is seen as a test from Allah, with the ultimate goal being to prompt believers to compete in good deeds. The verse concludes by affirming that all will return to Allah, who will then reveal the truth about the matters on which people had differed.

translation: And judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations and beware of them, lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. And if they turn away, then know that Allah only wants to afflict them with some of their sins. And indeed, many among the people are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine guidance in judgment and decision-making, warning against the influence of personal biases or external pressures that may lead one astray from the truth revealed by Allah. It suggests that when people reject or turn away from divine guidance, it may be a consequence of their own wrongdoing, implying a causal relationship between their actions and the afflictions they suffer. Furthermore, it highlights the prevalence of disobedience among people, underscoring the challenge of maintaining righteousness in a society where many are inclined to defy divine commands.

translation: Do they then seek the judgement of (the Days of) Ignorance? And who is better in judgement than Allah for a people who have firm Faith.
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that criticizes those who seek judgment based on pre-Islamic ignorance (Jahiliyyah) rather than the law of Allah. It asserts that for people who have true faith and conviction (yوقنون), there is no better or more just law than that of Allah, implying that seeking other forms of judgment is a rejection of faith or a lack of certainty in one's beliefs.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you - then indeed, he is [one] of them. Indeed, Allah guides not the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the believers against forming alliances or showing undue allegiance to those who are fundamentally opposed to the Islamic faith, specifically the Jews and Christians. It highlights that such groups are mutually supportive of one another, implying a solidarity that is contrary to the interests of the Muslim community. By allying with them, Muslims risk being assimilated into their ranks, not just in a political or social sense, but also in terms of their religious identity and values. The underlying message is that such allegiances can lead to a dilution of one's faith and commitment to the principles of Islam. The verse concludes by underscoring that God's guidance is withheld from those who engage in unjust behavior, suggesting that forming such alliances is not only unwise but also contrary to divine will, as it is considered a form of injustice or transgression against the faith and its adherents.

translation: So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening to them, saying, 'We fear lest a misfortune befall us.' But perhaps God will bring about a conquest or a decision from Him, and they will become regretful of what they have been hiding within themselves.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the behavior of hypocrites who hasten to befriend and curry favor with those in power, driven by their own self-interest and fear of being adversely affected by changing circumstances. It suggests that their eagerness to ingratiate themselves is motivated by a desire to avoid being caught out or harmed should the current state of affairs change for the worse ('دائرة' implying a turn of fortune or calamity). The verse then cautions that God may bring about a decisive event or command ('الفتح أو أمر من عنده') that will reveal the true nature of their actions and cause them to regret their secret intentions and duplicitous behavior.

translation: And those who believe will say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that they were with you?" Their deeds have become worthless, so they have become losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony and consequences of hypocrisy. Believers remark on the hypocrites' fervent oaths that they stood with the believers, yet their actions were in vain due to their lack of genuine faith, resulting in their deeds being rendered worthless and ultimately leading to their loss.

translation: O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - God will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him [who are] humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of God and do not fear the censure of a critic. That is the favor of God; He bestows it upon whom He wills. And God is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is a message of reassurance to the believers that if some of them were to apostatize, God would bring forth another group of people who would be devoted to their faith, humble towards the believers, and strong against the disbelievers. These new adherents to the faith would be characterized by their unwavering commitment to struggle in the cause of God, unswayed by the criticism or blame of others. This verse highlights God's ability to replace those who turn away from the faith with others who are more steadfast and devoted, underscoring the idea that God's favor is not limited to a particular group or individual, but is rather bestowed upon whomsoever He wills, as He is all-encompassing and all-knowing.

translation: Your (real) guardians are (no less than) Allah, His Messenger, and the believers,- those who establish regular prayers and regular charity, and they bow down humbly (in worship).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of loyalty and allegiance in Islam, stating that the true guardians and protectors of believers are Allah, His Messenger, and those who have faith, specifically highlighting those who establish prayer and give charity while in a state of humility (while bowing in prayer), indicating that true faith is demonstrated through both belief and righteous actions, particularly those performed with sincerity and devotion.

translation: And whoever takes Allah, His Messenger, and those who have believed [as allies] - indeed, the party of Allah - they will be the predominant.
