interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the believers of the consequences of not participating in jihad or striving in the cause of Allah. It signifies that failure to do so will result in Allah's punishment and that He has the power to replace them with others who are more willing to strive in His cause, emphasizing the importance of being proactive in one's faith and the potential consequences of inaction.

translation: If you do not help him, certainly Allah did help him when those who disbelieved had driven him out, being one of two, when they both were in the cave, when he was saying to his companion, 'Do not grieve; surely Allah is with us.' So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with soldiers you did not see, and He made the word of those who disbelieved the lower, and the word of Allah is the uppermost. And Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine support given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) during his migration from Mecca to Medina, particularly when he was in the cave with Abu Bakr. It signifies that even when human support seems minimal or absent, God's support is always present. The verse conveys that God's assistance is not contingent upon the number of followers or visible helpers; rather, it is based on the righteousness of the cause and the faith of the individuals involved. The 'armies' that supported the Prophet were unseen, referring to angels or other forms of divine aid, underscoring the idea that God's help can manifest in various, sometimes unseen, ways. The ultimate triumph of God's word over the disbelievers' word is assured because God is 'Aziz' (Mighty) and 'Hakim' (Wise), attributes that guarantee the effectiveness and wisdom behind His actions.

translation: March forth, whether you are lightly or heavily armed, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of Allah. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving in the cause of Allah with both one's wealth and oneself, regardless of the circumstances or challenges. It suggests that such striving is in the best interest of the believers, provided they understand the value and purpose of their actions.

translation: If there had been [nearly] immediate gain and an easy journey, they would have followed you, but distant was the journey to them. And they will swear by Allah, "If we were able, we would have gone out with you," destroying themselves [through false oaths], and Allah knows that indeed they are liars.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the hypocrisy of certain individuals who claimed to be willing to follow and support the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) but were actually unwilling to make the effort to do so. The verse suggests that if the goal was easily attainable and the journey was short, they would have followed, but because it required significant effort and travel, they were deterred. The verse is also pointing out that these individuals were willing to swear oaths to justify their inaction, essentially condemning themselves by their own false claims. The underlying message is that God is aware of their deception and that their excuses are nothing but lies.

translation: May Allah pardon you; why did you grant them permission [to stay behind] until those who told the truth were evident to you and you knew the liars?
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for allowing some hypocrites to stay behind or be excused from participating in a battle or an obligation without properly verifying their sincerity or truthfulness. The verse suggests that the Prophet should have waited until it became clear who among them were genuinely truthful in their excuses and who were lying. The phrase "عفا الله عنك" (Allah has pardoned you) indicates that despite this criticism, Allah has forgiven the Prophet for his action, implying that the Prophet's decision, although not ideal, was made out of compassion or due to a lack of clear information at the time.

translation: Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission to strive with their wealth and their lives. And Allah is Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristic of true believers, who are so devoted to their faith that they do not need to seek permission or make excuses to participate in jihad, using both their wealth and their lives. It signifies their eagerness and readiness to sacrifice for the cause of their faith, demonstrating a deep-seated conviction and commitment. The verse also underscores God's omniscience regarding those who are righteous and fearful of Him, implying that He knows who is genuinely devoted and will be rewarded accordingly.

translation: Only those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day ask your permission (to stay behind). And their hearts have doubted, and they are in their doubt, wavering.
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological state of hypocrites who lack conviction in their faith. The phrase 'their hearts are in doubt' suggests that they are uncertain and torn between belief and disbelief. As a result, they waver and are indecisive, indicating a lack of firm resolve or commitment. This verse implies that true faith is characterized by conviction and certainty, whereas hypocrisy is marked by doubt and indecision.

translation: And if they had intended to march out, they would certainly have made some preparation for it; but Allah disliked their being sent forth, so He made them lag behind, and it was said (to them), "Sit you among those who are sitting."
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the reluctance and lack of sincerity of some individuals who claimed to be willing to participate in a noble cause, likely a battle or a significant communal effort, but were actually hesitant. It suggests that had they truly intended to take part, they would have made necessary preparations. However, God was not pleased with their activation or participation, leading to their discouragement and being advised to remain with those who were already not participating, effectively being told to stay behind.

translation: Had they marched out among you, they would not have added to you [anything] except trouble and would have hurried about among you [spreading] sedition. And among you are listeners to them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the potential harm that certain individuals or groups could cause if they were to join or be among the believers. It suggests that their presence would not only lead to corruption and discord but also sow dissent and create divisions. The phrase 'ولأوضعوا خلالكم يبغونكم الفتنة' indicates that they would actively seek to spread strife and cause trouble among the believers. The verse further notes that there are those among the believers who are receptive to the whispers or plans of these troublemakers. Ultimately, it emphasizes God's awareness of those who are unjust or wrongdoers, implying that He is fully knowledgeable of the intentions and actions of these individuals and will hold them accountable.

translation: They had sought to cause strife before and had upset matters for you until the truth came and the command of Allah became manifest, much to their dislike.
interpretation: This verse highlights the behavior of those who opposed the truth, indicating that they had previously sought to cause strife and turmoil, and had manipulated matters against the Prophet and his followers. However, despite their efforts to thwart it, the truth ultimately prevailed, and God's command was fulfilled, even though it was against their will. It serves as a reminder that those who resist the truth will ultimately be unable to prevent its triumph.

translation: And among them is he who says, "Permit me [to remain at home] and do not put me to trial." Unquestionably, into trial they have fallen. And indeed, Hell will surround the disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological and spiritual weakness of some individuals who, when faced with the prospect of participating in a challenging or potentially dangerous situation, such as a battle, make excuses to avoid it. Their request to be excused is not just a practical request but also a reflection of their deeper fear of being tested or tempted beyond their endurance, indicating a lack of faith or resolve. The verse suggests that those who make such excuses have already succumbed to the test or trial (فتنة) by showing their weakness and lack of resolve. It further emphasizes the inevitability of punishment for those who reject faith, stating that Hell will encompass the disbelievers, underscoring the consequence of lacking the resolve to stand by one's faith in the face of adversity.

translation: If good befalls you, it grieves them; but if a misfortune befalls you, they say, "We had taken our precaution beforehand," and they turn away rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the duplicitous nature of the hypocrites towards the believers. It indicates that when good fortune or success befalls a believer, the hypocrites are displeased, showing their underlying envy or resentment. Conversely, if a believer is afflicted with misfortune, the hypocrites rejoice, attributing their own success or safety to their prior caution or decision-making, and they turn away with joy, reveling in the misfortune of others. It underscores the complex dynamics of social relationships during the time of the Prophet, where the faith and actions of true believers were often met with skepticism, jealousy, or outright hostility from those who did not share their convictions.

translation: Say, 'Never will we be struck except by what Allah has decreed for us; He is our protector.' And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine decree and the importance of trust in Allah. It reassures believers that nothing happens to them except what Allah has ordained, and therefore, they should place their trust in Him. The verse encourages the faithful to have unwavering confidence in Allah's plan and to rely on Him, as He is their guardian and protector.

translation: Say, 'Do you await for us except one of the two best things while we await for you that Allah will afflict you with punishment from Himself or at our hands? So wait; indeed we, along with you, are waiting.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the mutual anticipation between the believers and their adversaries, with the believers awaiting either victory or martyrdom, both of which are considered good outcomes, while their adversaries await the believers' downfall, either through divine punishment or at the hands of their enemies. It underscores the patience and readiness of the believers as they await the outcome, emphasizing their conviction in the face of adversity.

translation: Say, "Spend willingly or unwillingly; never will it be accepted from you. Indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and faith in one's actions. It suggests that even if people were to spend their wealth, either willingly or begrudgingly, their actions would not be accepted by Allah because their hearts are not pure and they are rebellious against His command. The underlying message is that outward actions, without the right inner disposition and faith, are devoid of true value in the sight of Allah.

translation: And nothing prevents their expenditures from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and in His Messenger and that they come not to prayer except while they are lazy and do not spend except while they are reluctant.
interpretation: The verse highlights that the hypocrites' reluctance to spend in the cause of Allah is rooted in their fundamental lack of faith in Allah and His Messenger. Their actions, such as performing prayer and giving charity, are done half-heartedly, indicating their inner disdain and unwillingness. This verse serves as a critique of superficial religiosity, suggesting that true faith is demonstrated not just by outward actions, but by the sincerity and willingness with which they are performed.

translation: So, let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only wants to punish them with these things in this worldly life and (that) their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers not to be deceived by the worldly possessions and the children of the disbelievers. It highlights that God allows them these blessings not as a favor, but as a means to increase their suffering in this life and to ultimately lead them to spiritual destruction while they remain in their state of disbelief. The verse underscores the concept that worldly prosperity is not necessarily a sign of divine favor, and that it can be used by God as a means to test and ultimately punish those who are ungrateful and disobedient.

translation: And they swear by Allah that they are indeed from among you while they are not from among you; but they are a people who are afraid (or divided).
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological and social dynamics of hypocrisy within a community. The hypocrites, despite swearing by Allah that they are among the believers, are actually not part of them. Their actions and oaths are driven by fear and a desire to avoid conflict or persecution, rather than genuine faith. The phrase 'قوم يفرقون' (a people who are afraid or divided) suggests that their fear or division leads them to adopt a duplicitous stance, highlighting the tension between outward professions of faith and inward doubts or allegiances. This verse serves as a commentary on the complexities of social identity and belonging, where individuals may outwardly conform to the norms of a group while inwardly harboring different beliefs or loyalties.

translation: If they could find a refuge, or caves, or a place to enter, they would turn to it while they rush headlong.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and lack of conviction of those who are not truly committed to their faith. It suggests that if they could find a safe refuge, a hiding place, or an escape route, they would hastily turn to it, indicating their readiness to abandon their professed beliefs or loyalties at the first sign of difficulty or danger. The phrase 'وهم يجمحون' (and they rush headlong) underscores the eagerness and haste with which they would seek to escape, revealing their lack of steadfastness and resolve.

translation: And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities. If they are given some of it, they are pleased, but if they are not given some of it, at once they become enraged.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing a group of hypocrites who were displeased with the Prophet's (peace be upon him) distribution of charity, implying that their faith is conditional upon their personal gain, and that they become discontented when their expectations are not met.

translation: And if they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them, and had said, 'Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us of His bounty and [so will] His Messenger; indeed to Allah we are desirous.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being content with what Allah has provided and having faith in His promise to grant more. It suggests that those who are satisfied with Allah's provision and trust in His generosity, expressing their reliance on Him, will be recipients of His bounty. The verse underscores the value of having a strong faith and trust in Allah's plan, indicating that those who are eager to return to Allah (راغبون) with sincere intentions will be rewarded.

translation: Zakat expenditures are only for the poor and for the needy and for those employed to collect [zakat] and for bringing hearts together [for Islam] and for freeing captives [or slaves] and for those in debt and for the cause of Allah and for the [stranded] traveler - an obligation [imposed] by Allah. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse outlines the categories of people who are eligible to receive Zakat (charity), emphasizing that Zakat is not to be distributed randomly but is specifically designated for those in need or serving particular roles in the community. It underscores the divine wisdom and knowledge behind the distribution of Zakat, highlighting that Allah is aware of the most appropriate ways to allocate charity, ensuring it reaches those who are deserving and serves the greater good of the community.

translation: And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say, "He is an ear." Say, "[It is] an ear of good for you; he believes in Allah and believes the believers and is a mercy for those who believe among you." And those who harm the Messenger of Allah - for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the duplicitous behavior of certain hypocrites who, despite their outward claims of faith, cause harm and distress to the Prophet Muhammad. The phrase 'they say, "He is an ear"' suggests that they accuse the Prophet of being overly credulous or gullible, implying that he listens to and believes everyone. The response 'Say, "An ear of good for you"' is a rebuttal, indicating that the Prophet's receptivity is actually a benefit, as he believes in God and is a source of mercy for the believers. The verse serves as a warning to those who harm the Prophet, stating that they will face a painful punishment, underscoring the gravity of their actions and the importance of treating the Prophet with respect and dignity. In a broader sense, this verse can be seen as emphasizing the importance of respecting and being mindful of the feelings of religious leaders and figures who are considered sources of guidance and mercy within their communities.

translation: They swear to you by Allah to please you, but Allah and His Messenger are more worthy of being pleased if they are believers.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the hypocrisy of certain individuals who swear oaths to please others, but in reality, they should be seeking to please Allah and His Messenger, as that is the true measure of their faith. It suggests that their actions are driven by a desire to appease others rather than a genuine commitment to their faith, and that true believers should prioritize pleasing Allah and His Messenger above all else.

translation: Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, for him is the fire of Hell, wherein he will abide eternally? That is the great disgrace.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who oppose or show enmity towards Allah and His Messenger, indicating that such individuals will face severe punishment in the form of eternal damnation in the fire of Hell. The verse underscores the gravity of opposing the divine authority and the messenger who conveys God's message, emphasizing that such opposition leads to the most humiliating and severe form of retribution, described as 'the great disgrace'. It highlights the importance of submission to God's will as communicated through His Messenger, and cautions against any form of resistance or hostility towards the divine commandments and the prophetic guidance.

translation: The hypocrites fear that a surah will be revealed about them, showing them what is in their hearts. Say, "Mock! Indeed, Allah will bring out what you fear."
interpretation: This verse highlights the duplicitous nature of the hypocrites, who outwardly professed faith but inwardly harbored doubt and disbelief. The verse suggests that the hypocrites were apprehensive about the revelation of a surah (chapter) that would expose their true inner beliefs. The response to their apprehension is a command to the Prophet to tell them to continue their mockery, for God will inevitably bring to light the very things they fear will be revealed about them, thus underscoring the inevitability of divine revelation exposing their hypocrisy.

translation: If you ask them, they will say, "We were only conversing and playing." Say, "Is it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?"
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the hypocrisy of those who mock the signs of Allah, His Messenger, and the faith. When confronted, they downplay their actions by claiming they were just jesting or engaging in idle talk. The verse is a rebuke, pointing out the gravity of their offense, as mocking Allah, His signs, and His Messenger is not a trivial matter but a serious form of disbelief and disrespect.

translation: Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon some of you, We will punish others amongst you because they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who have apostatized after having believed. It signifies that once a community or individuals within it have turned back from their faith after embracing it, excuses or justifications for such actions will not be accepted. The verse further indicates a divine principle of justice where, even if some are pardoned, others who have committed wrongdoing will face punishment due to their criminal actions. It underscores the concept that faith is not just a matter of initial belief but also of perseverance and consistency in that belief. Apostasy is viewed seriously, and the response to it is not uniform but is based on the justice and accountability of the individuals involved.

translation: The hypocrites, men and women, are from one another. They enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right and they close their hands. They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them [accordingly]. Indeed, the hypocrites - it is they who are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocritical behavior of those who claim to be believers but their actions contradict their claims. They promote evil and discourage good, and are stingy, indicating a lack of generosity and willingness to spend in the cause of righteousness. The verse suggests that their forgetfulness of God's commands and their failure to prioritize their faith leads to God 'forgetting' them, implying a reciprocal relationship between human remembrance of God and God's remembrance of humanity. Ultimately, it categorizes hypocrites as being among the disobedient and rebellious against God's will.

translation: Allah has promised the hypocrites, men and women, and the infidels, the fire of Hell, to abide therein; it is enough for them; and Allah has cursed them, and for them is a lasting torment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who harbor duplicity in their faith and those who outright reject it, indicating that their ultimate destination is a perpetual abode in the fire of Hell, which suffices as their recompense for their deeds. The verse underscores the severity of God's displeasure towards them, as they are not only condemned to suffer in Hell but are also subject to God's curse and a lasting punishment, emphasizing the gravity of their spiritual condition and the consequences of their actions in the hereafter.

translation: Like those before you, they were mightier than you in power, and more abundant in wealth and children. They enjoyed their portion, and you have enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion, and you have engaged [in vanities] like that in which they were engaged. Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and in the Hereafter, and it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the believers against following the footsteps of previous nations who were more powerful, wealthier, and more numerous, but ultimately lost their way. It cautions that merely enjoying worldly pleasures and engaging in frivolous discussions, just like those nations did, leads to the nullification of one's deeds in both this life and the hereafter, resulting in ultimate loss. The verse emphasizes that true success lies not in material wealth or fleeting pleasures, but in righteous actions that are pleasing to Allah.

translation: Has there not come to them the news of those before them, the people of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud, the people of Abraham, the companions of Midian and the overturned cities? Their messengers came to them with clear signs, and it was not God who wronged them, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the disbelievers of Mecca and others who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It reminds them of the fate of previous nations who were destroyed because of their disbelief and wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes that God is just and does not destroy people without warning them through His messengers and providing them with clear signs. The destruction that befell these nations was a result of their own actions, as they wronged themselves by rejecting the truth and persisting in their evil ways. The verse underscores the principle that God's judgment is based on justice, and people's suffering is a consequence of their own wrongdoing, not an arbitrary act by God.

translation: And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those - Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unity and solidarity among the believers, both men and women, who support and care for one another. It emphasizes their collective responsibility to promote virtue and prevent vice, maintain the pillars of their faith such as prayer and charity, and obey the commands of Allah and His Messenger. The verse concludes by promising that such a community will be blessed with Allah's mercy, underscoring the themes of divine sovereignty and wisdom in guiding the faithful.

translation: Allah has promised the believers, men and women, Gardens under which rivers flow, to dwell therein, and beautiful mansions in Gardens of 'Adn (Eden Paradise). But the greatest bliss is the Good Pleasure of Allah. That is the supreme success.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate goal of a believer's life, which is not just to attain paradise, but to gain the pleasure of Allah. The ' رضوان من الله أكبر' (Allah's pleasure is the greatest) signifies that the greatest reward is not the gardens, rivers, or beautiful dwellings, but the pleasure and approval of Allah Himself. It emphasizes the importance of living a life that is pleasing to Allah, as that is the greatest success.

translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be firm against them. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of taking a firm stance against those who reject faith (kuffar) and those who hypocritically claim to be believers (munafiqun). The instruction to 'jihad' against both groups signifies a comprehensive struggle against their rejection and hypocrisy, using all appropriate means available. The phrase 'waghlooz 'alayhim' (be harsh towards them) suggests that in dealing with such individuals, a firm and uncompromising attitude is necessary. The ultimate consequence for those who persist in their disbelief and hypocrisy is stated to be Jahannam (Hell), which is described as 'bi'sa al-masir' (a very bad destination), underscoring the severe and eternal nature of their punishment. This verse serves as a warning and a directive to the Prophet and the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to confront opposition with resolve, highlighting the stark contrast between the paths of righteousness and disobedience.

translation: They swear by Allah that they said nothing (bad), but certainly they spoke the word of disbelief, and disbelieved after their Islam, and they had purposed that which they were not able to attain; and they did not find fault except that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty. So if they repent, it will be better for them; and if they turn away, Allah will torment them with a painful torment in the world and the Hereafter; and they will not have on the earth any guardian or helper.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a group of hypocrites who, despite their outward claims of faith, harbored deep-seated resentment towards the Prophet and the Muslim community. Their discontent stemmed not from any moral or ethical grievance, but from the fact that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them through the spoils of war, which they perceived as a blessing. The verse suggests that their true issue was with the prosperity they had gained, implying that their faith was not genuine and was instead tainted by worldly desires. It warns that if they do not repent, they will face a painful punishment in both this life and the next, and will be left without any protector or helper on earth.

translation: And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah, [saying], "If He should give us from His bounty, we will surely give charity and will be among the righteous."
interpretation: This verse highlights the conditional nature of some people's faith, where they promise to be truthful and righteous only if they are blessed with wealth by Allah, indicating a test of their sincerity and commitment to their faith.

translation: But when He gave them of His bounty, they became niggardly with it and turned away, while they were averse.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ingratitude and arrogance that can arise when people are bestowed with blessings and wealth. It suggests that when individuals receive favors from Allah, they often become miserly with what they have been given and turn away, becoming indifferent and ungrateful. The verse serves as a warning against the corrupting influence of wealth and the importance of remaining humble and grateful for the blessings one receives.

translation: So He penalized them with hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they will meet Him, because they broke their promise to God and because they used to lie.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the consequence of breaking promises and lying to God is the development of hypocrisy in one's heart, which persists until the day of judgment. It implies that dishonesty and unfaithfulness to one's commitments can lead to a deep-seated spiritual corruption, manifesting as hypocrisy, that accompanies an individual until they face God on the day of reckoning.

translation: Do they not know that God knows their secrets and their private conversations and that God is the Knower of the unseen?
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who think they can conceal their true intentions and secret conversations from God. It emphasizes God's all-encompassing knowledge, not just of their outward actions, but also of their innermost thoughts and private discussions. The verse underscores the futility of attempting to hide one's true nature or intentions from God, as He is fully aware of all that is hidden and unseen. It is a call to mindfulness and sincerity, reminding individuals that their secretive behaviors and conversations are not beyond God's awareness, and thus, they should act with integrity and righteousness.

translation: Those who taunt those of the believers who give in charity freely, and those who give to the extent of their earnings, and ridicule them - God will throw back their ridicule on them, and they shall have a grievous chastisement.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and negative behavior of certain individuals towards the believers who are generous with their charity. It warns that those who mock or belittle others for their charitable efforts, whether they are able to give a lot or are limited to giving what little they have, will face divine retribution. The verse suggests that the act of mocking others' charity is not only a social transgression but also a spiritual one, inviting a similar response from God. It emphasizes the importance of sincerity and respect in charitable giving and warns against the consequences of deriding others' efforts to contribute to the welfare of the community.

translation: Whether you (O Muhammad) ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them. That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of intercession on behalf of those who have willfully rejected faith and disobeyed God and His Messenger. The number 'seventy times' is not meant to be taken literally but signifies a multitude of attempts or a generous and repeated effort to seek forgiveness for them. It underscores that the act of seeking forgiveness is not a mechanical or quantitative process that can override the qualitative condition of one's heart and faith. The verse emphasizes that God's guidance is not extended to those who are rebellious or disobedient, implying that their state of being 'Fasiqun' (those who have gone out of obedience to God's commands) is a result of their own choices and actions. It suggests that divine guidance is contingent upon an individual's willingness to comply with God's will and that persistent disobedience or rejection of faith leads to a state where divine mercy and forgiveness are withheld.

translation: Those who stayed behind were glad on account of their staying behind, contrary to the Messenger of Allah, and they disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah, and they said: 'Do not march forth in the heat.' Say: 'The fire of Hell is fiercer in heat.' If only they could understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the eagerness of the sincere believers to participate in jihad alongside the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the reluctance of the hypocrites who preferred to stay behind. The verse criticizes the hypocrites for their excuse of not joining the fight, suggesting that they were more concerned with avoiding the hardships of war than with the actual cause. The reference to 'the fire of Hell is hotter' serves as a stern warning, implying that the hardships of jihad in the path of God are far less severe than the eternal punishment that awaits those who shun their duty. It underscores the notion that true understanding and faith would lead one to prioritize the cause of God over personal comfort, and that the avoidance of jihad stems from a lack of true comprehension of the consequences of one's actions in the hereafter.

translation: So let them laugh a little and let them weep much - a recompense for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the rejoicing of those who have led a life of sin and disobedience will be short-lived and will ultimately be replaced by prolonged sorrow and regret, as a consequence of their past deeds. It implies that their worldly pleasures and temporary gains will not bring them lasting happiness, but rather, they will be requited with sorrow in the hereafter for their misdeeds.

translation: If God brings you back to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out [to fight], say, 'You will never go out with me, nor will you fight an enemy with me. You were content to sit [at home] the first time, so sit [this time] with those who remain behind.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of hypocrisy and lack of commitment to the cause of faith. It specifically addresses those who initially chose not to participate in a battle or a significant religious endeavor, opting instead to stay behind. When given a second chance to join, they are met with a stern refusal, underscoring the principle that those who show reluctance or lack of resolve in times of challenge or hardship are not to be entrusted with future responsibilities or privileges. The verse serves as a warning against the inconsistency and lack of dedication that can undermine the unity and strength of the community.

translation: And never pray (funeral prayer) for any of them who dies, nor stand by his grave. Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died while they were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against showing any form of reverence or respect to those who have died among the hypocrites or disbelievers. It signifies that their rejection of faith and their defiance against God's commandments render them unworthy of any posthumous honor or prayer. The act of performing funeral prayers (صَلاة الجنازة) was a significant social and communal acknowledgment of a person's standing within the community. By forbidding it for certain individuals, the verse underscores their spiritual and moral estrangement from the believing community. Furthermore, it highlights the importance of maintaining the integrity and purity of the community's religious practices by dissociating themselves from those who have willfully rejected the faith. The verse serves as a clear demarcation between the believers and the disbelievers, emphasizing that the latter's actions and ultimate fate are a result of their own choices and deeds.

translation: And let not their wealth and their children astonish you. Allah only wants to punish them with them in this life, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the abundance of wealth and children among the disbelievers should not be a cause for astonishment or admiration. Rather, it serves as a means for Allah to test and afflict them in this worldly life, ultimately leading to their spiritual downfall and demise while they remain in a state of disbelief. It underscores the idea that worldly prosperity is not necessarily a sign of divine favor, but can instead be a form of trial or punishment for those who reject faith.

translation: And when a Surah is revealed enjoining them to believe in Allah and to strive hard along with His Messenger, the wealthy among them ask permission to be exempted, and say, "Leave us to be with those who are to stay behind."
interpretation: This verse highlights the reluctance of those with means and influence to participate in jihad alongside the Prophet, instead opting to stay behind with those who are excused from fighting, indicating a lack of commitment to the cause and a preference for comfort over sacrifice.

translation: They were content to be with those who stayed behind, and their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who are content with being left behind and not participating in the struggle or effort alongside others, likely in the context of jihad or other communal obligations. The phrase 'طبع على قلوبهم' (sealed on their hearts) suggests that their complacency or lack of motivation has led to a spiritual or moral hardening, rendering them incapable of understanding or appreciating the significance of their actions or the importance of their participation. It implies a state of spiritual stagnation or decay resulting from their choice to remain behind.

translation: But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their lives. And it is they who will have the good things, and it is they who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those who are hesitant or refuse to strive in the cause of God and those who are committed to doing so. It emphasizes that true success and prosperity belong to the believers who are willing to sacrifice their wealth and themselves for the sake of their faith. The verse suggests that the ultimate rewards and blessings are reserved for those who demonstrate such commitment and perseverance, indicating that their efforts will not be in vain and that they will achieve a state of true flourishing.

translation: Allah has prepared for them Gardens under which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally. That is the supreme success.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate and eternal triumph for those who have faith and do righteous deeds. The 'Gardens under which rivers flow' symbolize a state of paradise where believers will experience unending bliss and peace. The promise of 'remaining therein forever' underscores the permanence of this reward, contrasting with the transient nature of worldly life and its pleasures. 'That is the supreme success' highlights the unparalleled value of this achievement, indicating that it surpasses all other forms of success or happiness one might attain in life. It serves as a powerful motivator for believers to adhere to their faith and perform good deeds, with the assurance of a magnificent and everlasting recompense.

translation: And those who had excuses among the bedouins came to be permitted [to remain], and those who had lied to Allah and His Messenger sat [at home]. There will befall those who disbelieved among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who are genuinely hindered by circumstances beyond their control and those who fabricate excuses to avoid fulfilling their obligations. It underscores the notion that true faith is not merely a matter of verbal affirmation but is demonstrated through actions and commitment, particularly in times of challenge or hardship. The verse serves as a warning that those who deceive themselves and others by feigning faith while lacking true commitment will face severe consequences.

translation: There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who do not find that which they shall expend [i.e., wealth], if they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. There is not [any cause for] blame upon the doers of good. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that individuals who are genuinely unable to participate in certain religious obligations, such as jihad, due to physical weakness, illness, or financial incapacity, are not held accountable or considered sinful, provided they are sincere and advise for the sake of Allah and His Messenger. It underscores the principle that those who do good and are sincere in their intentions are not to be blamed or punished. The verse reassures that Allah is forgiving and merciful, highlighting His leniency and understanding towards the believers who are constrained by circumstances beyond their control.

translation: Nor [is there blame] upon those who, when they came to you that you might provide them with mounts, you said, "I can find nothing for you to ride upon." They turned back while their eyes overflowed with tears out of grief that they did not find something to spend [for jihad].
interpretation: This verse highlights the compassion and understanding that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the early Muslim community were expected to show towards those who were unable to participate in jihad or other communal activities due to their lack of resources. It emphasizes the emotional toll on those who were left behind, not out of lack of willingness but due to their inability to afford the means to join in, such as mounts for travel. The verse underscores the importance of empathy and acknowledges the sorrow of those who were constrained by poverty, indicating that their emotional pain was recognized and validated within the community.

translation: The blame is only upon those who ask permission of you [Prophet] while they are rich. They are satisfied to be with those who are left behind, and God has sealed their hearts, so they do not know [the consequences of their choice].
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who are wealthy and yet excuse themselves from participating in jihad or other communal obligations alongside the Prophet, opting instead to stay behind with those who are exempt (such as women). It suggests that their decision is a sign of their lack of commitment to the cause and their prioritization of comfort and ease. The verse implies that their hearts have been sealed by God due to their hypocrisy and lack of true faith, resulting in their inability to understand the true nature of their actions and the consequences of their choices.

translation: They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say, 'Make no excuse; never will we believe you; God has already informed us of your news. And God will see your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger; then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the hypocrisy of those who claim to be believers but are not sincere in their faith. It suggests that even if they try to apologize or make excuses when confronted with their actions, their efforts will be in vain because God is already aware of their true intentions and deeds. The verse emphasizes that one's actions will be judged not just by their outward appearances but by the knowledge of God who knows both the seen and the unseen. Ultimately, it is to God that everyone will return, and He will reveal the truth about their deeds.

translation: They will swear to you by Allah, when you return to them, that you may turn away from them. So turn away from them. Indeed, they are an abomination, and their refuge is Hell - a recompense for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the hypocrisy of certain individuals who, upon being confronted or when the believers return to them, will swear oaths by Allah in an attempt to deflect attention or avoid accountability. The verse advises the believers to turn away from these individuals, deeming them impure (رجس) both spiritually and morally, and warns that their ultimate destination is Hell, serving as a recompense for their deeds.

translation: They swear to you that you may be pleased with them, but if you are pleased with them, surely Allah is not pleased with the rebellious people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of seeking the approval of hypocrites, as their oaths and attempts to appease the believers are ultimately futile if they remain disobedient to God. It underscores that divine displeasure is not mitigated by human approval, emphasizing the primacy of God's judgment over human sentiments.

translation: The desert Arabs are more stubborn in disbelief and hypocrisy, and more likely not to know the limits of what [laws] Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between the Bedouin Arabs (الأعراب) and the urban Muslims in terms of their faith and understanding of Islam. The Bedouins are described as being more prone to disbelief (كفر) and hypocrisy (نفاق), and less likely to understand the limits or boundaries (حدود) of what God has revealed to His Messenger. The verse suggests that the Bedouins' nomadic lifestyle and lack of exposure to the Prophet's teachings and the Muslim community in Medina contributed to their spiritual shortcomings. In contrast, the verse affirms God's omniscience and wisdom (عليم حكيم), implying that God's judgment and laws are based on His all-encompassing knowledge and wise purposes.

translation: And of the desert Arabs there is he who considers what he expends (in Allah's Cause) as a loss, and keeps waiting for misfortunes for you; upon them is the misfortune of evil. And Allah is Hearing, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the hypocrisy of some Bedouins who give charity begrudgingly, viewing it as a loss or a burden, and are waiting for adverse circumstances to befall the Muslims, hoping that their fortunes will change. However, the verse warns that it is they who will be afflicted by misfortune. The verse underscores God's awareness of their intentions and actions, emphasizing His omniscience and ability to hear and know all.

translation: And of the Bedouins are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and consider what they spend [for the cause of Allah] as a means of nearness to Allah and [a means] for the invocations of the Messenger. Unquestionably, it is a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them to His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the nuanced relationship between faith, charity, and the Prophet's role. It indicates that certain Bedouins not only believe in God and the Day of Judgment but also view their charitable acts as a means to draw closer to God and to earn the Prophet's prayers. The verse assures them that these acts are indeed a form of drawing closer to God, and it promises that God will include them in His mercy, underscoring God's forgiving and merciful nature.

translation: And the first forerunners [in the faith] among the Muhajireen and the Ansar and those who followed them with good conduct - Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for those who were among the first to migrate (Muhajirun) and support (Ansar) the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and for those who followed them with sincerity and goodness. It signifies that Allah is pleased with their actions and they are pleased with His reward. The ultimate reward for their faith and deeds is Gardens of Eternity where rivers flow, a state of eternal bliss described as the greatest success.

translation: And among the Bedouins around you there are hypocrites, and among the people of Medina [too]. They are persistent in hypocrisy. You do not know them [O Prophet]; We know them. We will punish them twice, then they will be returned to a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy that existed among the Bedouin tribes surrounding Medina and even within the city itself. It emphasizes that some individuals had become so entrenched in their hypocrisy that they were not recognizable as such by the Prophet or the general community. The verse serves as a warning that these hypocrites would face a double punishment for their duplicity - first, for their initial wrongdoing, and second, for their persistence in hypocrisy despite being aware of its gravity. Ultimately, they would be subjected to a severe and final punishment, underscoring the gravity of their actions and the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: And others have acknowledged their sins, they have mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. It is possible that Allah will relent towards them; surely Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the complexity of human nature and the mercy of God. It suggests that individuals who have mixed their good deeds with bad ones, but are aware of their mistakes and are willing to acknowledge them, may still be eligible for God's forgiveness and mercy. The verse implies that sincere recognition of one's wrongdoing and a willingness to make amends can be a crucial step towards redemption, and that God's forgiveness is not limited to those who are entirely sinless, but is also available to those who have erred but are willing to change their ways.

translation: Take, [O, Muhammad], from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to increase, and invoke [Allah's blessings] upon them. Indeed, your invocations are reassurance for them. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the multifaceted role of charity (sadaqah) in Islam, not only as a means of purifying the giver's wealth and soul but also as a source of comfort and solace. The act of giving charity is accompanied by the Prophet's prayer (or supplication) for the givers, which serves to reassure and calm them, underscoring the spiritual and psychological benefits of charitable acts. It emphasizes the importance of the relationship between the individual and the divine, with Allah being all-hearing and all-knowing, thus encouraging believers to engage in such righteous deeds with the understanding that they are seen and appreciated by God.

translation: Do they not know that it is God who accepts repentance from His servants and receives the charities, and that it is God who is the Accepter of Repentance, the Merciful?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to people that God is always ready to accept their repentance and is merciful towards them, encouraging them to turn to Him in sincere repentance and to give in charity, as these actions are pleasing to Him. It emphasizes God's attribute of being 'the accepter of repentance' and 'the merciful', highlighting His willingness to forgive His servants upon their return to Him.

translation: And say, "Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger and the believers. And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, then He will inform you of what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that one's actions are not only observed by God but also by the Prophet and the community of believers. It serves as a reminder that individuals will be held accountable for their deeds in the Hereafter, where they will be informed about the consequences of their actions. The verse encourages people to be mindful of their actions, as they will be judged based on their deeds. It highlights the importance of living a righteous life, as one's actions will be scrutinized and rewarded or punished accordingly.

translation: And [there are] others deferred for the command of Allah, whether He will punish them or whether He will forgive them. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and omniscience of Allah, indicating that there are individuals whose fate is deferred to Allah's decree, where they might either face punishment for their wrongdoings or receive Allah's mercy through repentance, underscoring the wisdom and knowledge that guides Allah's decisions.

translation: And [there are] those [who] have built a mosque to cause harm and [to promote] disbelief and division among the believers and as an outpost for those who have already waged war against Allah and His Messenger. And they will surely swear, "We intended only the best," And Allah testifies that they are indeed liars.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a group of hypocrites who built a mosque with ulterior motives. The interpretation is that their actions were driven by a desire to cause harm, promote disbelief, and create division among the believers. They were also trying to provide a safe haven for those who had already opposed God and His Messenger. The verse highlights the duplicity of these individuals, who claimed to have good intentions but were actually lying, as God bears witness to their falsehood.

translation: Do not stand [for prayer] in it - ever. A mosque founded on righteousness from the first day is more worthy for you to stand in it. In it are men who love to purify themselves; and Allah loves those who purify themselves.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of purity, both physical and spiritual, in the eyes of Allah. The verse highlights that there are individuals who are committed to purification, and Allah loves those who are purified, indicating that the state of being purified is not just a physical condition but also a spiritual one that is pleasing to Allah.

translation: Is one who lays his foundation on piety to Allah and His good pleasure better, or one who lays his foundation on the brink of a crumbling precipice, so that it collapses with him into the fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the contrast between two types of foundations upon which one's actions or deeds are built. The first is built upon 'Taqwa' (piety or fear of God) and 'Ridhwan' (God's pleasure), indicating a strong and righteous foundation. The second is built on the edge of a crumbling precipice ('Shafa Jurf Hār'), symbolizing a weak and unstable foundation that is prone to collapse. The verse suggests that the deeds or actions of those who are guided by righteousness and seek God's pleasure are stable and will lead to a good outcome, whereas those who are unjust and lack a righteous foundation will ultimately face a dire consequence, symbolized by being swept into the fire of Hell. The verse concludes by stating that God does not guide the unjust people, implying that their lack of guidance is a result of their own actions and choices.

translation: The structure which they have built will continue to be a cause of doubt in their hearts until their hearts are cut to pieces. And Allah is All-Knowing, Wise.
interpretation: The verse suggests that the actions or endeavors of those being referred to will continue to sow doubt and uncertainty in their hearts until their hearts are severed or torn asunder, implying a profound and potentially destructive impact on their inner selves. It highlights God's all-knowing and wise nature, suggesting that He is fully aware of the consequences of their actions and has a wise purpose behind allowing such outcomes.

translation: Indeed, Allah has purchased of the believers their lives and their properties [in exchange] for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah , so they kill and are killed. [It is] a true promise [binding] upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than Allah ? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And it is that which is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense value that Allah places on the sacrifices made by believers in His cause. It signifies that the ultimate reward for those who give their lives and wealth in the path of Allah is Paradise. The verse emphasizes the fulfillment of Allah's promise across different scriptures, reinforcing the notion that the bargain between Allah and the believers is not only sacred but also supremely rewarding. It encourages believers to rejoice in their commitment, as it represents the ultimate triumph.

translation: The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers [of Allah ], the travelers [for His cause], those who bow and prostrate [in prayer], those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and those who observe the limits [set by] Allah . And give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of the believers who are promised good news. It signifies that true believers are not just those who perform rituals like prayer (indicated by 'الراكعون الساجدون') but are also characterized by their active engagement in societal and moral reform ('الآمرون بالمعروف والناهون عن المنكر'). The verse underscores the importance of maintaining the limits set by God ('الحافظون لحدود الله') and living a life of repentance ('التائبون'), devotion ('العابدون'), gratitude ('الحامدون'), and striving or traveling in the path of righteousness ('السائحون'). The overall message is that faith is not just about individual acts of worship but also involves a commitment to moral and social responsibility, and those who embody these qualities are to be given glad tidings.

translation: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Hellfire
interpretation: This verse highlights the clear distinction between believers and disbelievers, emphasizing that once it becomes evident that certain individuals are destined for Hell due to their disbelief and polytheism, it is not permissible for the Prophet or the believers to pray for their forgiveness, even if they are relatives. It underscores the principle that faith and righteousness are the criteria for worthiness of divine mercy and forgiveness, rather than familial ties or personal relationships.

translation: And Ibrahim's praying for his father's forgiveness was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he dissociated himself from him. Indeed, Ibrahim was most tender-hearted, forbearing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the nuanced nature of Prophet Ibrahim's relationship with his father, who was an idolater and an enemy of God. Initially, Ibrahim's prayer for his father's forgiveness was based on a promise he had made to him. However, once it became clear that his father was an unrepentant enemy of God, Ibrahim dissociated himself from him. The verse showcases Ibrahim's character as being both 'awwah' (one who is prone to praying to God and is full of compassion) and 'halim' (one who is forbearing and gentle), demonstrating the complexity of his personality and his commitment to his faith.

translation: And Allah would not let a people stray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's justice and wisdom in guiding humanity. It suggests that once God has guided a people to the right path, He will not lead them astray until He has clearly communicated to them the things they should beware of or avoid, implying a principle of moral accountability that is predicated on clear knowledge and understanding. It underscores the idea that divine guidance is accompanied by clear warnings and that God's actions are always informed by omniscience.

translation: Indeed, to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death. And you do not have, besides Allah, any protector or any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of God over the universe, highlighting His power to give life and cause death. It serves as a reminder to believers of their dependence on God and the futility of seeking protection or support from other sources, underscoring the monotheistic principle that God is the sole guardian and helper.

translation: Allah has already forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajireen and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a party of them had almost swerved aside. Then He forgave them. Indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of the Prophet Muhammad's leadership and the unity of the early Muslim community during times of hardship. The phrase 'ساعة العسرة' (hour of hardship) refers to a particularly challenging period, likely during the Battle of Tabuk or another difficult time. The verse emphasizes that despite some initial wavering or doubt among a faction of the believers, Allah ultimately accepted their repentance, demonstrating His mercy and compassion towards those who followed the Prophet and struggled with their faith during adversity.

translation: And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind [and whose hearts were constricted] until, when the earth became straitened for them despite its vastness and their souls constricted them and they had thought that there is no refuge from God except in Him, then He turned to them that they might repent. Indeed, it is God who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse refers to the three individuals who were left behind during the Prophet Muhammad's campaign to Tabuk. The phrase 'until the earth, vast as it was, was straitened for them' is a metaphor indicating that they felt a deep sense of isolation and confinement, not just physically but also emotionally and spiritually. Their remorse and guilt were so overwhelming that they felt suffocated by their own selves, leading to a state where they believed that the only refuge from God's displeasure was to turn back to Him in repentance. The verse highlights God's merciful nature, as He accepted their repentance. It underscores the theme that true repentance is not just about regret but about turning back to God with the intention of changing one's ways, and that God's mercy is available to those who sincerely repent.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with those who are true (in word and deed).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of living a truthful life. It instructs believers to not only fear God and be mindful of their actions, but also to be among those who are truthful in their words and deeds. Being with the truthful implies adopting their qualities and characteristics, such as honesty, integrity, and sincerity. It suggests that the company one keeps, whether in a literal or figurative sense, has a significant impact on one's own moral character. Thus, the verse encourages believers to surround themselves with truthful individuals and to embody truthfulness in their own lives, fostering a community built on trust, authenticity, and righteousness.

translation: It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the bedouins that they should remain behind the Messenger of God and prefer their own lives to his life. That is because they will not be afflicted with thirst or fatigue or hunger in the cause of God, nor will they tread on ground that enrages the disbelievers, nor will they gain any advantage over an enemy, but a righteous deed will be written to their account. God does not waste the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual value of striving alongside the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the difficulties that come with it. It suggests that the act of accompanying the Prophet and facing hardships in the path of God is not just a physical endeavor but a spiritual one that earns one great reward. The verse implies that the companions of the Prophet, by enduring thirst, fatigue, and hunger for the sake of God, and by taking actions that enrage the disbelievers, are not just performing physical acts but are also cultivating a deep-seated desire to please God over their own selves. This selflessness and dedication are seen as acts of righteousness that are duly recorded and rewarded by God. The underlying message is that true devotion involves a willingness to put God's cause above personal comfort and safety, and that such devotion is not wasted but is acknowledged and rewarded by God.

translation: And they do not spend an expenditure, small or large, nor do they cross a valley, but it is recorded for them that Allah may reward them for the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the meticulous recording of every deed, no matter how insignificant it may seem, by Allah. It underscores the principle that every action, whether it is an expenditure, big or small, or traversing a valley (potentially indicating travel or effort for a cause), is accounted for. The underlying message is one of encouragement and assurance that Allah not only keeps a record of these deeds but will also reward them in the best manner, emphasizing the idea of divine justice and generosity. It suggests that the reward is not just commensurate with the deed but is given in the most excellent way, reflecting Allah's grace and bounty.

translation: And it is not for the believers to set forth in full strength [for battle]. Why should not a party from every section of them [i.e., the believers] go forth that they may gain understanding in the religion and that they may warn their people when they return to them, so that they may be cautious?
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of a knowledgeable group within the community who can educate and warn others about their religious obligations and the consequences of not adhering to them, thereby acting as a catalyst for others to be cautious and mindful of their actions.

translation: O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers and let them find firmness in you. And know that Allah is with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being firm and resolute when dealing with disbelievers who are in close proximity, as a means of deterring them and maintaining the integrity of the Muslim community. It also reassures the believers that God's support is with those who are mindful of Him and maintain righteousness, indicating that their strength lies not just in their own resolve but also in divine backing.

translation: And whenever a surah is revealed, there are some [hypocrites] among them who say, "Which of you has this [revelation] increased in faith?" As for those who have believed, it has increased them in faith, while they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the differing effects of the revelation of the Qur'an on people. For believers, the revelation of a new surah (chapter) increases their faith and brings them joy, as it provides further guidance and reassurance. The verse suggests that the Qur'an has a profound impact on the hearts of those who are already believers, strengthening their conviction and filling them with a sense of delight and optimism.

translation: And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it [i.e., the revelation] has increased them in evil [in addition] to their evil, and they have died while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the consequence of hypocrisy and the spiritual decay it leads to. The phrase 'في قلوبهم مرض' (in whose hearts is a disease) refers to those whose faith is tainted with hypocrisy or doubt. The 'disease' is a metaphor for the spiritual malady that afflicts them. The verse suggests that as they continue on their path of hypocrisy, they become increasingly hardened in their disbelief ('زادتهم رجسا إلى رجسهم'), accumulating more 'filth' or spiritual impurity. Ultimately, they die in a state of disbelief ('وماتوا وهم كافرون'), indicating that their spiritual condition worsens over time until they meet their end without having purified their faith. This verse serves as a warning about the dangers of hypocrisy and the importance of sincerity in one's faith.

translation: Do they not see that they are tried once or twice every year? Still they do not turn in repentance, nor do they take heed.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the stubbornness and lack of reflection among a group of people who are repeatedly faced with trials or hardships, yet they fail to take heed or repent. The phrase 'in every year once or twice' suggests that these trials are recurring, serving as a reminder or a call to reflection. However, despite these repeated opportunities for introspection and change, the individuals in question do not turn back to a righteous path or even remember to reflect on their actions and circumstances. It underscores a critique of their hardened state, where despite experiencing hardships meant to guide them, they remain unrepentant and unreflective.

translation: And whenever a surah is revealed, they look at one another [saying], "Does anyone see you?" Then they turn away. Allah has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of certain individuals who, upon the revelation of a new surah (chapter) of the Qur'an, would glance at each other, seemingly checking if anyone was watching them, before dispersing. The phrase 'صرف الله قلوبهم' (Allah turned their hearts away) indicates that their actions and behavior are a result of their spiritual deviation, stemming from their lack of understanding ('قوم لا يفقهون' - a people who do not comprehend). It suggests that their inability to grasp the true essence and message of the Qur'an leads to their hearts being diverted from the right path, resulting in their hypocritical behavior.

translation: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; [he is] concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's deep concern and compassion for his people, emphasizing his commitment to guiding them towards righteousness and his empathy for their struggles, showcasing the qualities of mercy and kindness that are characteristic of his prophetic mission.

translation: If they turn away, say, 'Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. On Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne.'
interpretation: This verse is a declaration of the Prophet's reliance on Allah in the face of adversity or opposition. When faced with those who turn away, the Prophet is instructed to affirm his trust in Allah, acknowledging that He is the sole deity worthy of worship and the Lord of the magnificent Throne, thereby conveying a message of reassurance and resolve in the face of challenges.

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the wise Book.
interpretation: This verse signifies the beginning of a profound and wise scripture, affirming the Qur'an's status as a source of guidance and wisdom, setting the tone for the revelations that follow.

translation: Is it a wonder for mankind that We have sent Our inspiration to a man from among themselves,- that he should warn mankind (of their danger), and give the good news to those who believe that they have before their Lord the lofty rank of (blessed) ones. (But) the Unbelievers say: "This is indeed an enchanter, plain and obvious."
interpretation: This verse addresses a common reaction of people to the message of Islam, specifically the astonishment and disbelief that a human being could be chosen by God to receive revelation and convey a warning to others. The interpretation is that the verse highlights the tendency of people to doubt the authenticity of the prophetic message when it comes from someone they consider to be one of their own, rather than accepting it as a divine appointment. The response of the disbelievers, labeling the Prophet as a 'clear magician,' indicates their refusal to accept the message and their attempt to discredit the Prophet. The underlying theme is the challenge faced by prophets and messengers in convincing their people of the truth of their message, and the various ways in which people react to divine guidance.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne, arranging [each] matter. There is not an intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Then, will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority and sovereignty of God over all creation. It highlights that God's management of the universe is not hindered by any external factors, and that intercession before Him is only possible with His permission. The verse serves as a reminder to humanity of their obligation to worship God alone, given His supreme authority and control over all affairs.

translation: To Him is your return all together. The promise of Allah is true. Indeed, He begins the creation and then repeats it that He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds, in justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability of accountability for one's actions in the hereafter. It underscores the justice of God, who not only creates beings but also resurrects them to reward the righteous with fairness and punish the disbelievers with severe torment for their denial of faith. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith, highlighting the consequences of their actions and encouraging believers to maintain their faith and perform good deeds.

translation: It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a derived light and determined for it phases - that you may know the number of years and account [of time]. Allah has not created this except in truth. He details the signs for a people who know
interpretation: This verse highlights God's wisdom and purpose in creating the universe with order and precision. The fact that God has made the sun and moon with specific roles and has ordained the lunar cycle for human reckoning indicates that creation is not arbitrary or meaningless. Rather, it is a deliberate and thoughtful act, designed to convey significance and facilitate human understanding. The verse suggests that the natural world is imbued with signs or 'ayat' that are meant to be deciphered and appreciated by those who possess knowledge, implying that the acquisition of knowledge is a means of grasping the deeper significance of creation and the intentions of the Creator.

translation: Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day and [in] what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth are signs for a people who fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of observing and contemplating the natural world as a means to develop taqwa (God-consciousness). The alternation of night and day, along with the vast creations in the heavens and earth, serve as signs or 'ayat' that are particularly meaningful to those who are mindful of God. The verse suggests that the natural world is imbued with spiritual significance and that recognizing this can foster a deeper sense of reverence and awe for the Creator among those inclined towards righteousness.

translation: Indeed, those who do not expect the meeting with Us and have been content with the life of this world and have become secure in it, and those who are heedless of Our signs
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who are heedless of the Hereafter and are content with the worldly life, having become complacent and secure in their material possessions and worldly pursuits. It highlights their negligence and lack of awareness regarding the signs and messages of Allah, indicating a spiritual blindness that stems from their preoccupation with worldly gains and pleasures.

translation: Those will have their abode in the Fire because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who have committed evil deeds will ultimately face the consequence of their actions in the afterlife, with Hell being their final abode, serving as a form of divine retribution for their wrongdoings.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - their Lord will guide them because of their faith. Beneath them rivers will flow in the Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse highlights the causal relationship between faith, righteous deeds, and divine guidance. It suggests that those who have genuine faith and act upon it by doing good deeds will be guided by their Lord due to their faith. This guidance is not just about showing them the right path but also about enabling them to stay on it and reap its rewards, which is symbolized by the flowing rivers in the gardens of bliss, indicating a state of eternal bliss and happiness.
