translation: Send him with us tomorrow that he may enjoy himself and play, and indeed, we will be his guardians.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of trust in God's protection. The speaker is confident that even when the child (presumably Joseph) is sent away and seemingly left to his own devices, God will watch over him. It underscores the belief that God's guardianship is more encompassing and reliable than human efforts to safeguard one's loved ones.

translation: He said, 'It saddens me that you should take him away, and I fear that a wolf may devour him while you are heedless of him.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep emotional bond between Jacob and his son Joseph, as Jacob expresses his sorrow at the prospect of being separated from Joseph. It also underscores the theme of trust and vigilance, as Jacob's concern is not just about the physical safety of Joseph (fearing that a wolf might devour him) but also about the lack of attention or care from Joseph's brothers, indicating a lack of trust in them to protect Joseph.

translation: They said, "If a wolf should eat him while we are a [strong] group, we would then be losers."
interpretation: The verse highlights the brothers' lack of faith in their own abilities and their tendency to shift the blame to external factors, in this case, a wolf, when faced with the challenge of taking care of their brother Joseph. It showcases their weak conviction and their readiness to be considered losers or failures if they were unable to protect Joseph, indicating a mindset that is more focused on avoiding blame than on taking responsibility.

translation: So when they took him away and decided to put him into the bottom of the well, and We revealed to him, "You will certainly inform them of this deed of theirs while they are not aware [of it]."
interpretation: This verse signifies that even when it seems like the plans of others against an individual are succeeding, as in the case of Joseph being put into the well, divine intervention is at play, and the individual is being prepared for a future revelation or role that will expose the truth about the actions taken against them, unbeknownst to their perpetrators.

translation: And they came to their father at night, weeping.
interpretation: The verse highlights the emotional manipulation and deception employed by the brothers of Prophet Yusuf, as they arrive at their father's house at night, weeping falsely to feign grief and conceal their malicious actions against their brother.

translation: They said, "O our father, indeed we went racing each other and left Yusuf (Joseph) by our belongings, and a wolf ate him; but you will not believe us, even if we are truthful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological insight of the Qur'an into the dynamics of family relationships and deception. The brothers of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) are attempting to convince their father, Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob), of a fabricated story about Yusuf being eaten by a wolf. The verse showcases the brothers' lack of faith in their father's ability to believe them, even if they were telling the truth, indicating a deep-seated understanding of their father's intuition and skepticism. It reflects the tension and mistrust within the family due to the brothers' jealousy and past actions towards Yusuf.

translation: And they came with false blood on his shirt. He said, 'Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allah is the one sought for help against that which you describe'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of patience and reliance on Allah in the face of adversity and false accusations. The speaker, Prophet Yaqub (Jacob), is demonstrating his resolve to endure the fabricated story presented by his sons regarding the fate of his son Yusuf (Joseph), and instead of reacting impulsively, he chooses to exercise patience and seek assistance from Allah, acknowledging that Allah is the ultimate source of help against the false narratives and hardships they are facing.

translation: And a caravan came [upon them], so they sent their water-drawer, and he let down his bucket. He said, 'O good news! Here is a boy.' And they concealed him as merchandise; and God was knowing of what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine providence and the unfolding of destiny. The fact that a caravan happened to pass by and rescue Yusuf (Joseph) is not a mere coincidence, but rather part of a larger divine plan. The verse suggests that even seemingly random events are part of a larger web of causality that is guided by God's knowledge and wisdom. The actions of the people involved, including the brothers of Yusuf who had sought to get rid of him, are all known to God, implying that their intentions and consequences are subject to divine scrutiny and judgment.

translation: And they sold him for a paltry price, a few dirhams counted out, and they were, of him, among the indifferent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of the undervaluation of something or someone precious, using the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) as an example. The fact that Yusuf was sold for a 'paltry sum' signifies how those who were supposed to value him did not recognize his worth, illustrating a broader message about the disparity between perceived and true value, and how worldly valuation can be shortsighted and misguided.

translation: And he who bought him in Egypt said to his wife, "Make his stay comfortable; perhaps he will benefit us or we will adopt him as a son." And thus, We gave power to Joseph in the land, and that We might teach him the interpretation of statements. And Allah is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's providence and sovereignty in the life of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). It illustrates how God enables Yusuf to gain a secure position in Egypt, not just physically but also in terms of knowledge and understanding, by teaching him the interpretation of events or discerning the deeper meaning behind occurrences. The verse underscores the theme that despite human plans and actions, it is God's will that ultimately prevails. The narrative suggests that Yusuf's rise to prominence was part of a divine plan to prepare him for a significant role, possibly in interpreting dreams or guiding others, and that this was achieved through God's enabling, even if many people are unaware of or do not acknowledge God's overarching control over events.

translation: And when he reached his full strength, We gave him wisdom and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for those who excel in doing good deeds. When an individual reaches the pinnacle of their maturity and capabilities, they are endowed with wisdom and knowledge. This signifies that the ultimate reward for righteous actions is not merely material or worldly but is deeply rooted in the acquisition of wisdom and understanding, which are considered the highest forms of blessings. It underscores the principle that divine recompense is directly proportional to one's deeds, with the virtuous being granted the most sublime of gifts, namely, wisdom and knowledge.

translation: And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, "Come, you." He said, "[I seek] Allah's refuge. Indeed, he is my master [who] has made good my residence. Indeed, wrongdoers will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse highlights the test of Prophet Yusuf's (Joseph's) moral character when faced with temptation. It demonstrates his strong faith and commitment to righteousness by refusing the advances of the woman in whose house he was a guest, invoking the concept of 'رب' (rabb) which signifies not just a master but also a guardian or caretaker, emphasizing his recognition of her husband's (the Aziz's) authority and his gratitude for being well taken care of. His response, 'معاذ الله' (I seek refuge in God), underscores his reliance on divine protection against succumbing to wrongdoing, illustrating the principle that those who wrong themselves (الظالمون) will not succeed.

translation: And certainly she desired him, and he would have desired her, were it not that he saw the proof of his Lord. Thus it is, that We may turn away from him evil and indecency. Surely he is one of Our chosen servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine guidance in preventing individuals from succumbing to sinful desires. The example given is of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), who was tempted by a woman but was saved from committing the sin because he saw the proof/evidence (burhan) of his Lord, indicating the guidance and clarity he received from his faith. This demonstrates how sincere servants of God, like Yusuf, are protected from evil and immorality through their devotion and the guidance they receive from Allah. It underscores the idea that divine intervention and guidance play a crucial role in helping the righteous resist temptation and maintain their moral integrity.

translation: And they both rushed to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back, and they both found her lord near the door. She said, 'What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your family except that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of moral accountability and justice in the face of wrongdoing. It illustrates that when someone intends harm to another's family, they should be met with severe consequences, such as imprisonment or a painful punishment, underscoring the societal and moral imperative to protect family integrity and deter malicious intentions.

translation: She said: 'It was he that sought to seduce me.' And a witness from her household bore witness: 'If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is of the liars.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of evidence and proof in determining the truth. The shirt of Yusuf (Joseph) is used as a physical evidence to resolve the dispute between his master's wife and Yusuf. The tearing of the shirt from the front or back is used to determine who is telling the truth. This indicates that in Islamic jurisprudence, physical evidence can be used to corroborate or contradict witness testimony, and that the presence of tangible proof can be crucial in establishing the facts of a case.

translation: And if his shirt is torn from behind, she has lied and he is of the truthful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of evidence and proof in determining the truth. The tearing of the shirt from behind indicates that Yusuf was trying to escape from the woman, thus proving his innocence and her guilt. It signifies that actions and their consequences can serve as evidence of one's intentions and truthfulness.

translation: So when he [Ya'qub] saw that his shirt was torn from the back, he said, 'Indeed, it is from your scheme. Indeed, your scheme is great.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the societal context where women's cunning or 'plot' is viewed with a certain level of distrust or fear by men, indicating a gender dynamic prevalent at the time. It suggests that the societal perception of women's actions or intentions could be biased, portraying them as potentially deceitful or manipulative.

translation: Joseph, ignore this; and (you, woman), seek forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you have been of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse is instructing Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) to ignore the advances made towards him by the wife of Al-Aziz and for her to seek forgiveness for her sin, as she was among those who had committed wrongdoing. It highlights the moral integrity expected of Yusuf and the acknowledgment of wrongdoing by the one who attempted to seduce him.

translation: And women in the city said, "The wife of al-'Aziz is seeking to seduce her young man; he has impassioned her with love. Indeed, we see her [to be] in clear error."
interpretation: This verse highlights the societal gossip and scrutiny that can arise when individuals deviate from expected norms of behavior, as exemplified by the women of the city talking about the wife of the Aziz and her inappropriate behavior towards Prophet Yusuf. It indicates how societal judgment can be swift and severe, labeling actions as being in clear error, and it underscores the tension between personal desires and societal expectations.

translation: So when she heard of their stratagem, she sent to them and prepared for them a feast and gave each one of them a knife and said [to Yusuf], "Come out to them." And when they saw him, they greatly admired him and cut their hands and said, "Perfect is Allah! This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the extraordinary beauty of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), as when the women of the city saw him, they were so astonished and mesmerized by his handsomeness that they cut their hands with the knives they were holding, not even realizing what they were doing. The verse highlights the transcendent nature of Yusuf's beauty, which was so divine that it led the women to exclaim that he could not be a human being but a noble angel, emphasizing the spiritual and moral stature he embodied.

translation: She said, 'That is the one about whom you blamed me. And I certainly sought to tempt him, but he held fast to his continence. And if he does not do what I command him, he will certainly be imprisoned, and he will be one of the despised.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the power dynamics and the societal pressures that can lead individuals to make certain choices. The speaker, likely a woman, is responding to accusations or criticisms, and in doing so, reveals the complexities of her relationship with the person she is talking about, likely Prophet Yusuf. The verse shows how societal norms and expectations can drive people to take actions that might not align with their personal desires or moral standings, as indicated by the threat of imprisonment and humiliation if certain demands are not met. It underscores the tension between personal integrity and societal or external pressures.

translation: He said, "O my Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me. And if You do not avert from me their scheme, I might incline toward them and [thus] be of the ignorant."
interpretation: This verse highlights the internal conflict faced by Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) as he is tempted by the advances of the women, including the wife of the Aziz. He expresses his preference for imprisonment over succumbing to their desires, indicating his strong moral resolve. The verse also underscores his awareness of his own vulnerability to temptation and his recognition of the need for divine intervention to protect him from falling into sin. By invoking God's intervention, Yusuf demonstrates his faith and reliance on God to safeguard him against the schemes of the women, thereby avoiding being swayed by his desires and becoming one of the ignorant or those who lack self-control.

translation: So his Lord responded to him, and He turned away from him their evil plotting. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's protective care for His prophets and the believers. It signifies that God is always aware of the plots against His faithful servants and has the power to thwart them. The verse underscores the themes of divine omniscience and providence, reassuring believers that God hears their prayers and knows their circumstances, thereby intervening on their behalf when they are subjected to trials or conspiracies.

translation: Then it seemed to them, after they had seen the signs, that they should imprison him for a time.
interpretation: This verse highlights the injustice and malice of the people around Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). Despite witnessing the clear signs and miracles that demonstrated his innocence and righteousness, they still decided to imprison him for a while. It shows how sometimes, truth and evidence can be overlooked due to preconceived notions, jealousy, or other ulterior motives, leading to unjust treatment of the innocent.

translation: And there entered the prison with him two young men. One of them said, "Indeed, I have seen myself [in a dream] pressing wine." The other said, "Indeed, I have seen myself carrying upon my head [some] bread, from which the birds were eating. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you to be of those who do good."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance from those who are perceived as righteous and knowledgeable. The two young men in the prison with Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) turn to him for interpretation of their dreams because they see him as one of the 'doers of good' (local translation of 'من المحسنين'). This indicates that Yusuf's character and behavior in the prison had earned him respect, and people were inclined to seek his help due to his perceived goodness and insight. It underscores the value of good character in gaining the trust and respect of others.

translation: He said, 'I will tell you about its interpretation before it comes to you. Indeed, it is among the things my Lord has taught me. I have abandoned the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah and are disbelievers in the Hereafter.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the knowledge and wisdom granted to Prophet Jesus (Isa ibn Maryam) by Allah. It signifies that the knowledge given to him is a sign of his prophethood and a demonstration of Allah's power to grant special abilities to His messengers. The verse also contrasts the faith of Prophet Jesus with the disbelief of his people, emphasizing their rejection of the hereafter and their lack of faith in Allah.

translation: And I follow the religion of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. It is not for us to associate anything with God. That is God's bounty upon us and upon the people, but most people are not grateful.
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of gratitude towards God's blessings. The prophets Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Ya'qub are mentioned as the ancestors whose monotheistic faith is being followed. The phrase 'ذلك من فضل الله علينا وعلى الناس' (that is a bounty from God to us and to people) suggests that the true faith and the ability to adhere to it is a divine gift not just to the believers but to humanity at large. The fact that 'أكثر الناس لا يشكرون' (most people are not grateful) underscores a universal human tendency to overlook or not appreciate divine favors, emphasizing the need for reflection and gratitude.

translation: O two companions of the prison, are separate lords better or Allah, the One, the Prevailing?
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and his fellow prisoners. Yusuf is being asked to interpret their dreams and seizes the opportunity to preach the oneness of God. The verse rhetorically questions whether being devoted to multiple, disparate deities is better than worshipping the singular, all-powerful God. It underscores the Islamic principle of Tawhid (monotheism), emphasizing the superiority and uniqueness of God's authority and dominion over the fragmented and potentially conflicting allegiances demanded by multiple deities. It serves as an invitation to recognize and affirm the unity and supremacy of God.

translation: You do not worship besides Him except [mere] names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority. The command is for none but Allah. He has commanded that you worship not except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse is a critique of the polytheistic practices of the pre-Islamic Arabs, where they worshipped idols and deities that were merely names they and their forefathers had coined, lacking any divine authority or proof. It underscores the Islamic principle of Tawhid (the oneness of God), emphasizing that true authority and judgment belong solely to Allah, and that the correct and upright religion (Din) is the worship of Allah alone, unadulterated by the attribution of divinity to other entities or beings. The verse highlights the ignorance of the majority who deviate from this monotheistic path.

translation: O my two companions of the prison, as for one of you, he will pour wine for his lord to drink; and as for the other, he will be crucified so that the birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire.
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) in the Qur'an. Here, Yusuf is interpreting a dream for two companions in prison. The verse signifies the inevitability and finality of the fate that has been decreed by Allah for the two prisoners, as foretold by Yusuf's interpretation of their dream. One will be executed by crucifixion, and the other will serve wine to his lord, likely indicating a return to favor or a position of service. The phrase 'qadiya al-amr' (the matter has been decreed) underscores the certainty and irreversibility of Allah's decree, suggesting that the outcome is not just a prediction but a divine judgment that has already been determined.

translation: And he said to the one whom he knew would be saved: 'Mention me to your lord.' But Satan made him forget to mention him to his lord, so he [Joseph] stayed in prison for several years.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of relying on human intermediaries for help and forgetting to turn to Allah. The individual who was supposed to help Joseph by mentioning him to the king forgot due to Satan's influence, leading to Joseph's prolonged imprisonment. It underscores the importance of directly seeking Allah's help and remembering Him in times of need, as reliance solely on human connections can lead to forgetfulness of Allah and adverse outcomes.

translation: And the king said, "Indeed, I have seen [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry. O eminent ones, explain to me my vision, if you should interpret visions."
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of seeking knowledge and guidance from those who possess it. The king's dream is a metaphor for the unknown future, and his request to the nobles to interpret it highlights the need for expertise and insight in understanding complex situations. The verse implies that true understanding and interpretation of life's events require a deep understanding and knowledge, much like Yusuf's ability to interpret dreams, which is a gift from Allah. It underscores the value of seeking guidance from those endowed with knowledge and insight, as they can provide clarity and direction in times of uncertainty.

translation: They said, "A jumble of dreams. And we are not knowledgeable in the interpretation of dreams."
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and dismissal of the people towards the message or warning given to them, likening it to mere confused or jumbled dreams, and they claim ignorance or lack of expertise in understanding or interpreting such matters, thus undermining the significance or validity of the message.

translation: And the one of the two who was freed and remembered after a while said, 'I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and the passage of time in gaining clarity and understanding. The individual who was freed and remembered after a period of time is now able to interpret the dream, indicating that sometimes, a lapse in time is necessary for gaining insight and understanding, and that knowledge and wisdom can be revealed when the circumstances are ripe.

translation: Joseph, O man of truth, explain to us [the meaning of a dream] of seven fat cows whom seven lean ones were devouring and of seven green ears of grain and [seven] others dry, that I may return to the people so they will know [the explanation].
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of knowledge and the role of those who possess it in guiding others. Prophet Yusuf's (Joseph) ability to interpret dreams is not just a skill, but a trust that he is called upon to fulfill, demonstrating the responsibility that comes with having knowledge that can benefit others. The king's request to Yusuf signifies the societal need for wise and knowledgeable individuals to interpret complex situations and provide guidance, underscoring the value of expertise and insight in leadership and decision-making.

translation: You will sow for seven years consecutively; then what you reap leave it in its ear, except a little from which you eat.
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) interpreting the dream of the king in Egypt. Here, Yusuf is advising the people to prepare for a period of abundance followed by a period of famine. He tells them that they will have seven years of continuous cultivation and prosperity, and during this time, they should harvest their crops and store them in their ears, leaving aside only a small amount for their immediate consumption. This advice is a prudent measure to conserve the crops for the forthcoming years of famine.

translation: Then after that will come seven severe [years] which will eat what you have stored for them, except a little from which you store.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a period of severe famine or hardship that will follow a period of prosperity. The 'seven severe years' will consume most of what has been stored or prepared for them, leaving only a little of what is strongly protected or safeguarded. The verse is highlighting the importance of storing and preparing for the future, but also indicating that even with preparation, the severity of the hardship will be such that most of what has been stored will be consumed.

translation: Then comes a year after that in which people are given relief and in which they press.
interpretation: This verse signifies a shift in fortune for the people, indicating that after a period of hardship, there will be a year of relief and abundance. The phrase 'فيه يغاث الناس' (in it, the people are given relief) suggests a time when people receive aid or succor, likely referring to a year of fertility or prosperity following a drought or famine. The phrase 'وفيه يعصرون' (and in it, they press) implies that this relief comes in the form of abundant produce, as 'يعصرون' can refer to the pressing of grapes or olives, indicating a fruitful harvest. Thus, the verse conveys a message of hope and divine providence, suggesting that periods of hardship are followed by times of plenty, underscoring the cyclical nature of fortune and the benevolence of God towards His people.

translation: And the king said, "Bring him to me." But when the messenger came to him, [Joseph] said, "Return to your lord and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plot."
interpretation: This verse highlights Joseph's cautious and wise nature. By asking the king to investigate the matter of the women who cut their hands, Joseph is seeking to clear his name and expose the truth behind the false accusations made against him. He is confident that his Lord is aware of the women's plot and will reveal the truth, demonstrating his trust in God's justice and providence.

translation: He said: 'What was your business, ladies, when you tempted Joseph to yield to your desires?' They said: 'God is pure and above all imputation of evil! We know no evil of him.' The wife of Al-'Aziz said: 'Now the truth has become manifest. It was I who tempted him to yield to my desires, and he is indeed one of the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological dynamics of guilt and the tendency to deflect responsibility. The women, who had previously been complicit in the Aziz's plot against Yusuf, now clear their names and shift the blame onto the Aziz's wife. The Aziz's wife, confronted with the evidence of her own wrongdoing, finally admits her guilt and acknowledges Yusuf's innocence. This verse illustrates the human tendency to deny or downplay one's own wrongdoing until confronted with irrefutable evidence, at which point the truth becomes undeniable ('al-haqqu hashasa'). It also underscores the theme of Yusuf's moral integrity and his resistance to temptation, as well as the eventual triumph of truth over deception.

translation: That He (Allah) may know that I have not been unfaithful to her in secret and that Allah does not guide the plan of the treacherous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of betrayal and deception, emphasizing that Allah does not guide the plots of those who are treacherous. It serves as a warning that actions driven by deceit and betrayal are ultimately futile and not supported by divine guidance. In the context it is given, it underscores the moral and spiritual ramifications of unfaithfulness, suggesting that such behavior is not only morally reprehensible but also spiritually misguided.

translation: And I do not absolve myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent tendency of the human soul towards evil, suggesting that it is prone to succumbing to base desires unless it is protected and guided by the mercy of Allah. It underscores the importance of divine guidance and mercy in preventing individuals from falling into sin and wrongdoing, and reassures that Allah is forgiving and merciful to those who seek His guidance and protection.

translation: And the king said, "Bring him to me that I may attach him to my person." And when he spoke to him, he said, "Indeed, you are today with us established and trusted."
interpretation: This verse highlights the king's recognition of Prophet Yusuf's exceptional qualities and his decision to appoint him to a position of trust and authority. The king is drawn to Yusuf's wisdom, integrity, and competence, as demonstrated during their conversation. By declaring Yusuf 'mechan' (powerful or strong) and 'amin' (trustworthy), the king acknowledges his capability to hold a high-ranking position, thereby setting the stage for Yusuf's rise to a leadership role in the kingdom.

translation: He said, "Set me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I will be a knowing guardian."
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities that make an individual worthy of responsibility and leadership. By stating 'I am a guardian, knowledgeable', Yusuf (Joseph) is asserting his capability and competence to manage the resources and treasures of the land, demonstrating that effective stewardship requires both the ability to protect and the knowledge to make informed decisions.

translation: And thus We established Joseph in the land to settle therein wherever he willed. We bestow of Our Mercy on whom We will and We do not waste the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's providential care for His righteous servants, as exemplified by Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), who was enabled to attain a position of power and influence in Egypt. The verse suggests that God empowers His chosen individuals to achieve their goals and fulfill their aspirations, as a manifestation of His mercy and reward for their good deeds. The phrase 'we do not waste the reward of those who do good' underscores the idea that God is just and appreciative of the righteous actions of His servants, implying that their efforts are not in vain and will be duly compensated.

translation: And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who have believed and have been fearing God
interpretation: This verse highlights the superiority of the reward in the hereafter for those who have faith and are mindful of God, suggesting that their righteous actions and piety will be compensated with a better outcome in the afterlife, implying a contrast between the fleeting nature of worldly rewards and the eternal, superior reward of the hereafter.

translation: And Joseph's brothers came (to Egypt) and they entered unto him, and he knew them, but they knew him not.
interpretation: This verse highlights the complex dynamics of recognition and anonymity in human interactions. Joseph, having been sold into slavery by his brothers and subsequently rising to a position of power in Egypt, is now faced with their arrival. The verse notes that while Joseph immediately recognizes his brothers, they fail to recognize him. This disparity underscores the transformative impact of time, circumstance, and perhaps even Joseph's deliberate actions to conceal his identity, on the perception and recognition of individuals. It also touches upon the theme of divine providence and the unfolding of destiny, as Joseph's ability to recognize his brothers amidst their unawareness of his true identity serves as a poignant moment in the narrative, laden with emotional and psychological depth.

translation: And when he had furnished them with their supplies, he said, "Bring me a brother of yours from your father; do you not see that I give full measure and I am the best of hosts?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the subtle yet effective way Joseph tests his brothers while maintaining his gracious hospitality. By asking for their brother Benjamin, Joseph is not only checking if they are telling the truth about having another brother but also creating an opportunity to reunite with his family. The statement 'Do you not see that I give full measure and I am the best of hosts' underscores Joseph's generosity and integrity, making it harder for his brothers to suspect his true intentions. It showcases Joseph's wisdom in handling the situation with kindness and fairness, ultimately paving the way for a greater reunion and resolution.

translation: But if you do not bring him to me, then there will be no measure for you with me, and you will not come near.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of honesty and trustworthiness in one's dealings. The condition set forth implies that failure to fulfill the requirement (bringing the person or proof as demanded) results in severe consequences (no measure or sale allowed and being kept at a distance), signifying the gravity with which unfulfilled obligations or deceit are viewed.

translation: They said, 'We will certainly try to persuade his father to let him come with us, and we will certainly do it.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the determination and cunning of Joseph's brothers as they devise a plan to separate him from his father, Jacob. Their statement, 'We will certainly try to persuade his father to let him come with us, and we will certainly do it,' reveals their resolve to achieve their goal, showcasing their manipulative intentions towards their father to get Joseph to accompany them. It underscores the complex dynamics within the family and the challenges Jacob faces in protecting his beloved son.

translation: And [Yusuf] told his servants to put their merchandise [i.e., the money with which they had bought grain] back into their saddlebags, so that they might recognize it when they return to their people, and thus they might return [to Yusuf].
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological insight and strategic thinking of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) as he devises a plan to test his brothers and potentially reunite with his younger brother, Benjamin. By secretly returning their money and placing his own cup in Benjamin's sack, Yusuf aims to create a situation that would make his brothers return to him, thereby assessing their changed behavior and commitment to their brother after their previous ordeal. This action demonstrates Yusuf's clever use of circumstances to achieve his goal of reuniting with his family, while also testing the sincerity and loyalty of his brothers.

translation: When they returned to their father, they said, "O our father, the measure has been withheld from us, so send with us our brother [Benjamin] that we may be given a measure [of grain], and indeed, we will be his guardians."
interpretation: This verse highlights the brothers' strategic and heartfelt plea to their father, Jacob, after being denied a full measure of grain by Joseph, who was testing their honesty and loyalty. By asking Jacob to send Benjamin with them, they not only sought to obtain more provisions but also demonstrated their commitment to ensuring Benjamin's safety, thereby showing a growth in their character and responsibility. Their promise to protect Benjamin indicates a change in their behavior, suggesting they have learned from their past actions and are now more reliable and trustworthy.

translation: He said, "Did I not entrust you with him except as I entrusted you with his brother before? So, Allah is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the comparative trustworthiness of Allah versus human guardians. It suggests that just as Allah protected the Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) when his brothers were entrusted with him, He will similarly safeguard the Prophet's brother Benjamin. The verse reassures that Allah's protection and mercy surpass human capabilities, emphasizing the futility of human schemes against divine will.

translation: And when they opened their [trunk] baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what [more] could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. And we will obtain supplies for our family and guard our brother and have an increase of one camel's load; that is an easy measurement."
interpretation: This verse highlights the cunning and cleverness of the Prophet Yusuf's brothers as they negotiate with their father, Ya'qub, to take their brother Binyamin with them to Egypt. The return of their money, which they had paid for the grain, is seen as a blessing and an opportunity to convince their father to let Binyamin accompany them. The brothers are trying to assure their father that they will take care of Binyamin and bring back more provisions, thus gaining his trust. The verse showcases the brothers' resourcefulness and their efforts to achieve their goal of being reunited with Yusuf, while also demonstrating their concern for their family's well-being.

translation: He said, "I will not send him with you until you swear to me by Allah that you will bring him [back] to me unless you are surrounded [i.e., prevented]." And when they had sworn their oath, he said, "Allah, over what we say, is Witness."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of making solemn promises and holding oneself accountable for one's commitments, with the understanding that ultimately, it is God who oversees and holds individuals responsible for their actions and promises.

translation: And he said, "O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from different gates; and I cannot avail you against [the decree of] Allah at all. The decision is only for Allah; upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who would rely [indeed] rely."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trusting in Allah's plan and decree, rather than relying solely on human strategies or precautions. The example given is that of Ya'qub (Jacob) advising his sons to enter the city from different gates, not to avoid any potential danger, but to illustrate that true security and protection come from Allah alone. The verse emphasizes that even with precautions, the outcome is ultimately determined by Allah's will, and that trust and reliance should be placed in Him.

translation: And when they entered from where their father had ordered them, it did not avail them against Allah except [it was] a need in the soul of Jacob which he satisfied. And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights that even the measures taken by Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob), guided by his wisdom and concern for his sons, were ultimately subject to the will of Allah. The phrase 'إلا حاجة في نفس يعقوب قضاها' suggests that Ya'qub's actions were driven by an inner need or desire that he was fulfilling, indicating that his decisions were influenced by his own understanding and emotional state. The verse underscores the idea that true knowledge and understanding come from Allah, and that human actions, no matter how well-intentioned, are limited in their ability to alter the divine decree. It emphasizes Ya'qub's possession of knowledge granted by Allah, contrasting it with the lack of knowledge among most people, thereby highlighting the distinction between divine guidance and human understanding.

translation: And when they entered upon Yusuf, he took his brother to himself; he said, "I am your brother, so do not despair over what they used to do."
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep emotional bond between Yusuf and his brother Benjamin. When they met, Yusuf revealed his true identity to Benjamin, and comforted him, alleviating his distress caused by their brothers' past wrongdoings. Yusuf's action demonstrates his compassion and brotherly love, showing that he was not only concerned about his own well-being but also about the emotional state of his brother.

translation: So when he had furnished them with their supplies, he put the drinking cup in his brother's saddlebag. Then a caller called out, 'O caravan, you are indeed thieves!'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the clever and subtle method adopted by Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) to test his brothers and to create an opportunity to reunite with his brother Benjamin. By placing the cup in Benjamin's sack, Yusuf sets the stage for the accusation of theft, which allows him to detain Benjamin and eventually reveal his identity to his brothers, thus reuniting with his family. The verse highlights Yusuf's wisdom and strategic thinking in achieving his goal of reconciliation with his family.

translation: They said, and they turned towards them, "What do you miss?"
interpretation: The verse highlights a moment of inquiry and introspection, where individuals are asked to reflect on their losses or what they are missing. It suggests a turning point or a moment of reckoning where people are prompted to assess their situation, consider what they have lost, and possibly redirect their focus or priorities.

translation: They said, "If he is caught stealing, [it is not surprising]; indeed his brother [Yusuf] had stolen before." But Joseph kept it to himself and did not reveal it to them. He said [to himself], "You are in a worse situation, and God knows best what you are describing."
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological manipulation employed by the brothers of Prophet Yusuf to lure their brother Benjamin into staying with them. By offering a substantial reward, 'a camel's load', for the return of the lost royal cup, they create a situation where Benjamin is tempted to stay behind, thereby separating him from his brothers. The verse showcases the intricate dynamics within the family of Prophet Yaqub and the clever tactics used by his sons to achieve their goals.

translation: They said, 'By Allah, you have certainly known that we did not come to cause corruption in the land and are not thieves.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the innocence and integrity of the brothers of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) as they defend themselves against the accusation of theft. They invoke God as a witness to their truthfulness, asserting that they came not to cause corruption in the land and that they were not thieves. This demonstrates their moral character and clears them of the false accusation, showcasing their commitment to righteousness and honesty.

translation: They said, 'Then what is the recompense of it, if you should be truthful?'
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the demand of the disbelievers for a consequence or punishment if the believers are proven to be lying about their warnings of a coming reckoning or punishment. The disbelievers are essentially challenging the believers to provide a consequence or penalty if their claims are false, indicating their skepticism and refusal to accept the truth.

translation: They said, 'The punishment for him in whose baggage it is found is that he himself shall be (held as) the punishment thereof.' Thus it is that we requite the wrong-doers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of divine justice, where the punishment or consequence is directly related to the action committed. It suggests that the act of wrongdoing inherently contains within it the seeds of its own retribution. The verse implies that the wrongdoers will face a consequence that is intrinsically linked to their wrongdoing, serving as a form of justice.

translation: So he began [searching] their bags before the bag of his brother; then he extracted it from the bag of his brother. Thus We contrived for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother within the religion of the king except that Allah willed. We raise to degrees whom We will, but over every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intricate balance between divine will and human actions, illustrating that even the most meticulously planned human endeavors are ultimately subject to God's sovereign decree. It underscores the layered nature of knowledge and capability, suggesting that every individual endowed with knowledge or power is, in turn, under the jurisdiction of a higher authority or a more knowledgeable being, culminating in the acknowledgment of God's omniscience and omnipotence.

translation: They said, 'If he steals, a brother of his has stolen before.' But Joseph kept it to himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, 'You are in a worse condition, and Allah is most knowing of what you describe.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and double standards of Yusuf's brothers, who accuse him of theft based on a past misdeed committed by his brother. Yusuf, instead of openly confronting them, keeps his feelings hidden and responds by subtly condemning their moral character, implying that they are in a worse state than he is. The verse also underscores the omniscience of Allah, who is aware of the true nature of their accusations and Yusuf's situation.

translation: They said, 'O Azizi, indeed he has a father [who is] an old man, so take one of us in place of him. Indeed, we see you as one of the doers of good.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the deep sense of familial responsibility and loyalty among the brothers of Yusuf. They are willing to sacrifice one of their own to save their father from the agony of being separated from Benjamin, demonstrating the strong familial bonds and the value they place on their father's well-being. By asking Yusuf (who is referred to here as 'Al-Aziz') to take one of them in place of Benjamin, they show their trust in Yusuf's character, having observed his kindness and fairness ('إنا نراك من المحسنين'). This reflects not only their perception of Yusuf's noble nature but also their own moral code that prioritizes family ties and the welfare of their elderly father.

translation: He said, 'God forbid that we take other than him with whom we found our possession; indeed we would then be unjust.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of evidence-based accusations. The speaker is asserting their innocence and fairness by stating that they would not unjustly accuse someone unless they had concrete evidence (in this case, finding their lost goods with that person). It underscores the principle of not making assumptions or accusations without substantial proof, reflecting a value of justice and fairness.

translation: And when they had lost all hope of him, they conferred together in private. The eldest of them said, 'Do you not know that your father took from you a solemn pledge in the name of God, and before that, you were remiss in the matter of Joseph? I shall not leave this land until my father permits me or God decides for me; and He is the Best of Judges.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of fulfilling one's commitments and covenants. The eldest son reminds his brothers of the oath they took before God in the presence of their father, Jacob, regarding their responsibility towards Joseph. By invoking this oath, the eldest son underscores the gravity of their past actions and his determination to remain steadfast until his father permits him to leave or until God intervenes on his behalf, emphasizing trust in divine judgment.

translation: Go to your father and say, 'O our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we did not testify except to what we knew. And we were not guardians of the unseen'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of honesty and the limitations of human knowledge. The brothers of Yusuf are advised to be truthful about what they know and acknowledge that they are not aware of things beyond their knowledge, demonstrating the value of admitting the boundaries of one's understanding and not making claims about things one is not certain about.

translation: And ask the town where we were, and the caravan in which we came, and indeed, we are telling the truth.
interpretation: The verse is highlighting the importance of verifying the truth by seeking evidence from reliable sources. The people of the town and the caravan they were with are being asked to confirm the events that took place. This verse emphasizes the need for corroborating testimony to establish the truth, indicating that the speakers are confident in the veracity of their account.

translation: He said, 'Nay, your souls have made a matter seem fair to you, so patience is befitting. Perhaps Allah will bring them to me all. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and trust in God's wisdom. The speaker, likely Prophet Yaqub (Jacob), is being consoled after being separated from his sons. The verse suggests that the difficulties and hardships faced are not necessarily a result of divine decree, but rather the product of one's own circumstances or the actions of others. The phrase 'فصبر جميل' (so patience is beautiful) indicates that the response to such challenges should be one of dignified and graceful patience. The verse then expresses hope that God will reunite him with his sons, demonstrating the speaker's faith in God's omniscience and wisdom, as indicated by 'إنه هو العليم الحكيم' (He is the Knowing, the Wise). This interpretation underscores the value of maintaining patience and trust in God's plan, even in the face of adversity.

translation: And he turned away from them and said, 'Oh, my sorrow over Joseph!' And his eyes became white/snowy because of the grief, so he became suppressed (of emotions).
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound grief and emotional pain that Ya'qub (Jacob) felt upon being separated from his son Yusuf (Joseph). The phrase 'ابيضت عيناه من الحزن' (his eyes turned white with grief) is a metaphor for the intense sorrow that consumed him, to the point where his eyes lost their natural luster, symbolizing the overwhelming nature of his emotional pain. The description of Ya'qub as 'كظيم' (suppressed his anger/grief) suggests that he bore his sorrow with patience and restraint, choosing not to express his emotions outwardly, despite the depth of his inner turmoil.

translation: They said, 'By Allah, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become chronically ill or become among the perishing'
interpretation: The verse highlights the concern of Joseph's brothers that their father, Jacob, is so consumed by his love for Joseph that he is risking his own health and well-being. They suggest that Jacob's constant remembrance of Joseph is to the point where he is either becoming severely ill or is among those who are perishing, implying that his grief is potentially fatal. This shows the depth of Jacob's emotional pain and the brothers' awareness of the impact their actions have had on him.

translation: He said, 'I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah that which you do not know.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of turning to Allah in times of distress and sorrow, and having faith that He possesses knowledge and wisdom beyond human understanding. The speaker, Prophet Yaqub (Jacob), is expressing his grief and hardship to Allah, demonstrating a deep trust in Allah's omniscience and providence. It underscores the value of patience and the belief that Allah is aware of what is best for His servants, even when they are unaware.

translation: O my sons, go and find out about Joseph and his brother and despair not of the comfort from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of the comfort from Allah except the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining hope in the face of adversity, especially when seeking reunion with loved ones. It suggests that even in difficult circumstances, one should not lose faith in God's mercy and providence. The verse implies that despair is a characteristic of those who lack faith, and that believers should continue to strive and hold onto hope, as it is a fundamental aspect of their trust in God's benevolence and grace.

translation: But when they came to Joseph, they said, 'O 'Aziz, hardship has touched us and our family, and we have come with merchandise poor in quality, so give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of charity and kindness, especially towards those in need. The brothers of Yusuf, having suffered hardship, come to him (though unrecognized by him) with a meager offering, and they appeal to his generosity. The verse suggests that acts of charity are not only a moral virtue but are also divinely rewarded, as indicated by the phrase 'Indeed, Allah rewards those who give charity.' It underscores the principle that charitable acts are pleasing to Allah and will be recompensed, encouraging believers to be generous and benevolent towards others.

translation: He said, "Do you know what you have done to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of human ignorance and the consequences of one's actions when driven by a lack of knowledge or understanding. The speaker, likely a figure of authority or someone with hindsight, is addressing individuals who had previously mistreated or wronged Yusuf (Joseph) and his brother, suggesting that their actions were the result of ignorance. The verse implies that the individuals being addressed are now being held accountable for their past deeds, and are being made to confront the reality of their actions. It underscores the idea that ignorance is not an excuse for wrongdoing and that one's actions have consequences that must be faced.

translation: They said, "Are you indeed Joseph?" He said, "I am Joseph, and this is my brother; God has indeed been gracious to us. Indeed, he who fears God and is patient, then God does not let the reward of the doers of good to be lost."
interpretation: This verse highlights the themes of divine providence and the reward for those who exhibit patience and righteousness. When Joseph reveals his identity to his brothers, he not only acknowledges his own identity but also expresses gratitude for God's favor upon him and his brother. The verse underscores the idea that God does not waste the reward of those who do good, emphasizing the importance of piety (taqwa) and perseverance (sabr) as key virtues that lead to divine recompense. Joseph's statement serves as a reassurance that virtuous conduct, even in the face of adversity, is ultimately recognized and rewarded by God.

translation: They said, 'By Allah, certainly Allah has preferred you over us, and indeed we have been wrongdoers.'
interpretation: The verse highlights a moment of introspection and acknowledgment of past wrongdoings by individuals who recognize they were surpassed by someone else due to divine favor, indicating a shift from jealousy or rivalry to an acceptance of God's will and a recognition of their own past errors.

translation: He [Allah] will say, 'There is no blame upon you today.' Allah will forgive you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.
interpretation: This verse is a declaration of divine mercy and forgiveness. It signifies that on the Day of Judgment, the believers will be absolved of any guilt or remorse for having been separated from their loved ones in this world due to death, or for having been unable to fulfill certain obligations. The verse is a reassurance that Allah's mercy encompasses all aspects of human life, and that His forgiveness is not limited by human shortcomings. It highlights the attribute of Allah as 'Arahmar al-Rahimin' (the Most Merciful of the merciful), emphasizing that His mercy surpasses all other aspects of His judgment.

translation: Take this shirt of mine and cast it over my father's face; he will become seeing. And bring to me all your family.
interpretation: This verse signifies the power of faith and the miraculous return of one's senses through the blessings associated with the sacred garments or relics of the righteous, as well as the importance of family unity and the joy of reunion after a period of separation and hardship.

translation: And when the caravan had departed, their father said, "Indeed, I find the smell of Joseph, if only you did not think me feeble-minded."
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep emotional connection and love that Jacob has for his son Joseph, even after many years of separation. Jacob's ability to smell Joseph's scent from a distance, despite being old and potentially feeble-minded in the eyes of his sons, signifies the strength of his faith and intuition. It also showcases Jacob's unwavering hope and conviction that he will be reunited with Joseph, as he is guided by his spiritual senses.

translation: They said, 'By God, you are certainly in your old error.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy and refusal of the disbelievers to accept the truth. They accuse the Prophet of being in his old error, implying that he has not changed or learned from his past. The phrase 'ضلالك القديم' (your old error) refers to their perception that the Prophet's message is a continuation of a long-standing deviation from the right path. The use of 'تالله' (by God) emphasizes their swearing and affirming that their accusation is true, demonstrating their conviction in their own beliefs and their rejection of the Prophet's message.

translation: So when the bearer of good tidings arrived, he cast it over his face, and he returned [once again] seeing. He said, 'Did I not tell you that I know from Allah that which you do not know?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of having faith in the unseen knowledge that Allah provides to certain individuals, in this case, Prophet Yaqub (Jacob). The verse demonstrates that despite the doubts and skepticism of those around him, Prophet Yaqub's conviction in the knowledge imparted to him by Allah proved to be correct when the bearer of good news (the Prophet's son) arrived and threw the shirt on Prophet Yaqub's face, restoring his sight. It underscores the idea that those who are given knowledge by Allah have insight that others may not possess, emphasizing the importance of trusting in divine knowledge and prophecy.

translation: They said, 'O our father, ask for us forgiveness of our sins; indeed, we have been sinful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and acknowledging one's mistakes. The sons of Jacob, upon returning from their ordeal, ask their father to seek forgiveness for them, demonstrating a recognition of their wrongdoing and a willingness to make amends. This shows that true repentance involves not only acknowledging one's sins but also seeking the help of others, in this case, their father, to intercede on their behalf with Allah. It underscores the value of humility and the acknowledgment of one's limitations in seeking divine mercy.

translation: He said, 'I will ask forgiveness for you my Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful'
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, as the speaker, likely a prophet or a righteous individual, is seeking forgiveness for others, demonstrating the intercessory role of righteous individuals in Islam and the boundless mercy of Allah towards His creation.

translation: And when they came to Joseph, he took his parents to shelter with him and said, "Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in safety."
interpretation: This verse signifies the culmination of a long and arduous journey for Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and his family. It highlights the theme of reunion and the providence of Allah. When Yusuf's family finally meets him in Egypt, he welcomes his parents, symbolizing a moment of great joy and reconciliation. The verse also underscores the importance of submitting one's plans to the will of Allah, as indicated by 'Insha'Allah' (if Allah wills). It suggests that safety and security are contingent upon Allah's will, emphasizing a profound trust in divine providence.

translation: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration. And he said, "O my father, this is the interpretation of my dream of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of the prison and brought you [here] from bedouin life after Satan had sown discord between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine providence and the ultimate triumph of good over adversity. Yusuf's expression of gratitude to his Lord for reuniting him with his family and fulfilling his dream underscores the idea that Allah's plan is always benevolent, even when circumstances appear bleak. The verse also illustrates the concept of 'lutf' (subtle kindness), suggesting that Allah's favors are often subtle and manifest in unexpected ways, requiring faith and patience to be fully appreciated.

translation: Lord, You have given me [part] of the kingdom and taught me the interpretation of narrations/events. Originator of the heavens and the earth, You are my guardian in this world and the hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of maintaining one's faith and righteous character until the end of one's life. The speaker, believed to be Prophet Solomon, is expressing his desire to die in a state of submission to God's will (as a Muslim) and to be joined with the righteous in the hereafter. It signifies the aspiration for a good ending and the companionship of the virtuous, underscoring the Islamic values of living a life of obedience to God and striving for moral excellence.

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. And you were not with them when they decided their affair, while they were plotting.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin of the knowledge being revealed to the Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing that the stories and events being shared with him are part of the unseen (al-ghayb) that only God knows. It underscores the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad, as he was not present at the events being described, such as the plotting of the people to whom the prophets were sent, thereby affirming the truth and authenticity of the revelation.

translation: And most of mankind will not be believers, even if you desire it eagerly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge faced by those who call people to guidance and faith, indicating that despite their sincerest efforts and desires, the majority of people will not believe. It underscores the reality that faith is a gift from Allah, and not everyone is blessed with it, regardless of the efforts made by the messengers or their followers to guide them.

translation: And you do not ask them for it any reward. It is not except a reminder for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the selfless nature of the Prophet's mission, emphasizing that he is not seeking any material reward or compensation from his people for conveying the message of the Qur'an. Instead, the Qur'an is presented as a universal reminder and guidance for all people, underscoring its role as a source of spiritual enlightenment and moral direction for humanity as a whole.

translation: And how many a sign within the heavens and earth do they pass over while they, therefrom, are turning away.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the phenomenon of people often being oblivious or indifferent to the signs and wonders of the natural world around them, despite being constantly exposed to them. It suggests that people tend to overlook or disregard the 'ayāt' (signs or verses) of God that are evident in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and instead, they pass by them without reflection or appreciation, indicating a lack of spiritual awareness or connection with the divine.

translation: And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the phenomenon where many people, despite claiming to believe in the oneness of God (Tawhid), still associate partners with Him in various forms, such as through superstitions, idolatrous practices, or attributing divine qualities to other beings or objects. It underscores the challenge of achieving pure monotheism in the face of deeply ingrained cultural and societal practices that often blur the lines of worship and devotion.

translation: Are they secure that there will not come to them a covering (sheet) from the punishment of Allah or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they are unaware?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that highlights the complacency of those who deny the truth. It warns them that they are not safe from the punishment of Allah, which can come upon them suddenly, either in the form of a catastrophic event or the Hour (the Day of Judgment) itself, catching them off guard and unaware. The verse is cautioning against a false sense of security and emphasizing the inevitability and unexpectedness of Allah's judgment.

translation: Say, 'This is my way; I invite unto Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah; and I am not of those who associate others with Him.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of conviction and clarity in calling others to the path of Allah. The phrase 'on insight' or 'with insight' signifies that the call to Allah should be based on knowledge and understanding, not mere speculation or blind following. It underscores the responsibility of those who claim to lead others spiritually to ensure they are guided by a deep understanding of their faith, and it distinguishes sincere monotheistic worship from polytheistic practices.

translation: And We did not send before you [Muhammad] except men to whom We revealed from among the people of cities. So have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah . Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the prophets sent by Allah were all human beings, not supernatural entities, and were from among the people of the towns. It invites reflection on the fate of those who came before, implying that the disbelievers should learn from history. The verse concludes by highlighting the superiority of the Hereafter for those who are righteous, suggesting that the focus should be on the eternal life rather than the temporary one, and questioning the ability of the disbelievers to understand this fundamental truth.

translation: until, when the messengers despaired and the people were convinced that they were lying, Our help came to them, and whoever We willed was saved. And Our punishment is not averted from the people who are guilty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of perseverance and the ultimate triumph of faith despite initial despair. It suggests that even when messengers of God lose hope and believe they have been deceived or disbelieved by their people, divine help arrives, saving whom God wills. The verse underscores the inevitability of God's punishment for those who are guilty, indicating that His decisive power cannot be deflected or deterred from those who have transgressed. It conveys a message of reassurance to the believers that divine succor is forthcoming, even when circumstances seem most dire, and serves as a warning to the transgressors of the inescapability of divine retribution.

translation: There is certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding. It is not a fabricated story but a confirmation of what is before it and a detailed explanation of all things and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of reflecting on the stories of past nations as a means to gain wisdom and insight. It suggests that these stories serve as a source of guidance and mercy for those who have faith, providing a deeper understanding of the world and its workings. The verse also underscores the authenticity of the Quran, affirming that it is not a fabricated narrative but rather a confirmation and detailed explanation of previous revelations, offering a comprehensive and nuanced understanding of the divine message.

translation: Alif Lam Mim Ra. These are the verses of the Book. And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the paradox of divine guidance and human skepticism. Despite the Quran being a clear and truthful revelation from God, as indicated by the phrase "which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth," many people still choose not to believe. This reflects a recurring theme in the Quran where it is observed that truth, when presented, is often met with disbelief by the majority. The verse suggests that the prevalence of disbelief is not due to a lack of clarity or authenticity in the message, but rather due to a resistance or unwillingness on the part of many people to accept it.

translation: Allah is He Who raised the heavens without any pillars that you can see, then established Himself on the Throne, and subjected the sun and the moon; each runs [its course] for a term appointed; He regulates the Affair, explaining the signs in detail that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omnipotence and sovereignty over the universe, emphasizing His ability to manage and regulate the cosmos without any visible support or constraint. The phrase 'raised the heavens without pillars that you can see' underscores the idea that God's creation is not bound by the physical laws or limitations that humans understand. The subsequent phrases, 'then established Himself on the Throne' and 'has subjected the sun and the moon,' reinforce the notion of God's supreme authority and control over the universe. The verse concludes by suggesting that God's meticulous management of the universe and the detailed explanation of His signs are intended to instill faith in the believers regarding their ultimate meeting with their Lord, reinforcing the concept of accountability and the hereafter.

translation: And it is He who spread the earth and placed in it firm mountains and rivers. And of all the fruits, He made in it pairs, two [of each kind]. He causes the night to cover the day. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intricate design and balance in the natural world as a sign of divine wisdom and power, inviting those who reflect to recognize the underlying unity and purpose in creation.

translation: And in the earth are neighbouring tracts and gardens of vines and cornfields and palm trees, growing from a single root and otherwise, watered with the same water; and We make some of them excel others in fruit. Surely in that are signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity and complexity within the natural world, using it as a metaphor for the multifaceted nature of truth and the varying capacities of individuals to understand and appreciate it. The different types of crops and plants, despite being watered by the same source, yield different outcomes in terms of their produce and utility, illustrating the concept that even when people are given the same guidance or truth, their understanding and application of it can vary greatly due to their individual capacities and perspectives. The verse suggests that these variations are not random but are instead signs or 'ayat' for those who use their intellect, indicating that there is a deeper wisdom and purpose behind the diversity observed in the world and in human understanding.

translation: And if you should marvel, then wondrous is their saying, "When we are dust, will we be in a new creation?" Those are the ones who have disbelieved in their Lord, and those will have shackles upon their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse highlights the astonishment and disbelief of those who deny the possibility of resurrection, questioning how they can be recreated after being reduced to mere dust. The verse interprets their skepticism as a manifestation of their deeper rejection of their Lord, leading to spiritual bondage and ultimately, eternal damnation in the fire.

translation: And they ask you to hasten the punishment before the reward, although there have already been examples of punishment before them. And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the impatient nature of the disbelievers who demand punishment rather than reward, despite the existence of precedents where similar demands were met with punishment in the past. However, it also underscores God's dual attributes: His mercy and forgiveness towards people despite their wrongdoing, and His severe punishment for those who deserve it. It serves as a warning and a reminder of God's justice and mercy.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" You are only a warner, and for every people is a guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy of disbelievers who demand miracles or signs as proof of the Prophet's message, despite previous revelations and warnings. It underscores the Prophet's role as a warner, emphasizing that guidance is specific to each community, implying that the Prophet is a guide for his people, and that divine guidance is tailored to the needs and contexts of different peoples.

translation: God knows what every female bears, and what the wombs lack or gain. And everything with Him is by measure.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's all-encompassing knowledge, particularly in relation to the mysteries of creation and the intricacies of human life. It signifies that God is aware of every detail concerning the conception and development of life within the womb, including any changes or adjustments that occur during pregnancy. The verse underscores the idea that God's knowledge is not limited to the visible or tangible aspects of existence but extends to the most intimate and hidden aspects of human experience. Furthermore, it suggests that God's knowledge is not just observational but is also actively engaged in the process of creation, with every aspect of existence being guided by a divine measure or plan. This interpretation emphasizes the theme of divine omniscience and the notion that human life is subject to a larger, divinely ordained order.

translation: The Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Great, the Exalted.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's all-encompassing knowledge and supreme authority. The phrase 'the Knower of the unseen and the seen' signifies that God has knowledge of both the manifest and the hidden, emphasizing His omniscience. The description of God as 'the Great, the Exalted' underscores His majesty and transcendence above all else, indicating that He is not only all-knowing but also possesses unparalleled greatness and is exalted beyond human comprehension.

translation: It is the same whether you conceal your speech or disclose it, whether you hide by night or go forth by day.
interpretation: This verse highlights the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, emphasizing that He is aware of all actions and intentions, whether they are kept hidden or made public. It underscores the futility of attempting to conceal one's deeds or words from Allah, as everything is known to Him, regardless of the time of day or the manner in which it is done.

translation: For him (each person) are angels in succession, before and behind him. They guard him by the command of Allah. Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah intends for a people ill, there is no repelling it. And there is not for them besides Him any patron.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intricate relationship between divine decree and human agency. It suggests that God's protection and preservation of an individual are conditional upon the individual's actions and state of being. The verse also underscores the idea that divine will is not arbitrary, but is instead responsive to changes within a people or individual. Furthermore, it emphasizes the notion that once God has willed a particular outcome, it is inevitable and cannot be averted. The verse ultimately conveys a message about personal responsibility and the limits of human control in the face of divine will.

translation: It is He who shows you the lightning, [causing] fear and aspiration, and generates the heavy clouds.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omnipotence and His ability to inspire both fear and hope in people through natural phenomena. The lightning is a manifestation of God's power that can evoke fear due to its potential to cause harm, yet it also inspires hope as it is associated with the coming of rain, which is essential for life and agriculture. The verse underscores the dual nature of God's signs, which can be both awe-inspiring and life-giving, reflecting the complex relationship between humanity and the natural world as ordained by God.
