translation: And the thunder glorifies [Allah] with His praise, and the angels [fear Him] out of reverence for Him, and He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills while they dispute about Allah; and He is severe in [the consequence of] His plan.
interpretation: This verse highlights the awe-inspiring power of God as manifested in natural phenomena like thunder and lightning. The thunder glorifies God, and the angels fear Him, indicating a universe where everything is in submission to God's will. The verse also criticizes those who dispute about God, suggesting that despite the evident signs of God's power, some people still argue about His existence or nature. It underscores God's immense power and the futility of disputing His authority.

translation: To Him [alone] is the supplication of truth. And those they call upon besides Him do not respond to them with a thing, except as one who stretches his hands toward water [from afar] to reach his mouth, but it will not reach it [thus]. And the supplication of the disbelievers is not but in error [i.e. futility].
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of idol worship and the uniqueness of Allah's ability to respond to supplications. It uses the metaphor of a person stretching out their hands to water, hoping it will reach their mouth, but it won't, to illustrate the ineffectiveness of praying to idols or false deities. The verse emphasizes that only Allah is capable of responding to prayers and that the supplications of those who disbelieve (in the oneness of God) are misguided and will not be answered.

translation: And to Allah prostrates whoever is within the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and their shadows [as well] in the mornings and the afternoons.
interpretation: This verse highlights the universal submission to Allah's will, indicating that everything in the heavens and on earth, whether willingly or unwillingly, submits to His authority. The reference to shadows in the morning and evening signifies the natural world's inherent obedience to Allah's command, as even inanimate objects are subject to His control, casting their shadows according to His ordained laws of nature. It underscores the theme of Tawhid (the oneness of God) and the comprehensive sovereignty of Allah over all creation.

translation: Say, 'Who is Lord of the heavens and earth?' Say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Have you then taken besides Him allies not possessing [even] for themselves any benefit or any harm?' Say, 'Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Or is darkness equivalent to light? Or have they attributed to Allah partners who create as He creates, so that creation became ambiguous to them?' Say, 'Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing.'
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the oneness and uniqueness of God as the creator of everything. It challenges the polytheistic beliefs of those who attribute partners to God, highlighting the stark contrast between the all-powerful, all-seeing God and the helpless, blind idols they worship. The rhetorical questions posed in the verse underscore the absurdity of equating God with other deities or entities that lack the power to benefit or harm even themselves. The verse asserts God's singular authority and creative power, affirming that He is the sole creator of all things, and that His creation is not comparable to that of others. This serves to reinforce the Islamic concept of Tawhid, or the oneness of God, and to refute the idea of associating partners with Him.

translation: He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their capacity, and the torrent carries a rising foam. And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking ornaments and goods, is a foam like it. Thus Allah presents the example of truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum; but as for that which benefits the people, it remains on the earth. Thus does Allah set forth the examples.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of water and flood to illustrate the fate of truth and falsehood. Just as the flood carries away the froth and scum, while the useful water remains, the verse suggests that falsehood is ephemeral and will be eliminated, whereas truth is enduring and will persist. The verse is highlighting the idea that just as the natural world has a way of separating the useful from the useless, God's truth will ultimately prevail and falsehood will be discarded. The verse is encouraging the reader to understand that the truth, like the water that nourishes the earth, is beneficial and will remain, while falsehood, like the froth, is useless and will be cast away.

translation: For those who have responded to their Lord is the best [reward]. And those who did not respond to Him - if they had all that is in the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would [surely] offer it as ransom. Those will have the worst reckoning, and their abode is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between those who respond to their Lord's call and those who do not. The obedients are promised the best reward, while the disobedient, despite their potential willingness to ransom themselves with all earthly possessions and more, will face a terrible reckoning. Their ultimate destination is Hell, a dreadful resting place, underscoring the severe consequences of rejecting divine guidance. It serves as a warning about the gravity of one's response to God's call, emphasizing the importance of obedience and the dire outcome of disobedience.

translation: Is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? It is those who are endued with understanding that receive admonition.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who possess spiritual insight and those who are spiritually blind. It suggests that only individuals endowed with intellect and wisdom ('ulu al-albab') are capable of deriving moral and spiritual lessons from divine revelations, implying that true understanding and guidance from scripture are reserved for those who are intellectually and spiritually receptive.

translation: Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the contract
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of believers who are committed to their covenants and promises, not just with God, but also with other people. It emphasizes the importance of integrity, faithfulness, and trustworthiness in one's relationships and agreements, reflecting a strong moral fabric that is foundational to a righteous community.

translation: And those who join that which Allah has commanded to be joined and fear their Lord and dread the evil reckoning.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of the righteous individuals who are obedient to Allah's commands, particularly in maintaining the ties that Allah has ordained to be kept, such as family bonds and other social relationships. Their actions are driven by a deep-seated fear of their Lord and an apprehension of the reckoning on the Day of Judgment, indicating a profound awareness of accountability in the Hereafter.

translation: And those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord, and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them secretly and publicly, and repel evil with good - those will have the good end of the abode
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of believers who will attain a good end. It emphasizes their patience, sincerity in seeking God's pleasure, establishment of prayer, and charitable spending in private and public. Moreover, they respond to evil with good, demonstrating a high level of moral character. The verse concludes by stating that such individuals will be rewarded with a favorable outcome in the hereafter, indicating that their righteous deeds and noble conduct will ultimately lead to their salvation and success in the afterlife.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence; they will enter them with whoever were righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. And the angels will enter upon them from every gate,
interpretation: This verse signifies that the believers will not be alone in their attainment of paradise; rather, their righteous family members and descendants will also be with them, emphasizing the importance of family ties and righteous living across generations. The image of angels entering from every gate symbolizes the comprehensive and multifaceted nature of the divine welcome and honor bestowed upon the righteous, underscoring the idea that their reward is not just for their individual deeds but is also intertwined with their familial and social bonds.

translation: Peace be upon you because you persevered. How excellent is the final abode!
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the reward for those who have endured hardships and difficulties with patience. The phrase 'peace be upon you' is a greeting of peace and tranquility, indicating that they have been blessed with a state of serenity due to their perseverance. The phrase 'fnعم عقبى الدار' (how excellent is the final abode) suggests that the ultimate reward for their patience is a wonderful and desirable outcome, implying that the hereafter is a place of bliss and happiness for those who have demonstrated patience and resilience in the face of challenges.

translation: And those who break the covenant of Allah after contracting it and cut what Allah has ordered to be joined and cause corruption on earth - it is those who are the losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who break their covenants with Allah after having made a firm commitment, sever ties that Allah has commanded to be maintained, and cause corruption on earth. Such individuals are not only condemned to receive Allah's curse, but they are also destined for a terrible abode in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes the gravity of violating divine commands and covenants, highlighting the consequences of such actions both spiritually and morally. It underscores the importance of upholding promises, maintaining familial and social bonds as ordained by Allah, and acting with integrity to avoid causing chaos and destruction on earth. The 'curse' and 'bad home' refer to divine displeasure and punishment, indicating a severe and dire outcome for those who engage in such reprehensible behavior.

translation: Allah extends the provision to whom He wills, and straitens it for whom He wills. And they rejoice in the life of this world, whereas the life of this world is nothing but a fleeting enjoyment compared to the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disparity in provision among people, emphasizing that Allah alone decides who receives abundance or scarcity in sustenance. It then critiques those who rejoice in worldly life, pointing out its fleeting nature and insignificance when compared to the Hereafter, suggesting that true value and lasting enjoyment are found in the afterlife, not in the temporary pleasures of this world.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'Indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy of those who reject faith, demanding miracles or signs as proof, despite previous revelations and guidance. The response given emphasizes God's sovereignty in guiding or misleading individuals, suggesting that He guides those who turn to Him in sincerity and repentance, while those who stubbornly refuse to believe are left in their error. It underscores the theme that faith is not merely about witnessing miracles but involves a turning of the heart towards God.

translation: Those who believe and whose hearts are set at rest by the remembrance of God. Behold, by God's remembrance hearts are set at rest.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of remembering God in achieving spiritual tranquility. It suggests that true believers are those whose hearts find peace and stability through the remembrance of God, indicating that the remembrance of God is a source of comfort and solace for the faithful.

translation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds - a state of supreme happiness is for them and a good final destination
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for those who have faith and lead a righteous life. 'Tuba' is often interpreted as a state of supreme happiness or a tree in paradise, symbolizing the immense joy and bliss that believers who do good deeds will experience. 'Hasun ma'ab' further emphasizes that their final destination is not only good but exceptionally good, indicating a return or abode that is highly commendable, referring to Paradise. Thus, the verse conveys that believers who act righteously will not only be happy in this life but will also have a wonderful afterlife in the hereafter.

translation: Thus We have sent you to a community before whom other communities have passed away, in order that you might recite to them what We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say, "He is my Lord; there is no deity worthy of worship except Him. In Him I have placed my trust, and to Him is my return."
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's role as a messenger to a community (ummah) that has been preceded by other nations. It underscores the significance of his message, which is based on the revelation he received from Allah. The verse also emphasizes the oneness of God (Tawhid), affirming that Allah is the sole deity worthy of worship and that the Prophet Muhammad trusts in Him and turns to Him in repentance. The mention of those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful (Al-Rahman) indicates the resistance faced by the Prophet and his message, underscoring the challenge of conveying the truth to those who reject it. The verse serves as a reassurance to the Prophet, directing him to reaffirm his faith and trust in Allah amidst adversity.

translation: And if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains were moved, or the earth was cut apart, or the dead were made to speak, [it would be this Qur'an]. But the matter is with Allah entirely. Have those who believed not come to know that, had Allah willed, He would have guided the people, all of them? And those who disbelieve will not cease to be struck, for what they have done, by calamity or it will settle close by their home, until the promise of Allah comes. Indeed, Allah does not fail in [His] promise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of human understanding and the futility of expecting miracles as proof of the truth. It emphasizes that true guidance is in God's hands and that those who have faith understand this. Meanwhile, those who reject faith will continue to face the consequences of their actions until the promise of God is fulfilled, underscoring the inevitability of divine justice and the reliability of God's promises.

translation: And indeed, messengers were mocked before you, but I gave respite to those who disbelieved, then I seized them, and how was My punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who mock or disbelieve in the messengers of God, indicating that despite initial leniency, divine punishment will ultimately befall them. It draws a historical parallel to previous nations who mocked messengers before Muhammad, suggesting that the consequence of their disbelief and mockery was severe. The verse implies that the punishment is not immediate but is certain, emphasizing the inevitability of God's retribution for those who persist in their disbelief and derision towards His messengers.

translation: Is He who is a guardian over every soul [as to] what it has earned, and they have attributed to Allah partners. Say, 'Name them.' Or do you inform Him of that which He does not know in the earth or of what is apparent of the speech? Rather, their [own] deceit has been made appealing to those who disbelieve, and they have been averted from the path. And whoever Allah sends astray - there will be for him no guide.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the stark contrast between the polytheistic beliefs of the disbelievers and the all-encompassing knowledge and authority of God. It is emphasizing that God is fully aware of the actions of every individual and holds them accountable, whereas the idols or partners that the disbelievers attribute to God are not only unknown to Him but also lack any real authority or power. The verse is suggesting that the elaborate schemes and plots devised by the disbelievers to evade accountability or to attribute partners to God are ultimately futile, as God is not unaware of their actions. Moreover, it is indicating that when God allows someone to go astray, there is no guide or savior to correct their path, underscoring the sovereignty of God's will over all matters.

translation: For them is punishment in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe. And they will not have from God any protector.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith and engage in wrongdoing, indicating that their punishment is not limited to the hereafter but begins in this life. The hardship and difficulties they face in this world are a precursor to the far more severe and lasting punishment that awaits them in the hereafter. The phrase 'وما لهم من الله من واق' underscores the inevitability of God's punishment, suggesting that there will be no protector or savior to shield them from God's retribution, emphasizing the futility of attempting to escape or mitigate divine justice.

translation: The example of the garden which is promised to those who are mindful ˹of Allah˺—through it flow rivers. Its produce is perpetual, and so is its shade. That is the reward of those who are mindful ˹of Allah˺. And the reward of the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: This verse is an allegory that contrasts the ultimate fate of the righteous and the unrighteous. The 'garden' or 'paradise' described is a metaphor for the reward of those who are mindful of God and live a virtuous life, where their spiritual nourishment is constant and their protection from harm is enduring. Conversely, the fate of those who reject faith is likened to the fire, symbolizing suffering and punishment. The verse underscores the moral consequence of one's actions in this life, emphasizing the importance of living a life of piety and righteousness to attain a favorable outcome in the hereafter.

translation: And those to whom We have given the Book rejoice at what has been revealed to you. And among the factions are some who deny parts of it. Say, "I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate [anything] with Him. To Him I invite, and to Him is my return."
interpretation: This verse highlights the division in response to the Prophet Muhammad's message among those who have received scripture before him. While some rejoice at the revelation sent down to him, indicating a recognition of its truth and continuity with their own beliefs, others from among the various factions deny parts of it, showing a resistance or disagreement. The verse then directs the Prophet to clarify his mission: to worship God alone without associating any partners with Him, and to call others to the same worship, emphasizing that his return is to God. This underscores the central Islamic principle of Tawhid (the oneness of God) and establishes the Prophet's role as a caller to this singular worship, unifying the message across previous scriptures and prophetic missions.

translation: And thus We have sent it down as a judgement in Arabic. And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would not have against Allah any ally or protector.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of adhering to the knowledge and guidance received from Allah, rather than following personal desires or the whims of others. It emphasizes that once one has been endowed with knowledge from Allah, deviating from it to follow one's own desires or those of others would result in being devoid of Allah's protection and guardianship.

translation: And We had certainly sent messengers before you and assigned to them wives and offspring. And it was not for a messenger to come with a sign except by permission of Allah . For every term is a decree.
interpretation: This verse highlights the humanity of the prophets sent by God, emphasizing that they were not superhuman beings but rather individuals with families and children, just like ordinary humans. It underscores the idea that the prophets were subject to the same natural and social experiences as others, thereby making their message and struggles more relatable to the people they were sent to guide. The verse also stresses that the ability of prophets to perform miracles or bring signs was not within their own power but was contingent upon God's permission, reinforcing the concept of divine sovereignty and the notion that prophetic miracles are manifestations of God's will rather than the prophets' own abilities. Furthermore, it suggests that every event or dispensation has a predetermined term or limit set by God, implying a divine plan unfolding over time.

translation: God effaces what He wills and confirms [what He wills], and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sovereignty and omnipotence of God, indicating that He has the authority to erase or confirm whatever He wills. The phrase 'and with Him is the Mother of the Book' suggests that God possesses the ultimate source of all knowledge and decree, often understood as the Preserved Tablet or the original, unaltered record of all that exists and occurs. It underscores the idea that God's knowledge and will are the foundation of everything, and that human understanding and destiny are subject to His divine plan.

translation: And if We show you some of what We have promised them or We take you in death, then upon you is only the [duty of] conveyance, and upon Us is the reckoning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet's role as a messenger, highlighting that his responsibility is to convey the message of Allah, regardless of whether he witnesses the fulfillment of the warnings given to those who reject the message or if he passes away before that happens. The accountability and reckoning of people's actions are Allah's prerogative, not the Prophet's. It underscores the distinction between the role of prophethood, which is about delivering the divine message, and the divine judgment that follows, which is beyond human or prophetic control.

translation: Do they not see that We are bringing to the land, reducing it from its sides? And Allah judges; there is no reverter of His judgment. And He is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: This verse is warning the disbelievers that just as Allah is reducing the land under their control, He can also take away their power completely. The reduction of the land is a sign of Allah's power and control over all things. The verse is also emphasizing that Allah's judgment is final and cannot be changed or delayed, and that He is swift in His reckoning, implying that those who are warned should take heed before it's too late.

translation: And those before them indeed plotted, but to Allah belongs the plot entirely. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know for whom is the [best] end of the [future] abode.
interpretation: This verse highlights that previous nations have also devised plots against their prophets and messengers, but ultimately, all such plots are under God's control and knowledge. It reassures the Prophet Muhammad that God is aware of the actions of every individual and that the outcome of the hereafter will be in favor of the believers, not the disbelievers.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'You are not a messenger.' Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine testimony in verifying the truth of the Prophet's mission. The phrase 'ومن عنده علم الكتاب' (and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture) refers to those who possess knowledge of previous revelations, such as Jews and Christians who are familiar with the Torah and the Gospel. The verse is suggesting that these individuals can serve as witnesses to the Prophet Muhammad's message, as it is consistent with the monotheistic message and prophetic traditions described in their own scriptures. The verse is emphasizing that the truth of the Prophet's message is not solely dependent on the testimony of his contemporaries, but is also corroborated by the knowledge and scriptures of other faith communities.

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. [This is] a Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that you might bring mankind out of darknesses into the light by permission of their Lord to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse signifies the purpose of the revelation of the Qur'an, which is to guide humanity out of the state of ignorance, disbelief, and moral darkness into the light of knowledge, faith, and righteousness, under the guidance of the Almighty, the Most Exalted and Praiseworthy. It underscores the role of the Prophet Muhammad as a guide and the Qur'an as the means through which this guidance is achieved, emphasizing the sovereignty and praise-worthiness of Allah.

translation: Allah is He to whom belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth. And woe to the disbelievers because of a severe torment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all that exists in the heavens and the earth, serving as a warning to those who reject faith, indicating that they will face severe punishment.

translation: Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter, and turn away from the path of God and seek to make it crooked. Those are in a far-reaching error.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting a group of people who prioritize worldly life over the hereafter, and in doing so, they not only stray from the right path themselves but also actively try to mislead others. Their actions are driven by a desire to distort the truth and lead people astray from the path of God. The verse concludes by stating that such individuals are lost in a profound and far-reaching error, indicating the severity of their deviation from the right path.

translation: And We did not send any messenger except [speaking] in the language of his people to state clearly for them, and Allah sends astray [thereby] whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the guidance or misguidance of individuals is ultimately determined by God's will. Despite the clear communication of God's message through prophets who speak the language of their people, some are led astray while others are guided. This underscores the sovereignty and wisdom of God, who has the power to guide or misguide according to His divine plan, emphasizing His omnipotence and wise judgment in all matters.

translation: And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs to [the people of] Pharaoh and his establishment, [saying], "Bring out your people from darknesses into the light and remind them of the days of Allah. Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of prophets as guides who lead people out of darkness (ignorance, oppression, and sin) into light (knowledge, justice, and righteousness). The reference to 'the days of Allah' signifies historical events or divine interventions that serve as lessons for those who are patient and grateful. The verse suggests that reflecting on these events can provide valuable signs or lessons for individuals who possess the qualities of patience (in the face of adversity) and gratitude (for blessings), implying that these qualities are essential for deriving moral and spiritual benefit from the experiences and revelations sent by Allah.

translation: And when Moses said to his people, 'Remember the favor of Allah upon you when He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with the worst torment and were slaughtering your sons and sparing your women. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of remembering and being grateful for God's blessings. The Israelites are reminded of their deliverance from the oppression and brutality of the Pharaoh's people, who were subjecting them to extreme hardship, including the killing of their sons and the sparing of their daughters for servitude. The verse suggests that this deliverance was a significant test from God, underscoring the magnitude of His favor upon them. It implies that the true test of faith lies not just in the adversity faced but also in the recognition and appreciation of the divine mercy that brings relief from such hardships.

translation: And [mention] when your Lord proclaimed, 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the reciprocal relationship between human gratitude and divine bounty. It suggests that when humans acknowledge and appreciate God's blessings (shukr), God responds by increasing those blessings (izdiad). Conversely, if humans reject or deny God's blessings (kufr), they risk facing severe punishment ('adhāb). The verse implies that human actions have consequences and that a conscious choice between gratitude and ingratitude determines one's fate. It encourages believers to cultivate a spirit of gratitude, not just as a moral virtue, but as a means to continue receiving divine favors.

translation: And Moses said, "If you should disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely - indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy."
interpretation: This verse highlights the independence and praise-worthiness of God, emphasizing that His existence and sustenance are not contingent upon human belief or disbelief. It underscores the idea that God's richness is not just material or financial but also encompasses His self-sufficiency in all aspects, including the acknowledgment and worship of His creation. The verse serves as a reminder to the Children of Israel, and by extension to all humanity, that their faith or lack thereof does not affect God's inherent nature or His worthiness of praise.

translation: Has there not come to you the news of those before you, the people of Noah, 'Aad and Thamud, and those after them? None knows them but Allah. Their messengers came to them with clear signs, but they turned their hands back into their mouths and said, 'Indeed we have disbelieved in that with which you have been sent, and indeed we are in doubtful, wavering disbelief about that to which you are calling us.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the people being addressed, drawing a parallel with the fate of previous nations who rejected their prophets. It highlights the obstinacy and disbelief of these nations, emphasizing their rejection of clear signs and their skepticism towards the message brought by the prophets. The verse underscores the universal pattern of prophetic rejection and the consequences that follow, cautioning the audience about the dangers of similar disbelief and skepticism.

translation: Their messengers said, "Is there doubt about Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth? He invites you to forgive you your sins, and to respite you till an appointed term." They said, "You are no more than mortals like us. You wish to divert us from what our fathers used to worship; bring us, therefore, a clear authority."
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern of resistance to the message of the Prophets throughout history. The Prophets, guided by God, call people to monotheism and righteousness, promising forgiveness and a respite until a predetermined term. However, their message is often met with skepticism and dismissal by those who adhere to the traditions of their forefathers. The demand for 'clear authority' (سلطان مبين) signifies a deeper issue - a reluctance to submit to the truth when it challenges established norms and practices, underscoring the tension between faith and inherited cultural or religious traditions.

translation: Their messengers said to them, 'We are not but human beings like you, but Allah bestows His grace upon whom He wills of His servants. It is not for us to bring you an authority except by permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the nature of prophethood and the relationship between the messengers and God. The messengers emphasize that they are human beings like their audience, but they have been chosen by God to convey His message. The verse underscores the idea that the ability to perform miracles or bring authoritative proof is not within the messengers' control but is dependent on God's permission. It concludes by emphasizing that true believers should place their trust in God, indicating that faith involves reliance on God's power and wisdom rather than on human capabilities or tangible evidence alone.

translation: And why should we not rely upon Allah while He has guided us to our ways? And we will surely be patient about what you harm us. And upon Allah let the reliant rely.
interpretation: This verse highlights the believers' conviction in their faith and their reliance on Allah's guidance and support. Despite facing harm and adversity from others, they remain steadfast and patient, trusting that Allah will ultimately vindicate them. The verse emphasizes the importance of putting one's trust in Allah, as He is the ultimate source of guidance and protection.

translation: And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, "We will surely drive you out of our land, or you shall return to our religion." So their Lord inspired to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers"
interpretation: This verse highlights God's unwavering stance against injustice and oppression. When the disbelievers threatened the prophets, either to be expelled from their land or to revert to their (disbelievers') way of life, God revealed to the prophets that He would destroy the wrongdoers, underscoring His support for the righteous and His condemnation of those who transgress His laws and persecute His messengers.

translation: And We will certainly settle you in the land after them. That is for he who fears My position and fears My threat.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the reward of settling in the land is specifically for those who are conscious of standing before Allah (خاف مقامي) and fear His warning or punishment (خاف وعيد), implying that it is not just a matter of physical conquest or dominance, but is deeply tied to the spiritual state and moral accountability of the individuals involved.

translation: And they sought a decisive judgment, and every stubborn tyrant failed.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate failure and humiliation of those who are arrogant and stubbornly refuse to submit to the truth. The phrase 'واستفتحوا' (wastaf-tahū) implies seeking a decisive judgment or victory from Allah, often in the context of the prophets or believers asking Allah to judge between them and their disbelieving opponents. 'وخاب كل جبار عنيد' (wa khāba kullu jabbarin 'anīd) indicates that every tyrant or oppressor who is stubbornly defiant will be disappointed or fail in their endeavors. It underscores the Quranic theme that divine support is with those who are righteous and patient, and that the arrogant and rebellious will ultimately face defeat and disgrace.

translation: Behind him is Hell, and he will be given to drink of festering pus.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the dire consequences for those who are destined for Hell. The phrase 'من ورائه جهنم' (behind him is Hell) metaphorically indicates that Hell is awaiting them, and they are inevitably heading towards it. The phrase 'ويسقى من ماء صديد' (and he is given to drink of festering pus) signifies the unbearable suffering they will endure, as they are forced to drink pus, emphasizing the torment and agony that awaits those who are condemned to Hell.

translation: He gulps it down with difficulty and can hardly swallow it. And death comes to him from every direction, but he is not to die. And besides that is a severe torment.
interpretation: This verse is describing the torment and suffering of the people of Hell. The phrase 'يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه' (he swallows it with difficulty and can hardly gulp it down) indicates the intense pain and distress caused by the punishment. The phrase 'ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان' (and death comes to him from every direction) signifies that the suffering is all-encompassing and inescapable. However, 'وما هو بميت' (yet he does not die) suggests that despite the extreme torment, the individual remains alive to continue suffering. The final phrase 'ومن ورائه عذاب غليظ' (and beyond that is a severe punishment) implies that there is an even more intense and harsh punishment awaiting him, underscoring the severity and perpetuity of the suffering in the afterlife for those who are condemned to Hell.

translation: The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes blown furiously by the wind on a stormy day; they are unable to gain anything from what they have earned. That is extreme misguidance.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the futility of the deeds of those who reject their Lord, comparing their actions to ashes that are blown away by a strong wind on a stormy day, leaving nothing behind. The interpretation is that just as the ashes are powerless against the force of the wind and are scattered, the deeds of those who disbelieve are similarly powerless and without consequence or benefit in the sight of God, illustrating the concept of spiritual futility and the misguidedness of those who reject faith.

translation: Do you not see that God created the heavens and the earth [in] truth? If He wills, He can do away with you and bring [in] a new creation.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omnipotence and sovereignty over creation. It underscores that God's creation is purposeful and just ('بالحق'), and that He has the power to replace existing creation with a new one if He so desires, serving as a reminder of human beings' dependence on God and their vulnerability to His will.

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah
interpretation: This verse signifies that accomplishing something, no matter how grand or difficult it may seem to humans, is not a challenge or a hardship for Allah. It underscores Allah's omnipotence and limitless capability, suggesting that what may appear impossible or daunting to human beings is, in fact, effortless for Allah.

translation: And they all shall appear before God, then the weak will say unto those who were arrogant, 'We were your followers, can you avail us anything against the chastisement of God?' They will say, 'Had God guided us, we would have guided you. It is the same to us whether we are impatient or patient; there is no place for us to flee'.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of relying on others for salvation on the Day of Judgment. The weak, who followed the arrogant in worldly life, turn to them for help, but the arrogant leaders deny any responsibility, attributing their own misguidance and that of their followers to God's will, emphasizing that neither their despair nor their patience can change their inevitable fate, as they have no escape from God's judgment.

translation: And Satan will say when the matter has been concluded, "Indeed, Allah had promised you a promise of truth. And I promised you, then I betrayed you. But I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; but blame yourselves. I cannot be your rescuer, nor can you be my rescuers. Indeed, I reject your associating me with Allah before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability of individuals for their actions on the Day of Judgment. Satan admits that he had no real authority over humans, but rather tempted them, and they willingly responded to his call. The verse emphasizes personal responsibility, indicating that individuals should not blame external temptations or forces, like Satan, for their wrongdoings, but rather acknowledge their own role in making choices. It underscores the idea that true culpability lies within oneself for succumbing to temptation, and that the consequences of one's actions are a result of one's own decisions.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally by permission of their Lord. Their greeting therein will be, "Peace."
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for believers who lead a righteous life. The greeting of 'peace' or 'salam' in Paradise signifies a state of complete serenity and harmony, free from any discord or negativity, underscoring the perfection of the afterlife for the righteous.

translation: Do you not see how Allah sets forth a parable? A goodly word is as a goodly tree, whose root is firmly fixed, and its branches (reach) to the heavens.
interpretation: This verse is an analogy that illustrates the characteristics of a righteous or good word or deed. Just as a good tree has firm roots and branches that reach towards the heavens, a good deed or word is one that is grounded in truth and righteousness and has a profound and far-reaching impact, touching the hearts and lives of people and elevating them spiritually.

translation: It gives its produce every season by the permission of its Lord. God strikes the parables for people so that they may be reminded.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consistent and reliable nature of a true servant of God, much like a good tree that yields its fruit at all times with the permission of its Lord. The verse suggests that just as the tree's productivity is a manifestation of God's will, the righteous individual's actions and achievements are also a result of divine permission and guidance. The purpose of God presenting such analogies is to encourage people to reflect on their own lives and turn towards righteousness.

translation: And the parable of a bad word is as a bad tree uprooted from the earth, having no stability.
interpretation: This verse is likening a disbelieving statement or ideology to a bad tree that has been uprooted from the earth, signifying that it lacks stability or foundation. The interpretation is that just as the tree is unstable and cannot sustain itself, a false or evil ideology or statement is also inherently unstable and will not endure, lacking the roots of truth or righteousness that could give it lasting presence or impact.

translation: Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. And Allah sends astray the wrongdoers. And Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's role in guiding believers and misguiding the unjust. The phrase 'firm word' refers to the declaration of faith, which God stabilizes in the hearts of believers both in this life and the next, enabling them to remain steadfast. Conversely, God allows the unjust to stray, illustrating His sovereignty over guidance and misguidance. The verse underscores the concept that God's actions are based on His will, and His decisions regarding who is guided or misguided are in accordance with justice and wisdom.

translation: Have you not seen those who have changed the favour of Allah into disbelief and caused their people to descend into the Abode of Ruin
interpretation: This verse is a critique of those who reject the blessings and favors they receive from Allah, and instead lead their people down a path of destruction. It highlights the consequences of ingratitude and disobedience, where individuals not only reject divine favors but also mislead others into a state of perdition, underscoring the severe repercussions of such actions both for the individuals and their communities.

translation: They will burn in Hell, and what a wretched abode.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who reject faith and engage in sinful behavior will face severe punishment in Hell, emphasizing the gravity of their actions and the dire consequences that await them in the afterlife.

translation: And they set up rivals to Allah that they may mislead (men) from His Path! Say: 'Enjoy (your brief power)! But verily ye are bound for the Fire!'
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who associate partners with Allah, indicating that their actions are a deliberate attempt to mislead others from the path of righteousness. The verse suggests that such individuals are not only misguided themselves but are also actively working to lead others astray. The phrase 'تمتعوا' (enjoy yourselves) is used to convey a sense of temporary reprieve, implying that their actions will have consequences in the hereafter. The ultimate destination of those who engage in such behavior is the fire of Hell, emphasizing the severe repercussions of their actions in the afterlife.

translation: Tell My servants who have believed to establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and openly, before a Day comes in which there will be no exchange, nor any friendships.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of performing righteous deeds, specifically establishing prayer and giving charity, before the Day of Judgment arrives, when such deeds will no longer be accepted or beneficial. The verse highlights that true faith is demonstrated not just by belief, but by actions that reflect devotion to God, such as prayer and charity given both privately and publicly. It underscores the urgency of engaging in these acts before the inevitable day when opportunities for redemption or salvation through good deeds will be lost, and when material wealth or social connections will offer no protection or intercession.

translation: It is God who has created the heavens and the earth and sends down water from the sky, and with it brings forth produce as provision for you, and has subjected to you the ships to sail through the sea by His command, and has subjected to you the rivers.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omnipotence and benevolence towards humanity. It showcases His ability to create the universe and control the natural phenomena, such as the cycle of water and the movement of ships, to provide for human sustenance and facilitate their lives. The verse emphasizes the idea that everything in the universe is subservient to God's will and is utilized for the benefit of humanity, underscoring the notion of Tawhid (the oneness of God) and encouraging humans to acknowledge and appreciate God's favors and blessings.

translation: And He has subjected to you the sun and the moon, both diligently pursuing their courses, and He has subjected to you the night and the day.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's immense power and benevolence by subjecting the celestial bodies and the cycle of day and night to humanity's benefit, emphasizing their consistent and predictable operation as a manifestation of divine control and providence.

translation: And He gave you from all that you asked Him. And if you count the blessings of Allah, you will not be able to enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is very unjust, very ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless nature of Allah's blessings upon humanity. It underscores the idea that humans are incapable of counting or fully appreciating the numerous favors they receive from Allah. The verse then transitions to caution about human nature, pointing out that despite these countless blessings, humans tend to be unjust and ungrateful, often forgetting or denying the source of these blessings. It serves as a reminder of the importance of gratitude and recognition of divine favors.

translation: And [mention, O Prophet], when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this city [Makkah] secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincere devotion to God, untainted by the influences of idolatry. Prophet Ibrahim's prayer demonstrates his awareness of the potential for idolatrous practices to infiltrate his life and that of his progeny, and his desire to be kept away from such practices. By praying to be protected from idolatry, Ibrahim is, in effect, seeking to maintain the purity of his faith and ensure that his descendants remain committed to the worship of one God alone. This verse serves as a reminder of the need for constant vigilance against the influences that can lead one astray from the path of true devotion to God.

translation: Lord, they have led many people astray. Whoever follows me is truly of me, and whoever disobeys me, then indeed You are [still] Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dichotomy between following the righteous path and succumbing to misguidance. It suggests that those who follow the speaker (understood to be a prophet or a righteous individual) are considered to be part of their community or on the right path, while those who disobey are still eligible for divine mercy and forgiveness, emphasizing God's attributes of being forgiving and merciful.

translation: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a valley without cultivation, by Your sacred House; our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people yearn towards them and provide for them from the fruits that they might be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of establishing a spiritual and economic hub that attracts people to a sacred place, in this case, the Kaaba. By invoking God's provision of sustenance and making people's hearts inclined towards the settlement, Ibrahim is essentially praying for the establishment of a thriving community centered around the sacred house, where people can come together to perform their religious duties and be grateful for God's blessings.

translation: Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare, and nothing is hidden from God of anything in the earth or in the heaven.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's all-encompassing knowledge, emphasizing that nothing is hidden from Him, whether it is kept secret or openly declared, in the heavens or on earth. It underscores the omniscient nature of God, suggesting that human actions and intentions are fully transparent to Him, and thus, it serves as a reminder of accountability before God.

translation: Praise be to Allah, Who has granted unto me in old age Ishmael and Isaac! for, behold, my Sustainer is indeed responsive to prayer.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of prayer and the responsiveness of Allah to the supplications of His servants. The fact that Prophet Abraham was granted children in his old age is seen as a manifestation of Allah's ability to respond to prayers, emphasizing the idea that with Allah, nothing is impossible, and that He is capable of granting blessings at any time, regardless of the circumstances.

translation: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of establishing a consistent and devoted prayer practice, not just for oneself, but also for one's progeny, and demonstrates the believer's reliance on Allah's acceptance and mercy in their supplications.

translation: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers the Day the account is established.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to Allah, asking for forgiveness for the speaker, their parents, and all believers on the Day of Reckoning. It highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and the interconnectedness of the community of believers, as the speaker's plea for mercy encompasses not just themselves, but also their parents and the broader community of the faithful. It underscores the Islamic values of compassion, familial piety, and communal solidarity, particularly in the context of the accountability that comes on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And do not think that Allah is heedless of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them for a Day when the eyes will stare in horror.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the wrongdoers, assuring them that their actions are not going unnoticed by Allah. The delay in their punishment is not a sign of divine negligence but rather a deferment until the Day of Judgment, a day so overwhelming and terrifying that it will leave people aghast, with their eyes wide open in horror and disbelief.

translation: Rushing forward, their heads raised up [in shame], their gaze does not return to them, and their hearts are void.
interpretation: This verse is describing the state of the people in Hellfire. The phrase 'مقنعي رءوسهم' indicates that they will be hanging their heads in shame and humiliation. 'لا يرتد إليهم طرفهم' suggests that their eyes will be fixed in a stare, unable to blink or look away from the horrors surrounding them, indicating a state of extreme terror and despair. 'وأفئدتهم هواء' implies that their hearts will be empty, devoid of any substance or vitality, symbolizing the complete loss of emotional and spiritual resilience due to the overwhelming fear and suffering they are experiencing.

translation: And warn people of the Day when the punishment will come to them, then those who did wrong will say, 'Our Lord, delay us for a short term, we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.' 'Did you not previously swear that you would suffer no decline?'
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to humanity about the inevitability of accountability on the Day of Judgment. It highlights the regret and plea for a second chance that will be expressed by those who have wronged themselves and others through their actions. The verse underscores the irony that these wrongdoers had previously sworn to the permanence of their worldly standings, indicating a profound denial of the afterlife and the consequences of their deeds. The essence of this verse is to emphasize the themes of accountability, the fleeting nature of worldly life, and the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth to you parables.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the people of Makkah, reminding them of the fate of previous nations who were destroyed due to their own injustices and wrongdoing. By dwelling in places where those nations once lived, the Makkans had the opportunity to witness the remnants of their civilizations and learn from their mistakes. The verse emphasizes the importance of reflecting on the consequences of one's actions and drawing lessons from history to avoid a similar downfall.

translation: And they have already contrived their plan, but with Allah is [recorded] their plan, even if their plan had been [sufficient] to cause the mountains to disappear.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of human plotting against the divine plan. It suggests that no matter how intricate or powerful human schemes may seem, they are ultimately known and countered by God. The imagery of mountains being moved by the sheer force of their plotting underscores the enormity of their efforts, yet it is implied that even such monumental schemes are not beyond God's control or knowledge.

translation: So do not think that God will fail in His promise to His messengers. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might, the Lord of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who might think that God will not fulfill His promise to His messengers. It asserts God's power and ability to exact revenge on those who reject His message and oppose His messengers, emphasizing that God is not only all-powerful (عزيز) but also capable of retribution (ذو انتقام) against those who defy Him. It underscores the certainty of God's promise and the inevitability of His justice.

translation: The Day the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well], and they [all creatures] will emerge before God, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse signifies a profound transformation that will occur on the Day of Judgment, where the current earth and heavens will be replaced or transformed into a new state, emphasizing the omnipotence and uniqueness of God as the sole authority over this transformation and the reckoning that follows.

translation: And you will see the criminals that Day, linked together in chains.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of the punishment for those who have committed crimes and rejected the truth. The image of being 'linked together in chains' signifies the loss of freedom and the humiliation that comes with being held accountable for one's actions on the Day of Judgment. It serves as a warning to individuals to be mindful of their deeds in this life, as they will be held accountable in the hereafter.

translation: Their garments will be of liquid pitch, and their faces will be covered by the Fire
interpretation: This verse signifies the punishment of the people of Hell, where their garments are made of tar or pitch, a substance that is highly flammable and thus intensifies their suffering. The phrase 'their faces will be covered by the Fire' suggests a comprehensive and intense punishment, where the fire engulfs them completely, symbolizing the all-encompassing nature of their suffering in the afterlife.

translation: That Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability and swiftness of divine justice. It signifies that God will reward or punish every individual according to their deeds, and this reckoning will be carried out with great speed, underscoring the omniscience and omnipotence of God. The verse serves as a reminder of the accountability of human actions in the hereafter.

translation: This is a message for mankind, that they may be warned thereby and that they may know that He is One God, and that those gifted with understanding may take heed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purpose of the revelation: to serve as a warning to people, to affirm the oneness of God, and to remind those endowed with understanding, emphasizing the importance of recognizing and reflecting on the unity of God.

translation: Alif Lam Ra. These are the verses of the Book and of a clear Recitation.
interpretation: This verse signifies the commencement of a profound revelation, where 'Al-Kitab' (the Book) and 'Qur'an' (the Recitation) are presented as sources of clear guidance and enlightenment. The use of 'مبين' (Mubin), meaning clear or manifest, underscores the lucid nature of the Qur'an's message, implying that its verses are not only a source of spiritual guidance but are also unambiguous in their conveyance of divine truth.

translation: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they had been Muslims.
interpretation: This verse highlights the regrets of those who rejected faith when they witness the consequences of their actions in the hereafter. It suggests that at that point, they will wish they had been among the submitters to God's will, indicating a deep realization of their past mistakes and the path not taken.

translation: Leave them to eat and enjoy, and let them be beguiled by hope. For they will come to know.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to the disbelievers, indicating that He will allow them to continue in their worldly pursuits and enjoy their lives for a time, distracted by their hopes and desires, but ultimately they will come to know the consequences of their actions, facing the reality of their wrongdoings and the punishment that awaits them.

translation: And never would We destroy a township but [We do] so while its term is known.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the destruction of a civilization or community is not arbitrary, but rather it is predetermined by Allah based on a known decree or appointed term, suggesting a divine plan or justice that governs the rise and fall of societies.

translation: No nation can outstrip its term, nor can they put it back.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine decree that governs the rise and fall of nations, emphasizing that their destinies are predetermined by Allah. It underscores the idea that the lifespan of a nation is fixed and cannot be altered by human intervention, serving as a reminder of the inevitability of Allah's will and the futility of attempting to hasten or delay the course of events ordained by Him.

translation: And they say, "O you upon whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad."
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) upon receiving the revelation. They accused him of being possessed or mad, likely due to their unfamiliarity with the concept of divine revelation and their skepticism towards his prophetic claims. This response underscores the challenge faced by the Prophet in conveying the message of Islam to a society that was deeply entrenched in its pre-Islamic beliefs and practices.

translation: If you are truthful, why do you not bring us the angels?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and obstinacy of those who reject faith, as they demand tangible proof in the form of angels to validate the truth-claims of the Prophet, despite the clear and convincing message he brings. It underscores the psychological barrier that prevents them from accepting the truth, as they condition their belief on a manifestation that is beyond human experience and not within the realm of their everyday reality.

translation: We do not send down the angels except with truth, and they would not then be given respite.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the descent of angels is not a random or frivolous event, but rather it occurs with a specific purpose and truth, often associated with significant events such as the Day of Judgment or the delivery of divine messages. The latter part of the verse emphasizes that when the angels do descend, those who are being addressed or judged are not given any respite or delay, indicating the finality and seriousness of the occasion.

translation: Indeed, it is We who have sent down the Reminder (the Qur'an), and indeed, We will be its guardian.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah has taken upon Himself the responsibility of preserving the Qur'an, ensuring its protection from any alteration, distortion, or loss, thereby guaranteeing its authenticity and integrity for all time.

translation: And We have certainly sent [messengers] before you, [O Muhammad], among the sects of the former [nations].
interpretation: This verse signifies that before the Prophet Muhammad, messengers were sent to various groups or communities among the previous nations, indicating a continuity in God's practice of guiding different peoples through His messengers across different eras.

translation: And never did there come to them a messenger but that they mocked at him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern of the people rejecting and mocking the messengers sent by Allah, indicating their stubbornness and refusal to accept the truth, and serving as a warning to those who would follow in their footsteps.

translation: Thus do We cause it to enter the hearts of the criminals
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah allows or causes the path of disobedience or transgression to become ingrained or firmly established in the hearts of those who are guilty of major sins or crimes, implying a form of divine retribution where their persistent wrongdoing leads to a hardening of their hearts against guidance and righteousness.

translation: They do not believe in it, although the precedent of the former peoples has already passed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern of human behavior where people tend to reject the truth when it is presented to them, despite the historical evidence of the consequences faced by those who rejected the truth in the past. It underscores the idea that the disbelievers of today are following in the footsteps of those who came before them, ignoring the lessons that history should have taught them.

translation: And if We opened unto them a gate of heaven and they were to continue ascending through it
interpretation: This verse signifies the stubbornness and obstinacy of those who reject faith. Even if they were given a miraculous and undeniable sign, such as being able to ascend into heaven through a gate opened for them, they would still not believe, attributing their experience to being under some sort of magical or bewildering influence rather than accepting the truth.

translation: They would have said, 'Our eyes have been dazzled, rather we are a people bewitched.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the truth, suggesting that when faced with clear signs or miracles, they attribute their inability to see or understand the truth to being bewitched or enchanted, rather than acknowledging the reality of the signs they are witnessing.

translation: And indeed, We have made constellations in the sky and have beautified it for the observers.
interpretation: This verse signifies God's immense power and wisdom in creating the universe, as indicated by the 'buruj' or constellations in the sky, which are not just aesthetically pleasing to those who look at them, but also serve as a sign of divine providence and order in the cosmos.

translation: And We have guarded it (the heaven) from every cursed devil
interpretation: This verse signifies that the heavens or the celestial realm is protected from the influence of rebellious or cursed satans, implying that the divine revelation or the celestial messages are safeguarded against corruption or interference by malevolent entities.

translation: Except one who snatches [some words] by stealth, and he is pursued by a visible flame.
interpretation: This verse highlights the protection of the heavenly realm from eavesdropping by devils. It signifies that any devil attempting to listen in on the heavenly council is immediately chased away by a visible, blazing meteor, indicating the safeguarding of divine deliberations from satanic intrusion and emphasizing the boundary between the divine and the satanic realms.

translation: And the earth We have spread out, and cast therein firm mountains, and We have made to grow therein every thing in (due) proportion
interpretation: This verse highlights God's meticulous planning and control over the creation, emphasizing that everything in the earth is created in a balanced and harmonious proportion, reflecting the wisdom and order of the divine design.

translation: And We have provided therein means of livelihood for you and for those for whom you are not the providers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the all-encompassing nature of Allah's provision. It not only provides for the basic needs of human beings but also for other creatures, emphasizing the boundless generosity and care of Allah towards all of creation, not just humanity.

translation: And there is not a thing but that with Us are its stores, and We do not send it down except in a known measure.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's sovereignty and control over all things. It suggests that everything is stored with Him and is dispensed according to His wisdom and in a measured quantity, underscoring the idea that nothing happens without His knowledge and will, and that He is the ultimate source of all provision and blessing.

translation: And We send the winds fertilizing, then We send down from the sky water, and We give you to drink of it, and you are not its storers.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power and provision in the natural world. The winds are described as 'fertilizing' or 'لواقح' (luwaaqih), which not only refers to their role in pollination but also underscores the intricate web of life that God has created. The verse suggests that God's provision is not just a matter of creating the initial conditions for life, but also of sustaining it through ongoing processes like the water cycle. Furthermore, the phrase 'وما أنتم له بخازنين' (and you are not its storers) serves as a reminder of human limitations and dependence on God's provision, emphasizing that even the resources we manage are ultimately under God's control.

translation: And indeed, it is We Who give life and cause death, and it is We Who are the Inheritors.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's sovereignty over life and death, and His eternal legacy. It signifies that God is the one who gives life and causes death, and that He is the ultimate inheritor of all that exists, emphasizing His enduring and unchanging nature amidst the transience of creation.

translation: And We have certainly known those of you who have gone ahead and We have certainly known those who will come later
interpretation: This verse highlights God's all-encompassing knowledge, emphasizing that He is aware of the past, present, and future generations of humanity. It underscores the idea that God's knowledge is not limited by time or space, and that He has always been and will always be aware of all individuals, regardless of when they lived or will live.

translation: And indeed, your Lord will gather them; indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omnipotence and wisdom in gathering all individuals on the Day of Judgment, suggesting that He possesses the knowledge and wisdom to judge them justly based on their deeds.

translation: And indeed, We created man from sounding clay of altered black smooth mud.
interpretation: This verse highlights the humble origins of humanity, emphasizing that humans were created from a lowly material, a type of clay that has been altered and transformed. The use of the word 'sounding clay' and 'altered black smooth mud' suggests a process of transformation and molding, underscoring the idea that human existence is a result of divine craftsmanship and intentional creation, rather than a random or autonomous occurrence.

translation: And the jinn We had created before from the fire of a very hot blaze.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinct origin of the jinn, created from a potent and intense fire, signifying their unique nature and characteristics that differentiate them from humans, who were created from clay. The use of "نار السموم" (fire of intense heat) underscores the jinn's fiery essence, potentially alluding to their inherent qualities such as being volatile or having a strong presence.

translation: And [mention] when your Lord said to the angels, 'I will create a human being out of clay from an altered black mud.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the beginning of humanity's creation, highlighting the humble origin of man from clay, emphasizing the power and creative ability of God, as well as the lowly beginnings from which humans were created, setting the stage for understanding human nature and our relationship with God.

translation: And when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse signifies the honor bestowed upon humanity by Allah, as He breathes His spirit into Adam, indicating a special connection between the divine and human beings. The command for the angels to prostrate before Adam underscores the elevated status of humanity in the eyes of Allah and the angels, highlighting a theme of human dignity and the reverence due to the human form as a vessel for the divine spirit.

translation: So the angels prostrated themselves, all of them together.
interpretation: This verse highlights the obedience and unity of the angels in response to God's command, demonstrating their unwavering commitment to His will. The phrase 'كلهم أجمعون' (all of them together) emphasizes the totality and unanimity of their prostration, underscoring the angels' role as faithful and obedient servants of God.

translation: Except Iblis, he refused to be among those who prostrated.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of obedience and disobedience to God's command. Iblis's refusal to prostrate before Adam signifies his arrogance and pride, as he considers himself superior to Adam, who was created from clay, while Iblis was created from fire. This act of defiance sets the stage for the subsequent narrative in the Qur'an, where Iblis becomes the embodiment of evil, tempting humans to stray from the right path. The verse serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of pride and the importance of humility in the face of divine commands.

translation: He (Allah) said: 'O Iblees (Satan)! What is your reason for not being among the prostrators?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability of those who have been given the capacity for choice and free will. Iblees, having been commanded to prostrate alongside the angels, refused, and is subsequently questioned by Allah about his disobedience. This serves as a warning to those who might follow in Iblees' footsteps, emphasizing that choices have consequences and that disobedience to divine commands will be met with inquiry and judgment.

translation: He said: 'I am not one to prostrate to a human being whom You have created from sounding clay of altered black smooth mud.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of pride and disobedience, as Iblis (Satan) refuses to prostrate to Adam, citing his own superiority in creation, thereby illustrating the dangers of arrogance and the importance of humility before God's creation and command.

translation: He said: 'Then get out of it, for verily, you are outcast'
interpretation: This verse signifies the expulsion of Iblis (Satan) from the heavens due to his disobedience to Allah's command to prostrate before Adam. The term 'رجيم' (rajim) means being stoned or cursed, indicating that Iblis is not only expelled but also condemned and ostracized, setting the stage for the eternal conflict between good and evil.

translation: And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Judgment
interpretation: This verse signifies a severe and eternal condemnation upon an individual or group, indicating that they are subject to divine displeasure and curse until the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the gravity of their actions or beliefs that have incurred such a fate.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected'
interpretation: This verse is a part of the conversation between Iblis (Satan) and Allah. Iblis, after being condemned for his disobedience, requests a respite until the Day of Judgment, indicating his intention to continue misleading humans until that day. The interpretation of this verse highlights the cunning and the persistence of Satan in his rebellion against Allah's command, and his determination to lead humans astray until the Day of Resurrection.

translation: He said, 'Then indeed, you are of those reprieved.'
interpretation: This verse signifies a reprieve or a postponement of punishment. It implies that the individual being addressed is granted a temporary reprieve or respite, often used in the context of those who have been warned but are given time before facing the consequences of their actions.

translation: Until the day of the known time
interpretation: This verse refers to a specific time appointed by Allah, known only to Him, when a particular event or reckoning will take place. It signifies a day of reckoning or judgment that is predetermined and inevitable, emphasizing the certainty and inevitability of Allah's plan and timing.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, because You have put me in error, I will surely make (disobedience) attractive to them on earth, and I will mislead them all'
interpretation: This verse highlights the cunning and rebellious nature of Iblis (Satan) as he vows to mislead humanity. By stating that he will beautify evil deeds to mankind and lead them astray, it illustrates the tactics Satan employs to deceive people, making wrongdoing appealing and tempting. It serves as a warning to believers to be cautious of Satan's whispers and to remain steadfast on the right path.

translation: Except Your chosen servants among them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that even among those who are generally considered to be misguided or disobedient, there are individuals who are sincerely devoted to God and have purified their faith and actions. It suggests that God's mercy and salvation are not limited to a particular group or community, but are available to those who genuinely seek to follow His guidance and live a righteous life, regardless of their background or circumstances.

translation: He said, 'This is a straight path unto Me.'
interpretation: The given verse is not from the Qur'an. The correct verse is likely 'قال هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ' (Surah Al-Hijr, 15:41). The interpretation of this verse is that Satan, after being cast out of heaven, vows to mislead humanity, and this phrase is part of his statement where he affirms that he will lie in wait for them on the straight path (the path of righteousness), indicating his intent to tempt and misguide those who follow the right path.

translation: Indeed, My servants - no authority will you have over them, except those who follow you of the deviators.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Satan has no authority or power over the righteous servants of Allah. The only individuals who fall under his influence are those who willingly follow him and are misguided, indicating that one's susceptibility to Satan's influence is a result of their own choices and inclinations rather than any inherent power Satan has over the righteous.

translation: And indeed, Hell is their promised meeting place, all together.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Hellfire is an inevitable destination for those who have rejected faith and persisted in their disbelief and evil deeds, serving as a stern warning about the consequences of one's actions in the hereafter.

translation: It has seven gates; for every gate is a (special) class (of sinners) assigned.
