interpretation: This verse highlights God's comprehensive provision for humanity's well-being and safety. The creation of shadows, mountains as shelters, and clothing that protects from both the heat and harm (through armor or protective garments) are all seen as aspects of God's grace. The completion of His favor upon humanity is aimed at guiding them towards submission to His will, indicating that the appreciation of these blessings should lead to a deeper commitment to faith and righteousness.

translation: But if they turn away, your duty is only to convey the clear message.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet's role as a messenger, indicating that his responsibility is to clearly convey the message of Allah, and if the people turn away, it is not his duty to guide them or be responsible for their actions; his duty is fulfilled by delivering the clear message.

translation: They recognize Allah's favor, then they deny it, and most of them are the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contradiction in human behavior where people acknowledge the blessings they receive from God but subsequently deny or refuse to recognize them, often due to ingratitude or arrogance, and it notes that the majority of people fall into the category of being ungrateful or disbelieving.

translation: And [mention] the Day when We will resurrect among every nation a witness. Then it will not be permitted to the disbelievers [to apologize or make excuses], nor will they be allowed to make amends.
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability and justice on the Day of Judgment, where representatives from each community will testify, and those who rejected the truth will face unrelenting judgment without an opportunity to apologize or make amends, underscoring the finality and severity of divine reckoning.

translation: And when those who have wronged see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irreversible nature of the punishment for those who have committed wrongdoing. Once they behold the punishment, it is too late for them to be given respite or for their punishment to be alleviated. The punishment is a consequence of their actions, and they are not given a second chance. This emphasizes the importance of accountability for one's deeds and the inevitability of justice.

translation: And when those who associated others with Allah saw their associates, they said, "Our Lord, these are our associates whom we used to invoke besides You." But they will throw at them the saying, "Indeed, you are liars."
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony and futility of polytheistic beliefs. On the Day of Judgment, when the polytheists see their so-called 'partners' or deities, they will acknowledge them, but this acknowledgment will be met with a rebuke from their deities, exposing the polytheists' false claims and lies about their supposed divine partners. The deities will essentially tell the polytheists that they are liars for having attributed divinity or partnership with God to them.

translation: And they will offer submission to God on that Day, and lost from them will be what they used to fabricate.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of false deities and fabricated beliefs when faced with the reality of the Day of Judgment. On that day, those who had attributed partners to God or fabricated lies against Him will be forced to submit to God's will, and their false constructs will be revealed to be nothing but illusions, having strayed far from the truth.

translation: Those who disbelieve and hinder [others] from the path of Allah - We will increase them in punishment over [their] punishment for the corruption they used to cause.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle that those who not only reject the truth but also actively work to prevent others from following the path of righteousness will face a compounded punishment. The additional punishment is a consequence of their efforts to cause corruption and mislead others, indicating that the severity of their punishment is directly related to the extent of their negative influence and actions.

translation: And [mention] the Day when We will resurrect among every nation a witness against them from among themselves. And We have brought you, [O Muhammad], as a witness against these [people]. And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation for every matter and as guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a witness over his followers on the Day of Judgment, just as a witness will be raised from among every other community to testify against them. The verse also underscores the comprehensive nature of the Qur'an, revealed to the Prophet, serving as an explanation for all matters, a guidance, a mercy, and a glad tiding for those who submit to God's will. It emphasizes the universal and all-encompassing guidance provided by the Qur'an, not just limited to legal or ritual matters but extending to all aspects of life, serving as a source of mercy and good news for believers.

translation: Indeed, Allah commands justice and good conduct and giving to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of God's commandments, which encompass not only justice and righteousness in actions (al-'adl and al-ihsan) but also the importance of maintaining familial ties. It prohibits not just outright evil (al-fahsha'), but also more subtle forms of wrongdoing (al-munkar) and transgression (al-baghy). The verse suggests that God's commandments are designed to guide humanity towards a balanced and virtuous life, and that by following these commandments, individuals can cultivate a deeper sense of moral awareness and responsibility.

translation: And fulfill the Covenant of Allah when you have covenanted, and do not break the oaths after making them firm, and you have made Allah a guarantor over you. Indeed, Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's commitments and oaths made in the name of God. It warns against breaking promises after they have been solemnly made, with God as a witness. The verse highlights God's omniscience, implying that one's actions, including the keeping or breaking of oaths, are known to Him. It serves as a moral directive to be truthful and reliable in one's covenants, using the awareness of God's knowledge as a motivator for integrity.

translation: And be not like her who unravels her yarn, breaking it into pieces, after she has spun it strongly. You take your oaths as a means of deceit between you, lest a people be more numerous than another people. Allah only tests you by this [deception]. And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that wherein you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse is cautioning against inconsistency and hypocrisy in one's actions and oaths. It uses the metaphor of a woman who spins her yarn strong and then unravels it, rendering her effort futile. Similarly, taking oaths as a means to deceive others and gain an advantage is futile and wrong. The verse is highlighting that such actions are tests from Allah to distinguish between those who are sincere and those who are not. On the Day of Judgment, Allah will clarify the truth regarding the matters that people disputed about, implying that the inconsistencies and deceptions will be exposed.

translation: And if Allah had willed, He could have made you [of] one religion, but He causes to stray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the complex relationship between divine will and human agency. On one hand, it suggests that God has the power to unify humanity under a single faith or path, implying a level of determinism. On the other hand, it indicates that God chooses to allow diversity in human beliefs and actions, guiding some while letting others stray. The verse concludes by emphasizing accountability, suggesting that individuals will be judged based on their actions, underscoring the importance of personal responsibility alongside the acknowledgment of divine sovereignty.

translation: And take not your oaths as means of deceit between you, lest a foot slip after its stability and you taste evil for having turned away from the path of Allah, and for you is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against using oaths as a means to deceive and manipulate others, leading to a downfall after initial stability. It cautions that such actions not only result in negative consequences for oneself, but also incur a severe punishment from Allah for obstructing others from His path.

translation: And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price. Indeed, what is with Allah is better for you, if you should know.
interpretation: This verse warns against compromising one's commitment to God or violating a pledge made in His name for a meager or temporary gain. It emphasizes that true and lasting benefit lies in being faithful to one's covenant with God, suggesting that worldly advantages are fleeting and insignificant in comparison to the spiritual rewards and divine approval that come from honoring one's obligations to Him.

translation: What is with you is exhaustible. And what is with Allah is remaining. And We will surely pay those who were patient their reward for the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the fleeting nature of worldly possessions and the enduring nature of what is with Allah. It serves as a reminder to believers that the rewards and blessings that come from Allah are not only lasting but also superior to anything the world can offer. The verse specifically mentions that those who demonstrate patience (sabr) in the face of challenges will be rewarded by Allah not just according to their deeds, but according to the best of their deeds, indicating a generosity and mercy that goes beyond mere justice.

translation: Whoever does good deeds, whether male or female, and is a believer, We will certainly give them a good life, and We will reward them with a recompense better than their deeds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle that a life of righteousness and faith is rewarded not only in the hereafter but also in this world. The 'good life' (hayatan tayyibah) refers to a life of contentment, peace, and spiritual fulfillment. It suggests that living a virtuous life according to one's faith leads to a positive quality of life, regardless of external circumstances. The verse emphasizes the dual reward for the righteous: a good life in this world and a recompense in the hereafter that exceeds their good deeds.

translation: So when you recite the Qur'an, [first] seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the expelled [from His mercy]
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of seeking refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan before engaging with the Quran. It highlights the need to purify one's intention and protect oneself from Satan's influence, which may lead one astray or cause distraction, thereby ensuring a sincere and receptive state for understanding and benefiting from the Quranic recitation.

translation: Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the devil or evil has no authority or power over those who have faith and put their trust in their Lord. It implies that true believers who rely on God are protected from the influence of evil forces, as their trust and faith serve as a shield against such influences.

translation: His authority is only over those who take him as a guardian and those who associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the influence or authority of Satan is limited to those who take him as their guardian or friend and those who associate others with Allah, implying that Satan's power is over those who willingly submit to his will and reject the oneness of God.

translation: And when We substitute one verse in place of another - and Allah is most knowing about what He sends down - they say, "You, [O Muhammad], are but a fabricator." But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and lack of understanding among those who reject the divine origin of the Qur'an. When a new verse or ruling is revealed in place of a previous one, they accuse the Prophet of fabricating it. However, this reaction stems from their ignorance, as they fail to comprehend the divine wisdom behind such changes, which are guided by God's superior knowledge of what is beneficial to be revealed at any given time.

translation: Say, "The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth to solidify those who believe, and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of the Holy Spirit (identified as the angel Gabriel) in revealing the Quran. The revelation is described as being sent down 'with the truth' from the Lord, indicating its authenticity and divine origin. The purpose of this revelation is twofold: firstly, to provide steadfastness and stability to those who have faith, reinforcing their belief and resolve; and secondly, to serve as guidance and a source of glad tidings for those who have surrendered to God's will (the Muslims). It underscores the Quran's function as a source of spiritual strength, guidance, and reassurance for believers.

translation: And indeed, We know that they say, "Only a human being teaches him." The tongue of him to whom they incline is foreign, while this is a tongue Arabic, clear.
interpretation: The verse is addressing the claim made by the disbelievers that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was being taught by a human being. The verse counters this claim by pointing out that the person they are referring to is a non-Arab (أعجمي), whereas the Qur'an is revealed in clear Arabic (لسان عربي مبين). The argument is that if the Prophet was indeed being taught by this non-Arab, it would be impossible for him to receive a revelation in eloquent and clear Arabic. This serves as evidence that the Qur'an is not of human origin but is a divine revelation.

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the verses of Allah - Allah will not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting the signs and revelations of God. It suggests that those who disbelieve in God's verses are deprived of divine guidance, and as a result, they will face a painful punishment. The underlying message is that faith in God's signs is a prerequisite for receiving guidance, and rejection of these signs leads to spiritual waywardness and ultimately to suffering.

translation: Only those who do not believe in the verses of Allah fabricate falsehood, and it is they who are the liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the fabrication of lies is a characteristic of those who lack faith in the signs of Allah, and it is they who are truly the liars. It underscores the connection between disbelief and dishonesty, suggesting that a lack of faith in divine signs is associated with a propensity to deceive and fabricate falsehoods.

translation: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief... except for one who is forced [to renounce his religion] while his heart is secure in faith. But those who [willingly] open their breasts to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and theirs is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between outward actions and inner convictions, emphasizing that true faith is a matter of the heart. It suggests that those who are coerced into disbelief but remain steadfast in their faith internally are not held accountable for their outward actions. In contrast, those who willingly and wholeheartedly embrace disbelief invite divine wrath and severe punishment, underscoring the gravity of rejecting faith with conviction.

translation: That is because they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter and that Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This is because they have preferred the fleeting life of this world over the eternal life of the hereafter, and Allah does not guide those who reject faith, implying that their preference for worldly life is a manifestation of their lack of faith and that this lack of faith is the reason for their misguidance.

translation: Those are the ones on whose hearts, hearing, and eyesight God has set a seal. It is they who are heedless.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the consequences of a person's persistent rejection of guidance and truth. It suggests that those who continually turn away from God's signs and messages will eventually find themselves in a state where their hearts, ears, and eyes are sealed off from the truth, rendering them unable to perceive or understand it. The verse implies that this is not a punishment inflicted by God, but rather a natural consequence of their own actions and choices. The term 'غافلون' (ghaflun) refers to those who are heedless or negligent, indicating that these individuals have become oblivious to the truth and are no longer aware of their own spiritual state.

translation: Undoubtedly, they in the Hereafter will be the losers.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who reject faith and engage in wrongdoing will ultimately face loss in the Hereafter, as their actions will not yield any positive outcome for them, and they will be subject to the consequences of their deeds.

translation: Then indeed your Lord, to those who emigrated after they had been forced [to renounce their religion] and thereafter fought [for the cause of Allah] and were patient, indeed your Lord, after that, is most forgiving and merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards those believers who, despite facing trials and persecution, persevered in their faith, migrated from their homes for the sake of Allah, and continued to strive in His cause with patience. It underscores the idea that the hardships and tests faced by the believers are not an end in themselves but are followed by Allah's mercy and forgiveness for those who remain steadfast.

translation: The Day when every soul will come disputing for itself, and every soul will be recompensed fully for what it did, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Day of Judgment where every individual will be held accountable for their actions, and will ardently argue in their own defense. It signifies that on that day, each soul will be recompensed fully for their deeds, be it good or bad, and there will be no injustice meted out to anyone, as the recompense will be commensurate with their actions.

translation: And God puts forward as an example a township (that was) safe and secure, enjoying its livelihood in abundance from every place: then it became ungrateful to the favors of God; so God made it taste the garb of hunger and fear because of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to communities that become complacent and ungrateful for the blessings they receive. It highlights the consequences of ingratitude and disobedience towards God's favors, illustrating that when a community fails to appreciate and acknowledge the blessings it has been given, it risks facing hardship and punishment. The 'clothing of hunger and fear' is a metaphor for the comprehensive nature of the punishment, affecting both the physical and emotional well-being of the people. The verse underscores the principle that divine blessings are conditional upon the recipients' gratitude and righteous behavior.

translation: And there certainly came to them a Messenger from among them, but they denied him; so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tragic fate of communities that reject their own messengers, emphasizing that divine punishment is a consequence of willful wrongdoing and rejection of truth, rather than a result of ignorance or misguidance by external forces.

translation: So eat of that which Allah hath provided for you, lawful and good; and be grateful for the bounty of Allah, if it is Him ye worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of being mindful of the sustenance provided by Allah, ensuring that it is lawful (halal) and wholesome (tayyib). It connects the act of consuming such provisions with the expression of gratitude for Allah's blessings, suggesting that true worship involves not just the acknowledgment of Allah as the sole deity, but also the appreciation and proper utilization of the blessings He bestows. It underscores a holistic approach to faith that encompasses both the spiritual and material aspects of a believer's life.

translation: He has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than God. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of understanding the context and conditions under which certain prohibitions can be relaxed. It establishes that while certain things are generally forbidden (like consuming carrion, blood, pork, and animals dedicated to other than God), there are exceptions for those who are compelled by necessity, provided they do not seek to transgress or indulge excessively. The essence is that God's mercy and forgiveness are available to those who, out of genuine need and not out of desire or excess, are forced to violate these prohibitions. It underscores the balance between the rules and the compassion that is integral to their application, reflecting a broader theme in Islamic jurisprudence of balancing between the letter of the law and the spirit of mercy and understanding.

translation: And do not say about what your tongues assert of untruth, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent falsehood about Allah. Indeed, those who invent falsehood about Allah will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse is cautioning against making false claims about what is lawful and unlawful based on personal whims, thereby attributing falsehood to God. It warns that those who fabricate lies against God will not succeed, emphasizing the importance of adhering to the truth as guided by God's revelations rather than inventing one's own rules or categorizations of what is permissible or forbidden.

translation: (It is) a little enjoyment; and they will have a painful punishment
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the fleeting nature of worldly pleasures and the severe punishment that awaits those who reject faith or engage in wrongdoing. The phrase 'a little enjoyment' underscores the temporary and insignificant nature of earthly delights, while 'a painful punishment' emphasizes the severity and intensity of the suffering that will be endured in the hereafter.

translation: And to those who were Jews, We prohibited that which We have related to you before. And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the prohibitions imposed on the Jews were a result of their own actions and not an arbitrary decision by God. The verse implies that the Jews had deviated from the right path and that the prohibitions were a consequence of their own wrongdoing, indicating that their hardship was self-inflicted.

translation: Then indeed your Lord, to those who do wrong out of ignorance and then repent after that and correct themselves - indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy towards those who initially commit wrongdoings out of ignorance but later repent and correct their actions. It underscores the idea that true repentance, accompanied by a genuine effort to reform, can lead to divine forgiveness. The verse emphasizes God's attributes of being forgiving and merciful, especially towards those who have turned away from their past mistakes and are striving to lead a righteous life.

translation: Indeed, Abraham was a nation, obedient to Allah, inclining toward the truth and he was not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character of Prophet Ibrahim, describing him as a paragon of faithfulness and devotion to God. The term 'أمة' (ummah) here signifies a model or exemplar community, indicating that Ibrahim was a singular individual who embodied the qualities of an ideal community. His being 'قانتا لله' (qanitan lillah) means he was obedient and devoted to God, and 'حنيفا' (hanifan) signifies his inclination towards the true faith, unadulterated and sincere. The verse concludes by affirming that he was not among the polytheists, underscoring his monotheistic belief and his distinction from those who associate partners with God. This portrayal serves to emphasize the importance of sincere devotion and the rejection of polytheism, presenting Ibrahim as a role model for believers.

translation: Grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's favor towards certain individuals whom He chooses and guides to the right path. The phrase 'شاكرا لأنعمه' (shakira li ni'amihi) indicates that the individual is grateful for God's blessings, suggesting a reciprocal relationship between God's grace and the individual's acknowledgment and appreciation of it. The overall interpretation is that divine guidance is often bestowed upon those who are receptive and thankful for God's favors, leading them to a path of righteousness.

translation: And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter, he is among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual reward that is bestowed upon the righteous individuals. The phrase 'حسنة في الدنيا' (a good in this world) suggests that they are granted a favorable and virtuous life in this world, which may include blessings such as a good family, wealth used for righteous purposes, or a position of influence used for justice. The second part, 'وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين' (and indeed, in the Hereafter, he is among the righteous), indicates that their righteousness is recognized and rewarded in the Hereafter, placing them among those who are saved and honored. This verse underscores the Islamic belief in a two-fold recompense for the righteous: a good life in this world and an honorable status in the Hereafter.

translation: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], to follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth; and he was not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse signifies a divine directive to the Prophet Muhammad to follow the monotheistic faith of Abraham, emphasizing the importance of adhering to a pure and unadulterated form of worship, untainted by the practices of polytheism.

translation: The Sabbath was only ordained for those who differed about it. And indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the imposition of the Sabbath was specifically for those who disagreed about it, implying that the law was given as a test or a point of contention. It further reassures that on the Day of Judgment, the Lord will judge between those who differed, indicating that the truth will be revealed and justice will be served regarding the matters they disputed.

translation: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of wisdom, good counsel, and gracious debate in inviting others to the path of one's Lord. It underscores that the method of invitation is as crucial as the message itself, suggesting that the approach should be tailored to the audience's receptivity and understanding. The verse also reassures the believer that God is fully aware of those who have strayed from the right path and those who are guided, implying that the outcome of one's efforts to guide others is in God's knowledge and hands.

translation: And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for those who are patient.
interpretation: This verse suggests that when faced with adversity or injustice, one has two options: to retaliate in a similar manner or to exercise patience. The verse implies that while retaliation is permissible, it should be proportionate to the initial wrongdoing. However, it emphasizes that patience is a superior choice, likely because it allows one to maintain moral high ground, avoid escalation, and possibly lead to a more peaceful resolution. The verse seems to encourage believers to adopt patience as a virtue, suggesting that it is a characteristic of those who are considered righteous or commendable.

translation: And be patient, and your patience is not but through Allah and do not grieve over them and do not be in distress from what they plot.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and trust in Allah during times of adversity. It reminds the believer that their ability to remain steadfast is a gift from Allah, and that they should not be disheartened by the actions or plots of others, as their concern should be to remain firm in their faith and not be constrained by the machinations of those who oppose them.

translation: Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah's support and assistance are with those who are mindful of Him and maintain a high level of moral and ethical behavior, being conscious of their actions and striving to do good.

translation: Glory be to He who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed, that We might show him some of Our signs. Surely, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse signifies the exceptional status and divine honor bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), highlighting his unique spiritual journey, known as the Isra' and Mi'raj. The journey from Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa symbolizes the connection between the two sacred sites and the prophetic mission that bridges different communities and faiths. The verse underscores God's omnipotence and omniscience, suggesting that the miracles and signs (ayat) shown to the Prophet are manifestations of God's all-encompassing knowledge and power. It invites reflection on the nature of divine revelation and the prophetic experience, emphasizing the role of the Prophet as a recipient of divine signs and guidance.

translation: And We gave Moses the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel: not taking anyone other than Me as a trustee.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusive authority and sovereignty of Allah, warning the Children of Israel against assigning any other being or entity as their guardian or trustee, thereby underscoring the monotheistic principle that Allah alone is worthy of such devotion and allegiance.

translation: Offspring of those whom We bore with Noah. Indeed, he was a grateful servant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of Noah's character and the continuity of his righteous lineage. By describing Noah as 'a grateful servant,' it underscores the importance of gratitude and servitude to God. The verse implies that the descendants of those who are righteous and grateful, like Noah, are blessed and noteworthy. It suggests a spiritual legacy that is passed down through generations, emphasizing the value of the company one keeps and the heritage one inherits, not just in terms of lineage but also in terms of spiritual and moral values.

translation: And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture, that they would surely cause corruption on the earth twice and would surely reach [a state of] great arrogance.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the fate of the Children of Israel, as foretold in the Scripture, is to cause corruption on earth twice and to exhibit great arrogance. It suggests that their destiny is intertwined with their actions of mischief and pride, indicating a pattern of behavior that is predicted to recur. The verse serves as a warning or a declaration of the consequences of their actions, highlighting the theme of accountability for one's deeds on earth.

translation: When the first of the two (warnings) came to pass, We sent against you servants of Ours, of great military strength, and they traversed through your homes. And it was a decree that was bound to be fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a future event where God will send a powerful and ruthless people against the Israelites as a punishment, likely referring to the conquest of Jerusalem by the Babylonians. The phrase 'عبادا لنا أولي بأس شديد' (servants of Ours, people of great strength) indicates that despite their strength and ferocity, they are still under God's control and are being used to fulfill His will. The phrase 'فجاسوا خلال الديار' (they traversed through the homes) suggests a thorough and devastating destruction, not just a superficial or limited one. The phrase 'وكان وعدا مفعولا' (and it was a decree that was bound to be fulfilled) emphasizes that this is not a random or arbitrary event, but rather a predetermined and inevitable consequence of the Israelites' actions.

translation: Then We gave you back the turn to prevail over them, and We supplied you with riches and children and made you a numerous band.
interpretation: This verse signifies that after a period of hardship or defeat, Allah restored the Muslims' power and dominance over their enemies, providing them with material wealth (amwal) and offspring (banin), and increasing their numbers, thereby strengthening their community.

translation: If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, [you do it] to them. And when the promise of the Hereafter came, [We raised your enemies] to make your faces wretched and to enter the mosque as they entered it the first time, and to utterly destroy what they had taken over.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who have been given power and authority, reminding them that their actions have consequences not just for others, but for themselves. It highlights the dual nature of human actions, where doing good ultimately benefits oneself, and doing evil harms oneself. The verse then specifically addresses the fate of those who have been given authority but have misused it, foretelling that they will be humiliated and that their attempts to dominate and destroy will ultimately lead to their own downfall. The reference to entering the mosque as they did the first time is likely an allusion to the historical context of the Muslims' struggle against their enemies, and the prophecy that they will be able to reclaim and purify what they had previously lost, signifying a cycle of restoration and justice.

translation: It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you; but if you return [to sin], We will return [to punishment]. And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who have been given a respite from punishment, that if they revert to their previous disobedient ways, God will again turn to punishing them. It highlights the reciprocal nature of God's actions in response to human behavior, emphasizing that His mercy is available for those who turn back to Him, but His punishment awaits those who persist in their disbelief and disobedience, with Hell being their ultimate destination.

translation: Indeed, this Quran guides to that which is most upright and gives good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Quran's role as a guide to the most upright and just path, and it promises a great reward to believers who perform righteous deeds, emphasizing the Quran's function as both a guide and a source of glad tidings for those who adhere to its teachings and live a virtuous life.

translation: And those who do not believe in the Hereafter - We have prepared for them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of disbelieving in the Hereafter, indicating that those who reject the idea of an afterlife and accountability for their deeds will face a severe and painful punishment, serving as a warning to emphasize the importance of faith in the Hereafter.

translation: And man invokes (Allah) for evil as he invokes (Allah) for good and man is ever hasty [i.e., if he is angry with somebody, he invokes (Allah) for his destruction, etc., and that is not in Allah's Will].
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to act impulsively, especially in times of distress or adversity. It suggests that when faced with hardship, humans often pray or wish for evil or negative outcomes, contrary to their usual supplications for good. This behavior is attributed to human impatience, indicating that people often lack the patience to endure difficulties and instead react hastily, sometimes to their own detriment.

translation: And We have made the night and the day two signs, then We made the sign of the night to pass away and the sign of the day giving light, that you may seek bounty from your Lord, and that you may know the numbering of years and the reckoning; and everything We have explained with a clear explanation.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omnipotence and wisdom in creating the universe with a purpose. The alternation between night and day is not merely a natural phenomenon but is imbued with deeper significance, serving as a sign for humans to seek sustenance and to understand the passage of time, thereby organizing their lives. The erasure or dimming of the night's sign (moon) in comparison to the day's sign (sun) symbolizes the balance and harmony in creation, where each element has its role. The detailed explanation (tafseel) of everything signifies God's meticulous planning and order in the universe, encouraging humans to reflect on the intricacies of creation and their place within it.

translation: And [for] every person We have imposed his fate upon his neck, and We will produce for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will encounter spread open.
interpretation: This verse signifies that every individual's deeds are inescapably linked to them and will be presented to them on the Day of Judgment in the form of a book that contains a comprehensive account of their actions, emphasizing personal responsibility and accountability for one's actions in this life.

translation: Read your book. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a Reckoner.
interpretation: This verse signifies the idea that on the Day of Judgment, an individual's own self or conscience will be enough to hold them accountable for their actions. It implies a profound level of personal responsibility, suggesting that one's own self-awareness and recollection of deeds will serve as a sufficient reckoner or auditor, eliminating the need for external witnesses or evidence. It underscores the Islamic belief in the omniscience of the self on that Day, where every action, thought, and intention will be recalled and assessed.

translation: Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul. And whoever errs only errs against it. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And never would We punish until We sent a messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility and the role of guidance in Islam. It underscores that an individual's guidance or misguidance is for their own benefit or detriment, respectively. The verse also highlights the principle that no one bears the burden of another's sins, emphasizing individual accountability before God. Furthermore, it notes that divine punishment is not inflicted without prior warning through the sending of a messenger, underscoring God's justice and mercy in providing clear guidance before holding individuals accountable for their actions.

translation: And when We decide to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones [to obey Our laws], but they commit transgressions therein. Thus, the decree [of destruction] is realized against it, and We destroy it utterly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle that the fate of a community is often tied to the actions of its affluent and influential members. When God decides to destroy a town or community due to its corruption, He first tests its wealthy and powerful individuals by giving them the opportunity to lead by example and adhere to His commands. If they fail to do so and instead indulge in disobedience and corruption, the entire community is held accountable for their actions, leading to its downfall. This emphasizes the responsibility that comes with privilege and influence, suggesting that the moral failure of a community's elite can precipitate its destruction.

translation: And how many generations have We destroyed after Nuh (Noah)! And your Lord is sufficient as an All-Knower, All-Seer of the sins of His slaves.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and follow the path of destruction, reminding them that they are not the first to do so, and that many civilizations before them have been destroyed for their disobedience. It emphasizes God's all-encompassing knowledge and awareness of the deeds of His servants, implying that He is fully cognizant of their actions and will hold them accountable accordingly.

translation: Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him from it what We will to whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will burn, censured and banished.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of prioritizing worldly gains over spiritual and moral objectives. It suggests that those who are driven by a desire for immediate, worldly success may be granted their wishes, but this will ultimately lead to their downfall. The verse implies that such individuals will be held accountable for their priorities and will face punishment in the afterlife, being condemned and rejected.

translation: And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it, [while] he is a believer - those were their effort [is] appreciated [by Allah].
interpretation: This verse highlights that those who prioritize the hereafter and strive for it with the appropriate effort, while being believers, will have their endeavors appreciated and rewarded by Allah. It underscores the importance of having the right intention (seeking the hereafter) and taking the correct actions (striving appropriately), coupled with faith, to have one's efforts valued.

translation: No indeed! We provide for these and for those from the bounty of your Lord, and the bounty of your Lord is not restricted.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of divine generosity and abundance, suggesting that God's provision is not limited or restricted. It implies that God's blessings are available to everyone, regardless of their background or circumstances, and that His giving is not constrained by human concepts of scarcity or exclusivity.

translation: Behold how We have favored some of them over others. And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in favor.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom behind the varying levels of provision and abilities among people. It suggests that the differences in worldly blessings are a test and a means to understand the true nature of human existence. The verse then shifts focus to the Hereafter, emphasizing that the distinctions and rewards in the afterlife will be far greater and more significant than those in this world, underscoring the importance of striving for the eternal and spiritual over the temporal and material.

translation: Do not set up another god along with Allah, lest you sit down blamed and forsaken.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against associating partners with Allah, emphasizing that doing so will lead to being disgraced and left unsupported. It underscores the importance of maintaining the oneness of God (Tawhid) in one's belief and worship, suggesting that deviation from this fundamental principle results in both moral condemnation and divine abandonment.

translation: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be kind to parents. Whether one or both of them attain old age in your care, never say to them a word of contempt, nor repel them, but address them in terms of honor.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of treating parents with kindness and compassion, particularly as they age. It suggests that showing respect and care to one's parents is not just a moral obligation, but a divine command that is closely tied to the worship of God. The verse implies that the way we treat our parents reflects our understanding of and commitment to the values of compassion, humility, and gratitude that are central to faith. By instructing believers to speak to their parents with kindness and respect, even when they may be difficult or demanding, the verse highlights the need for patience, empathy, and self-control in our relationships with others, particularly those who have cared for us.

translation: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, 'My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of treating one's parents with kindness and compassion, particularly as they age. The 'wing of humility' is a metaphor for being gentle and submissive, indicating that one should be willing to humble themselves in the service of their parents. The verse is encouraging a deep sense of empathy and care, rooted in the recognition that one's parents have shown similar care and nurturing when the individual was young and vulnerable. It suggests that the appropriate response to this parental care is to pray for their mercy and well-being, invoking the same kind of nurturing that they provided.

translation: Your Lord is most knowing of what is in your souls. If you should be righteous [in intention] - then indeed He is ever, to the [ruly] repentant, Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and repentance. It suggests that God is aware of one's innermost thoughts and intentions. For those who are righteous and repentant (awwabun), God's forgiveness is readily available, emphasizing the value of turning back to Him in genuine remorse and the promise of mercy that follows.

translation: And give the relative his right, and [also] the poor and the traveler, and do not squander wastefully.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of social responsibility and financial prudence. It instructs believers to fulfill their obligations towards their relatives, the poor, and travelers, indicating that one's wealth is not just for personal enjoyment but also for the welfare of others. The prohibition against extravagant spending ("not to be prodigal") suggests that charity and generosity should be balanced with wisdom and moderation, avoiding wastefulness. It promotes a sense of justice and compassion in the distribution of one's resources, highlighting that true righteousness involves both giving to those who have a rightful claim and doing so in a responsible manner.

translation: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and ever has Satan been to his Lord ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and moral affinity between those who are extravagant and the devil. It suggests that extravagance is not just a financial mismanagement but a reflection of a deeper issue - a deviation from the righteous path, akin to the devil's rebellion against God's will. The verse also underscores the devil's ingratitude towards his Lord, setting a stark contrast to the expected behavior of humans, implying that those who indulge in extravagance are, in essence, following the devil's path of disobedience and ingratitude.

translation: And if you turn away from them awaiting a mercy from your Lord which you expect, then speak to them a gentle word.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of balancing between being kind to those in need and being mindful of one's own circumstances and responsibilities, particularly when one is awaiting provision or relief from Allah. It advises the Prophet to speak gently to those he is unable to help at the moment, likely due to awaiting divine provision, indicating that kindness and gentle speech are essential even in times of personal hardship or when one is expecting a blessing from Allah.

translation: And do not make your hand [as] chained to your neck, nor extend it completely, lest you sit [being] blamed and exhausted.
interpretation: This verse cautions against two extremes in spending: being overly stingy (having one's hand tied to their neck) and being excessively generous (stretching one's hand out completely). The former leads to miserliness, while the latter can result in depletion of resources, leaving one blamed and depleted. It advises a balanced approach to spending, encouraging moderation and prudence in financial dealings.

translation: Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sovereignty and wisdom of Allah in distributing sustenance among His creatures. It signifies that Allah alone has the authority to decide who receives abundance and who faces scarcity, based on His infinite wisdom and knowledge of what is best for His servants. It encourages believers to trust in Allah's providence and to understand that His decisions are guided by His all-encompassing knowledge and insight into the needs and circumstances of His creation.

translation: And do not kill your children out of poverty; We will provide for you and them. Indeed, killing them is a great sin.
interpretation: This verse is cautioning against the desperation and poverty-driven decisions that can lead to harmful actions, such as killing one's children. It reassures believers that Allah is the provider for both the children and their parents, emphasizing that the sustenance comes from Him. The act of killing children out of fear of poverty is considered a grave sin, highlighting the importance of trusting in Allah's provision and avoiding such drastic measures. It encourages a reliance on divine providence rather than resorting to actions that are morally reprehensible and harmful.

translation: And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and is evil as a way.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of adultery or fornication, categorizing it as a heinous act (فاحشة) that not only harms the individuals involved but also destabilizes societal norms and family structures. The phrase 'وساء سبيلا' (and an evil path) suggests that engaging in such behavior leads to a destructive and reprehensible course of life, implying that it is contrary to the righteous path that believers should follow.

translation: And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have given his heir authority, but let him not exceed the limits in [the matter of] taking life. Indeed, he has been supported.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sanctity of human life as ordained by God, emphasizing that taking a life is only justified under the law (i.e., 'by right'). For those who are wrongfully killed, the verse provides a mechanism for justice by granting authority to the victim's guardian or next of kin to seek retribution. However, it cautions against excessive retaliation, underscoring that the avenger is supported and thus should act within the bounds of the law, reflecting a balance between seeking justice and maintaining restraint.

translation: And do not approach the property of the orphan, except in the way that is best, until he reaches maturity. And fulfill [every] commitment. Indeed, the commitment is ever [that about which one will be] questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of handling the property of orphans with utmost care and integrity. It advises against exploiting or mismanaging their wealth and instead encourages improving it until the orphan reaches maturity. Additionally, it stresses the significance of fulfilling covenants and promises, as one will be held accountable for their commitments.

translation: And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with an even balance. That is better and fairer in the end.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of honesty and fairness in commercial transactions. It instructs believers to give full measure when selling and to weigh goods accurately using a straight balance. The underlying message is that honesty in trade is not only a moral virtue but also beneficial in the long run, as it fosters trust and leads to better outcomes. The phrase 'أحسن تأويلا' (better in the end) suggests that fairness and integrity will ultimately yield more favorable results, both in this life and the next.

translation: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against making judgments or assertions without having certain knowledge. It highlights the accountability of human faculties - hearing, sight, and the heart (or intellect) - implying that individuals will be held responsible for how they utilize these faculties. Essentially, it underscores the importance of being mindful and responsible in one's perceptions and understanding of the world, cautioning against the reckless or uninformed use of one's abilities to perceive and comprehend.

translation: And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], and you will never reach the mountains in height.
interpretation: This verse is cautioning against arrogance and pride. It is reminding the individual that despite their confidence and swagger, they are still limited by their human capabilities and cannot achieve the impossible, such as piercing through the earth or reaching the height of mountains. The verse is emphasizing the futility of arrogant behavior, as it is not backed by any real power or ability to transcend the natural limitations of human existence.

translation: All that is hateful in the sight of your Lord.
interpretation: This verse suggests that certain actions or behaviors are viewed unfavorably by Allah, emphasizing the importance of moral accountability and divine displeasure towards wrongdoing, serving as a cautionary note to believers to adhere to righteous conduct.

translation: That is among the wisdom that your Lord has revealed to you. And, [O Muhammad], do not make with Allah another deity, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and banished.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and, by extension, to all believers, cautioning against the association of any other deity with Allah. It underscores the importance of maintaining the purity of monotheistic worship. The verse implies that the wisdom and guidance (referred to as 'الحكمة') received by the Prophet are part of a broader divine plan aimed at establishing and reinforcing the oneness of God (Tawhid). The severe consequence of associating other gods with Allah—being cast into Hell, reproached and rejected—emphasizes the gravity of such a transgression. It highlights the exclusivity of worship due to Allah and the dire outcome of deviating from this fundamental principle of faith.

translation: Has your Lord favoured you with sons and taken for Himself daughters from among the angels? Indeed, you say a grave saying.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the polytheistic beliefs of the pagans, specifically their attribution of daughters to Allah and their preference for sons. The verse suggests that the pagans' claims are baseless and that they are uttering a grave and serious falsehood. It highlights the inconsistency and illogic in their beliefs, questioning why they would attribute sons to themselves but daughters to Allah, and why they would consider angels, who are servants of Allah, to be female. The verse is emphasizing the gravity of their false claims and challenging their distorted understanding of the nature of Allah and the divine.

translation: And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an that they may be reminded, but it does not increase them except in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to resist the truth when it is presented repeatedly. Despite the various ways the Quran explains and elaborates on its message to make people remember and reflect, many people instead become increasingly averse to it. This aversion is not due to a lack of clarity or repetition in the message but rather due to an internal resistance to accepting the truth, indicating a hardened heart or a strong predisposition against the guidance being offered.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'If there had been with Him other gods, as they say, then they [each] would have sought against the Owner of the Throne a way.'
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the absurdity of the polytheistic claim that there are other gods alongside Allah. It argues that if there were multiple gods, they would surely try to overpower or compete with the supreme deity, Allah, who is the possessor of the 'Arsh (Throne), symbolizing ultimate power and authority. The verse suggests that the inability or lack of attempt by these supposed other gods to challenge or reach Allah indicates their non-existence or powerlessness, thus refuting the polytheistic belief.

translation: Glory be to Him and exalted be He above what they say by a great elevation.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's transcendence and supreme elevation above the false and blasphemous claims made against Him by those who deny the truth. The phrase 'علوا كبيرا' (a great elevation) emphasizes the magnitude of God's loftiness and separation from the misconceptions and lies spread by His detractors, underscoring His absolute glory and purity.

translation: The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them glorify Him. There is not a thing but glorifies Him with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse highlights the universal nature of worship and glorification of God, indicating that everything in the universe, whether conscious or not, is engaged in praising and glorifying Him in its own way. It underscores the idea that all creation is inherently and intrinsically connected to and acknowledges God, even if humans may not understand or perceive the forms of glorification exhibited by other beings or elements of the universe. The verse concludes by describing God as being forbearing and forgiving, suggesting that despite human limitations in understanding the universal glorification of God, He remains patient and merciful towards them.

translation: And when you recite the Qur'an, We put between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a concealed partition.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that when the Prophet recites the Quran, a veil is placed between him and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, suggesting that the disbelievers are unable to truly comprehend or be affected by the message due to their spiritual blindness and disconnection from the truth, thereby emphasizing the spiritual barrier that exists between the believers and the disbelievers.

translation: And We have put covers over their hearts lest they understand it, and a heaviness in their ears. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn back in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual state of those who reject the truth. The 'covers on their hearts' and 'heaviness in their ears' signify a divine consequence of their persistent rejection of faith, rendering them incapable of understanding or accepting the message of the Qur'an. When the verse mentions 'your Lord alone being mentioned in the Qur'an,' it points to the monotheistic message that is central to the Islamic faith. The reaction of those who turn their backs in aversion underscores the intense dislike and aversion some people have towards the pure monotheistic teachings, indicating a deep-seated issue of spiritual rejection and hostility towards the truth.

translation: We know best what they listen to when they listen to you and [are] when they confer in private, when the wrongdoers say, "You follow only a man affected by magic."
interpretation: This verse highlights the duplicity and malice of the disbelievers who, despite listening to the Prophet's recitation of the Qur'an, do so with the intention of discrediting him. When they confer among themselves in private, they malign the Prophet, claiming he is under the influence of magic, indicating their deep-seated prejudice and refusal to accept the truth.

translation: See how they coin similitudes for you, so they have gone astray, and cannot find a path.
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who fabricate false analogies and comparisons against the Prophet and the truth he brought. It signifies that their attempts to liken or compare the Prophet and the revelation to something else, in order to discredit or mock them, have led them astray and rendered them incapable of finding the right path. The verse highlights the consequence of their actions as being lost and misguided, unable to discern or follow the correct course.

translation: And they say, 'When we are bones and crumbled, are we indeed going to be resurrected as a new creation?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism of the disbelievers regarding the Day of Judgment and the Resurrection. They question the possibility of being revived after having turned into mere bones and dust, suggesting that the idea of being recreated anew is implausible to them. The verse underscores the challenge faced by the Prophet in convincing those who doubted the afterlife, emphasizing the theme of resurrection and the power of God to recreate life even from what appears to be lifeless remains.

translation: Say, "Be stones or iron"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical challenge posed to those who deny the afterlife and the power of God to resurrect the dead. It is saying, 'Be stones or iron,' implying that even if you were as hard and unyielding as these materials, God can still bring you back to life. The verse is highlighting the omnipotence of God and the ease with which He can accomplish even the most seemingly impossible tasks, such as reviving the dead.

translation: Or some other creature of those that are great in your conception. They will then say, 'Who will return us?' Say, 'He who brought you forth at first.' Then they will shake their heads at you and say, 'When is that?' Say, 'Perhaps it is near.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who deny the afterlife. Despite being reminded of God's power to create them in the first place, they still express skepticism and ridicule the idea of resurrection. The verse suggests that their denial is not based on a genuine lack of understanding, but rather on a refusal to acknowledge the truth. The response 'Perhaps it is near' serves as a warning, implying that the event is not only certain but also potentially imminent, thus underscoring the urgency of heeding the warning.

translation: The day when He will call you, and you will respond with His praise, and you will think that you tarried but a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the suddenness and unexpected nature of the Day of Judgment. On that day, people will be summoned, and they will respond immediately, praising God. The verse also underscores the fleeting nature of worldly life, as people will believe they had tarried but a short while, emphasizing the brevity of human existence in relation to the eternal hereafter.

translation: And tell My servants to say that which is best. Indeed, Satan induces strife between them. Indeed Satan is ever an outright enemy to mankind.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of speaking kindly and using gentle language when interacting with others. It warns that Satan often tries to sow discord among people by provoking them to argue or fight with one another. By using the best words, believers can thwart Satan's attempts to create conflict and maintain harmony, as Satan is a sworn and overt enemy to humanity, constantly seeking to lead them astray.

translation: Your Lord is most knowing of you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you; or if He wills, He will punish you. And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], over them as a guardian.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sovereignty and omnipotence of Allah, emphasizing that He has the authority to decide the fate of individuals and communities based on His wisdom. It serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that his role is to convey the message of Allah, not to control or dictate the outcomes for people; their accountability is directly to Allah. It underscores the concept of divine justice and mercy, suggesting that Allah's decisions are based on a broader understanding and wisdom that may not be immediately apparent to humans. The verse encourages a posture of humility and trust in Allah's plan, acknowledging that His knowledge of humanity is comprehensive and His actions towards them are guided by His infinite wisdom.

translation: And your Lord is most knowing of whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And We have made some of the prophets exceed others [in various ways], and We gave David the Psalms.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omniscience of God, emphasizing that He has complete knowledge of all beings in the heavens and the earth. It then moves on to discuss the varying degrees of excellence among the prophets, indicating that some were given greater favors than others. The specific mention of David receiving the Psalms (Zabur) illustrates this point, showing that different prophets were given different scriptures and roles, underscoring the diversity and richness of God's revelation to humanity.

translation: Say, 'Call those you claim besides Him, then they do not own the removal of adversity from you nor [its] transference'
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical challenge to the polytheists, asking them to call upon the deities they claim to worship alongside God, in times of hardship and distress. The verse highlights the futility of their beliefs by pointing out that these deities are powerless to alleviate their suffering or change their circumstances, underscoring the omnipotence and sole authority of God.

translation: Those whom they call upon [i.e., the righteous servants] themselves seek the means of nearness to their Lord, vying with each other to be closer to Him. They hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is something to beware of.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of the righteous servants of God. They are those who, in their worship and supplications, seek to draw closer to their Lord through various means, striving to be among those who are nearest to Him. Their actions are driven by a dual motivation: hope for His mercy and fear of His punishment. The verse underscores the importance of having a balanced spiritual disposition, marked by both the aspiration for divine benevolence and the apprehension of divine retribution. It serves as a reminder that the punishment of one's Lord is something to be feared and avoided, thereby encouraging believers to lead a virtuous life.

translation: And there is not a town but We shall destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment. That is written in the Book (of Decrees)
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of divine judgment and the certainty of punishment for those who have committed wrongdoing. It suggests that every community or civilization will face destruction or severe punishment before the Day of Judgment, as it is predestined and recorded in the divine book, emphasizing God's sovereignty and justice.

translation: And nothing stops Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a clear sign, but they wronged her. And We do not send the signs except as a warning.
interpretation: The verse highlights that the disbelievers' demand for miracles or signs is not a genuine quest for truth, but rather a continuation of a pattern of denial and disbelief that has been observed throughout history. The example of the tribe of Thamud and the she-camel sent to them as a sign is cited, where despite the clear and manifest miracle, they still chose to wrong and disobey. The sending of such signs or miracles is not to satisfy the demands of the disbelievers but serves as a warning, intended to instill fear of the consequences of disobedience and to prompt reflection and repentance.

translation: And [remember] when We told you that your Lord has encompassed the people. And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and [so too] the accursed tree in the Qur'an. And We threaten them, but it increases them not except in great transgression.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of obstinacy in the face of divine signs and warnings. The vision shown to the Prophet and the accursed tree mentioned in the Qur'an served as tests for the people. Instead of leading to guidance and righteousness, these signs and warnings only led to increased rebellion and transgression among those being addressed, indicating a hardened resistance to the truth.

translation: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' they prostrated, except for Iblis. He said, 'Should I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of disobedience and pride. Iblis's refusal to prostrate to Adam is rooted in his arrogance and sense of superiority, as he considers himself to be made of a nobler substance (fire) compared to Adam, who was created from clay. This demonstrates that Iblis's disobedience is not just a simple act of defiance, but is motivated by a deeper sense of pride and a refusal to acknowledge the superiority of others, even when commanded by God. This sets the stage for the ongoing conflict between those who follow God's commands humbly and those who resist them out of pride and arrogance.

translation: He said, 'Do You see this one whom You have honoured above me, if You give me respite until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely destroy his progeny, except for a few.'
interpretation: This verse is part of a conversation between Iblis (Satan) and Allah, where Iblis, having been condemned for his disobedience, vows to mislead humanity. The interpretation of this verse is that Iblis is boasting to Allah that he will corrupt the majority of humanity, except for a few who will remain faithful and on the right path, by leading them astray until the Day of Judgment.

translation: He said, 'Go, and whoever follows you among them, indeed Hell will be your recompense, an ample recompense.'
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who follow the path of the one being addressed, likely a leader or figure of misguidance. It signifies that for those who choose to follow such an individual, their recompense will be a full and ample punishment in Hell. The verse emphasizes the severity and completeness of the punishment, indicating that it is not just a minimal or partial consequence, but a full and just retribution for their actions. It serves as a caution against following leaders or ideologies that lead people astray from the righteous path.

translation: And incite whoever you can among them with your voice and assault them with your horses and foot soldiers and be their partner in their wealth and their children and promise them.
interpretation: This verse is a warning about the tactics and temptations employed by Satan (Shaytan) to mislead people. It signifies that Satan uses various means to entice and deceive individuals, including using his 'voice' (or call) to lure them astray, mobilizing his 'cavalry' and 'infantry' (symbolizing different forms of temptations and agents of evil), and involving himself in people's wealth and children (indicating the corruption of material and familial aspects of life). Satan makes false promises to people, and these promises are nothing but deceptions or illusions, as they ultimately lead to disappointment and harm. The verse serves as a cautionary message to beware of Satan's deceitful strategies and to remain steadfast against his temptations.

translation: Indeed, My servants - no authority will you have over them. And sufficient is your Lord as a Guardian.
interpretation: This verse signifies that despite the efforts of satanic forces or tempters, they lack the authority to influence or control the sincere servants of Allah. It reassures that those who are devoted to Allah are under His protection. The phrase 'وكفى بربك وكيلا' (And your Lord is sufficient as a Guardian) underscores the idea that Allah is enough to protect and manage the affairs of the believers, emphasizing trust in His providence and care.

translation: Your Lord is the One who moves the ships for you in the sea, so that you may seek of His bounty. Indeed, He is ever Merciful to you.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy and benevolence towards humanity by facilitating their livelihood through the ease of navigation and trade across the seas, underscoring the notion that God's provision and mercy are fundamental to human existence and prosperity.

translation: And when distress afflicts you at sea, those you invoke vanish except for Him; but when He delivers you to the land, you turn away. For man is ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural human tendency to turn to the one true God in times of distress, but to forget Him and return to polytheistic practices when the crisis has passed. It suggests that humans are prone to ingratitude and that their faith is often tested by their circumstances, with genuine devotion being revealed in times of hardship, but frequently forgotten in times of ease.

translation: Are you then secure that He will not cause a tract of land to swallow you up or send against you a violent tornado (with showers of stones), so that you shall not find a protector?
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the Prophet and feel secure from Allah's punishment. It highlights the powerlessness of human beings against Allah's wrath, emphasizing that even the most seemingly secure individuals or communities can be struck by disaster at any moment, whether it be a cataclysmic event like an earthquake or a devastating storm. The phrase 'then you will not find for yourselves a guardian' underscores the idea that when Allah's punishment comes, no human intermediary or protector can intercede on their behalf or shield them from His wrath, leaving them utterly helpless.

translation: Or are you secure that He will not take you back into it [i.e., the sea] another time and send upon you a hurricane of wind and drown you because of what you disbelieved? Then you will not find for yourselves against Us in that an avenger.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who have been saved from destruction, cautioning them against becoming complacent and forgetting the power of God. It highlights the theme of divine retribution and the consequences of ingratitude. The verse implies that just as God had saved them once, He has the power to destroy them again if they continue in their disbelief. It emphasizes the idea that God's mercy is not a guarantee against future punishment if one persists in their rejection of faith. The verse is meant to instill a sense of awe and reverence for God's power and to encourage believers to remain steadfast in their faith, lest they suffer the consequences of their ingratitude.

translation: And indeed, We have honored the children of Adam, and We have carried them on land and sea, and have provided them with good things, and have preferred them above many of those whom We have created with a marked preference.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status granted to humanity by God. It signifies that humans have been endowed with dignity and have been favored with various blessings and provisions. The mention of transportation on land and sea indicates the facilitation of human life through various means, and being provided with good sustenance underscores God's generosity. The verse concludes by affirming that humans have been preferred over many other creations, suggesting a unique position of honor and responsibility within the created order.

translation: The day [Judgment Day] We will call forth every people with their record [of deeds]. Then whoever is given his record in his right hand, those will read their record, and they will not be wronged a thread [that is, the smallest amount].
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, people will be held accountable for their deeds based on the guidance they received and followed in their lives. Those who received and followed the right guidance (imam) will be given their record of deeds in their right hand, and they will be able to read it with ease, indicating their righteousness. Moreover, they will not be wronged even to the extent of the thread (fatila) that is found in the groove of a date stone, signifying the utmost justice and fairness in the judgment.

translation: And whoever is blind in this [life] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray from the path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity between one's spiritual state in this life and the next. It suggests that being 'blind' in this world - metaphorically, being spiritually blind or unaware of the truth - not only persists in the afterlife but is compounded by being further astray from the right path.
