It underscores the idea that the opportunities for spiritual guidance and correction are primarily in this life, and failing to take them results in a more profound loss in the hereafter.

translation: And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from that which We have revealed to you, so that you might invent something else against Us; and then they would certainly have taken you as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense pressure and temptation the Prophet Muhammad faced from his detractors to alter or compromise the divine revelation he received. The phrase 'لتفتري علينا غيره' (to fabricate something else against Us) suggests that they wanted him to attribute to God something other than the true revelation, essentially to falsify the message. The response 'وإذا لاتخذوك خليلا' (and then they would certainly have taken you as an intimate friend) implies that had he yielded to their pressure, they would have accepted him as a friend or ally, indicating a deep-seated desire to corrupt the prophetic message and the Prophet's integrity for their own benefit. This verse underscores the Prophet's unwavering commitment to the genuine message of God despite the adversities and temptations he faced.

translation: And were it not that We had made you stand firm, you would have certainly inclined to them a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine support and guidance in maintaining one's moral and spiritual integrity. It suggests that without God's firming up of the Prophet Muhammad's resolve, he would have been on the verge of inclining, albeit slightly, towards the disbelievers, indicating the human propensity to falter without divine assistance.

translation: If you were to do so, We would certainly make you taste double [punishment] in this life and double [punishment] after death, then you would not find any helper against Us.
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that if he were to associate partners with Allah or disobey Him in any way, He would make him taste double the punishment in this life and double the punishment in the hereafter, and that he would not find any helper or supporter against Allah's will. It highlights the severity of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of remaining steadfast in one's faith.

translation: And indeed, they were about to incite you to drive you out from the land; but in that case they would not have stayed after you except for a little while
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense hostility of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and their desperate attempts to expel him from Makkah. It also serves as a warning and a promise to the Prophet that even if they succeed in expelling him, their own stay in Makkah would be short-lived, implying that the Prophet's eventual return or victory is near. This interpretation underscores the transient nature of the disbelievers' power and the ultimate triumph of the Prophet and his message.

translation: (Such has been) the practice (approved) of Allah among those who lived aforetime: No change wilt thou find in the practice (approved) of Allah
interpretation: This verse signifies that the struggles and hardships faced by the Prophet Muhammad are part of a pattern or tradition (sunnah) that Allah has established for all the prophets He sent before him. It reassures the Prophet that he is not alone in facing opposition and hardship, and that the divine law or tradition (sunnah) that governs the treatment of prophets by their people does not change.

translation: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun [from its meridian] to the darkness of the night and [the] recitation of the Qur'an at dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur'an at dawn is ever witnessed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of establishing prayer at specific times, from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, and the recitation of the Qur'an at dawn, which is witnessed by angels, highlighting the significance of these acts of worship in the sight of Allah.

translation: And during a part of the night, pray Tahajjud as an additional prayer for you; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy position.
interpretation: This verse is encouraging the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to perform the Tahajjud prayer, a voluntary night prayer, as a means to attain a praiseworthy position (Maqama Mahmuda) before Allah. The 'praiseworthy position' refers to the Station of Praise (Maqam al-Mahmud) that will be granted to the Prophet on the Day of Judgment, where he will be allowed to intercede on behalf of the believers. The verse suggests that the Prophet's devotion and worship, including the Tahajjud prayer, will be a means to attain this esteemed position, and by extension, serves as an encouragement to the believers to follow his example in their own worship and devotion.

translation: And say, 'My Lord, cause me to enter a righteous entry and cause me to exit a righteous exit and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.'
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to Allah, seeking guidance and support in all aspects of life. The speaker is asking Allah to grant them a righteous entry and exit, which can be interpreted as seeking a virtuous beginning and end to their endeavors. The phrase 'grant me from You a supporting authority' suggests that the speaker is seeking empowerment and validation from Allah to carry out their mission or purpose in life with confidence and conviction. In essence, the verse is a prayer for divine guidance, empowerment, and righteousness in all undertakings.

translation: And say, "Truth has come, and falsehood has departed. Indeed is falsehood, [by nature], ever perishing."
interpretation: This verse signifies that truth will inevitably prevail and falsehood will be vanquished. It emphasizes the transient nature of falsehood, indicating that it is inherently prone to being eradicated when confronted with truth.

translation: And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual effect of the Qur'an on people based on their faith and actions. For believers, the Qur'an serves as a source of healing for their spiritual ailments and a mercy that guides them towards righteousness. In contrast, for those who are unjust (or disbelievers), engaging with the Qur'an only leads to further loss, as it either hardens their disbelief or increases their deviation from the right path, ultimately exacerbating their spiritual and moral decay.

translation: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; and when evil touches him, he is in despair.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to be ungrateful and forgetful of God's blessings. When God bestows favors upon a person, they become arrogant and turn away from Him, but when faced with hardship, they become despondent, losing hope in God's mercy. It underscores the human condition of being prone to extremes of behavior based on their circumstances, rather than maintaining a consistent attitude of gratitude and trust in God.

translation: Say, 'Everyone acts according to his own disposition, but your Lord is most knowing of who is best guided in path.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity in human nature and behavior, suggesting that individuals act according to their inherent dispositions or characteristics. It underscores the idea that true guidance is known only to Allah, who understands the inner workings and intentions of all beings. The verse implies that while humans may judge others based on their outward actions, it is Allah who has complete knowledge of one's true path and guidance.

translation: And they ask you, [O Muhammad], about the soul. Say, 'The soul is of the affair of my Lord. And you have not been given knowledge except a little.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of human knowledge and understanding, emphasizing that there are aspects of reality that are beyond human comprehension, and that the knowledge granted to humans is limited in comparison to the vastness of divine knowledge. The specific reference to 'the spirit' (al-rūḥ) signifies a realm or aspect of creation that is not fully accessible to human inquiry or understanding, pointing to the mysterious and divine nature of certain aspects of existence.

translation: And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you, then you would not find for yourself because of it an advocate against Us.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute power and control of Allah over the revelation He has sent down to the Prophet Muhammad. It signifies that if Allah willed, He could take away or nullify the revelation (the Qur'an) that was given to the Prophet, leaving him without any intermediary or advocate to reinstate it. This emphasizes Allah's sovereignty over His messengers and the revelations, underscoring that the continuation of the revelation is entirely dependent on Allah's will. It serves as a reminder to the Prophet and believers of their complete dependence on Allah's grace and mercy.

translation: Except as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, His bounty to you was great.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that any mercy or favor bestowed upon an individual is ultimately an act of grace from their Lord. It underscores the notion that God's bounty is vast and His generosity towards certain individuals can be immense, indicating a special status or role for them. In this context, it suggests that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) has been particularly favored by God, emphasizing the magnitude of God's grace upon him.

translation: Say, 'If all of humanity and the jinn were to gather together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they could not produce the like of it, even if they were to back one another up.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Quran's inimitability and challenges all of humanity and the jinn collectively to produce something similar to it, emphasizing its divine origin and uniqueness.

translation: And We have certainly varied the examples for the people in this Qur'an, but most of the people refused except to be ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and ingratitude of humanity. Despite the Quran presenting various examples and parables to guide people to the truth, most people refuse to accept it and instead show ingratitude, indicating a deep-seated resistance to the message of the Quran.

translation: And they say, 'We will not believe you until you cause for us to gush forth from the earth a spring'
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy and arrogance of the disbelievers, who demanded a miracle from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that was beyond his control and outside the realm of prophetic miracles. They asked him to make a spring gush forth from the earth, a demand that was not only unreasonable but also a test of his prophethood that was not in line with the gradual and wisdom-based approach of divine signs and miracles. This reflects their stubborn refusal to believe based on the clear signs and proofs already presented to them, and instead, they sought an extraordinary and unprecedented miracle to satisfy their skepticism, indicating their lack of sincerity in seeking guidance.

translation: Or you have a garden of date-palms and grapes and you cause rivers to gush forth in their midst abundantly
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the futility of worldly possessions and wealth. It is suggesting that even if one were to possess a grand and lush garden filled with date palms and grapevines, and were to have rivers flowing abundantly through it, it would not guarantee their salvation or proximity to Allah. The verse is emphasizing that true worth and value lie not in material wealth, but in one's faith and deeds.

translation: Or the sky falls upon us in pieces, as you have claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before [us] as a guarantee.
interpretation: This verse is a response to the disbelievers who demanded that the Prophet (peace be upon him) bring about a miracle to prove his prophethood. They asked him to make the sky fall upon them in pieces, or to bring God and the angels before them as a witness to his truthfulness. The verse is highlighting the obstinacy and arrogance of these people, who were not satisfied with the signs and miracles that had already been shown to them, and were instead making outlandish and impossible demands. The verse is also emphasizing that even if such impossible things were to happen, it would not necessarily lead to faith, as the disbelievers were not willing to submit to the truth even in the face of overwhelming evidence. It is a demonstration of the futility of their demands and the unreasonableness of their expectations.

translation: Or you have a house of ornament, or you ascend into the sky. And never will we believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book that we can read.' Say, 'Exalted is my Lord; am I more than a human being, a messenger?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge faced by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as he was asked by his detractors to perform miracles or show tangible signs of his prophethood, such as having a lavish house or ascending to heaven. The response given by the Prophet, as guided by Allah, emphasizes the limitations of human capability, even for a Prophet, and underscores the true nature of his mission as a messenger. It asserts that the Prophet is merely a human being tasked with conveying the message of Allah, and that the demand for physical or material proofs overlooks the essence of faith, which lies in the acceptance of the divine message as conveyed through the Prophet. The verse serves as a reminder that faith is not necessarily tied to observable miracles but to the belief in the message and the trust in the messenger as guided by Allah.

translation: And nothing prevents people from believing when the guidance comes to them except that they say, 'Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and disbelief of those who were unwilling to accept the message of Islam when it was presented to them by the Prophet Muhammad, who was a human being like themselves. The underlying issue was their inability to comprehend or accept the idea that a human being, rather than an angel or some other supernatural being, could be chosen by God as a messenger to guide humanity. This reflects a deeper issue of arrogance and a preconceived notion about how divine guidance should be delivered, rather than an openness to the message itself.

translation: Say, "If there were in the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel [as a] messenger."
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom behind God's choice of messengers. It suggests that if the inhabitants of the earth were angels, God would still have chosen an angel as a messenger to them, implying that the messenger should be of the same nature or kind as the people being addressed. The verse underscores the significance of the Prophet Muhammad being a human, emphasizing that his humanity was a crucial aspect of his prophethood and his ability to connect with humanity. It serves as a response to the disbelievers who demanded that an angel be sent as a messenger, arguing that a human prophet was not acceptable. The verse reinforces the idea that the prophethood of Muhammad is not diminished by his humanity but is rather suited to his role as a messenger to humans.

translation: Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you. Indeed, He is of His servants Acquainted and Seeing.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge and awareness of Allah, highlighting that He is not only aware of the actions of His servants but also fully cognizant of their innermost intentions and the subtleties of their circumstances. It serves as a reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad that Allah is a sufficient witness to the truth of his message and the opposition he faces, underscoring the trustworthiness of Allah as a mediator and judge in the dispute between the Prophet and his detractors.

translation: And whomsoever Allah guides, he is the one who follows the right path; and whomsoever He causes to err, you will never find for him protectors besides Him. And We shall gather them together on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb, and deaf. Their abode will be Hell; every time it abates, We shall increase for them the fierceness of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of being guided or misguided by Allah. Those whom Allah guides are on the right path, while those whom He allows to go astray will have no protectors or guardians other than Him. On the Day of Judgment, the misguided will be resurrected blind, dumb, and deaf, symbolizing their spiritual incapacitation. Their ultimate destination is Hell, which will continue to burn fiercely, and every time it subsides, it will be intensified further, indicating a perpetual and escalating punishment for their deeds.

translation: That is because they disbelieved in Our verses and said, "When we are bones and crumbled, are we [truly] going to be resurrected [in] a new creation?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of disbelieving in the signs of Allah, emphasizing the resurrection and the afterlife. The disbelievers, who deny the power of Allah to revive the dead, are met with the reality of their own resurrection, a new creation, after being reduced to mere bones and dust. The verse serves as a rebuke to those who doubt the afterlife, affirming that despite their skepticism about being revived from a state of decay, they will indeed be recreated anew.

translation: Have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is Able to create the likes of them, and He has appointed for them a term, there is no doubt in it? But the wrongdoers refuse everything except disbelief.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting God's omnipotence by pointing out that if He was able to create the heavens and the earth, He is certainly capable of recreating similar creations. The reference to an appointed term (ajal) that is certain underscores the inevitability of a reckoning or judgment. The response of the wrongdoers (al-zalimoon) is one of ingratitude (kufur), indicating their refusal to acknowledge or be thankful for God's power and the implications of His ability to recreate, likely referring to the concept of resurrection or rebirth. The verse is emphasizing the contrast between God's capability and the disbelief or ungratefulness of those who wrong others, likely by associating others with God or denying His power.

translation: Say, "If you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold out of fear of spending." And ever has man been miserly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency towards miserliness and the fear of scarcity. It suggests that even if people were in control of God's infinite bounty, they would still be reluctant to spend out of fear that it might run out. This reveals a fundamental distrust in God's promise to provide and replenish, and underscores the human inclination towards greed and stinginess.

translation: And We had certainly given Moses nine clear signs, so ask the Children of Israel [about] when he came to them and Pharaoh said to him, "Indeed I think, O Moses, that you are affected by magic."
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy and arrogance of Pharaoh in the face of clear evidence. Despite being presented with nine clear signs by Moses, Pharaoh attributes Moses' abilities to sorcery, indicating his refusal to acknowledge the divine origin of the signs and his attempt to delegitimize Moses' prophetic claim. This reaction underscores the theme of obstinacy in the face of truth, a recurring motif in the Qur'an when discussing the responses of unbelievers to prophetic messages.

translation: He said, 'You have already known that these [miracles] have been sent down by none but the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear insight, and indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the conviction of Moses as he addresses Pharaoh, affirming that the signs and miracles he has presented are not mere tricks or illusions but are profound truths revealed by the Lord of the heavens and the earth, serving as clear insights or proofs. Moses expresses his certainty that Pharaoh is doomed or destroyed, underscoring the inevitability of divine judgment upon those who refuse to acknowledge and submit to God's will.

translation: So he wanted to drive them out from the land, but We drowned him and those with him all together.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah's punishment is not limited to the individual wrongdoer, but can extend to those associated with them, highlighting the social and communal consequences of defying God's commands and the importance of righteousness in maintaining the well-being of a community.

translation: And We said after him to the Children of Israel, 'Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you all together.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that after a particular event or a certain group of people, the Children of Israel were allowed to settle in the land. The phrase 'if the promise of the Hereafter comes' refers to the Day of Judgment or the end times. The verse suggests that on that day, people from various backgrounds and places will be gathered together, implying a universal gathering or reckoning. It highlights the idea that the current state of affairs is temporary and that there will be a future gathering or judgment where people will be brought together, regardless of their origins.

translation: And with the truth We have sent it down and with the truth it has descended. And We have not sent you except as a giver of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse highlights the authenticity and truthfulness of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad. It signifies that the Qur'an was revealed with truth and Muhammad was sent as a bearer of good news for those who follow the right path and as a warner to those who deviate from it, emphasizing the dual role of a prophet in guiding humanity towards righteousness.

translation: And the Qur'an We have divided [into portions], so that you might recite it to the people over a [long] period. And We have sent it down progressively.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gradual and deliberate nature of the Qur'an's revelation, tailored to the needs and circumstances of the early Muslim community, facilitating its comprehension and implementation.

translation: Say, "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it - when it is recited to them, they fall upon their faces in prostration."
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound impact of the Quran on those who possess knowledge. When the Quran is recited to them, they are deeply moved, falling to their knees in prostration, indicating that the Quran resonates with their understanding and confirms the truth they already know. It underscores the Quran's role in validating and deepening the knowledge of those who are already learned, suggesting a continuity between prior knowledge and the Quranic revelation.

translation: And they say, "Glory to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled."
interpretation: This verse highlights the believers' conviction in the promise of their Lord, acknowledging that His decree is inevitable and will certainly come to pass. The phrase 'Subhan Rabbana' (Glory be to our Lord) is an expression of their reverence and acknowledgment of Allah's transcendence above any inability to fulfill His promise. It signifies their faith and trust in the divine plan, emphasizing that the promise made by Allah is not just a statement but a commitment that will be fulfilled.

translation: And they fall upon their chins weeping, and it increases them in humility.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound impact of spiritual guidance on the believers, where the act of prostrating and weeping signifies a deep emotional and spiritual surrender to the truth of the Qur'an. The phrase 'ويخرون للأذقان يبكون' (they fall upon their chins weeping) illustrates the intense emotional response of those who are touched by the divine message, and 'ويزيدهم خشوعا' (and it increases them in humility) suggests that this emotional and physical surrender leads to a deeper state of spiritual humility and devotion.

translation: Say, "Invoke Allah or invoke the Most Merciful. Whichever [name] you invoke - to Him belong the best names." And do not recite [too] loudly in your prayer or [too] quietly but seek between that an [intermediate] way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and moderation in worship. It begins by emphasizing that whether one invokes God by the name 'Allah' or 'al-Rahman' (the Most Merciful), it is ultimately the same Being being addressed, as all beautiful names belong to Him. The verse then cautions against extremes in the practice of prayer, advising against being too loud or too silent, instead advocating for a moderate approach. This moderation is not just about the audible aspect of prayer but can be interpreted more broadly as a call for balance in one's devotional practices, reflecting a broader principle of avoiding extremes and seeking a middle path in religious observance.

translation: And say, "Praise be to Allah who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in the sovereignty, nor has He had a protector out of weakness; and glorify Him with [great] glorification."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of Allah, affirming that He has no offspring, partners, or helpers due to any weakness. It underscores the majesty and greatness of Allah, commanding believers to glorify Him. The verse is a declaration of Tawhid (the oneness of God), rejecting the ideas of polytheism and the attribution of divine characteristics to anyone or anything else. By proclaiming Allah's greatness, believers reaffirm their faith and demonstrate their devotion to the singular, all-powerful Creator.

translation: Praise be to Allah, Who has sent down upon His Servant the Book, and has not made therein any crookedness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the perfection and flawlessness of the Qur'an. The phrase 'لم يجعل له عوجا' (He has not made any crookedness in it) signifies that the Qur'an is free from contradictions, inconsistencies, and deviations from the truth, underscoring its divine origin and authenticity. It emphasizes the reliability and trustworthiness of the scripture as a guide for believers.

translation: To be upright, that he might warn of a severe punishment from Him and give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual purpose of the revelation: to warn those who are heedless of the severe consequences of their actions and to give glad tidings to the believers who perform righteous deeds, indicating that their efforts will be rewarded with great recompense.

translation: Abiding therein forever
interpretation: This verse signifies the eternal nature of the afterlife, whether it be in paradise or hell. Those who are destined to dwell in paradise or hell will remain there forever, with no end or termination to their stay. It highlights the permanence and irreversibility of the final judgment, underscoring the gravity of one's deeds in this life and their consequences in the hereafter.

translation: And warn those who say, 'Allah has taken a son.'
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who attribute a child to Allah, a belief held by some pre-Islamic Arabian pagans and certain Christian sects. The verse is cautioning these individuals about the gravity of their claim, which is considered a form of shirk (polytheism) or a deviation from the true monotheistic belief in Allah. The warning suggests that such a belief will have severe consequences, likely in the hereafter, as it contradicts the fundamental Islamic belief in the oneness and uniqueness of Allah.

translation: They have no knowledge of it, nor did their forefathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak not except a lie.
interpretation: This verse is a critique of blindly following tradition or the opinions of one's ancestors without having any knowledge or evidence to support such claims. It highlights the danger of uncritical acceptance and the propagation of falsehoods. The phrase 'كبرت كلمة' (a grave/serious statement) emphasizes the severity of uttering false statements, indicating that the claims being made are not only baseless but also significantly problematic or offensive. The verse suggests that such utterances are characteristic of a lack of intellectual or spiritual rigor, and that they represent a form of dishonesty or falsehood.

translation: Perhaps you would consume yourself with grief over their tracks, if they do not believe in this narration.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense emotional investment the Prophet Muhammad had in conveying the message of Islam to his people. The phrase 'باخع نفسك' (consuming yourself) suggests a deep sorrow or grief that could potentially lead to self-destruction due to the people's rejection of the faith. It serves as a gentle reprimand or caution to the Prophet, reminding him not to overly distress himself over the disbelief of others, as it was beyond his control to change their hearts. It underscores the human aspect of the Prophet's experience, showing that despite his prophetic role, he was not immune to the pain of rejection, and it offers a message of comfort and reassurance.

translation: Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them [as to] which of them is best in deed.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the adornments and beauties of the world are a test for humanity, to discern who among them will act with righteousness and virtue, rather than being consumed by worldly desires.

translation: And We will surely make what is on it bare and desolate.
interpretation: This verse signifies that everything on the earth will be reduced to nothing, leaving it barren and devoid of life, emphasizing the transient nature of worldly existence and the inevitability of a day when all that is on the earth will be levelled and made desolate.

translation: Or did you think that the Companions of the Cave and the Inscription were among Our signs a wonder?
interpretation: This verse is rhetorical, emphasizing that the story of the Companions of the Cave is not more astonishing than the signs and miracles of God, and that it is just one of many wondrous signs that demonstrate God's power and wisdom.

translation: When the youths took refuge in the cave and said, “Our Lord, grant us mercy from You and guide us rightly in our affair.”
interpretation: This verse highlights the desperation and faith of the young believers who sought refuge in the cave. They invoked Allah, asking for mercy and guidance, demonstrating their reliance on divine assistance in times of hardship and persecution. The verse underscores the theme of seeking divine help and guidance in the face of adversity, emphasizing the importance of faith and trust in Allah's providence.

translation: So We cast a veil over their ears for a number of years in the cave.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Allah caused the sleep of the youths in the cave to be deep and sound, rendering them insensible to their surroundings for a considerable number of years, thereby protecting them from the persecution they would have faced if they had remained awake. The phrase 'ضربنا على آذانهم' (We sealed their ears) is a metaphorical expression signifying the depth of their slumber, as if their ears were sealed off from hearing any external sounds, emphasizing the completeness of their isolation and protection.

translation: Then We awakened them that We might make evident which of the two parties was more accurate in calculating the span of time they had passed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine purpose behind reviving the Sleepers of the Cave after their long slumber. It was not merely an act of resurrection but a test to determine which group among those who knew about them could more accurately reckon the duration of their sleep. The verse underscores the theme of the limits of human knowledge and the inevitability of divine will, suggesting that even the most seemingly inexplicable events are part of a larger divine plan, often beyond human comprehension.

translation: We narrate to you their story in truth. Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the causal relationship between faith and guidance. The youths mentioned in the verse had faith in their Lord, and as a result, they were granted additional guidance. This implies that faith is not a static state, but rather a dynamic process that can lead to further spiritual growth and understanding. The verse suggests that true faith is not just a matter of affirming certain beliefs, but also involves a deepening of one's understanding and connection with the divine.

translation: And We bound their hearts when they stood up and said, "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth; we will not invoke besides Him any deity. We would have then said an extravagance."
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering faith and conviction of a group of believers, likely the Companions of the Cave, who stood firm in their monotheistic beliefs despite potential adversity. The phrase 'ربطنا على قلوبهم' (We bound their hearts) suggests that Allah strengthened and steadied their hearts, enabling them to proclaim their faith unshakeably. Their declaration, 'ربنا رب السماوات والأرض لن ندعو من دونه إلها' (Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, we will never invoke any deity other than Him), demonstrates their commitment to the oneness of God, and their recognition that invoking other deities would be an extreme deviation from the truth, as indicated by 'لقد قلنا إذا شططا' (We would have then uttered an enormity). This verse underscores the importance of maintaining purity of faith and the consequences of deviating from it.

translation: These are our people, who have taken other deities besides Him. If only they could bring clear authority for them. And who is more unjust than the one who fabricates lies against Allah?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the issue of polytheism and the fabrication of falsehoods against Allah. It is questioning the rationale behind the people who have taken other deities besides Allah, and pointing out that there is no clear authority or evidence to justify this practice. The verse then asserts that there is no one more unjust than the person who fabricates lies against Allah, implying that attributing partners or equals to Allah is a grave injustice. This verse is emphasizing the importance of evidence-based belief and the gravity of inventing falsehoods about Allah.

translation: And when you withdrew from them and that which they worshipped besides Allah, then seek refuge in the cave; your Lord will unfold for you of His mercy and will make easy for you your affair.
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of separating oneself from a society that is hostile to faith and seeking refuge in a safe haven where one can preserve their beliefs and practices. The 'cave' serves as a metaphor for a sanctuary or a place of safety where believers can escape persecution and await divine assistance and relief. The verse underscores the idea that those who take refuge in their faith during times of hardship and persecution will be provided with divine mercy and guidance, and their circumstances will be eased.

translation: And you will see the sun when it rises, inclining away from their cave on the right, and when it sets, passing away from them on the left, while they are in an open space within it. That is from the signs of Allah. He whom Allah guides is the rightly guided; but he whom He leaves to err, you will not find for him a protecting friend to guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of God's guidance and misguidance. It suggests that those whom God guides are truly on the right path, while those whom He leaves to err will not find a guardian or guide to lead them aright, underscoring the idea that true guidance comes from God alone.

translation: And you would have thought them awake, whereas they were asleep. And We turned them on their right and on their left sides, and their dog stretching forth his two forelegs on the threshold. If you had looked at them, you would surely have turned back from them in flight, and you would surely have been filled with awe of them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of the sleep of the Companions of the Cave, where despite being asleep for an extended period, they appeared as if they were awake, and their bodies were periodically turned to prevent decay. The verse conveys the awe-inspiring and supernatural aspect of this event, suggesting that witnessing it would evoke a strong reaction of fear and flight, underscoring the divine power at play.

translation: And thus We awakened them that they might question one another. A speaker among them said, "How long have you remained [here]?" They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day." They said, "Your Lord is most knowing of how long you remained. So send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city and let him look to which is the purest food and bring you provision from it and let him be cautious. And let no one be aware of you."
interpretation: The verse highlights the miraculous nature of the Companions of the Cave's awakening after a long period of sleep, and their subsequent interactions. The interpretation lies in understanding the psychological and social dynamics at play. The Companions, upon waking, are disoriented and unsure of how long they have slept. Their discussion and decision to send one of their own to procure food, while being cautious not to be detected, illustrates their gradual return to a state of awareness and normalcy. Furthermore, their acknowledgment that "Your Lord is most knowing of how long you remained" demonstrates their recognition of a higher power and their humility in the face of the unknown, underscoring a key Islamic value of submitting to the will of Allah.

translation: If they gain the upper hand over you, they will stone you or force you back to their faith, and you will never succeed then.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences that the early Muslims faced from their persecutors. It warns that if the disbelievers were to gain power over the Muslims, they would either stone them to death or force them to revert to their (disbelievers') faith. The verse serves as a reminder of the intense hostility and the life-threatening situation the early Muslim community endured, emphasizing the impossibility of their success or survival if they were to return to the disbelievers' fold or be coerced into abandoning their faith. It underscores the gravity of apostasy and the dire circumstances that necessitate steadfastness in faith.

translation: And thus We made their story known to the people that they might know that the promise of Allah is true and that there can be no doubt about the Hour. ˹Some˺ of them said ˹to one another˺, “Build a structure over ˹the Cave˺.” Their Lord knows best about them. Those who prevailed in ˹the˺ matter said, “We will certainly build a place of worship over ˹the Cave˺.”
interpretation: This verse highlights the differing opinions among the people regarding the Companions of the Cave. Some suggested building a structure over their resting place, while others, who gained the upper hand, decided to construct a mosque. This divergence in views serves as a reflection of human nature, where individuals have varying perspectives on how to honor or commemorate significant events or people. The verse subtly underscores the potential for religious sites to be established based on the graves or resting places of righteous individuals, a practice that has been a subject of debate throughout Islamic history. The phrase 'their Lord knows best about them' indicates that the true nature and fate of the Companions of the Cave are known only to Allah, emphasizing the limitations of human knowledge and understanding.

translation: They will say, 'They were three, their dog the fourth,' and they say, 'They were five, their dog the sixth,' guessing at the unknown; and they say, 'They were seven, and their dog the eighth.' Say, 'My Lord is most knowing of their number. None knows them except a few. So, do not argue about them except with an obvious argument and do not inquire about them among [the people of] conjecture anyone.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of engaging in speculative debates about matters that are beyond one's knowledge, particularly when Allah has not provided clear information. It cautions against delving into conjectures and instead advises sticking to what is evidently known and verifiable. The context is the story of the People of the Cave, where various guesses were made about their number, illustrating how people often indulge in unproductive and unverifiable discussions about the unseen. The verse encourages believers to refrain from such debates and to rely on certain knowledge, directing them to focus on matters that are within their realm of understanding and to avoid seeking information from those who speculate or conjecture.

translation: And do not say of anything, 'Indeed, I will do that tomorrow,'
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of human limitations and the importance of humility, cautioning against making definitive plans for the future without acknowledging one's dependence on God's will, emphasizing the need to condition future actions with the acknowledgment of God's ultimate authority and control over all that will come to pass.

translation: Except as God wills; and remember your Lord when you forget and say, 'Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something nearer to right guidance than this.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility and reliance on God's will. The phrase 'except as God wills' underscores the understanding that human intentions and actions are subject to God's divine plan. The instruction to 'remember your Lord when you forget' suggests a need for self-reflection and a return to faith when one strays or forgets. The expression 'perhaps my Lord will guide me to something nearer to right guidance than this' conveys a sense of openness to correction and a willingness to be guided towards a better path, indicating a virtuous attitude of seeking truth and righteousness.

translation: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years, and they added nine.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of the sleep of the People of the Cave, emphasizing the extraordinary length of time they remained asleep, which was 300 solar years plus an additional 9 lunar years, demonstrating God's power to suspend the natural order and preserve His servants.

translation: Say, 'God is most knowing of how long they remained. To Him is the unseen of the heavens and the earth. How Seeing is He and how Hearing! They have not, apart from Him, any guardian, and He does not associate anyone with His judgment.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's omniscience and sovereignty, highlighting that He is the sole possessor of knowledge regarding the unseen, including the duration of time spent by certain individuals or groups in a particular state. It underscores God's absolute authority and dominion over the heavens and earth, and asserts that He is the only true guardian and decision-maker, with no one sharing in His judgment or authority. The verse is urging the Prophet to proclaim God's supremacy and exclusive knowledge of the unseen, reinforcing the idea that God's wisdom and governance are unparalleled and unchallenged.

translation: And recite, [O Muhammad], what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord. There is no changer of His words. And never will you find in other than Him a refuge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of conveying the message of the Qur'an as revealed by Allah, without alteration or modification. It signifies that the words of Allah are immutable and unchangeable, and that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is commanded to recite and convey the revelation as received. Furthermore, it underscores the idea that there is no refuge or alternative to be found outside of or apart from Allah's guidance and words, highlighting the exclusivity and sufficiency of divine guidance.

translation: And keep yourself patient [by being] with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His countenance. And let not your eyes pass beyond them in desire for the adornments of this world. And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire and whose affair is ever [in] excess.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of companionship with those who are devoted to their faith and consistently remember Allah. It advises against being swayed by worldly allurements and against following individuals who have become heedless of Allah's remembrance, succumbing to their own desires, and whose affairs have become excessively disordered. The verse encourages perseverance in the company of the righteous, seeking Allah's pleasure, and warns against being distracted by the fleeting attractions of this world.

translation: And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve." Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a fire whose canopy will surround them. And if they implore for relief, they will be relieved with water like murky oil that scalds their faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of divine justice and the consequences of rejecting faith. It emphasizes that the decision to believe or disbelieve is left to individual choice, but warns that those who choose to be unjust (or disbelievers) will face severe punishment in the form of hellfire. The vivid imagery of the hellfire and its torment, including the scorching water that disfigures faces, serves to underscore the gravity of the consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing. The verse thus serves as a stark warning to those who might choose to reject the truth, emphasizing the dire outcome of such a choice.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds, indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of any who did well in deeds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's justice and fairness in rewarding individuals. It suggests that those who have faith and perform good deeds will not have their efforts go in vain. The phrase 'إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا' (We do not waste the reward of those who do good) implies that God will reward individuals according to the quality of their actions, and that their good deeds will not be lost or unappreciated. It encourages believers to maintain their faith and continue doing good, as their efforts will be recognized and valued by God.

translation: Those will have gardens of perpetual residence; rivers will flow beneath them. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and will wear green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade, reclining therein on adorned couches. It is an excellent reward and a fine resting place.
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate reward for the righteous in the afterlife, emphasizing the luxurious and eternal nature of their paradise. The mention of 'gardens of perpetual residence' and 'rivers flowing beneath them' signifies a life free from the toils and troubles of the worldly life, where one's every need is met with ease and comfort. The adornments and attire described, such as 'bracelets of gold' and 'green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade,' symbolize the honor and splendor bestowed upon them. The act of 'reclining on adorned couches' further underscores a state of serene contentment and bliss. The verse concludes by affirming that this paradise is not only a good reward but also a beautiful resting place, highlighting the perfection of the afterlife for those who have led a righteous life.

translation: And present to them the parable of two men: We granted to one of them two gardens of grapevines and surrounded them with palm trees and placed between them [fields of] crops.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the parable of two men, one of whom is given two gardens of grapevines surrounded by palm trees and with cultivated land in between, serving as an allegory to illustrate the contrasting outcomes of gratitude and ingratitude towards God's blessings. It symbolizes the test of human character when faced with abundance and prosperity, emphasizing the themes of faith, gratitude, and the transience of worldly possessions.

translation: Both gardens yielded their produce and failed not in anything thereof; and We caused a river to gush forth therein
interpretation: This verse highlights God's bounty and provision for those who are righteous. The fact that both gardens yielded their fruit without failing and that a river was made to flow through them signifies the abundance and richness of God's blessings. It underscores the idea that God's provision is not limited and that He can bless abundantly, emphasizing the theme of divine generosity and care for the believers.

translation: And he had fruit, so he said to his companion while he was conversing with him, "I am greater than you in wealth and stronger in respect to men."
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the dangers of pride and arrogance that come with worldly possessions. The owner of the garden is boasting to his companion about his wealth and the number of people at his disposal, showing a clear disregard for the blessings of Allah and an inflated sense of self-importance. The verse serves as a warning against the corrupting influence of wealth and the tendency to forget one's accountability to Allah when one becomes consumed by material possessions.

translation: And he entered his garden, while he was unjust to himself. He said, 'I do not think that this will ever perish'
interpretation: This verse highlights the dangers of arrogance and complacency. The owner of the garden, having become wealthy, becomes unjust to himself by being overly confident and ungrateful. His statement 'I do not think this will ever perish' indicates his arrogance and lack of faith in the power of Allah, showing that his prosperity has led him away from humility and gratitude towards Allah.

translation: And I do not think the Hour will occur. And even if I should be returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than that as a return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disbelief of those who doubt the Hereafter. The speaker is expressing their skepticism about the Hour (Judgment Day) and boasting that if they were to return to their Lord, they would receive a better outcome. This reflects the mindset of those who are materialistic and lack faith, as they prioritize worldly gains over spiritual reckoning. The verse serves as a critique of such an attitude, underscoring the need for humility and faith in the face of the unknown.

translation: His companion said to him, as he conversed with him, 'Have you disbelieved in He who created you from dust then from a sperm-drop, then proportioned you as a man?'
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the absurdity of denying the power of Allah, the Creator, by pointing to the stages of human creation, from dust to a sperm drop, and finally to a fully formed human being. It is emphasizing that if one acknowledges their own creation and development, they should not deny the One who has the power to create and shape them. The verse is an argument against disbelief and a reminder of the power and capability of Allah.

translation: But it is Allah who is my Lord, and I do not associate with my Lord anyone.
interpretation: This verse signifies the affirmation of the oneness of God and the rejection of polytheism, emphasizing the speaker's conviction that God is their sole Lord and that they do not associate any other being or entity with Him in divinity or worship.

translation: If only, when you entered your garden, you had said: 'It is (all) what Allah willed (that has come to pass)! There is no power except with Allah. If (you) consider me less than you in wealth and children'
interpretation: This verse is cautioning against pride and arrogance when one is blessed with wealth and children. The phrase 'ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله' (what Allah wills, there is no power except with Allah) is a reminder to acknowledge that all blessings come from Allah and that one's success is not solely due to their own abilities. The verse is highlighting the importance of humility and recognizing the role of divine providence in one's life, rather than attributing one's success to personal strength or wealth.

translation: It may be that my Lord will give me something better than your garden and will send on it a thunderbolt from the sky, then it will become a barren land.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who are arrogant and proud of their worldly possessions. It highlights the possibility that despite having gardens and wealth, one might still face a calamity from above, resulting in the loss of everything they have. The 'حسبانا من السماء' (a shower from the sky) is often interpreted as a punishment or a calamity that comes unexpectedly from above, and 'صعيدا زلقا' (slippery earth) signifies a land that has become barren and devoid of any vegetation or resources, emphasizing the totality of the loss. The verse is cautioning against the pride and arrogance that comes with wealth, reminding that true and lasting provision comes from Allah.

translation: Or its water becomes deep sunk [into the earth], then you will never be able to seek it.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the futility of human endeavor when faced with the absolute power of Allah. The image of water sinking into the earth, becoming inaccessible, serves as a metaphor for the way in which Allah's will can render human efforts and possessions worthless. It underscores the theme of reliance on Allah and the recognition of His sovereignty over all aspects of life.

translation: And his fruits were encompassed [by ruin], so he turned his hands about [in dismay] over what he had spent on it, while it had collapsed upon its trellises, and said, 'Oh, I wish I had not associated with my Lord anyone.'
interpretation: This verse is a cautionary tale about the consequences of associating partners with God (shirk) and the fleeting nature of worldly possessions. The owner of the garden, having neglected his duty to God and attributed his success to others or to his own power, is left with nothing when his garden is destroyed. His regret and despair are underscored by his physical gesture of wringing his hands in frustration and sorrow, symbolizing the loss of his wealth and the futility of his actions. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining the oneness of God (Tawhid) and being mindful of one's deeds and their consequences in this life and the next.

translation: And he had no group to help him instead of Allah, and he was not to be helped.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of relying on anything or anyone other than Allah for support or salvation. It signifies that true salvation and support come solely from Allah, and that any other source of aid is ultimately futile. The verse serves as a warning against polytheism and the misplaced trust in other entities or beings for rescue or victory.

translation: There, the authority is for Allah, the Truth. He is the best in reward and the best in outcome.
interpretation: This verse signifies that ultimate authority and judgment rest with Allah, who is the embodiment of truth. It emphasizes that Allah's reward for the righteous and His outcome for all affairs are superior to any other. It underscores the idea that while humans may have temporary authority or control, the true and lasting power is Allah's, and He will judge and reward according to His justice and mercy.

translation: And present to them an example: the life of this world is like water which We send down from the sky, and the plants of the earth mingle with it. [Then] it becomes dry remnants which the winds scatter. And Allah is ever, over all things, competent.
interpretation: This verse is a parable that illustrates the fleeting and ephemeral nature of worldly life. Just as rainwater mixed with the earth's vegetation causes it to flourish, only to wither away and be dispersed by the winds, so too is the life of this world - it flourishes for a time, but ultimately perishes. The verse serves as a reminder that true power and control rest with Allah, who has the ability to bring about such changes, and that one should not become too attached to the transient nature of worldly life. The parable is meant to caution against placing too much emphasis on the material aspects of life, and to encourage a focus on the eternal and enduring aspects of existence.

translation: Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world. But the enduring good deeds are better in the sight of your Lord for reward and better in respect of hope.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fleeting nature of worldly possessions and the importance of focusing on righteous deeds that have lasting value in the eyes of Allah. It suggests that while wealth and children may bring temporary joy and prestige, they are ultimately ephemeral and can be a source of distraction or pride that leads one away from Allah. In contrast, 'the enduring good deeds' (al-baqiyat al-salihat), which are often interpreted as acts of worship and remembrance of Allah, are considered superior because they are not only rewarded in the hereafter but also provide a sense of hope and spiritual fulfillment that is not subject to the vicissitudes of worldly life.

translation: And [on] the Day when We will cause the mountains to pass away and you will see the earth [clearly] exposed, and We will gather them and not leave behind from them anyone
interpretation: This verse highlights the Day of Judgment, where the existing world order is completely overturned. The mountains, symbols of stability and permanence, are made to 'pass away', indicating a profound transformation of the physical world. The earth, once hidden by the mountains and other features, is 'exposed', symbolizing the unveiling of all that was hidden, including secrets and deeds. The gathering of all people without leaving anyone behind signifies the universal accountability before God, where every individual is brought forth to face judgment for their actions.

translation: And they will be presented before your Lord in rows. 'You have come to Us just as We created you the first time. But you claimed that We would not make for you an appointment.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark reality of human accountability before God. The image of being presented 'in rows' before the Lord underscores the uniformity and equality of all individuals in the divine judgment, stripping away the worldly distinctions and hierarchies. The phrase 'as We created you the first time' serves as a poignant reminder of the simplicity and humility of human origins, contrasting sharply with the pride and arrogance that often characterize human life. The verse also touches upon the theme of human presumption and denial of the afterlife, as indicated by the phrase 'you claimed We would not make for you an appointment.' This denial is a form of hubris, reflecting humanity's tendency to doubt or reject the notion of accountability for their deeds. The verse, therefore, serves as a commentary on the human condition, emphasizing the themes of equality before God, the simplicity of human creation, and the folly of denying the afterlife.

translation: And the Book is placed, then you see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they say, 'Oh, woe to us! What is this Book that does not leave a small [transgression] nor a great one except that it has enumerated it?' And they found what they had done present [in it]. And your Lord does injustice to no one.
interpretation: This verse highlights the meticulous justice of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where every individual will be held accountable for their actions, no matter how small or large. The verse emphasizes that the record of deeds, as mentioned in 'the Book', is exhaustive and present before the wrongdoers, instilling in them a deep sense of dread and regret. It underscores the principle that Allah's judgment is perfectly just and equitable, ensuring that no one is wronged.

translation: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except for Iblees. He was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord. Then will you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me while they are enemies to you? Wretched it is for the wrongdoers as a replacement.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against following the footsteps of Satan and his progeny, who disobeyed God's command. It highlights that Satan, despite being among the angels or having a close association with them, refused to prostrate before Adam, thus exemplifying the danger of allowing enmity towards others to lead one to disobey God's commands. The verse cautions against taking Satan and his followers as allies instead of God, emphasizing that they are enemies to humanity. It underscores the grave consequences of such allegiance for those who are unjust, indicating that choosing Satan over God leads to a terrible replacement or consequence, implying a severe form of punishment or deviation from the right path.

translation: I did not make them witness to the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor to the creation of themselves; and I would not have taken the misguiders as helpers.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omnipotence and sole authority in creation, emphasizing that He did not require any assistance or counsel from others, including the misguiders or those who lead people astray, in creating the heavens, the earth, or human beings themselves. It underscores the idea that God's creative power is unmatched and unassisted, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid (the oneness of God) in Islamic theology.

translation: And [mention] the Day when He will say, "Call 'My partners' whom you claimed," so they will invoke them, but they will not respond to them, and We will put between them [a valley of] destruction.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of associating partners with Allah. On the Day of Judgment, those who claimed that certain entities or beings were partners with Allah will be asked to call upon these supposed partners for help. However, these 'partners' will not respond, illustrating their powerlessness and the falsehood of the claims made about them. The verse further emphasizes the separation and barrier (موبقا) that will be placed between these individuals and their false deities, signifying not just the failure of their intercession but also the irreversible consequences of their misguided beliefs.

translation: And the criminals saw the Fire and apprehended that they are going to fall therein. And they found no escape from it.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, those who have committed sins and rejected the truth will see the Hellfire and become certain that they will inevitably fall into it. They will realize that there is no escape or diversion from their fate, emphasizing the inescapable nature of divine justice for those who have defied God's commandments.

translation: And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an for the people, from every [kind of] example; but man has ever been more than anything, most argumentative.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to engage in dispute and argumentation, even when faced with clear explanations and examples, as presented in the Qur'an. It suggests that despite the diverse illustrations and clarifications provided in the scripture to guide people to the truth, human nature inclines towards contentiousness, indicating a propensity to challenge or dispute the truth rather than accepting it graciously.

translation: And nothing has prevented people from believing when the guidance came to them and from asking forgiveness of their Lord except that there should come to them the [same] precedent of the former peoples or that the punishment should come before them.
interpretation: This verse suggests that people's obstinacy and adherence to past practices or expectations of a particular form of punishment can hinder their ability to accept guidance and seek forgiveness when it is presented to them, highlighting a pattern where people often require a tangible manifestation of divine intervention before they are willing to change their ways.

translation: And We send not the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners. And those who disbelieve dispute by [using] falsehood to [attempt to] extinguish thereby the truth and have taken My signs and that which they are warned [of] in ridicule.
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy of those who reject faith. Despite the clear message brought by prophets, which includes both the good news of reward for the righteous and the warning of punishment for the disobedient, those who disbelieve resort to false arguments to undermine the truth. Furthermore, they mock the signs of God and the warnings given to them, indicating a profound level of disdain and resistance to the divine message. This behavior is characteristic of those who are determined to cling to their disbelief, using any means, no matter how baseless, to challenge the truth and diminish its impact.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord; then he turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forth? Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears, deafness. And if you invite them to guidance, they will never be guided, then - ever.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of spiritual blindness and the consequences of willful ignorance. It suggests that those who are reminded of God's signs and yet turn away, are not just passive recipients of misguidance, but are actively prevented by their own hardened hearts and deafened ears from understanding the truth. The verse implies that their past actions have led to a state where they are now incapable of guidance, and that calling them to the right path will be futile. It underscores the concept that one's deeds can lead to a form of spiritual deafness and blindness, making it impossible for them to receive guidance.

translation: And your Lord is the Forgiver, Owner of Mercy. If He were to hold them [i.e., people] to account for what they have earned, He would have hastened for them the punishment. But they have an appointed time beyond which they will find no refuge.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's merciful nature, indicating that if He were to punish people immediately for their wrongdoings, He would hasten their suffering. Instead, there is an appointed time for their reckoning, suggesting that people have a window of opportunity to reflect, repent, and change their ways before facing the consequences of their actions. It underscores the concept that divine justice is tempered with mercy, allowing for a period of respite before accountability.

translation: And those towns, We destroyed them when they did wrong, and We made for their destruction an appointed time.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who are unjust and oppressive, indicating that their destruction is not arbitrary or without prior notice. It suggests that when communities or nations engage in wrongdoing, they are given a respite, a period during which they could potentially reform or mend their ways. However, when they persist in their injustice, their destruction becomes inevitable, and the timing of this destruction is predetermined by God. The verse implies a moral and cosmic order where justice is ultimately served, and those who transgress beyond a certain limit face the consequences of their actions.

translation: And [mention] when Moses said to his servant, "I will not cease [traveling] until I reach the junction of the two seas or continue for a long period."
interpretation: This verse signifies Moses' determination and perseverance in his quest for knowledge. He is resolute in his journey to attain a specific goal, which is to reach the junction of the two seas, even if it takes him a long period of time ('or I go on for many years'). This demonstrates the importance of persistence and patience in the pursuit of knowledge and understanding.

translation: But when they reached the junction between them, they forgot their fish, and it took its course into the sea, slipping away.
interpretation: This verse signifies the moment when Moses and his companion, Joshua, reached a significant point in their journey together, yet they forgot about the fish they were carrying, which then miraculously came to life and escaped into the sea, symbolizing a divine intervention and marking the beginning of a new and unexpected turn in their journey.

translation: But when they had passed on, Moses said to his attendant, 'Bring us our morning meal; certainly we have suffered much fatigue at this journey.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the human aspect of even the most spiritually advanced individuals, as it shows that even a prophet like Moses, who is on a significant spiritual journey, experiences fatigue and the need for basic necessities like food, underscoring the shared human experience across different levels of spiritual attainment.

translation: He said, "Did you see when we retreated to the rock? Indeed, I forgot [there] the fish. And none made me forget it except Satan - that I should mention it. And it took its course into the sea amazingly"
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of Satan in causing forgetfulness and distraction. The speaker had forgotten the fish, and it is attributed to Satan's influence that this forgetfulness occurred. The miraculous escape of the fish into the sea is also noted, suggesting that even in moments of forgetfulness or distraction, there can be divine signs or interventions at work.

translation: He said, 'This is what we were seeking.' So they both returned on their tracks, following (the path).
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of perseverance and retracing one's steps when seeking knowledge or a solution. It suggests that sometimes, one may need to revisit their previous actions or decisions in order to find what they are looking for, and that this process of retracing can lead to a deeper understanding or discovery.

translation: And they found a servant among Our servants, whom We had granted mercy from Us, and whom We had taught knowledge from Us.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status of certain individuals whom Allah has chosen to bestow His mercy and knowledge upon. It indicates that true knowledge is not just acquired through human means, but can also be directly granted by Allah to those He deems worthy. The verse sets the stage for the story of Moses and the righteous servant, often identified as Khidr, where Moses is about to learn from someone who has been given knowledge directly from Allah, underscoring the theme of divine knowledge and its superiority over human understanding.

translation: Moses said to him, 'May I follow you so that you may teach me some of the guidance you have been taught?'
interpretation: This verse highlights Moses' humility and eagerness to learn from someone he recognizes as having knowledge he does not possess, indicating a willingness to transcend conventional boundaries of knowledge and authority, and to learn from others even if they are not traditionally considered teachers or authorities.

translation: He said, 'You will not be able to have patience with me.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the acknowledgment by the individual addressed, likely a companion or follower, of their own limitations in enduring or understanding the actions or decisions of the speaker, often interpreted as Moses being told by Khidr that he cannot have the patience to follow Khidr's seemingly inexplicable actions, highlighting the human condition of limited understanding and the need for faith in the face of the unknown.

translation: And how can you be patient about something you have no comprehensive knowledge of?
interpretation: This verse highlights the impossibility of being patient about something when one lacks comprehensive knowledge about it. It suggests that patience requires understanding and awareness of the situation at hand. The verse is cautioning against undertaking a task or enduring a hardship without having full knowledge or insight into it, implying that such an endeavor would be challenging, if not futile.

translation: He said, 'You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in [any] order.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of humility, obedience, and reliance on Allah's will. The speaker is committing to being patient and obedient, but also acknowledges that their ability to do so is contingent upon Allah's will, demonstrating a recognition of their limitations and a reliance on divine guidance and support.

translation: He said, 'Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I make mention of it to you.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of trust and patience in the pursuit of knowledge. When Moses follows the unknown servant of God, he is instructed not to inquire about anything until he is given a full explanation. This indicates that true understanding often requires waiting for the right moment to receive insight, rather than demanding immediate clarification. It highlights the value of restraint and the willingness to learn without constant questioning, trusting that the teacher knows the appropriate time to reveal the underlying reasons or wisdom.

translation: So they both set out, until when they had boarded the ship, he damaged it. [Musa] said, 'Have you damaged it to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing.'
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the tension between the apparent injustice of an action and the underlying wisdom or greater good that may not be immediately apparent. The act of damaging the boat seems inherently wrong, as it potentially harms the people relying on it. However, the narrative suggests that there is a deeper reason or divine wisdom behind this action that is not immediately clear to the observer, illustrating the complex interplay between visible actions and their underlying, possibly divine, intentions.

translation: He said, "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge of being patient and persevering when faced with events or circumstances that are beyond one's understanding or seem inexplicable. It underscores the difficulty of maintaining composure and trust when the wisdom or rationale behind certain happenings is not immediately apparent, emphasizing the test of faith and character in the face of uncertainty or adversity.

translation: He said, 'Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair'.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to make mistakes due to forgetfulness and the need for divine leniency. The speaker is asking for forgiveness and ease in their affairs, indicating a recognition of human fallibility and a reliance on God's mercy and understanding. It underscores the importance of compassion and the removal of hardship in one's responsibilities or obligations, reflecting a broader Qur'anic theme of God's desire to ease the burden on believers rather than to impose undue hardship.

translation: So they both set out until when they met a boy, he killed him. [Musa] said, 'Have you killed a pure soul for other than [having killed] a soul? You have committed something reprehensible.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tension between divine decree and human morality, as the act of killing an innocent soul appears unjust to human eyes, yet is justified by a divine wisdom that is not immediately apparent. The reaction of Musa (Moses) to the act underscores the natural human aversion to unjust killing, while the narrative sets the stage for an explanation that will reconcile this act with divine justice.

translation: He said, "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge of being patient when faced with events that seem inexplicable or contrary to one's expectations, emphasizing the difficulty of trusting in a greater plan or wisdom when immediate understanding is lacking.

translation: He said, 'If you ask me about anything after this, then do not be my companion. You have attained from me an excuse.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the condition or the limit set by the guide (Khidr) to the one being guided (Moses) that the latter must have faith and patience in the guidance being provided without questioning it, indicating the importance of trust and acceptance in the process of gaining knowledge or spiritual growth.

translation: So they both proceeded, until they came to the people of a town. They asked them for food, but they refused to entertain them as guests. Then they found therein a wall which was about to collapse, so he (Khidr) set it up straight. (Musa) said: 'If you had wished, surely you could have taken wages for it.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the apparent ingratitude of the people they encountered and the selfless act of the wall's repair by Khidr. It also underscores Moses' bewilderment at Khidr's actions, as he expected compensation for their efforts, reflecting a worldly perspective on labor and reward.
