It implies that the message is intended to serve as a reminder for those who are already inclined towards righteousness and are mindful of their actions in relation to God's will. The underlying idea is that the reminder or warning will be effective or beneficial only for those who are receptive to it due to their fear of God, indicating a selective efficacy of the message based on the recipient's spiritual disposition.

translation: A revelation from the One who created the earth and the highest heavens.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Quran is a revelation from the Creator of the universe, emphasizing the divine origin and authority of the scripture. It establishes the credibility of the Quran by attributing its source to the all-powerful being who has created the heavens and the earth, thus underscoring the importance and truthfulness of its message.

translation: The Most Merciful [who is] on the Throne is established.
interpretation: This verse signifies God's establishment of His authority and dominion over the universe, indicating His absolute power and control over all creation. The term 'استوى' (istawa) on the 'عرش' (Arsh, or throne) is often understood to represent the culmination of God's creative act, where He has assumed His rightful position of authority and sovereignty. It underscores the concept of God's omnipotence and His reign over all that exists.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is under the soil.
interpretation: This verse signifies the absolute sovereignty and dominion of Allah over all that exists, encompassing not just the heavens and the earth, but everything in between, as well as what lies beneath the earth's surface, emphasizing His all-encompassing power and knowledge.

translation: And if you speak aloud, then indeed, He knows the secret and what is [even] more hidden.
interpretation: This verse highlights the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, emphasizing that He is aware not only of what is openly expressed but also of the innermost secrets and thoughts that individuals may keep hidden, even from themselves. It underscores the idea that Allah's knowledge transcends human capabilities of expression and concealment, touching upon the deepest and most subtle aspects of human thought and intention.

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the uniqueness and singularity of God, affirming that there is no other deity worthy of worship besides Him. The phrase 'له الأسماء الحسنى' (To Him belong the most beautiful names) highlights God's attributes of perfection and excellence, suggesting that His names and qualities embody the utmost beauty, goodness, and virtue, thus underscoring the reverence and awe with which He should be regarded.

translation: And has there come to you the story of Moses?
interpretation: This verse is an introduction to the story of Moses, drawing the reader's or listener's attention to a significant event or narrative that follows, serving as a reminder or a lesson. It signifies the importance of the story that is about to be told, relating it to the broader context of guidance, faith, and the consequences of one's actions as conveyed in the Qur'an.

translation: When he saw a fire, he said to his family, 'Stay here; indeed I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a burning brand therefrom or find at the fire some guidance.'
interpretation: This verse signifies a moment of spiritual and physical quest for guidance. The narrative revolves around Prophet Moses, who, upon perceiving a fire, instructs his family to remain in place while he proceeds towards the fire. His intention is not merely to fetch a burning ember for warmth or light but to potentially discover guidance at the site of the fire. The verse symbolizes the pursuit of enlightenment and divine direction, highlighting the importance of seeking knowledge and spiritual illumination. The 'fire' in this context becomes a metaphor for a source of divine revelation and guidance, underscoring the theme of spiritual quest and the receptiveness to divine signs and messages.

translation: But when he came to it, he was called, "O Moses!"
interpretation: This verse signifies a pivotal moment in the prophetic journey of Moses, as it marks the beginning of his direct communication with Allah. The calling of Moses by Allah at this specific location underscores the sanctity and importance of the site, transforming it into a sacred space where divine revelation occurs. It highlights the transition of Moses from being a mere observer of a miraculous event (the burning bush) to becoming the recipient of a divine message, thereby initiating his role as a prophet entrusted with conveying Allah's will to his people.

translation: Indeed, I am your Lord! So take off your sandals; you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
interpretation: This verse signifies a moment of spiritual preparation and reverence. By instructing Moses to remove his shoes, God is indicating that Moses is standing on sacred ground, and thus, he needs to shed the mundane aspects of his life to engage in a spiritual or divine encounter. The act of removing shoes is a symbol of humility, respect, and readiness to receive divine guidance or to undertake a sacred task.

translation: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed.
interpretation: This verse signifies a special selection and mission bestowed upon the Prophet Musa (Moses), emphasizing the importance of attentively receiving and following the divine revelation being conveyed to him, highlighting the responsibility that comes with being chosen by God for a significant prophetic role.

translation: Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God, affirming that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. It commands the establishment of prayer as a means of remembering Allah, highlighting the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual connection through regular worship. The verse underscores the exclusivity of worship for Allah alone, reinforcing the central tenet of monotheism in Islam.

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming; I almost conceal it so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives for.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and secrecy of the Hour (Judgment Day), suggesting that its exact timing is known only to Allah. The phrase 'I almost conceal it' implies that while the exact time is hidden from human knowledge, there are signs and indications that it is approaching. The purpose of the Hour is to hold each individual accountable for their deeds and efforts in life, underscoring the Islamic belief in personal responsibility and divine justice.

translation: So let not the one who does not believe in it and follows his desire divert you from it [i.e., the Hour] so you would perish.
interpretation: This verse warns against being deterred from the truth by those who do not believe in it and instead follow their own desires, lest one falls into destruction. It highlights the danger of being swayed by the opinions or actions of those who are not guided by faith, and cautions against the potential consequences of such influence, which can lead one astray and into ruin.

translation: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?
interpretation: The verse is questioning Prophet Moses about the staff in his right hand, which is a rhetorical question that leads to a demonstration of God's power, as the staff is subsequently transformed into a snake, signifying the beginning of a miraculous sign that would be a proof of Moses' prophethood and a means to convince Pharaoh of his message.

translation: He said, "It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I fend off [thorns] with it for my sheep, and I have other uses for it."
interpretation: The verse highlights the multifaceted significance and personal attachment one can have with everyday objects, using the example of a staff. It not only serves a practical purpose, like providing support or helping with daily chores, but also holds other, perhaps emotional or symbolic, values for the individual. This reflects the human tendency to attribute meaning and importance to objects beyond their immediate utility, often linking them to personal experiences, memories, or emotional connections.

translation: He said, 'Throw it down, O Moses.'
interpretation: This verse is a command from Allah to Prophet Musa (Moses) to throw down his staff. The context of this verse is when Prophet Musa was given two miracles by Allah, the staff that turned into a snake and his hand that became white, as signs of his prophethood. The throwing down of the staff is often seen as a demonstration of Musa's prophethood and a sign for Pharaoh and his people. In a broader interpretation, this act signifies the surrender and obedience of a prophet to the will of Allah, demonstrating the absolute trust and faith that prophets have in the commands of Allah, even when those commands may seem inexplicable or daunting.

translation: So he threw it down, and behold! It was a snake, moving quickly.
interpretation: This verse signifies a miraculous event where an inanimate object, a staff, transforms into a living being, a snake, upon the action of throwing it, demonstrating divine power and intervention, often associated with prophetic signs and miracles in the Qur'anic narrative.

translation: He said, "Take it; do not fear. We will return it to its former state."
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power to restore something to its original state, emphasizing the idea that even if something is altered or damaged, God has the capability to return it to its pristine condition, illustrating the theme of divine restoration and renewal.

translation: And draw your hand close to your side; it will come out white, not diseased, as another sign.
interpretation: This verse signifies a miracle given to Prophet Moses as a sign of his prophethood. The act of withdrawing his hand under his armpit and then producing it white and radiant, without any disease or blemish, is a demonstration of divine power and a reassurance to Moses of his mission.

translation: That We may show thee of Our greatest signs.
interpretation: This verse signifies that God is about to reveal to the Prophet Muhammad some of His greatest signs or miracles, serving as evidence of his prophethood and the truth of his message. It is an assurance to the Prophet of the forthcoming manifestations of divine power and wisdom, likely referring to significant events or miracles that will validate his mission.

translation: Go to Pharaoh, indeed he has tyrannized
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine mandate given to Prophet Moses to confront Pharaoh, who had transgressed the boundaries of righteousness and justice, embodying the struggle between divine authority and human tyranny, and highlighting the role of prophetic leadership in challenging oppressive regimes.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, expand for me my chest [with assurance]'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of spiritual and mental preparedness for the challenges that lie ahead. Prophet Moses, upon being tasked by Allah to confront Pharaoh, a formidable and tyrannical ruler, prays for his heart to be expanded or enlightened. This prayer is not just a request for courage but also for clarity of mind, wisdom, and the ability to convey the message effectively. It signifies the need for inner peace and confidence that comes from faith and trust in Allah's support and guidance.

translation: And ease my affair
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to Allah to ease one's affairs, indicating a plea for guidance and facilitation in navigating life's challenges, reflecting a deep-seated human desire for divine assistance in simplifying complexities and overcoming obstacles.

translation: And untie a knot from my tongue
interpretation: This verse is a supplication made by Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) to Allah, asking Him to remove the impediment from his speech, so that his people may understand what he is conveying to them. The 'knot' or 'impediment' refers to a difficulty in speech that Moses had, which made it hard for others to comprehend his message. By 'untying this knot', Moses is seeking clarity and eloquence in his speech, enabling him to effectively communicate the message entrusted to him by Allah.

translation: That they may understand my saying
interpretation: This verse is not a standalone verse and appears to be a part of a larger context, likely from the Quranic chapter where the Prophet is being instructed or where a narrative is unfolding. The phrase 'يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي' (yafqahū qawlī) translates to 'that they may understand my speech' or 'that they may comprehend my words.' The interpretation of this phrase suggests that the speaker, likely the Prophet Muhammad, is being commanded or is wishing for his audience to gain a deeper understanding of his message. It highlights the importance of comprehension and reflection upon the words being conveyed, which in the context of the Quran, are considered to be the words of Allah as revealed to the Prophet. This indicates a divine concern not just with the delivery of the message, but with the recipients' ability to grasp its meaning and significance, underscoring the value of understanding and contemplation in the reception of divine guidance.

translation: And appoint for me a helper from my family
interpretation: Moses is asking God to appoint his brother Aaron as his helper and assistant, to support him in his prophetic mission and to share the burden of conveying God's message to Pharaoh, thereby strengthening his resolve and enhancing his ability to fulfill the task.

translation: Aaron, my brother
interpretation: Moses is invoking his brother Aaron, likely to support his plea or request to God, emphasizing their familial bond and Aaron's role as a helper or companion to Moses in his mission or plea.

translation: Strengthen my back with him
interpretation: This verse signifies the request made by Prophet Musa (Moses) to Allah to appoint his brother, Harun (Aaron), as his helper and assistant in his prophetic mission. Musa is asking Allah to strengthen his resolve and capabilities by having Harun by his side, indicating the importance of support and companionship in fulfilling a significant task or responsibility, particularly in the context of prophethood and conveying Allah's message to Pharaoh.

translation: And include him (Aaron) in my affair
interpretation: This verse is part of a prayer that Prophet Moses (Musa) is making, asking God to grant him his brother Aaron (Harun) as a helper and to involve him in his prophetic mission. The interpretation is that Moses is seeking a collaborative leadership or shared responsibility with his brother Aaron in conveying God's message to Pharaoh, thereby seeking strength and support in his daunting task of calling Pharaoh to the worship of one God.

translation: that we may extol You much
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of remembrance and glorification of Allah in one's life. The phrase 'that we may extol You much' suggests a deep desire to engage in the remembrance of Allah frequently, indicating a strong spiritual inclination towards maintaining a close relationship with the Divine. It underscores the belief that through such remembrance, one can attain spiritual growth and closeness to Allah.

translation: And We will remember you abundantly
interpretation: This verse highlights the special bond between the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and Allah, where Allah reminds the Prophet of His favors and blessings upon him, and commands him to remember and glorify Allah frequently, signifying a reciprocal relationship of remembrance between Allah and His Prophet.

translation: Indeed, You were ever watching over us.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah is all-aware and all-seeing of the actions and circumstances of His servants, indicating His omniscience and oversight over the believers, providing them comfort that their struggles and efforts are not unseen.

translation: He said, 'Your request has been granted, O Moses.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the fulfillment of Moses' request to God, indicating that his supplication has been granted. It highlights God's responsiveness to the sincere prayers of His prophets and servants, underscoring the theme of divine mercy and the granting of requests to those who are devoted to Him.

translation: And indeed, We have conferred upon you (O Prophet) a bounty again.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah has bestowed multiple favors upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), highlighting a particular instance or period where He showed special grace or blessing, possibly referring to the conquest of Makkah or another significant event in the Prophet's life that marked a turning point or a notable divine favor.

translation: When We inspired to your mother what was inspired
interpretation: This verse highlights the special connection between Allah and the mother of Moses, where Allah inspires her with guidance on how to protect her son from the evil plans of Pharaoh, illustrating the theme of divine providence and care for the righteous even in the face of adversity.

translation: Cast him into the chest, then cast it into the river, so the river may cast it onto the bank, and he will be taken by an enemy to Me and an enemy to him. And I have cast upon you love from Me, and that you may be brought up under My Eye.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's ability to turn what seems like adversity into a means of protection and care. It shows how God can make even enemies into unwitting guardians of His plan, as seen in the story of Moses where his enemy, Pharaoh, ultimately becomes the one who takes him in. It also underscores the idea that when God is behind an event or a person's life, He can instill love and affection in the hearts of others towards that person, making their path smoother. Furthermore, it suggests a special relationship between God and the individual, where the person's life or actions are under God's watchful eye and are being guided or 'manufactured' according to His will.

translation: When your sister went and said, 'Shall I show you one who will nurse him?' So We returned you to your mother that she might be comforted and not grieve. And you killed a soul, but We saved you from distress and tried you with a trial. Then you stayed for some years among the people of Madyan. Then you came [here] at the appointed time, O Moses.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's providence and guidance in the life of Prophet Moses from his early days. It underscores how various events in his life, including being returned to his mother, being saved from punishment for killing a person, and his sojourn in Madyan, were all part of a divine plan that ultimately led him to fulfill his prophetic mission at the appointed time, illustrating the intricate ways in which God orchestrates the lives of individuals to achieve His purposes.

translation: And I have chosen you for Myself.
interpretation: This verse signifies a special relationship between Allah and Moses, where "اصطنعتك" (I chose/selected you) implies a deliberate and purposeful selection for a specific task or role, and "لنفسي" (for Myself) suggests that Moses was chosen for a unique and intimate relationship with Allah, indicating a special status and responsibility entrusted to him.

translation: Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and do not slacken in remembering Me
interpretation: This verse is instructing Moses to go with his brother Aaron to convey the signs (miracles) from God to Pharaoh, and not to be lax or negligent in remembering or invoking God, implying that they should remain steadfast and mindful of their divine mission.

translation: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has tyrannized.
interpretation: This verse signifies that both Moses and Aaron are being tasked by God to confront Pharaoh due to his excessive tyranny and rebellion against God's will, indicating the severity of Pharaoh's actions and the importance of the mission to admonish or correct him.

translation: And speak to him with gentle speech that perchance he may be reminded or fear [Allah].
interpretation: This verse suggests that when interacting with others, especially those who may be obstinate or resistant to guidance, one should adopt a gentle and soft approach in speech. The underlying idea is that harshness or severity might push the individual further away, whereas a gentle tone could potentially make them more receptive to the message, encouraging them to reflect or heed the warning being given.

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, indeed we fear that he will hasten [punishment] against us or that he will transgress.'
interpretation: Musa and Harun are expressing their fear that Pharaoh might either hasten to punish them or become more tyrannical and oppressive towards them, highlighting their concern for their safety and well-being in the face of Pharaoh's potential reaction to their message.

translation: He said, 'Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of divine companionship and reassurance. When Moses and Aaron express their fear of Pharaoh, God reassures them that He is with them, not just in a general sense, but specifically through His all-encompassing awareness, as He hears and sees everything that is happening. The presence of God with His prophets is not just a matter of proximity, but also of active engagement and support, providing them with the courage and confidence needed to fulfill their mission.

translation: So go to him and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace will be upon whoever follows the guidance.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that the message of God is accompanied by a sign or miracle that validates the authenticity of the messenger, and that those who follow the guidance will be at peace. It also highlights the demand for the liberation of the Israelites from oppression and the cessation of their suffering, underscoring the role of divine messengers in advocating for justice and the welfare of the faithful.

translation: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment is for whoever denies and turns away.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the punishment is destined for those who reject the truth and turn away from it, highlighting the consequences of obstinacy and denial in the face of divine guidance.

translation: He said: 'And who is the Lord of you two, O Moses?'
interpretation: This verse highlights Pharaoh's arrogance and disbelief as he questions Moses about the identity of their Lord, demonstrating his refusal to acknowledge the sovereignty of Allah.

translation: Said our Lord, 'Who gave every creature its creation, then guided.'
interpretation: This verse highlights God's role as the Creator and Guide. The phrase 'who gave everything its creation' suggests that God has endowed each being with the characteristics and form suitable for its existence and function. The subsequent phrase 'then guided' implies that God not only created but also provided guidance, enabling creatures to fulfill their purposes and navigate their existence according to their innate nature and the divine plan. This interpretation underscores the idea of God's comprehensive providence, encompassing both the initial act of creation and the ongoing guidance that sustains and directs His creation.

translation: He said, 'Then what is the condition of the previous generations?'
interpretation: The verse highlights the curiosity and skepticism of those who are not believers, as they inquire about the fate or state of previous generations, likely seeking evidence or signs that would validate the message being conveyed to them, indicating a mindset that requires historical precedent or tangible proof to accept the truth.

translation: The knowledge of it is with my Lord, in a Book. My Lord neither errs nor forgets.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omniscience and infallibility of Allah, emphasizing that He has complete knowledge of all things, including the unseen, and that this knowledge is recorded in a divine Book, often interpreted as the Preserved Tablet or the Mother of the Book. It underscores the idea that Allah is not only all-knowing but also never errs or forgets, providing reassurance of His perfect governance over the universe.

translation: Who has made the earth a resting place for you and has made paths for you in it, and sends down water from the sky, and with it We bring forth pairs of various plants.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's benevolence and power in creating a habitable world for humanity. By making the earth a 'resting place' or 'cradle', God has provided a stable and nurturing environment. The 'paths' or 'ways' He has created facilitate movement and interaction. The verse also underscores the cycle of life through the sending down of rain and the growth of diverse plants, symbolizing the intricate web of life and the interconnectedness of natural phenomena, all of which are sustained by God's providence.

translation: Eat and pasture your livestock. Indeed in that are signs for those endowed with understanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intricate balance and harmony in the universe, suggesting that the provision of sustenance for both humans and their livestock is a sign of divine wisdom and power, intended to be recognized and reflected upon by those endowed with intellect and understanding.

translation: From it (the earth) We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you out again.
interpretation: This verse highlights the cyclical nature of human existence, emphasizing that just as humans are created from the earth, they will return to it upon death, and will be resurrected from it again on the Day of Judgment, underscoring the power and capability of Allah to bring about creation, destruction, and re-creation.

translation: And We had certainly shown him Our signs all together, but he denied and refused.
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy and arrogance of those who reject the truth despite being presented with clear evidence. It suggests that some individuals are so entrenched in their denial that no amount of proof or miracles can sway their beliefs, indicating a deep-seated issue of pride and refusal to submit to the truth.

translation: He said: 'Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and defiance of Pharaoh towards Moses, as he accuses Moses of using magic to threaten their land and way of life, rather than acknowledging the divine message Moses brought. It reflects the resistance of those in power to the call of truth and righteousness, often labeling it as a threat or a form of deception.

translation: We shall certainly bring you magic like it, so make an appointment between us and you, which we shall not fail to keep - neither we nor you - in a place equidistant (for both parties).
interpretation: This verse signifies a challenge and a call for a fair test. The Pharaoh's magicians, after being impressed by the miracle of Moses' staff turning into a serpent, challenge Moses to a contest to prove whose magic is superior. They propose setting a specific time and place for the contest, ensuring that neither party will fail to attend, and that the location will be neutral, underscoring the importance of fairness and impartiality in the competition.

translation: He said, 'Your appointment is on the day of the festival, and that the people be gathered in the forenoon.'
interpretation: This verse is referring to a specific event in the story of Prophet Moses, where he challenges the magicians of Pharaoh. The 'Day of Decoration' (يوم الزينة) refers to a day of celebration and festivity, likely a day when the people would adorn themselves and gather. The phrase 'and the people are gathered in the forenoon' (وأن يحشر الناس ضحى) indicates that the confrontation between Moses and the magicians will take place during a time when people are typically busy with their daily activities, emphasizing the public nature of the event and the significance of the challenge to the magicians. It signifies a test of divine power and truth in a public setting.

translation: So Pharaoh turned away, then gathered his cunning, then came.
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy and arrogance of Pharaoh in the face of divine signs and warnings. It indicates that despite being confronted with clear evidence of Moses' prophethood, Pharaoh turned away, gathered his cunning and resources, and then came back to confront Moses, symbolizing the relentless resistance of those in power against divine guidance.

translation: Moses said to them, 'Woe to you! Do not forge a lie against Allah, lest He destroys you with a punishment. He who forges a lie will indeed fail.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences of attributing falsehood to Allah, emphasizing that such an act can lead to divine punishment and ultimate failure, serving as a stern warning against fabricating lies or misinterpreting divine signs.

translation: Then they disagreed with one another regarding their affair and concealed their counsel.
interpretation: This verse highlights the behavior of those who are divided and secretive in their decision-making, often indicating a lack of unity and transparency among them, which can be seen as a sign of their weakness and internal strife.

translation: They said, "Indeed, these are two magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and take away your most exemplary way."
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of the people to the miracles performed by Prophet Moses and his brother Aaron. The people perceived their miracles as magic and believed that their intention was to dominate them by making them abandon their land and their traditional way of life. This reaction underscores the tension between the established norms and the new message brought by the prophets, as well as the people's misunderstanding of the divine signs.

translation: So gather your strategy, then come to me in a row; and indeed, he has succeeded today who overcomes.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the inevitability of the triumph of truth over falsehood. It is suggesting that those who oppose the truth may devise their plans and strategies, but ultimately, it is those who stand firm and steadfast, holding to the truth and righteousness, who will be the ones to prevail and achieve success on the Day of Judgment.

translation: They said, 'O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological pressure and the test of faith that Prophet Musa (Moses) faced when he was asked by the magicians of Pharaoh to either throw his staff first or let them throw theirs first. The magicians' demand to throw first was a challenge to Musa, testing his faith and trust in Allah. By letting them throw first, it became evident that their magic was outdone by Musa's miracle, as their staffs and ropes appeared to be snakes but were actually just an illusion, whereas Musa's staff turned into a real snake that consumed theirs. This event demonstrates the supremacy of divine miracles over human sorcery and showcases Musa's unwavering faith in the face of adversity.

translation: He said, "Nay, you throw." Then lo! their ropes and their rods - it seemed to him by their magic that they were moving [like snakes].
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological and visual manipulation that can occur when people are under the influence of powerful illusions or deceptions. It suggests that the reality of a situation can be distorted to the point where the observer is convinced of something that is not actually happening, illustrating the potent impact of mass deception or magic on human perception.

translation: So Moses conceived in his mind a [certain] fear.
interpretation: This verse indicates that Moses felt a sense of fear within himself when he encountered the sorcerers of Pharaoh who were casting a spell, but upon seeing the miracle performed by his staff, he realized that it was not magic but a divine sign, thus his initial fear turned into reassurance of his prophethood and the truth of his message.

translation: We said, "Fear not, for you are the higher."
interpretation: This verse is a reassurance from Allah to the Prophet Moses, indicating that he should not fear the Pharaoh or his threats, because Moses is superior in the sight of Allah due to his prophethood and the truth he carries. It signifies divine support and superiority over worldly powers that oppose the truth.

translation: And throw down that which is in thy right hand; it shall swallow up that which they have wrought; they have wrought only the device of a sorcerer, and the sorcerer shall not prosper wherever he comes
interpretation: This verse signifies that the truth will ultimately prevail over falsehood, as represented by Moses' staff consuming the magicians' illusions, indicating that no matter how convincing or elaborate deceit may be, it is ultimately doomed to fail when confronted with the truth.

translation: So the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, "We have believed in the Lord of Moses and Aaron."
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of the supremacy of divine truth over human deception and the transformative power of witnessing a miracle. When the sorcerers, who were initially practitioners of magic and thus representatives of Pharaoh's power, witnessed Moses' miracle and saw that their own magic was surpassed by it, they immediately recognized the divine origin of Moses' action. Their immediate prostration and declaration of faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron signify not only their acknowledgment of the truth of Moses' message but also their recognition of the limitations and falsity of their own craft when compared to divine power. This event underscores the Qur'anic narrative's emphasis on the triumph of faith and truth over falsehood and deception, as well as the potential for transformation and redemption even for those initially opposed to the truth.

translation: He said, 'You believed him before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees and you will surely know which of us is more severe in [giving] punishment and more enduring.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disobedience and rebellion against divine authority. The Pharaoh's threat to cut off the hands and feet of the sorcerers who believed in Moses from opposite sides and to crucify them on palm trees signifies the severity of the punishment for those who defy the established order. The verse also underscores the Pharaoh's arrogance and his claim to supremacy, as he asserts his own power and knowledge, contrasting it with that of Moses. Ultimately, the verse serves as a warning about the nature of tyranny and the consequences of challenging it, while also foreshadowing the ultimate futility of the Pharaoh's power in the face of divine will.

translation: They said, "Never will we prefer you over what has come to us as clear evidence and [over] He who created us. So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this life of the world."
interpretation: The verse highlights the unwavering commitment of the believers to their faith, indicating that they will not prioritize worldly gains or the whims of others over the clear signs and guidance they have received from Allah. It signifies the understanding that true judgment and decision-making should be grounded in the knowledge that this life is transient and that the ultimate reckoning is with Allah.

translation: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive for us our sins and what you compelled us to [do] of magic. And Allah is better and more lasting.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that true faith is not just about believing in God, but also about acknowledging one's mistakes and seeking forgiveness. The verse suggests that the believers are not only seeking forgiveness for their voluntary wrongdoings but also for the actions they were coerced into, in this case, sorcery. The phrase 'the good and the lasting' underscores the notion that God's reward and mercy are superior to any worldly gain or fleeting pleasure, implying that the believers are willing to endure hardship in this life for the promise of a better outcome in the hereafter.

translation: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, then indeed for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark consequences of approaching one's Lord (for judgment) with a history of criminal or sinful behavior, emphasizing that such an individual will face eternal punishment in Hell, where they will neither experience a merciful death nor a life of comfort and peace.

translation: And whoever comes to Him as a believer [who] has done righteous deeds, for them are the highest ranks.
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who come to their Lord with faith and good deeds will be rewarded with the highest ranks in the hereafter, signifying a direct correlation between righteous actions in this life and elevated status in the afterlife, emphasizing the importance of combining faith with good deeds to attain the highest level of divine reward.

translation: Gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow, they will abide therein. And that is the reward for those who purify themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for those who purify themselves spiritually and morally. The 'Gardens of Eden' symbolize a state of eternal bliss and paradise, where the righteous dwell forever, surrounded by the beauty and bounty of nature, represented by the rivers flowing beneath them. The promise of eternity in such a state underscores the permanence and completeness of the reward for those who have achieved spiritual purification, or 'Tazkiyah'. It suggests that the efforts to lead a virtuous life, to cleanse oneself of sin and to cultivate good character, are ultimately and richly rewarded in the hereafter.

translation: And We had revealed to Moses, "Travel with My servants by night and strike for them a dry path in the sea; you will not fear being overtaken [by Pharaoh] nor be afraid [of drowning]."
interpretation: This verse signifies God's intervention in the lives of believers, providing them with a miraculous escape from danger. The instruction to Moses to lead the Israelites through the sea, making a dry path for them, demonstrates God's power to create a way out of seemingly insurmountable challenges. The reassurance to Moses not to fear being overtaken or being anxious highlights the trust believers should have in God's providence and protection. It underscores the theme of divine salvation and the removal of fear for those who are faithful and obedient to God's commands.

translation: So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and there covered them of the sea that which covered them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of Pharaoh's relentless pursuit of the Israelites, indicating that his actions ultimately led to his own downfall and the destruction of his army. The phrase 'فغشيهم من اليم ما غشيهم' (and the sea overwhelmed them with what it overwhelmed them) signifies the complete submersion and engulfment of Pharaoh's forces by the sea, symbolizing the totality of their defeat and the fulfillment of God's promise to save the Israelites and destroy their oppressors.

translation: And Pharaoh misled his people and did not guide [them].
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of leadership and accountability. It suggests that the actions and decisions of leaders have a profound impact on their followers. In this context, Pharaoh's leadership is characterized by misguidance, implying that his influence led his people astray. The verse underscores the responsibility that comes with leadership, indicating that leaders are not only accountable for their own actions but also for the consequences of their guidance or misguidance on their followers.

translation: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy and made a covenant with you on the right side of Mount Tur and sent down upon you manna and quails.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Children of Israel of God's past favors to them. It signifies God's continuous benevolence and care for His people, even in times of hardship and struggle. The verse highlights the themes of salvation, divine covenant, and provision, emphasizing God's role as a guardian and provider for those who are faithful. The mention of specific events such as being saved from their enemy, being summoned to the right side of Mount Tur, and being given manna and quails as sustenance, serves to underscore the depth of God's mercy and the reciprocal nature of the divine-human relationship, where God's blessings are contingent upon human faithfulness and obedience.

translation: Eat from the good things which We have provided for you, and do not transgress in them, or My wrath will befall you. And he upon whom My wrath befalls has certainly fallen.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who are given blessings and provisions by Allah. It cautions against becoming ungrateful and rebellious when enjoying these blessings, as this can lead to Allah's wrath. The verse implies that those who succumb to such behavior are on a path of downfall, both spiritually and morally. It highlights the importance of being mindful of one's actions and maintaining gratitude when receiving Allah's provisions, lest one invites divine displeasure and consequently suffers a downfall.

translation: And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteous deeds and then remains guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, emphasizing that He forgives those who turn to Him in repentance, have faith, perform righteous deeds, and follow the right guidance. It underscores the importance of a combination of sincere repentance, faith, good actions, and steadfastness on the right path for receiving Allah's forgiveness.

translation: And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke from Allah to Prophet Musa (Moses) for leaving his people behind and hastening to the appointed meeting with Allah. The verse implies that Musa was expected to be more concerned about the welfare and guidance of his people, and his haste to meet Allah was seen as a departure from that responsibility. It highlights the importance of a leader's or a prophet's duty towards their community.

translation: They said, "They are just behind us; and we hastened to You, our Lord, that You be pleased."
interpretation: This verse is part of a conversation between Moses and his brother Aaron. Moses is saying that his brother Aaron was left behind by the Israelites and they misled him. Moses is defending Aaron by stating that the Israelites followed him and he was unable to control them, and that he (Moses) has come back quickly to please God.

translation: He said, 'We have tested your people after you, and the Samari has led them astray.'
interpretation: This verse is referring to the incident where the Prophet Moses had left his people in the care of his brother, Prophet Aaron, and had gone to Mount Sinai to receive the Torah. Upon his return, he found that his people had been led astray by the Samari, who had created a golden calf for them to worship. The verse suggests that the deviation of the people was not merely a result of their own actions, but was also a test from Allah, highlighting the inherent weakness in their faith and their tendency to stray from the right path when not directly guided by a prophet. It underscores the theme of the struggle between faith and misguidance, and how easily the latter can take hold when the former is weak.

translation: Moses returned to his people in a state of anger and sorrow. He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make you a fair promise? Then, has the time (of its fulfillment) become too long for you, or have you wished that wrath from your Lord should descend upon you, that you broke your promise to me?"
interpretation: Moses' return to his people is marked by anger and sorrow, indicating the gravity of their actions. He questions them about their commitment to the promise made by their Lord, highlighting a potential breach of faith or a failure to uphold their end of the covenant, which could result in divine wrath. The verse underscores the consequences of failing to adhere to divine commands and the importance of maintaining faith and obedience.

translation: They said, 'We did not break our promise to you by our own will, but we were made to carry burdens of the ornaments of the people, then we threw them, and thus the Samiri cast.'
interpretation: This verse is referring to the story of the Children of Israel and the incident of the calf. The Samiri, who is often interpreted as a person who led the Israelites astray during Moses' absence, is being held accountable for misleading them. The verse indicates that the people claim they were not responsible for breaking their promise to Moses, but were instead burdened with the ornaments of the people they had taken from Egypt, which they then threw into the fire. The phrase 'فكذلك ألقى السامري' (and thus the Samiri cast) suggests that just as the people threw their ornaments into the fire, the Samiri took some action that led to the creation or worship of the calf, implying a connection between the act of throwing the ornaments and the Samiri's role in creating the calf. The interpretation here is that the verse is highlighting the attempt by the people to deflect responsibility for their actions, while also pointing to the role of the Samiri in leading them astray, possibly by using the ornaments to create the calf, symbolizing how external influences or temptations can lead individuals away from their commitments and faith.

translation: So he brought out for them a calf, a body that had a lowing sound, and they said, 'This is your god and the god of Moses, but he has forgotten.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of misguided worship and the tendency of people to be easily swayed by superficial appearances or false promises. The creation of the calf with a sound, despite being an inanimate object, symbolizes the human inclination towards idolatry when deprived of true guidance. It underscores the psychological and spiritual vulnerability that can lead individuals or communities to abandon the monotheistic worship of the true God for a fabricated deity, as seen in the case of the Israelites while Moses was away. This incident serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of idolatry and the importance of steadfast adherence to true faith.

translation: Do they not see that it (the idol) does not return to them a reply and does not possess for them either harm or benefit?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the futility of idol worship by pointing out that the idols cannot respond, harm, or benefit their worshippers, emphasizing the powerlessness of false deities and, by contrast, the omnipotence of the true God.

translation: And Aaron had already said to them before [that], 'O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of following the guidance of righteous leaders and the consequences of being misled. It suggests that the community was tested by the influence of a false or misleading figure, and that they should have instead followed the guidance of Harun (Aaron), who was a righteous leader and a prophet, and obeyed the command of their Lord, who is the Most Merciful (Al-Rahman). The verse implies that the community's deviation from the right path was a result of their failure to adhere to the guidance of their righteous leader and their Lord.

translation: They said, 'We will not cease to be devoted to it until Moses returns to us.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and misguided devotion of those who had begun to worship the calf, indicating that their commitment to this false idol was so strong that they were willing to continue in their error until Moses returned, showing a lack of willingness to listen to reason or correction in his absence.

translation: He [Musa] said, 'O Aaron, what prevented you when you saw them going astray'
interpretation: This verse is a reprimand by Prophet Moses to his brother, Prophet Aaron, for not taking action when he saw the Israelites going astray by worshiping the calf. The verse highlights the importance of leadership and the responsibility that comes with it, emphasizing that those entrusted with guiding others should not remain passive in the face of deviation or wrongdoing.

translation: Will you not follow (the right path)? Have you then disobeyed My command?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that serves as a rebuke, emphasizing the consequence of disobedience. It implies that those being addressed have chosen to follow their own desires or other leaders rather than adhering to the command or guidance given by Allah, thereby committing disobedience. The verse underscores the gravity of deviating from divine commands and suggests a prior warning or directive that was not heeded.

translation: He said, "O son of my mother, do not seize [me] by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You caused division among the Children of Israel, and you did not await [or expect] my word.'"
interpretation: The verse highlights the importance of maintaining unity and harmony among the community, as well as the need to be mindful of one's actions and their potential consequences on others. The speaker is expressing a concern that his brother might accuse him of causing division among the Israelites, indicating the significance of avoiding actions that could lead to discord and strife.

translation: He said: 'What is the matter with you, O Samiri?'
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of the Children of Israel and the incident of the calf. The question posed by Moses to the Samiri indicates a turning point where Moses seeks to understand the actions and motivations behind the Samiri's role in leading the people astray by creating the calf. The interpretation of this verse revolves around the theme of accountability and the consequences of one's actions that mislead others. Moses' inquiry signifies his intent to confront the Samiri about his deeds, reflecting a broader Qur'anic theme of individual responsibility, especially for those who lead others astray. The verse underscores the importance of understanding the reasons and motivations behind actions that result in deviation from the right path, highlighting the moral and spiritual accountability of individuals towards their community and their faith.

translation: He said, 'I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful [of dust] from the track of the messenger and threw it, and thus my soul commended it to me.'
interpretation: The verse is referring to a story where a person claims to have seen something that others did not, and then acted upon it. The interpretation is that the human tendency to follow one's own desires and whims can lead to misguided actions, as the person's own self (nafs) has embellished and made the action appealing to them, illustrating the human vulnerability to being misled by one's own inclinations.

translation: He said, "Then go; indeed, it is for you in life to say, 'No contact.' And indeed, you have an appointment you will not fail to keep. And look at your god to which you have remained devoted. We will surely burn it and then surely scatter it into the sea in scattering."
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of the Prophet Moses (Musa) and the Pharaoh. The Pharaoh, having been warned by Moses of the impending doom due to his refusal to believe and his tyranny, is being told to await his punishment. The verse signifies the inevitability of divine retribution for those who defy God's commands and mistreat His messengers. The Pharaoh's idolatrous attachment to his 'god' (likely a statue or symbol of his power or deity) is to be destroyed, symbolizing the downfall of his power and the futility of his resistance against the divine will. The destruction of the 'god' by burning and then scattering its remains into the sea serves as a demonstration of the powerlessness of the objects of his worship and the omnipotence of the true God. This event is a manifestation of God's capability to humiliate the proud and the tyrants, and it underscores the theme of divine justice and retribution that permeates the Qur'an.

translation: Your God is the one God; there is no god but He; He has encompassed all things in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God, affirming that there is no deity other than Allah, and highlighting His all-encompassing knowledge that pervades every aspect of existence, underscoring the omniscient nature of the divine.

translation: Thus We relate to you [O Muhammad] some stories of what has already preceded; and We have certainly given you from Us a remembrance.
interpretation: This verse signifies that just as the story of Moses has been revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), similarly, other past narratives are being communicated to him through the Qur'an. The phrase 'ذكرا' (dhikra) refers to the Qur'an itself, which is a reminder or a scripture that reminds people of their duties towards Allah and serves as a guidance. The interpretation is that the Qur'an is not just a collection of historical stories but a source of guidance and wisdom bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad from Allah, emphasizing its divine origin and purpose.

translation: And whoever turns away from it, then surely he will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection
interpretation: This verse implies that those who turn away from the message or teachings being referred to will bear a burden or responsibility on the Day of Judgment, suggesting a consequence for neglecting or ignoring divine guidance.

translation: Abiding therein; and evil it is for them on the Day of Resurrection to carry -
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of one's actions in the hereafter, where those who have burdened themselves with sin and disobedience will be weighed down by their own deeds on the Day of Judgment, signifying the gravity of accountability for one's actions in the divine reckoning.

translation: The day when the Trumpet is blown, and We will gather the criminals on that Day, blue-eyed.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, those who have committed sins and transgressed the bounds set by Allah will be resurrected in a state of blindness, indicated by 'blue-eyed' or 'zurqa', signifying their moral and spiritual blindness during their worldly life. The blowing of the Trumpet (صور) marks the end of the world as we know it and the beginning of the Day of Reckoning, where the wicked are gathered in a state that reflects their inner spiritual condition, emphasizing the consequences of their actions and the justice of Allah's reckoning.

translation: They whisper to one another: 'You tarried but ten [days]'
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelievers' astonishment and mockery at the idea of resurrection, as they whisper to each other, downplaying the duration of their stay in the worldly life, suggesting it was merely a brief period, like ten days, thereby underscoring their underestimation of the Day of Judgment's significance.

translation: We know best what they say when the most methodical among them says, 'You have not lingered but a day.'
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the fact that the disbelievers will be astonished on the Day of Judgment when they realize the brevity of their stay in the worldly life. The phrase 'أمثلهم طريقة' (the most methodical among them) refers to the most sensible or rational person among the disbelievers, who will still be astonished at the short duration of their worldly life. The verse is indicating that even the most rational among the disbelievers will be surprised by how quickly time passed, and they will be made to realize that their stay in the world was just a day or a part of a day, emphasizing the swiftness with which the worldly life passes away.

translation: And they ask you about the mountains, so say, 'My Lord will blast them into fragments.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the immense power of Allah, illustrating that the mountains, often perceived as unshakeable and permanent fixtures on earth, will be utterly destroyed and scattered by Allah on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the transient nature of worldly constructs in comparison to Allah's eternal and unchallenged authority.

translation: And He will leave it a barren plain.
interpretation: This verse signifies a state of utter desolation and devastation. The phrase 'قاعا صفصفا' describes a land that has been completely leveled and stripped bare, devoid of any vegetation or features, much like a barren plain. It implies a severe and total destruction, where everything that once stood is now laid to waste, leaving behind a vast, flat expanse devoid of any signs of life or previous habitation. This imagery is often used in the Qur'an to convey the consequences of divine punishment upon disobedient communities, serving as a stark warning to others.

translation: You will not see in it any crookedness or unevenness
interpretation: This verse signifies the perfection and flawlessness of God's creation, indicating that when one gazes upon the universe or the earth, they will not perceive any irregularity or unevenness, suggesting a profound harmony and balance in the natural order, reflecting the meticulous craftsmanship of the Creator.

translation: That Day, they will follow the caller, [with] no crookedness; and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a whisper.
interpretation: On the Day of Judgement, people will be so overwhelmed by the horrors of the scene unfolding before them that they will be unable to speak out loud or make any noise, and the only sound that will be audible is the soft murmur of their footsteps as they follow the caller to the place of reckoning, with all voices humbled in awe and reverence for the Most Merciful.

translation: On that Day, no intercession will benefit except from one to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and is pleased with his statement.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, intercession will be of no avail except for the individual to whom the Most Merciful (Allah) has granted permission and is pleased with their statement or word, highlighting the sovereignty and authority of Allah in determining who can intercede and under what conditions.

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, but they do not encompass it in knowledge.
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of human knowledge in comprehending the divine. It suggests that while humans have knowledge of their past and future, their understanding is restricted and they cannot fully grasp or encompass the knowledge that belongs to Allah.

translation: And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever Living, the Sustainer of existence. And he will have failed who carries injustice.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate accountability and justice on the Day of Judgment, where all faces will be humbled before the Eternal and Self-Subsisting God, and those who carried injustice or wrongdoing will be disappointed and lose out, as their wrong actions will be brought to light and they will face the consequences.

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer - will neither fear injustice nor [any] diminution.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that a person who performs righteous deeds and has faith will not be subject to injustice or loss regarding their rewards. The phrase 'ظلمًا' (zulman) refers to the deduction or subtraction of their good deeds, while 'هضمًا' (haddman) refers to the addition of their bad deeds or being wronged in the evaluation of their actions. The verse reassures believers that their righteous actions will be fully rewarded without any diminishment or unfair treatment.

translation: And thus We have revealed it as an Arabic Qur'an and have diversified therein the warnings that perhaps they will avoid [the punishment] or it would cause them remembrance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purpose behind the revelation of the Quran in the Arabic language, emphasizing that the warnings and threats contained within it are intended to inspire piety and mindfulness among the people, or to provoke a remembrance or reflection that could lead to a change in their behavior or beliefs.

translation: So exalted is Allah, the true Sovereign; and do not hasten the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you, and say, 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and receptivity in receiving divine guidance. It cautions against hastening or trying to grasp the revelation before it is fully conveyed, emphasizing the need to wait for the completion of the divine message. The verse also underscores the significance of seeking knowledge and understanding, as the Prophet is instructed to pray for an increase in knowledge, illustrating the value of continuous learning and spiritual growth.

translation: And certainly We gave Adam a commandment before, but he forgot; and We did not find in him (any) firm resolve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of determination and resolve in fulfilling one's responsibilities and obligations. The fact that Adam forgot the command given to him and lacked firm resolve suggests that a lack of determination can lead to failure in adhering to divine guidance, underscoring the need for steadfastness and commitment in one's faith and actions.

translation: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' they prostrated, except for Iblis; he refused.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of obedience and disobedience, as well as the nature of free will. The command to the angels to prostrate before Adam signifies the honor and distinction bestowed upon humanity by God. Iblis's refusal to comply, despite being commanded alongside the angels, illustrates the concept of individual responsibility and the consequences of choosing to disobey divine commands. It sets the stage for understanding the dynamics between divine will, free will, and accountability in Islamic theology.

translation: So We said: O Adam! This is an enemy to you and to your wife; so let him not get you both out of the Garden, so that you should be unhappy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the warning given to Adam by Allah regarding the enmity of Satan towards him and his spouse, cautioning that Satan's influence could lead to their expulsion from the Garden of Paradise and subsequently to hardship or misery, underscoring the spiritual struggle that humans face in resisting Satan's temptations to maintain their righteous path and avoid the hardships that come with disobedience.

translation: Indeed, it is for you that you will not be hungry therein nor bare.
interpretation: This verse is a promise from Allah to the believers that they will never go hungry or be naked in Paradise, indicating a life free from physical needs and discomforts, where all their necessities are met, and they can focus on spiritual joy and closeness to Allah.

translation: and that you will neither feel thirsty in it nor suffer from the sun.
interpretation: This verse signifies that in Paradise, believers will be free from the hardships and discomforts of the worldly life, such as feeling thirsty or being exposed to excessive heat from the sun, indicating a state of perfect comfort and ease.

translation: Then Satan whispered to him; he said, 'O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that will not deteriorate?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the cunning nature of Satan and his ability to deceive even the most righteous of individuals. By tempting Adam with the promise of eternal life and unending kingdom, Satan exploits Adam's innate desires and ambitions, demonstrating how he can manipulate human psychology to achieve his goals. The verse serves as a warning about the subtle and insidious ways in which evil can infiltrate human hearts, often disguising itself as something desirable or beneficial.

translation: So they both ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with the leaves of the Garden. And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and went astray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human vulnerability to forgetfulness and the inevitability of error, even for a being as noble as Adam. The act of eating from the forbidden tree symbolizes the moment when Adam's attention was diverted from his covenant with God, leading to disobedience. The consequence of this disobedience was not just a punitive measure but a revelation of their true nature, indicated by the exposure of their private parts. The immediate response to cover themselves signifies the innate human tendency to seek modesty and privacy. The verse suggests that human error is a part of the human condition, and it is through acknowledging and learning from these errors that one can begin the journey towards righteousness and closeness to God.

translation: Then his Lord chose him, so He turned to him in forgiveness and guided (him)
interpretation: This verse signifies the special selection and favor that God bestows upon certain individuals, guiding them towards righteousness after they have erred. It indicates a process of repentance and divine guidance that is available to those who have strayed, suggesting that God's mercy and guidance can lead to redemption and a return to the right path.

translation: He said, "Get down from it, all of you, as enemies to one another. And if there comes to you guidance from Me, then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray [in the world] nor suffer [in the Hereafter]."
interpretation: This verse signifies that guidance from Allah is available to help individuals stay on the right path and avoid going astray, both spiritually and in their worldly lives, as long as they follow it. It implies that the consequences of disobedience and straying from the right path are not just spiritual, but can also manifest in worldly hardship and misery.

translation: And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed, he will have a depressed life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who deliberately turn away from the remembrance of Allah and His guidance as revealed in the Qur'an. The 'remembrance' here refers to the Qur'an and the teachings of Islam. The consequence of such aversion is a life of distress and hardship, not necessarily in material terms, but more so in spiritual and psychological terms. The person who turns away from the guidance of Allah is likely to live a life of anxiety, dissatisfaction, and spiritual emptiness, regardless of their material wealth or worldly success. Furthermore, on the Day of Judgment, such a person will be resurrected blind, symbolizing their spiritual blindness in this life due to their refusal to follow the right path. This blindness is not just a physical condition but signifies their inability to see the truth and understand the reality. It underscores the gravity of ignoring divine guidance and the severe consequences that follow in the hereafter.

translation: He will say, "My Lord, why have you raised me blind, while I was [once] seeing?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability of human beings for their deeds in this life. The individual is lamenting their state on the Day of Judgment, having been resurrected blind, despite having had sight in the worldly life. The underlying message is that one's faculties and abilities in this life come with responsibilities; failing to use them for righteous purposes will result in a diminished state in the hereafter, serving as a form of divine justice.

translation: He said, 'Thus came your signs to you, and you forgot them; and thus you are forgotten today'
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the theme of forgetfulness as a consequence of one's actions and state of being. It suggests that just as the individual being addressed forgot the signs (ayat) of God in the past, they will be forgotten or left to their fate on the Day of Judgment. It implies a form of divine justice where the manner in which one treats God's signs and messages is reflected in how they are treated by God on the day of reckoning.

translation: And thus We recompense him who transgressed and did not believe in the verses of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of transgressing the limits set by Allah and rejecting the signs and messages He has revealed. It signifies that those who overstep the boundaries and do not have faith in the verses of their Lord will be recompensed accordingly. Furthermore, it underscores that the punishment in the hereafter is not only more severe but also more enduring compared to any worldly punishment, emphasizing the gravity of disbelief and transgression in the divine reckoning.

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, [as] they walk among their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the fact that previous civilizations that were destroyed by Allah for their wrongdoing left behind remnants and ruins that still exist and are walked upon by people. The verse is suggesting that these remnants serve as a lesson and a sign for those who possess understanding and intellect (أولي النهى), reminding them of the consequences of disobedience and the power of Allah. It is urging people to reflect on the fate of those who came before them and to take heed, so as not to suffer a similar fate.

translation: And were it not for a prior decree from your Lord, it would have been inevitable and a predetermined time.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and patience of Allah, indicating that if it weren't for His prior decree to delay punishment, the consequences for the wrongdoers would have been immediate and unavoidable, tied to a specific, predetermined time.

translation: So be patient (O Muhammad) over what they say, and glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting; and during periods of the night [exalt Him] and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience in the face of adversity and hardship, and encourages the believer to maintain a strong connection with their Lord through acts of worship and remembrance, specifically through the performance of prayer at various times of the day and night, in order to attain spiritual satisfaction and contentment.

translation: And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given certain pairs of them to enjoy, [its being but] a flower of the worldly life, that We may test them through it. And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the believers not to be envious of the worldly luxuries and pleasures that have been bestowed upon some of the disbelievers or those who are not on the right path. The 'provision of your Lord' refers to the spiritual provisions and rewards that come from following the right path, which are not only better in quality but also more lasting compared to the fleeting worldly pleasures. It emphasizes the importance of focusing on what is truly valuable and enduring, rather than being distracted by the superficial attractions of this world.

translation: And enjoin prayer upon your family [and people] and be steadfast therein. We ask you not for provision; We provide for you, and the [best] outcome is for [those who have] taqwa.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of establishing a righteous household by prioritizing prayer and perseverance. It reassures the Prophet that his sustenance is not dependent on the people's actions or their provision for him, but rather it is Allah who is responsible for providing for him. The verse concludes by highlighting that a successful outcome is reserved for those who are mindful of Allah and maintain a life of piety, indicating that the ultimate reward is for those who cultivate taqwa (God-consciousness).

translation: And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them evidence of what was in the previous scriptures?
interpretation: The verse critiques the disbelievers for demanding a miracle or sign from the Prophet, despite the clear evidence and guidance already provided in the previous scriptures. It implies that the message of the Prophet is a continuation and fulfillment of the previous revelations, and that the demand for a new sign is a sign of obstinacy rather than a genuine search for truth.

translation: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it [i.e., the message], they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to seek guidance and justification for their actions. It suggests that people often demand clear signs or messengers from God before they are willing to follow His guidance, and that they tend to justify their past disobedience by claiming that they were not properly guided. The verse implies that God's justice is not arbitrary, and that He provides sufficient guidance to humanity before holding them accountable for their actions.

translation: Say, 'Wait, for indeed we [believers] are waiting.' And you will know who are the companions of the right path and who is [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse is a declaration of a test or trial that will distinguish between those who are on the right path and those who are not. The phrase 'اصحاب الصراط السوي' refers to individuals who are on a straight or correct path, implying a moral or spiritual trajectory that is considered righteous or virtuous according to Islamic belief. The verse suggests that, despite the current uncertainty or ambiguity, it will become clear in the future who is following the right path and who has achieved true guidance ('من اهتدى'). It is an expression of reassurance to the believers that the truth will ultimately be manifest, and that patience is required until that time.

translation: The time of their account has drawn near for mankind, while they heedlessly turn away.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to people that the Day of Reckoning is near, yet they remain heedless and turned away from it. The verse suggests that people are so engrossed in their worldly lives that they have become oblivious to the inevitability of the Hereafter, and are thus unprepared to face the consequences of their actions. It serves as a reminder to turn back to God and be mindful of the accountability that awaits.

translation: Never comes there unto them a renewed reminder from their Lord but they listen to it while they play
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who do not take the remembrance of Allah seriously. The phrase 'they listen to it while they are playing' suggests that they are not giving their full attention to the message, and are instead treating it lightly. The implication is that they are not taking the message to heart, and are not allowing it to have a profound impact on their lives. This verse is highlighting the superficial nature of their engagement with the divine message, and suggesting that they are not truly receptive to guidance.

translation: Their hearts are heedless. And they have concealed their private counsels - those who have wronged: "Is this [Prophet] other than a human being like you? So would you yield to magic while you see [its effects]?
interpretation: This verse highlights the heedlessness and secret plotting of those who have committed wrongdoing. It critiques their gullibility in accepting falsehood, specifically sorcery, despite having the capacity for discernment. The verse suggests that the disbelievers are being deceived by false claims, likening their leaders or objects of their devotion to mere humans, and questions their willingness to follow magical or deceptive practices when they should be able to see through them.

translation: My Lord knows every speech in the heaven and the earth; and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's all-encompassing knowledge, emphasizing that He is aware of every statement made, whether it is spoken openly or kept secret. The phrase 'in the heaven and the earth' signifies the vast scope of His knowledge, indicating that nothing is beyond His awareness, be it in the celestial realm or on earth. The attributes 'the Hearing' (السميع) and 'the Knowing' (العليم) underscore God's ability to perceive and comprehend all things, reinforcing the notion that His knowledge is both comprehensive and penetrating.

translation: Nay! they say, "Confused dreams"; "Nay! he has forged it"; "Nay! he is a poet." Let him then bring us a miracle, as the earlier (prophets) were sent (with miracles)."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn denial and varied accusations of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Qur'an. They dismiss the Qur'an as mere confused dreams, accuse the Prophet of fabricating it, or label him a poet. The verse shows their inconsistency and refusal to accept the truth, demanding a miracle similar to those sent with previous prophets, indicating their skepticism and challenge to the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him).

translation: And never did a town believe before them [then when they believed] which We had destroyed - so will they believe?
