translation: Say, "Is that [i.e., disbelievers' claim of having a god other than Allah] better or the Garden of Eternity which is promised to the righteous? It will be for them a reward and destination."
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the stark contrast between the fleeting pleasures of this world and the eternal reward of the hereafter for those who are righteous. It is suggesting that the true and lasting bliss is the 'Garden of Eternity' promised to the God-conscious, serving as their recompense and final destination, far surpassing any temporary delight or comfort of this life.

translation: They will have therein whatever they wish, [while] remaining [there] forever. [It is] a promise binding upon your Lord, [who is] to be asked.
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless nature of the rewards in the afterlife for the righteous, emphasizing that their desires will be fulfilled without limit or disappointment. It underscores the reliability and obligation of God's promise, suggesting that His commitment to rewarding the faithful is not only certain but also a moral and divine responsibility that He is bound to fulfill.

translation: And [mention] the Day when He will gather them and that which they worship besides Allah and will say, 'Did you mislead these My servants or did they stray from the [right] path?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability of those who are falsely worshipped or revered, alongside their worshippers, on the Day of Judgment. It signifies that on that Day, Allah will question the false deities or leaders as to whether they misled their followers or if the followers went astray on their own accord, thereby emphasizing the responsibility that comes with influence and leadership.

translation: They said, "Exalted are You; it was not for us to take besides You any guardians, but You provided for them and their forefathers until they forgot the Reminder and were a corrupt people."
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to forget the guidance and teachings of Allah when they are indulged in worldly pleasures and comforts. The phrase 'until they forgot the Reminder' suggests that the abundance of worldly goods and the influence of their forefathers led them away from the true guidance and remembrance of Allah. The term 'a people lost' underscores the consequence of such forgetfulness, implying a state of spiritual and moral decay.

translation: They have certainly denied you [the believers] in what you say, so you are not able to deflect [punishment] or [find] help. And whoever among you commits wrongdoing - We will make him taste a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who are being oppressed and are seeking help, but are being denied by those they trust or rely on. It highlights the consequence of rejecting the truth and the futility of seeking help from those who have turned away from it. The verse implies that those who have rejected the message or testimony of the believers will be unable to deflect or avert the consequences of their actions, nor will they be able to provide any assistance. Furthermore, it threatens those who commit injustice with a severe punishment, emphasizing the gravity of their wrongdoing and the inevitability of divine retribution.

translation: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], any messengers except that they surely ate food and walked in the markets. And We have made some of you [people] a test for others - will you be patient? And your Lord is ever Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the prophets were not exempt from the natural human needs and experiences, as they ate food and walked in the markets like ordinary people. The verse is emphasizing that the prophets were humans and not supernatural beings, and this is used to test people's faith. The test is whether people can see beyond the human aspects of the prophets and believe in their message, or whether they are deterred by their humanity. The verse concludes by stating that God is all-seeing, implying that He is aware of the true intentions and faith of individuals.

translation: And those who do not expect [i.e., believe in] a meeting with Us say, "Why were the angels not sent down to us, or [why] do we [not] see our Lord?" They have certainly been arrogant toward themselves and [behave] in great defiance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of those who reject the idea of an afterlife or accountability before God. They demand tangible proof of God's existence, either through the appearance of angels or a direct manifestation of God Himself. Their demand is not driven by a genuine quest for truth but rather by their pride and refusal to submit to God's will. The verse suggests that their insistence on such signs is a manifestation of their deep-seated arrogance and rebelliousness against God's authority.

translation: The day they see the angels - no good news that day for the criminals, and they [the angels] will say, "A barrier [that is] prohibited."
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the stark contrast between the believers and the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. On that day, the angels will appear, and while they will bring glad tidings to the righteous, they will be a source of despair and hopelessness for the criminals. The disbelievers will be met with a stern rebuke, as if the angels are putting up a barrier between them and any potential salvation or mercy, emphasizing the idea that their fate is sealed and they are cut off from any possibility of redemption.

translation: And We shall turn to whatever deeds they (disbelievers, polytheists, sinners, etc.) did, and We shall make such deeds as dust scattered about (i.e. they will be of no profit)
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, all the deeds done by those who have disbelieved or been misguided will be rendered null and void, devoid of any reward or benefit, as if they were mere dust particles scattered in the air, emphasizing the futility of worldly actions when not guided by faith and righteousness.

translation: The companions of Paradise on that Day are better in their abode and more excellent in their resting place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the ultimate destinations of the righteous and the wicked. The 'People of Paradise' are described as having the 'best dwelling place' and the 'best resting place', indicating a state of perfect peace, comfort, and contentment. The use of 'مقيلا' (maqila), which refers to a midday rest or a resting place, signifies not just a final abode but also a state of serene and tranquil repose, free from any hardship or discomfort. It underscores the idea that the reward of the righteous in the hereafter is not just a pleasant abode but a state of being that is characterized by complete peace and satisfaction, untainted by the vicissitudes and troubles of worldly life.

translation: And [on] the Day when the heaven will be rent asunder with [a] cloud, and the angels will be sent down, a sending down.
interpretation: This verse signifies a dramatic and awe-inspiring event on the Day of Judgment, where the heavens will be rent asunder by a dense cloud, and the angels will descend in a grand and majestic manner, highlighting the enormity and solemnity of the occasion.

translation: The sovereignty on that Day will be the true sovereignty of the Most Merciful (Allah), and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, the true authority and sovereignty will belong to the Most Merciful (Al-Rahman), Allah. It highlights the contrast between the power dynamics in this world and the hereafter, where the disbelievers, who often felt powerful or in control in this life, will face a difficult and challenging day, underscoring the theme of divine justice and the reversal of fortunes.

translation: And the Day when the wrongdoer will bite on his hands, he will say, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way."
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who reject the truth and follow their own desires. It signifies the regret that wrongdoers will feel on the Day of Judgment when they realize they had rejected the Messenger and his path. They will wish they had followed the same path as the Prophet, indicating the Prophet's path is the correct and righteous one, and that deviation from it leads to severe consequences.

translation: Oh, woe is me! I wish I had not taken so-and-so as a friend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and remorse one may feel on the Day of Judgment for having chosen the wrong companions or friends in life. The speaker is lamenting their association with someone who led them astray or caused them harm, now realizing that this friendship was a source of their downfall. It serves as a warning about the importance of choosing righteous companionship and being mindful of the company one keeps, as it can significantly influence one's path in life and ultimately their fate in the hereafter.

translation: He verily led me astray from the Reminder after it had come unto me. Satan is to man a deserter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan, who leads individuals astray even after they have been guided by the revelation (الذكر). It underscores the vulnerability of human beings to Satan's influence and their tendency to be misled, emphasizing that Satan ultimately abandons (خذولا) those he deceives, leaving them without support or succor.

translation: And the Messenger said, 'O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as [something] abandoned.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the profound sorrow and disappointment of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as he observes that his people have abandoned the Quran, not just by not following its teachings, but by completely disregarding it, indicating a deep level of rejection and neglect.

translation: And so We have made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. And sufficient is your Lord as a Guide and Helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern throughout history where prophets and messengers of God have faced opposition and hostility from those who reject and defy God's laws. It serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers that they are not alone in their struggles against the disbelievers and that previous prophets have endured similar challenges. The verse then offers reassurance by affirming that God is sufficient as a guide and helper, emphasizing His role in guiding His messengers and providing them with the support they need against their adversaries.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not revealed to him all at once?" Thus [it is] that We may strengthen thereby your heart. And We have recited it to you in a measured manner.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom behind the gradual revelation of the Qur'an. The phrase 'لنثبت به فؤادك' (to firm up your heart with it) suggests that the gradual revelation was a means of strengthening the Prophet Muhammad's heart and resolve in the face of adversity and opposition. The verse implies that the piecemeal revelation helped to reinforce the Prophet's faith and conviction, allowing him to persevere in his mission despite the challenges he faced.

translation: And they do not bring you any similitude (i.e., example or argument) except that We bring you the truth and a better explanation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Qur'an's role as a definitive and superior response to any challenge or argument brought against it or the Prophet Muhammad. It signifies that whenever opponents present a counterargument or a comparable example to dispute the Qur'an's message, Allah responds with the truth and provides a better, more comprehensive explanation, underscoring the Qur'an's unmatched authority and the futility of opposing it.

translation: Those who are gathered on their faces to Hell - those are worse in position and more astray in path.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the stark contrast between those who will be gathered on the Day of Judgment in a state of humiliation and those who will be honored. The image of being gathered 'on their faces' to Hell is a powerful metaphor for the utter helplessness and degradation of those who have rejected faith and lived a life of disobedience. The verse is emphasizing that such individuals have not only chosen the worst possible destination (Hell) but have also followed the most misguided path in life, underscoring the consequences of rejecting guidance and living in defiance of God's commands.

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture and appointed with him his brother Aaron as an assistant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of companionship and support in times of responsibility and leadership. By appointing Aaron as Moses' helper, it demonstrates that even prophets, who are chosen by God for their roles, are not exempt from the need for assistance and companionship in fulfilling their duties. It suggests that having a supportive companion can be a source of strength and comfort, enabling one to carry out their responsibilities more effectively.

translation: So We said, "Go both of you to the people who have denied our signs." Then We destroyed them with [complete] destruction.
interpretation: This verse signifies the severe punishment that awaits those who reject the signs and messages of Allah, emphasizing the total destruction that befalls communities that persist in their disbelief and disobedience, serving as a warning to others.

translation: And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them and made them for mankind a sign. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting divine messengers, as exemplified by the people of Noah. Their denial of the messengers led to their downfall and destruction, serving as a lesson and a warning to others. The verse underscores the severity of the punishment that awaits those who transgress and refuse to heed the call to righteousness, indicating that a painful torment is prepared for the wrongdoers.

translation: And 'Aad and Thamud and the companions of the Rass and many generations in between
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the destruction of various ancient civilizations, such as 'Aad and Thamud, as well as others, to serve as a warning to the people being addressed. The mention of these civilizations is meant to illustrate the consequences of disobeying God's messengers and rejecting His signs, emphasizing the pattern of divine retribution that has occurred throughout history.

translation: And to each of them We gave examples, and each of them We destroyed utterly.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's justice and the consequences of rejecting His message. It indicates that despite being given examples and warnings, those who refused to heed the message were ultimately destroyed. The verse suggests that the destruction was complete and utter, emphasizing the severity of the consequences for those who rejected God's guidance.

translation: And indeed, they have passed by the town on which was rained the evil rain. Did they not then see it? But they were not expecting resurrection.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the irony that the disbelievers, despite witnessing the destruction of previous nations as a result of their disobedience, did not take heed or learn from these historical events. The phrase 'لا يرجون نشورا' (they do not hope for resurrection) suggests that their lack of belief in the afterlife and the accountability that comes with it led to their indifference to the lessons of history. Essentially, the verse is pointing out that their disbelief in the hereafter rendered them insensitive to the warnings and signs provided by the ruins of civilizations that were destroyed for their wrongdoing.

translation: And when they see you, they take you in ridicule, "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a Messenger?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of rejection and ridicule faced by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from his detractors. It underscores the human tendency to judge others based on superficial criteria, such as social status or material wealth, rather than on the truth of their message. The verse suggests that the Prophet's opponents were so entrenched in their disbelief that they could not conceive of someone like Muhammad, whom they likely viewed as unremarkable or unworthy by their standards, being chosen by Allah as a Messenger. This reaction is portrayed as a manifestation of their arrogance and close-mindedness, reflecting a deeper spiritual issue - their inability to recognize the truth when it is presented to them, especially when it comes from an unexpected source.

translation: Indeed, he has almost led us astray from our gods if not that we were steadfast in their devotion.” And they will know, when they see the punishment, who is most astray in path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubborn adherence of the polytheists to their false gods and their recognition, in the face of impending punishment, of their grave error in deviating from the true path.

translation: Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god? Can you then be a guardian over him?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the issue of personal desires and whims overtaking one's moral and spiritual compass. The phrase 'اتخذ إلهه هواه' (one who has taken his desires as his god) suggests that some individuals allow their personal inclinations and lusts to dictate their actions and decisions, effectively making their desires their ultimate authority. The verse is rhetorically questioning whether one can be held responsible or act as a guardian ('وكيلا') over someone who is so deeply entrenched in following their desires, implying a loss of moral agency and accountability. It underscores the challenge of guiding or being responsible for those who are driven by their whims rather than by a higher moral or divine principle.

translation: Or do you think that most of them hear or understand? They are not except like livestock. Rather, they are [even] more astray in [their] way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between those who are guided by reason and revelation, and those who are driven solely by their base instincts. The comparison of the latter to livestock is not a denigration of animals, but rather a commentary on the human condition. Just as animals are guided by their natural instincts without the capacity for rational thought or moral agency, so too are those who reject guidance and refuse to use their faculties of hearing and understanding to discern truth from falsehood. The verse suggests that such individuals are not merely misguided, but are in fact more lost than animals, for they have the capacity for reason and understanding, but choose not to exercise it, thereby exacerbating their own spiritual and moral waywardness.

translation: Have you not considered (the attitude) of your Lord towards the shadow? If He had willed, He could have made it stationary, then We have made the sun an indicator of it
interpretation: This verse highlights God's absolute power and control over the natural world, using the example of shadows and the sun to illustrate His ability to manipulate and govern the universe according to His will, and suggests that the natural world is a reflection of God's omnipotence and a sign of His existence.

translation: Then We drew him forth unto Us, a gentle drawing.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ease with which Allah takes the souls of believers at the time of their death, as opposed to the difficulty faced by those who are not believers. The 'gentle drawing' indicates a smooth and easy transition, reflecting the mercy and care that Allah has for the believers.

translation: And it is He who has made the night for you as clothing and sleep as repose and has made the day a resurrection.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy and care for humanity by creating a natural cycle that allows for rest and activity. The night serves as a 'garment' that covers and protects, sleep is a state of tranquility and rejuvenation, and the day is a time for people to arise and go about their lives. It underscores the idea that the natural world is designed to facilitate human well-being and productivity, reflecting a benevolent divine intention.

translation: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy [i.e., rainfall], and We send down from the sky pure water.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy and provision for His creation. The winds that precede rainfall serve as a harbinger of God's bounty, bringing life-giving water to the parched earth. The 'pure water' sent down from the sky not only quenches the thirst of humans and animals but also purifies and rejuvenates the land, symbolizing God's grace and sustenance for all living things.

translation: That We may bring to life thereby a dead land and give it as drink to many of Our creation, of livestock and humans, many.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy and power by reviving dead lands with rain, symbolizing spiritual renewal for people, and providing sustenance for both humans and animals, emphasizing God's provision and care for all creation.

translation: And indeed, We have distributed it among them so that they may be reminded, but most people refuse to be anything but ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse suggests that despite the clear presentation of the truth and the signs of God's existence and power, many people still choose to be ungrateful and reject the truth, indicating a deep-seated issue of ingratitude and stubbornness among humanity.

translation: And if We willed, We could have sent into every town a warner.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's capability and authority to send messengers to every town or village to warn people of the consequences of their actions, emphasizing the idea that God's power is not limited and that He could have chosen to guide people in various ways, but instead, He has chosen a specific method for conveying His message.

translation: So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it [i.e., the Qur'an] a great striving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of perseverance in the face of opposition and adversity. It instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) not to yield to the disbelievers and to strive against them with unrelenting effort using the Qur'an as a guiding force, indicating that the struggle against disbelief requires a profound and sustained commitment.

translation: And it is He who has released the two seas, this one fresh and sweet and that one salty and bitter, and He has placed between them a barrier and a prohibiting boundary.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom and power in creating a balance between two contrasting bodies of water, symbolizing the harmony and order in the universe. The 'barrier' (barzakh) between them signifies a natural law or boundary that maintains their distinct characteristics, illustrating God's control over the natural world and the intricate design of creation.

translation: And it is He who has created out of water a human being, and has made him a relative by blood and by marriage; for thy Lord is All-Powerful.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's immense power and ability to create human beings from a humble beginning, water, and to establish complex social relationships among them through lineage (nasab) and affinity through marriage (sihir or sihr). It underscores the idea that God is not only the creator but also the one who ordains the social fabric of human society, emphasizing His omnipotence and capability in shaping human lives and relationships.

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which neither profits them nor harms them. And the disbeliever is [often] an ally against [his] Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the misguided nature of those who worship other than Allah, emphasizing that their objects of worship are powerless to either benefit or harm them. It further underscores the attitude of disbelievers towards their Lord, suggesting that they actively support or ally themselves with forces opposed to Allah's will, thereby acting as adversaries or opponents to Him.

translation: And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Prophet Muhammad's role is not to enforce or dictate the outcome, but to convey the message of guidance and warning, bringing good news to those who believe and warning to those who disbelieve, thus emphasizing the responsibility of the individual to choose their path.

translation: Say, "I do not ask you for this message any payment [i.e., reward] except for whoever wills to take to his Lord a way."
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not asking for any material reward in return for conveying the message of Islam. The 'reward' he seeks is not monetary but rather the willingness of individuals to turn towards their Lord, indicating a spiritual and moral recompense. It emphasizes the selfless nature of prophetic mission and underscores the idea that the true 'reward' lies in the guidance and righteousness that result from following the divine path.

translation: And put your trust in the Ever Living who does not die, and glorify Him with His praise. And sufficient is He as the Knower of the sins of His servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of placing one's trust in Allah, who is the Ever-Living and never dies, and to glorify Him with His praise. It highlights Allah's all-encompassing knowledge of His servants' sins, implying that He is fully aware of their wrongdoings and is capable of reckoning with them. The verse encourages believers to have faith in Allah's power and wisdom, and to acknowledge His omniscience, which includes being aware of their innermost thoughts and actions. By doing so, believers can cultivate a sense of accountability and strive to lead a righteous life, knowing that they are ultimately answerable to Allah.

translation: The One Who created the heavens and the earth and all between them in six Days, then established Himself on the Throne, the Most Merciful; so ask about Him one well-informed.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of seeking knowledge from those who are well-versed in the attributes and actions of Allah, specifically His creation of the universe and His establishment on the throne, described as Rahman (the Most Merciful). It suggests that one should turn to someone who is 'well-informed' or 'an expert' (Khabeera) about the Rahman to understand or appreciate the significance of Allah's actions and attributes.

translation: And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate to that which you command us?" And it increases them in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject faith. The demand to prostrate to 'the Most Merciful' (Al-Rahman) is met with ignorance and defiance, as they question the identity of Al-Rahman, indicating their lack of understanding or unwillingness to acknowledge God's attribute of mercy. Their response signifies not just a lack of knowledge but a deep-seated aversion to submission to God's command, which further drives them away from faith.

translation: Blessed is He Who made constellations in the skies, and placed therein a Lamp and a Moon giving light.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's immense power and wisdom as Creator of the universe. The creation of the 'buruj' (constellations or stars) in the sky, the 'sirāj' (sun) as a source of light and warmth, and the 'qamar' (moon) as a reflector of light, demonstrates God's ability to design and order the cosmos with precision and purpose, inspiring awe and gratitude in those who reflect on these celestial phenomena.

translation: And it is He who made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires to be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's wisdom in creating the alternating cycle of night and day. The alternation is not random, but rather serves a purpose - it is for those who wish to reflect and be reminded of God's signs ("يذكر") and for those who wish to be grateful ("شكورا"). The verse suggests that the natural world is designed to facilitate spiritual growth and that the rhythm of day and night provides opportunities for humans to cultivate mindfulness, gratitude, and remembrance of God.

translation: And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in sedateness, and when the ignorant address them [harshly], they say [words of] peace.
interpretation: This verse describes the characteristics of the servants of the Most Merciful (عباد الرحمن), highlighting their gentle and peaceful nature. The phrase 'يمشون على الأرض هونا' (they walk on the earth in a gentle manner) suggests that they carry themselves with humility and modesty, avoiding arrogance and pride. When confronted with ignorant or foolish individuals, they respond with 'سلاما' (peace), choosing to maintain their composure and dignity rather than engaging in futile arguments or conflicts. This verse encourages believers to adopt a similar approach, prioritizing peace and tranquility over confrontation and discord.

translation: And those who spend the night prostrating and standing before their Lord
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristic of the believers who are devoted to their Lord, spending their nights in prayer and worship, alternating between prostration (sajda) and standing (qiyam), indicating their humility, reverence, and dedication to their faith, showcasing the intimate and personal relationship they have with Allah.

translation: And those who say, 'Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell. Indeed, its punishment is persistent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the believers' profound fear of the torment of Hellfire and their sincere supplication to Allah to protect them from it, underscoring the enduring and inescapable nature of its punishment, as indicated by the term 'gharrama' which signifies a lasting and unrelenting affliction.

translation: Indeed, it is an evil abode and resting place.
interpretation: This verse is a severe warning and condemnation. It signifies that something or some place has become extremely undesirable as a dwelling or residence, and a terrible abode. The interpretation is that Hellfire is being described as a terrible and miserable place to reside, emphasizing its unpleasantness and the suffering it entails for those who are condemned to it.

translation: And those who, when they spend, are not extravagant and not niggardly, but hold a just balance between those (extremities)
interpretation: This verse highlights the balanced approach to spending that believers should adopt. It emphasizes moderation in charity and financial dealings, warning against both extravagance (israaf) and stinginess (taqtir). The ideal is to maintain a middle ground (qawaman), suggesting that true righteousness involves being neither excessively generous to the point of waste nor so frugal that one withholds what is rightfully due to others. This balance reflects a broader Islamic ethic of moderation and responsibility in all aspects of life.

translation: And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever should do that will meet a penalty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of righteous individuals who refrain from major sins. It signifies that those who avoid polytheism, unjust killing, and adultery are on the path of righteousness. The verse serves as a warning that committing such grave sins will result in severe consequences, implying a doubling of punishment or facing accountability for their actions on the Day of Judgment.

translation: The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of the punishment for those who commit certain grave sins or acts of disobedience. The doubling of the punishment signifies the gravity of their wrongdoing, while being made to abide in it in a state of humiliation underscores the eternal nature of their suffering and the loss of their dignity. It serves as a stern warning against such actions, emphasizing the accountability of individuals on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds; for those, God will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transformative power of repentance and righteous deeds. It signifies that individuals who turn away from their past wrongdoings, embrace faith, and engage in virtuous actions can experience a profound change in their spiritual state. The verse suggests that God can replace their past evil deeds with good ones, underscoring the mercy and forgiveness that are fundamental attributes of God. It emphasizes the idea that true repentance, coupled with faith and good works, can lead to a complete transformation of one's moral and spiritual standing before God.

translation: And whoever repents and does righteousness, then indeed he turns to Allah a sincere repentance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, emphasizing that an individual who repents and subsequently performs righteous deeds is considered to have made a sincere and acceptable repentance to Allah. The condition of performing good deeds after repentance underscores the importance of a change in behavior following remorse for past actions, indicating a genuine commitment to reform and return to a righteous path.

translation: And those who do not witness falsehood, and if they pass by futility, they pass by it with dignity.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of righteous individuals who avoid falsehood and frivolous behavior. 'Not bearing witness to falsehood' implies that they do not participate in or support untruthful or unjust acts, maintaining their integrity. 'Passing by frivolous talk with dignity' suggests that when they encounter meaningless or inappropriate conversations, they do so with grace and decorum, choosing not to engage in such discussions and instead maintaining their dignity and moral stature.

translation: And those who, when reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not turn away from them as if they were deaf and blind.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristic of believers who, when reminded of the verses (ayat) of their Lord, do not turn away from them as if they are deaf and blind to their truth and significance. Instead, they are receptive and attentive, indicating their openness to guidance and their willingness to reflect on the divine message.

translation: And those who say, 'Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring the comfort of our eyes and make us a leader (Imam) for the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of having a righteous family and leadership. The believers pray to Allah to grant them spouses and offspring who bring them comfort and joy (قرة أعين), indicating a desire for a harmonious family life that is pleasing to Allah. Furthermore, they ask Allah to make them leaders (إماما) for the righteous (المتقين), signifying a desire to be exemplary figures who guide others on the path of righteousness. This demonstrates the believers' aspiration not only for personal righteousness but also to be a source of guidance and inspiration for others, embodying the values of leadership and responsibility in their communities.

translation: Those will be rewarded with the highest [level in] Paradise because of their patience, and they will be greeted therein with greetings of peace and welcome.
interpretation: Those who are patient in their devotion to Allah will be rewarded with the highest levels of Paradise, and they will be greeted with salutations of peace and welcome, indicating the honor and reverence they will receive in the afterlife.

translation: Abiding eternally therein. Good as a settlement and a residence.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Paradise is not just a temporary abode but a permanent residence for the righteous, where they will dwell eternally. The phrase 'حسنت مستقرا ومقاما' (beautiful as a place of settlement and residence) highlights the excellence and desirability of Paradise, indicating that it is a place of ultimate bliss and satisfaction, where believers will find peace and contentment in the presence of Allah.

translation: Say, 'My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication. For indeed, you have denied, so the punishment is bound to come.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who have turned away from their Lord, indicating that their rejection of faith and persistent disobedience will lead to inevitable and inescapable consequences. The phrase 'فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزَامًا' (then it will be inevitable) suggests that the punishment or reckoning for their actions is not just impending, but also unavoidable and binding. The verse underscores the gravity of their denial and the certainty of their accountability before their Lord, emphasizing that their disbelief and falsehoods will not go unanswered.

translation: Ta Sin Mim
interpretation: These are disjointed letters, known as 'muqatta'at', whose meaning is known only to Allah. They serve as a sign of the Qur'an's miraculous nature and a challenge to those who doubt its authenticity, highlighting the tension between the divine message and human understanding.

translation: These are the verses of the clear Book
interpretation: This verse signifies the clarity and evident truth of the Qur'an, emphasizing its role as a clear guide for those seeking knowledge and understanding, dispelling any ambiguity or doubt about its message.

translation: Lest you [Prophet] destroy yourself with grief that they will not be believers.
interpretation: This verse is a reprimand to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for his intense grief and worry over the disbelievers' refusal to accept faith. It is a reminder that his role is to convey the message, and it is not for him to grieve himself to death over their disbelief, as their guidance is ultimately in the hands of Allah.

translation: If We willed, We could send down to them from the sky a sign to which their necks would be humbled.
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability of submission to the truth when it is manifestly revealed. The 'sign from the heavens' represents a clear and unmistakable miracle or proof that, when presented, would compel those who are resistant or disbelieving to acknowledge its authenticity and submit to its implications, symbolized by their 'necks being humbled.' It underscores the theme that divine signs, when clearly demonstrated, are not to be denied or resisted, highlighting the tension between the desire for tangible proof of divine intervention and the human tendency to resist or deny the truth when it is revealed.

translation: And never comes there unto them a Reminder from the Most Merciful, renewed, but they turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and obstinacy of those who reject the message of the Quran. It suggests that the disbelievers are not just ignorant of the truth, but they are also deliberately turning away from it, even when it is presented to them in a new or fresh manner. The phrase 'من الرحمن محدث' implies that the Quran is a continuous and ongoing reminder from the Most Merciful, and yet, the disbelievers consistently turn away from it, indicating a deep-seated resistance to the truth.

translation: They have already denied, so the news will come to them of what they used to mock.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who deny the truth and mock the warnings given to them. It signifies that the consequences of their actions will eventually catch up with them, and they will witness the realization of what they had been ridiculing, serving as a form of divine retribution or proof of the truth they had disbelieved.

translation: Have they not looked at the earth, how many noble pairs We have caused to grow in it?
interpretation: This verse is an invitation to reflect on the natural world and the diversity of creation. The phrase 'كل زوج كريم' (every noble pair) refers to the variety of plants and organisms that grow on earth, highlighting the complexity and richness of God's creation. The verse is suggesting that the diversity and multiplicity of creation is a sign of God's power and generosity, and that it should inspire people to recognize and appreciate His blessings.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reality that despite the presence of clear signs and evidence (referred to as 'آية'), many people still fail to have faith. It underscores the disconnect between the availability of spiritual guidance and the willingness or ability of individuals to embrace it, suggesting that faith is not solely dependent on the presence of signs but also on the receptivity and heart of the individual.

translation: And indeed, your Lord is most surely the Mighty, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual attributes of Allah, being both 'Al-Aziz' (The Almighty, The Invincible) and 'Ar-Rahim' (The Most Merciful). It signifies that Allah's power and mercy are intertwined, suggesting that His invincibility is not devoid of mercy, and His mercy is backed by His unchallengeable power. This duality serves as a comfort to believers, indicating that they are under the protection of a powerful yet merciful Lord.

translation: And when thy Lord called Moses, saying: Go to the people who are wrongdoers
interpretation: This verse signifies the commencement of a divine mission entrusted to Moses, where he is commanded by God to confront a people characterized by their injustice and wrongdoing, highlighting the prophetic role of Moses as a messenger tasked with guiding or admonishing those who have strayed from the path of righteousness.

translation: The people of Pharaoh. Will they not fear God?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that serves as a warning to the people of Pharaoh, emphasizing their need to be mindful of their actions and to adopt a path of righteousness and piety. It underscores the importance of having a consciousness of God (Taqwa) and living in accordance with divine guidance to avoid the consequences of disobedience and sin.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, I fear that they will deny me'
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep-seated fear of Prophet Moses that the people he is being sent to might reject his message, showcasing the anxiety and concern that prophets often felt when faced with the daunting task of conveying God's word to their communities.

translation: And my breast is constricted and my tongue is not eloquent so send for Harun
interpretation: The verse highlights the psychological and emotional turmoil experienced by Prophet Musa (Moses) as he is tasked by Allah to confront Pharaoh. The constriction in his chest signifies the anxiety and apprehension he feels about undertaking this daunting mission, while the impediment in his speech underscores his self-perceived inadequacy to eloquently convey his message. By requesting that his brother Harun (Aaron) be sent with him, Musa is seeking support and reinforcement, leveraging the complementary strengths of his brother to alleviate his own perceived shortcomings, thereby illustrating the human aspect of prophetic leadership and the importance of companionship in facing significant challenges.

translation: And they have a grievance against me, so I fear that they may kill me.
interpretation: The verse highlights the psychological state of the Prophet Musa (Moses) as he expresses his fear of being harmed or killed by his brother Harun's (Aaron's) killers, due to a perceived or real grievance they held against him. It showcases the human emotion of fear in the face of potential retribution, even for someone as divinely supported as a prophet. This verse can be seen as illustrating the complex interplay between divine providence and human vulnerability, suggesting that even those chosen by God are not immune to the fears and vulnerabilities that come with being human.

translation: No! Go forth, both of you, with Our signs; indeed, We are with you, listening.
interpretation: This verse is part of the story of Moses and Aaron in the Qur'an. Here, God is responding to Pharaoh's demand for a sign from Moses and Aaron. The response 'قال كلا ۖ فاذهبا بآياتنا ۖ إنا معكم مستمعون' translates to 'He said,

translation: So go to him [Pharaoh] and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds'
interpretation: This verse signifies the commencement of the prophetic mission of Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh, where they are commanded to approach him with the message that they are messengers from the Lord of the universe, emphasizing the universal sovereignty of God over Pharaoh's claimed divinity.

translation: That you send with us the Children of Israel
interpretation: This verse is a part of the conversation between Prophet Musa (Moses) and Pharaoh. Here, Prophet Musa is asking Pharaoh to release the Children of Israel, who were being oppressed and enslaved by the Egyptians. The verse signifies a pivotal moment in the narrative of the Qur'an, highlighting the struggle for freedom and the confrontation between divine will and human tyranny. It underscores the theme of liberation and the prophetic mission to challenge unjust rulers and societal norms.

translation: He said, 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life?'
interpretation: This verse is part of a dialogue between Pharaoh and Moses. Pharaoh is questioning Moses, reminding him that he was raised among them (the people of Egypt) as a child and lived among them for many years. Pharaoh is attempting to assert his authority and familiarity with Moses, suggesting that Moses should be grateful for the care he received in Egypt. This verse highlights Pharaoh's attempt to manipulate Moses by recalling their past interaction, trying to make Moses feel indebted to him and the Egyptian society.

translation: And you did your deed which you did, and you were among the ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse is a reference to an act committed by someone, likely a significant and negative one, and is tied to their state of being among the disbelievers or ungrateful. The speaker is highlighting a past action that is associated with the person's lack of faith or ingratitude, suggesting a causal or correlative link between their deed and their spiritual or moral state.

translation: He said, 'I did it then, while I was among the misguided.'
interpretation: This verse is part of a narrative where an individual is reflecting on a past action they regret. The speaker is acknowledging having done something wrong and is now admitting to being among those who have gone astray. The interpretation here is that the verse highlights the human capacity for error and the importance of acknowledging and learning from mistakes, serving as a reminder of the need for self-reflection and personal accountability in one's actions.

translation: So I fled from you when I feared you. Then my Lord granted me wisdom and made me one of the messengers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transformative power of divine guidance and support. The speaker, likely Moses based on the context, initially fled out of fear, but upon receiving divine favor, not only was he gifted with wisdom (حكما) but was also elevated to the esteemed status of a messenger. This transformation underscores the idea that divine intervention can turn what might be perceived as weakness or failure into a source of strength and a pivotal role in fulfilling a greater purpose.

translation: And that is a favor with which you reproach me that you have enslaved the Children of Israel
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the favor that Allah bestowed upon the speaker, possibly Prophet Moses, by saving or rescuing him from a certain fate or hardship, and contrasting it with the servitude or enslavement of the Children of Israel. The interpretation here revolves around the idea that the speaker is being reminded of a divine favor they received, which is then juxtaposed with the suffering or oppression of the Israelites, possibly under Pharaoh. This contrast serves to underscore the magnitude of Allah's blessings and the injustice or hardship faced by the Israelites, thereby emphasizing a moral or theological point relevant to the context of the verse.

translation: And Pharaoh said: And what is the Lord of the worlds?
interpretation: This verse is part of the dialogue between Pharaoh and Moses, where Pharaoh questions the identity and authority of the Lord of the universe, indicating his arrogance and disbelief. It signifies Pharaoh's challenge to the concept of a supreme deity governing all existence, reflecting his obstinacy against acknowledging the God that Moses preached.

translation: He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them; if you are certain [in your faith]
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the authority and dominion of the Lord over the entirety of creation, encompassing the heavens, the earth, and everything in between. The phrase 'إن كنتم موقنين' (if you are certain) is a rhetorical device that underscores the certainty and conviction that should accompany the acknowledgment of God's lordship over the universe, suggesting that those who are truly convinced of their faith should also be convinced of God's absolute authority and control over all existence.

translation: He said to those around him, "Do you not listen?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of listening and paying attention to the truth. The speaker is expressing frustration or astonishment that those around him are not heeding or listening to what is being said, implying that the message is significant and worthy of attention.

translation: Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers
interpretation: This verse is a declaration by the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) to his people, where he invokes the Lord he worships and the Lord of his forefathers, establishing a continuity of worship and belief between him and his ancestors, and challenging the polytheistic beliefs of his people by affirming the unity of God worshipped across generations.

translation: He said, "Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is a madman."
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy and arrogance of the disbelievers, who, despite the clear and convincing message brought by the Prophet, resort to personal attacks, labeling him as mad. This reaction underscores their refusal to accept the truth and their reliance on disparagement rather than engaging with the substance of the Prophet's message.

translation: He is the Lord of the East and the West and whatever is between them, if you have any intellect.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the omnipotence of God by referring to His lordship over the entire cosmos, symbolized by the east and the west and everything in between. The phrase is used to assert God's absolute authority and control over the universe, urging those addressed to use their intellect to acknowledge this reality. It serves as a call to reason and reflection on the part of the listeners, inviting them to recognize the oneness and sovereignty of God.

translation: He said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you one of the imprisoned."
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of polytheism and the importance of worshiping Allah alone. The speaker, who is Prophet Joseph, is warning someone that if they were to take another deity besides Allah, he would be among the prisoners. This emphasizes the monotheistic message of Islam and the severe repercussions of deviating from it, as even a righteous individual like Prophet Joseph would face dire consequences for such an act.

translation: They said, "Even if we bring you something manifest (or clear)."
interpretation: This verse is part of a narrative in the Qur'an where a group of people, often interpreted as the magicians or sorcerers of Pharaoh's court, challenge Moses after they have been defeated by him in a display of magical prowess. The phrase 'قال أو لو جئتك بشيء مبين' translates to 'They said, "Even if we bring you something manifest (or clear)."' The interpretation here revolves around the magicians' defiance and stubbornness. Despite being outdone by Moses and subsequently believing in the message of Moses and the God he represents, they still express a level of obstinacy or defiance, suggesting that even if they were to bring forth a miracle or a clear sign, they would still be resistant or challenging. This highlights the theme of obstinacy in the face of clear evidence, a common motif in the Qur'an when discussing those who resist the message of the prophets.

translation: He said: 'Then bring it (the proof or evidence) if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse signifies a challenge to prove the truthfulness of a claim. It is often used in the context of Abraham's dialogue with Nimrod or in the context of Moses' dialogue with Pharaoh, where the speaker is demanding a miracle or a sign as proof of the veracity of the claimant's assertion, emphasizing the need for tangible evidence to support one's truth claims.

translation: So he threw his staff, and suddenly it was a serpent, manifest.
interpretation: This verse signifies a miraculous event where the ordinary becomes extraordinary, symbolizing the power of faith and divine intervention in the face of adversity, as Moses' staff, a simple object, transforms into a snake, demonstrating God's ability to transform the mundane into something extraordinary to achieve a greater purpose.

translation: And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to the beholders.
interpretation: This verse signifies a miracle performed by Prophet Moses as a sign of his prophethood. The removal of his hand and its appearance white (or radiant) to the onlookers is a demonstration of divine power and a challenge to the prevailing Pharaonic claims of divinity, serving as a clear indication of Moses' divine backing and authority.

translation: He said to the chiefs around him, "This is indeed a well-versed sorcerer"
interpretation: This verse highlights the acknowledgment by Pharaoh's courtiers of Moses' exceptional knowledge and mastery over sorcery, underscoring the perceived threat he posed to their beliefs and practices, and setting the stage for the confrontation between Moses and the magicians of Egypt.

translation: He wants to get you out of your land by his sorcery, so what do you counsel?
interpretation: This verse highlights the cunning and manipulative tactics employed by Pharaoh against the Children of Israel, as he attempts to expel them from their land through sorcery. It serves as a warning to the Children of Israel to be cautious and discerning in the face of such deceitful actions, and to consider their response carefully, underscoring the importance of collective decision-making and unity in the face of adversity.

translation: They said: "Put him off, and his brother, and send callers into the cities"
interpretation: This verse signifies the Pharaoh's defiance and arrogance as he and his people demand that Moses and Aaron be detained, and that gatherers be sent to the cities to assemble the magicians, showcasing the Pharaoh's attempt to counter Moses' message with magical prowess, highlighting the spiritual struggle between truth and falsehood.

translation: They will bring to you every skillful magician.
interpretation: This verse signifies the determination and cunning of the opponents of Prophet Musa (Moses), as they vow to bring every skilled magician to confront him, highlighting the intense spiritual and ideological conflict between truth and falsehood, with the magicians representing the epitome of falsehood and deception at that time.

translation: So the magicians were gathered together for a meeting on a certain day.
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between truth and falsehood, as represented by Prophet Moses and the sorcerers, respectively. The gathering of the sorcerers at an appointed time signifies the inevitability of the showdown between divine truth and human deception, with the outcome predetermined by God. It underscores the theme that falsehood, no matter how powerful or organized, is ultimately destined to be exposed and defeated when it confronts the truth.

translation: And it will be said to the people, 'Are you [all] gathered?'
interpretation: This verse signifies a call or inquiry made to humanity regarding their readiness or willingness to gather or assemble, potentially indicating a day of reckoning or judgment when all people will be brought together, highlighting the inevitability and universality of the event.

translation: Perhaps we may follow the magicians if they are the ones who prevail.
interpretation: This verse highlights the internal conflict and temptation faced by the Pharaoh and his courtiers, as they waver between their loyalty to their own beliefs and the evident magical prowess of Moses and Aaron. It showcases the human tendency to be swayed by outward appearances of power and success, and the moral compromise that can result from such inclinations.

translation: When the magicians arrived, they said to Pharaoh, 'Will we certainly be rewarded if we are the ones who prevail?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the materialistic motivations of Pharaoh's magicians, who were more concerned with personal gain than with the truth. Their inquiry about a reward if they emerged victorious indicates that their allegiance was to Pharaoh and his promises, rather than to any higher principle or belief. This sets the stage for a contrast between their worldly ambitions and the spiritual conviction of Moses and his followers.

translation: He said, 'Yes, and indeed, you will then be among those brought near [to Me]'
interpretation: This verse signifies an affirmation and an honor bestowed upon certain individuals, indicating that they are among those who are brought near to Allah, enjoying a privileged status and closeness to Him. It implies a special relationship and acceptance, highlighting their elevated spiritual standing.

translation: Moses said to them, 'Throw what you are throwing.'
interpretation: This verse signifies a moment of confrontation between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh. By saying 'Throw what you are throwing', Moses is challenging the magicians to demonstrate their magical abilities, thereby setting the stage for a divine test of truth against sorcery, highlighting the supremacy of divine power over human deception.

translation: So they threw their ropes and their sticks and said, 'By the might of Pharaoh, indeed it is we who are the predominant.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and confidence of Pharaoh's magicians as they challenge Moses. Their statement, 'By the might of Pharaoh, it is we who will certainly triumph,' reflects their reliance on worldly power and authority rather than faith or truth. It underscores the theme of the struggle between faith and worldly power, setting the stage for a miraculous demonstration of God's power when Moses' staff consumes their deceptions.

translation: So Moses threw his staff, and suddenly it swallowed up all their fabricated lies.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous power of Moses' staff, demonstrating God's support for Moses against the falsehoods and deceptions of the magicians, symbolizing the triumph of truth over falsehood.

translation: So the magicians fell down in prostration
interpretation: This verse indicates the miracle performed by Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) when he confronted the magicians of Pharaoh. The magicians, realizing the truth and the divine origin of Moses' staff turning into a serpent, which was beyond their magical capabilities, were humbled and prostrated in acknowledgment of the truth and in submission to the will of God, thus becoming believers.

translation: They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds"
interpretation: This verse signifies an affirmation of faith in the Lord of all existence, acknowledging His sovereignty and dominion over all that is in the universe. It reflects a declaration of monotheistic belief, recognizing Allah as the Creator and Sustainer of everything.

translation: (The) Lord of Moses and Aaron
interpretation: This phrase is invoking the Lordship of Moses and Aaron, emphasizing God's authority and power over these two significant prophets. It highlights the belief in the unity and sovereignty of God, who is not only the Lord of these prophets but of all creation. The mention of Moses and Aaron together underscores their joint mission and the divine support they received in their prophetic endeavors, particularly in confronting Pharaoh and delivering the Israelites from bondage. The phrase serves as a declaration of faith and an acknowledgment of God's omnipotence and His role in guiding His messengers.

translation: He said, 'You believed him before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic, but you are going to know. I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you all.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of disobedience and deception. Pharaoh, upon discovering that Moses and Aaron had acted without his permission, revealed his true nature by threatening severe punishment to those who had followed them, demonstrating the tyrannical behavior of those in power when their authority is challenged.

translation: They said, 'No harm; indeed, to our Lord we will return.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the believers' unwavering faith and trust in Allah's decree, as they respond to the challenges and hardships they face with the conviction that they will ultimately return to their Lord, who will reward them for their steadfastness and compensate them for their losses.

translation: Indeed, we hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins because we were the first of the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of precedence in faith. By stating 'that we were the first of the believers,' it indicates that being among the earliest to embrace Islam is considered a virtue that can potentially lead to divine forgiveness. The verse suggests that the companions of the Prophet, being the first to believe, held a special status in the eyes of God, and their early adoption of the faith could be a means for them to attain forgiveness for their sins.

translation: And We inspired to Moses, "Travel by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued."
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah is aware of the plans of the oppressors and that He guides His servants to take necessary precautions to escape persecution, indicating a divine plan that encompasses both the actions of the oppressors and the protection of the righteous.

translation: So Pharaoh sent gatherers into the cities.
interpretation: This verse signifies the beginning of Pharaoh's reaction to the signs brought by Moses. By sending out gatherers (حاشرين) to the cities, Pharaoh is mobilizing his resources and people to counter the threat posed by Moses and his message, indicating the escalating tension between the two and the Pharaoh's determination to maintain his power and authority.

translation: These people are indeed a small band
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the minority status and insignificance of a particular group, emphasizing that they are a small, fragmented faction, and is often used to convey a sense of dismissal or belittling of their influence or power.

translation: And indeed, they are certainly, to Us, full of hatred
interpretation: This verse indicates that the disbelievers harbor intense anger and hatred towards the believers, stemming from their rejection of the truth and their envy towards those who have accepted it.

translation: And indeed, we all are cautiously watchful.
interpretation: This verse signifies a state of collective vigilance or caution among a group, emphasizing unity in being watchful or prepared for potential challenges or threats, suggesting a shared awareness and readiness.

translation: So We expelled them from gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse signifies the severe punishment inflicted upon those who reject the truth and indulge in arrogance. The 'gardens and springs' symbolize the blessings and luxuries that the disbelievers enjoyed, which were then taken away as a form of divine retribution, highlighting the transient nature of worldly possessions and the consequences of ungratefulness towards God's bounty.

translation: And treasures and a noble station
interpretation: This part of the verse is likely referring to the rewards that will be given to the believers in the hereafter. 'Konuz' (كنوز) or treasures implies abundant and precious gifts, while 'maqam karim' (مقام كريم) or a noble or honorable station suggests a high and revered status in the eyes of Allah. Together, they signify that believers will be granted not only material riches but also a dignified and esteemed position in the hereafter.

translation: Thus. And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit it.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the destruction of the previous nations who were disobedient and the inheritance of the Holy Land by the Children of Israel was a demonstration of God's power and will to reward the righteous and punish the wicked, serving as a lesson for future generations.

translation: So they followed them at sunrise.
interpretation: This verse indicates that the followers of Moses, the Children of Israel, pursued the Pharaoh and his people towards the east, as they were escaping towards the sea, ultimately leading to the miraculous parting of the sea.

translation: So when the two hosts saw each other, the companions of Moses said: 'We are going to be overtaken.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological state of the followers of Moses when they were faced with the seemingly insurmountable challenge of being trapped between the pursuing Egyptian army and the sea. Their statement 'We are going to be overtaken' reflects their despair and loss of hope, as they perceived the situation to be hopeless. It underscores the human tendency to succumb to fear and doubt when confronted with overwhelming odds, and sets the stage for the miraculous intervention that follows.

translation: He said, 'No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the unwavering faith of the speaker, Prophet Moses, in the guidance and support of Allah. When faced with a seemingly insurmountable challenge, as indicated by the context preceding this verse, Moses asserts his confidence in divine guidance, indicating that even in the most daunting circumstances, Allah's assistance is forthcoming, and that with faith, one can overcome any adversity.

translation: So We inspired Moses (saying): "Strike the sea with your staff." Then it parted, and each part was like a huge mound.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's miraculous intervention on behalf of Moses and the Israelites as they faced the pursuing army of Pharaoh. The splitting of the sea is not just a physical event, but a demonstration of God's power and salvation for those who are faithful and persecuted unjustly. It signifies that God can create a way out of seemingly insurmountable challenges for those who trust in Him.

translation: And We brought near the later ones.
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability and closeness of judgment or reckoning for those who follow in the footsteps of the previous nations that were punished or held accountable. It implies a sequence of events where the later generations or 'the others' are brought near to the same fate or judgment as the earlier ones, suggesting a continuity of divine justice or reckoning across different communities or nations.

translation: And We saved Moses and all those with him
interpretation: This verse signifies God's consistent pattern of rescuing the righteous and the faithful, as exemplified by the salvation of Moses and his followers, highlighting the divine principle of protecting those who adhere to the truth and righteousness.

translation: Then We drowned the others
interpretation: This verse signifies the consequence of disobedience and rejection of divine guidance. The 'others' refers to those who refused to heed the warnings and admonitions given by the prophets, and as a result, they were overwhelmed by a deluge, symbolizing a catastrophic and irreversible punishment. It underscores the theme of accountability and the inevitable fate that awaits those who defy God's commands and reject His messengers.

translation: Indeed, in that is a sign. But most of them were not to be believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reality that despite clear signs and evidence (referred to as 'آية'), many people still refuse to believe. It underscores the challenge faced by those who call to faith, as they often encounter resistance and disbelief from the majority, suggesting that faith is not just about the presence of evidence, but also about the willingness to accept it.

translation: And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual attributes of Allah, emphasizing His unmatched power and mercy. 'Al-Aziz' signifies that Allah is the most powerful being, capable of enforcing His will without any hindrance, while 'Ar-Rahim' underscores His merciful nature, indicating that His power is not exercised arbitrarily but is tempered with compassion and benevolence towards His creation. This duality serves as a reminder to believers of the balance between Allah's justice and mercy, encouraging trust and righteousness.

translation: And recite to them the story of Abraham
interpretation: This verse is an instruction to Prophet Muhammad to recount the story of Prophet Ibrahim to the people, likely as a reminder of his unwavering commitment to monotheism and his unshakeable faith in the face of adversity, serving as an exemplary model for the believers.

translation: When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?"
interpretation: This verse signifies the beginning of Prophet Abraham's call to monotheism, as he questions his father and community about their objects of worship, initiating a dialogue that challenges their beliefs and practices, and sets the stage for his advocacy of the worship of one God.

translation: They said, "We worship idols and remain to them devoted."
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy and misguidance of those who adhere to idol worship, indicating a deep-seated commitment to their beliefs and practices, despite being misguided. It reflects the stubbornness of the disbelievers in holding on to their ancestral traditions and idolatry, even when faced with the call to monotheism and righteousness.

translation: He (Abraham) said: 'Do they hear you when you call (upon them)?'
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the futility of calling out to idols or false deities, questioning whether they have the ability to hear or respond to the prayers of those who worship them. It underscores the idea that these idols are inanimate and lack the capacity for perception or action, serving as a critique of idolatry and a call to recognize the futility of worshiping entities that cannot hear or respond.

translation: or benefit you or harm you
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of idolatry by pointing out that the idols worshipped by the polytheists are incapable of either benefiting or harming them, thus underscoring the powerlessness of false deities and the folly of seeking help or salvation from them.

translation: They said, 'Nay, we found our fathers doing thus.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to follow tradition blindly, without questioning or critically evaluating the actions of their predecessors. It suggests that the act of following in the footsteps of one's ancestors can be driven by a lack of independent thought or a reluctance to challenge established norms, rather than a considered decision based on reason or evidence. In this context, it is being used to illustrate a form of uncritical conformity or adherence to inherited practices.

translation: Have you considered what you used to worship,
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question posed by Ibrahim (Abraham) to his people, challenging their idolatrous practices. The question 'أفرأيتم ما كنتم تعبدون' or 'Have you considered what you have been worshipping?' is meant to provoke thought and reflection on the part of his people regarding the objects of their worship. Ibrahim is essentially asking them to evaluate the worthiness and capability of the idols they worship, implying that these idols are incapable of providing any real benefit or harm. This verse is part of a larger narrative where Ibrahim is engaging in a theological debate with his people, highlighting the futility of idol worship and pointing towards the worship of the one true God. It signifies a critical moment in the Qur'anic narrative where the prophet Ibrahim is not just questioning the practices of his people but is also laying the groundwork for the monotheistic belief that is central to the Islamic faith.

translation: You and your forefathers
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the blind following of ancestral traditions and practices. It suggests that both the current generation and their forefathers were misguided, implying a continuity of error or ignorance passed down through generations. The verse is likely being used to chastise those who adhere to outdated or incorrect beliefs simply because they have been inherited from their ancestors, rather than being based on truth or evidence.

translation: They are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the speaker, likely referring to the Prophet Ibrahim as understood from the context of the surrounding verses, is declaring that his enemies are, in fact, enemies to him alone except for the Lord of the worlds, who is the universal Lord and Sustainer. It highlights the distinction between personal enmity and the universal sovereignty and justice of Allah. The verse underscores the idea that while individuals may have personal enemies, the true enemy of righteousness is ultimately opposed to the will of Allah. It emphasizes the supremacy and universality of Allah's authority over personal vendettas or conflicts.

translation: Who created me, and He guides me.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the same Being who has the power to create is also capable of guiding. It underscores the idea that creation and guidance are not separate entities but are interconnected, emphasizing the omnipotence and benevolence of the Creator towards His creation, ensuring that He not only brings into existence but also provides the means and direction for sustenance and purpose.

translation: And it is He who feeds me and gives me drink
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound dependence of human beings on Allah's provision and care. The act of eating and drinking, which are fundamental to human survival, are framed not just as natural or mundane activities, but as blessings directly bestowed by Allah. It underscores the theme of gratitude and recognition of Allah's sustenance in the lives of believers, inviting a deeper reflection on the source of all nourishment and the providence that underlies human existence.

translation: And when I am ill, it is He who cures me
interpretation: This verse highlights the unique role of Allah as the ultimate healer. The use of 'يشفين' (yashfeen), which is a causative form of 'shifa'' (healing), emphasizes that true healing comes from Allah. It underscores the Islamic belief in Allah's omnipotence and His control over all aspects of life, including health and sickness. The verse encourages believers to turn to Allah in times of illness, seeking His mercy and healing.

translation: And who causes me to die, then gives me life
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence of Allah, specifically His power over life and death. The speaker is affirming their faith in Allah's ability to not only cause death but also to revive or resurrect. This underscores the Islamic belief in the afterlife and the Day of Judgment, where individuals are brought back to life to face accountability for their deeds.

translation: And the One who I hope will forgive my sin on the Day of Judgment
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and awareness of one's own fallibility even among the righteous. The speaker, likely a prophet or a righteous individual, acknowledges their own shortcomings and expresses hope for divine forgiveness on the Day of Judgment, demonstrating an understanding that even the most devout are not immune to error and that divine mercy is essential for salvation.

translation: My Lord, grant me wisdom and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication from Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) to Allah, asking for wisdom and to be joined with the righteous. The request for wisdom (حكما) signifies a deep desire for understanding and the ability to judge and act justly. Being 'joined with the righteous' implies a longing not just for personal righteousness but also for being part of a community of believers who uphold justice, compassion, and truth. This verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and moral integrity, and the aspiration to be among those who are considered righteous in the sight of Allah.

translation: And give me a good reputation among later generations
interpretation: This verse is a supplication to Allah to grant the speaker a good reputation and a positive legacy among future generations, so that they are remembered and spoken of in a favorable manner.

translation: And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of Delight
