translation: You do not guide whom you love, but God guides whom He wills, and He is most knowing of the guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of human agency in guiding others towards righteousness, emphasizing that true guidance is a divine prerogative. It underscores the idea that even the Prophet, despite his best efforts, cannot ensure the guidance of those he cares about, as guidance is ultimately determined by God's will. The verse thus serves as a reminder of the supremacy of divine wisdom and the futility of human endeavor without divine support, pointing to the importance of humility and reliance on God's knowledge and plan.

translation: And they say, "If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be swept from our land." Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.
interpretation: The verse highlights the irony in the disbelievers' demand for a miracle or a sign from the Prophet (peace be upon him) as a condition for following him, despite the fact that they were already living in a sacred and secure environment, the city of Mecca, which was blessed with abundant provisions and peace, a blessing they should have recognized as a sign of God's favor and a reason to be grateful and believe.

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed, which was ungrateful for its means of livelihood! And those are their dwellings, which have not been inhabited after them except a little. And indeed, We have been the inheritors.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those communities that become complacent and arrogant due to their material wealth and prosperity. It highlights the transient nature of worldly success and the inevitability of divine retribution when a society becomes morally corrupt and forgets the purpose of its creation. The verse reminds us that true inheritance and lasting legacy belong to God, emphasizing the importance of living a righteous life rather than merely enjoying temporary worldly gains.

translation: And never would your Lord destroy the cities until He had sent to their mother a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not destroy the cities except while their people were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights that divine punishment is not arbitrary, but rather it is preceded by a clear warning and guidance through the sending of a messenger to convey God's message to the people. The destruction or punishment of a community occurs only when its people have willfully persisted in wrongdoing despite having been given the opportunity to understand and heed God's signs and warnings.

translation: And whatever you have been given is but a provision of the life of this world and its adornment, whereas what is with Allah is better and more lasting; so will you not use reason?
interpretation: This verse is cautioning against the fleeting nature of worldly possessions and pleasures. It is highlighting the distinction between the temporary and perishable nature of worldly goods and the eternal and enduring nature of what is with God, suggesting that one should prioritize the latter over the former, and implying that those who do not are lacking in understanding or wisdom.

translation: Is he who has a promise from Us which is good, and he will meet it, like one whom We have granted the enjoyment of worldly life, then on the Day of Judgment, he will be among those brought forth (for punishment)?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between those who have been promised a good reward in the hereafter and those who are merely granted temporary worldly pleasures. It serves as a warning that the fleeting enjoyment of worldly life does not exempt one from accountability on the Day of Judgment, whereas those who have been promised a good reward are assured of meeting their recompense, underscoring the importance of focusing on the hereafter rather than being deceived by the transient nature of worldly life.

translation: And [mention] the Day when He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' that you used to claim?"
interpretation: This verse signifies a day when God will interrogate those who associated partners with Him, challenging their false claims and confronting them with the reality of their polytheism, highlighting the accountability for their beliefs and actions on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Those against whom the word (of judgment) has been pronounced will say, 'Our Lord, these are they whom we led astray. We led them astray as we ourselves were astray. We declare our innocence before You. It was not us that they worshipped.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability of individuals for their own actions on the Day of Judgment. The leaders or influencers who misguided others will be held responsible, and they will attempt to deflect their responsibility by claiming they were also misled. However, this deflection will not absolve them of their guilt. The verse underscores the theme that every individual is accountable for their choices and actions, and that blame-shifting will not be an effective strategy on the Day of Reckoning.

translation: And it will be said, "Call your 'partners' " Then they will call them, but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment. If only they were guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of relying on false deities or partners attributed to God during times of distress. It signifies that on the Day of Judgment, when faced with the inevitability of punishment, those who had associated others with God in worship will call upon these false deities for help. However, these deities will not respond, illustrating their powerlessness and the error of the polytheistic beliefs held by those who invoked them. The verse serves as a poignant reminder of the consequences of deviating from the path of righteousness and the exclusive worship of God, underscoring that true guidance lies in the worship and obedience to God alone.

translation: And on the Day when He will call unto them, and say: "What answer gave ye to the Messengers?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability of nations and communities on the Day of Judgment for their response to the messengers sent by God. It signifies that the messengers were not just sent to convey a message, but to elicit a response, and that response will be scrutinized on the Day of Judgment, underscoring the importance of heeding divine guidance.

translation: So the news (or signs) on that day will be blinded (or obscured) to them, so they will not ask (one another) questions.
interpretation: This verse suggests that on the Day of Judgment, the truth about their deeds and the messages they were given in life will become obscured to those who disbelieved or were wrongdoers, to the point where they will be unable to ask questions or seek clarification about their fate or the reasons behind it, implying a state of regret and realization too late to be of any avail.

translation: But as for him who repents and believes and does righteous deeds, then perhaps he will be among the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincere repentance, faith, and righteous deeds in achieving success. It suggests that one who genuinely turns away from their past wrongdoings, has faith, and performs good actions may be among those who attain true success or salvation, indicating a hopeful and positive outcome for those who reform and live a virtuous life.

translation: And your Lord creates and chooses whom He wills; they have not the power of choice. Glory be to God, and exalted be He above what they associate.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's absolute sovereignty and freedom in creation and decision-making. It asserts that God creates and chooses as He wills, without any constraint or external influence. The phrase 'ما كان لهم الخيرة' (they have not the power of choice) underscores that humans or other beings do not have the capacity to dictate or influence God's decisions. The verse concludes with 'سبحان الله وتعالى عما يشركون' (Glory be to God, and exalted be He above what they associate), which is a declaration of God's transcendence and purity, emphasizing that He is far above the false associations or partners that people attribute to Him. This serves as a rebuke to the practice of associating other beings or entities with God in worship or attributing divine qualities to them, affirming the doctrine of Tawhid (the oneness of God).

translation: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's all-encompassing knowledge, emphasizing that He is aware not only of what people outwardly express but also of the innermost thoughts and feelings they keep hidden. It underscores the idea that God's understanding is not limited to external actions or declarations but extends to the deepest, most private aspects of human consciousness, suggesting a profound level of divine awareness and insight into human nature.

translation: And He is Allah, there is no deity except Him. To Him belongs [all] praise in the first [life] and the Hereafter. And His is the [final] judgment, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and uniqueness of God, affirming that He is the sole deity worthy of worship. It highlights that all praise belongs to Him in both the life of this world and the hereafter, underscoring His eternal and omnipresent nature. Furthermore, it asserts that all judgment and authority rest with Him, and ultimately, all beings will return to Him for accountability and judgment.

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, which deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear?"
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that challenges the polytheists to consider a hypothetical scenario where God makes the night perpetual, lasting until the Day of Judgment. The verse is meant to highlight the absurdity of attributing partners to God, as it is God who has the power to control the natural world, including the cycle of day and night. By asking if they would be able to find an alternative deity to bring them light, the verse emphasizes the polytheists' reliance on God and their inability to find substitutes for His blessings. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the futility of seeking alternatives to His power, thus urging the polytheists to listen to the truth and acknowledge God's sole authority.

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the day continuous until the Day of Resurrection, who is a deity other than Allah who could bring you a night in which you may rest? Then will you not see?"
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the omnipotence of Allah and the natural order He has established. It rhetorically asks people to consider a hypothetical scenario where daylight is perpetual until the Day of Judgment, and then questions who else but Allah could bring about the night for rest. The underlying message is to acknowledge Allah's sovereignty and the cyclical nature of day and night as a sign of His power and wisdom, prompting humans to reflect on their surroundings and the creator behind it.

translation: And of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and that you may seek from His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy towards humanity by creating a cycle of night and day, allowing humans to rest and seek provision, ultimately guiding them towards gratitude for these blessings.

translation: And [mention] the Day when He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' that you used to claim?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the Day of Judgment when God will question those who associated partners with Him, about the false deities they claimed to be gods alongside Him, exposing the falsity of their polytheistic beliefs and their accountability for such claims.

translation: And We will draw out from every nation a witness, and We will say, "Bring your proof," and they will know that the truth is with Allah, and lost from them is that which they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability of nations and communities on the Day of Judgment. The 'witness' (شهيدا) from each community signifies a leader or representative who will testify to the deeds of their people. When asked to provide proof (برهانكم) for their actions and beliefs, they will realize that the truth belongs to Allah alone, and their false attributions and fabrications will be rendered null and void, illustrating the futility of their worldly deceptions.

translation: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he tyrannized them. And We gave him of treasures whose keys would burden a band of strong men; thereupon his people said to him, "Do not exult. Indeed, God does not like the exultant."
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against arrogance and excessive pride in one's wealth and material possessions. It highlights that true strength and success are not measured by the accumulation of riches, but by humility, righteousness, and a healthy relationship with God. The story of Qarun (Korah) is used as a cautionary tale to illustrate the consequences of becoming overly proud and disobedient due to one's wealth, and to emphasize that God does not favor those who excessively rejoice in their worldly gains.

translation: But seek, through that which Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and [yet], do not forget your share of the world. And do good as Allah has done good to you. And desire not corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not like corrupters.
interpretation: This verse is urging believers to strike a balance between their worldly life and their pursuit of the hereafter. It advises them to seek the rewards of the afterlife through the resources and blessings they have been given by Allah, while not neglecting their share of worldly pleasures and responsibilities. It encourages them to be virtuous and generous, just as Allah has been generous to them. At the same time, it warns against causing corruption and disorder on earth, as Allah does not love those who spread mischief. The verse promotes a lifestyle that is mindful of both spiritual and worldly duties, emphasizing the importance of being a positive force in society.

translation: He said, "I was only given it because of knowledge I have." Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him of generations those who were greater than him in power and greater in accumulation [of wealth]? But the criminals, about their sins, will not be asked.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the arrogance of those who attribute their success or wealth to their own knowledge or abilities, rather than acknowledging God's role in their achievements. It suggests that such individuals forget or ignore the fact that God has destroyed previous civilizations that were stronger and more numerous than they are, implying that their own success is not solely due to their own merits, but is rather a test from God. The verse is cautioning against the complacency and lack of accountability that can come with success, as those who are guilty (of such arrogance) will not be questioned about their sins, implying that their punishment is a foregone conclusion.

translation: So he went forth before his people in his pomp. Those who were desirous of the worldly life said, 'Oh, would that we had like what Qarun has been given! Indeed, he is one of great fortune.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the envy and materialism of those who prioritize worldly life. They are drawn to Qarun's wealth and status, illustrating how the pursuit of earthly possessions can lead people to admire and aspire to the fortunes of others, even if they are attained unjustly. It underscores the human tendency to measure success and happiness by material standards, often overlooking the spiritual and moral implications of one's wealth and actions.

translation: And those who have been given knowledge say, 'Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and none are granted it except the patient.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the fleeting nature of worldly rewards and the enduring reward of the Hereafter. The people of knowledge emphasize that the true and lasting reward comes from Allah for those who believe and perform righteous deeds. They also underscore that this reward is reserved for those who possess the quality of patience, indicating that perseverance through trials and hardships is a crucial characteristic of those who will attain this divine recompense.

translation: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling. And there was for him no company to help him other than Allah, and he was not among those who can defend themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of arrogance and disobedience. The story is often associated with Qarun, a man from the time of Moses who was known for his immense wealth and arrogance. The verse indicates that he and his wealth were swallowed by the earth as a punishment for his actions. The phrase 'فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله' (and he had no group to help him against Allah) suggests that despite his wealth and influence, Qarun had no one to save him from Allah's punishment, emphasizing the futility of earthly power against divine judgment. Furthermore, 'وما كان من المنتصرين' (and he was not among those who can defend themselves) reinforces the idea that Qarun was unable to protect himself, underscoring the theme that true security and salvation come from Allah alone.

translation: And those who yesterday were longing to be in his place are now saying, 'Ah, it is indeed Allah who expands the provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. If not that Allah had conferred a favor on us, He would have caused it to sink with us. And indeed, it is not but the disbelievers that do not prosper'.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of gratitude and recognition of God's bounty. The people who previously envied the blessings of others now, upon reflection of their own circumstances, acknowledge that God is the one who expands or restricts provision to His servants as He wills. They come to realize that it is God's favor that has spared them from adversity, and they understand that it is the disbelievers, or those ungrateful for God's blessings, who ultimately do not prosper.

translation: That is the Home of the Hereafter. We shall assign it to those who do not desire exaltation in the earth, nor (do they desire) corruption. And the (blissful) end is for the God-fearing.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate abode of the Hereafter is reserved for those who refrain from seeking superiority and causing corruption on earth, highlighting the importance of humility and righteousness. It underscores that the final outcome is favorable for those who are mindful of their duties towards Allah and maintain a righteous lifestyle, indicating that their actions will be rewarded in the Hereafter.

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it; and whoever comes with an evil deed - then those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except [as much as] what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the generosity and justice of Allah. It indicates that those who perform good deeds will be rewarded with something even better than their actions, showcasing Allah's generosity. On the other hand, it states that those who commit evil deeds will be punished in a manner that is commensurate with their actions, illustrating Allah's justice. The verse emphasizes the principle of reciprocity in Allah's judgment, where the reward or punishment is directly related to the nature of the deed.

translation: Indeed, He who has imposed the Qur'an upon you will surely return you to a place of return. Say, 'My Lord is most knowing of who has brought guidance and who is in manifest error.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate triumph of divine guidance over human endeavors, assuring the Prophet Muhammad that he will be returned to a place or state of great significance (معاد), likely referring to either a triumphant return to Makkah or a high status in the hereafter, as a result of the revelation of the Qur'an. It contrasts those who are guided by the truth, brought forth by the Qur'an, with those lost in manifest error, underscoring God's omniscience in discerning between the two paths.

translation: And you did not expect that the Book would be cast to you except as a mercy from your Lord. So do not be a supporter of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that his receipt of the Quran was a mercy from his Lord, and he should not be swayed or influenced by the disbelievers. It serves as a warning against being an ally or supporter of those who reject the truth, emphasizing the importance of maintaining his prophetic mission with integrity and independence from external pressures or expectations.

translation: And do not be turned away from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you. And invite to your Lord. And never be of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against being deterred or swayed from conveying and upholding the message of Allah, once it has been revealed. It emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in calling people to the path of their Lord, and cautions against succumbing to pressures or influences that might lead one to associate partners with Allah, thereby compromising the fundamental principle of Tawhid (the oneness of God). It underscores the need for unwavering commitment to the divine message and the avoidance of any form of polytheism or compromise on the core beliefs of Islam.

translation: And do not invoke with Allah another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face (Essence). To Him belongs the Judgment, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God, warning against associating any other deity with Him. It highlights God's eternal nature, stating that everything perishes except His essence, and asserts His sole authority over judgment, to whom all will return.

translation: In the name of Allah, the most compassionate, the most merciful, Alif, Laam, Meem.
interpretation: These are disjointed letters, known as 'muqatta'at', which appear at the beginning of several chapters in the Qur'an. The interpretation of these letters is a subject of much debate among scholars. One interpretation is that they serve as a challenge to the Arabs of the time, who were known for their mastery of language and poetry, to understand or replicate the Qur'an, given that it begins with letters that, on their own, seem nonsensical or lacking in clear meaning. This interpretation underscores the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, suggesting that despite being composed of the same letters and sounds familiar to the Arabs, it presents a unique and inimitable form of expression that conveys divine guidance and wisdom.

translation: Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, 'We believe,' and will not be tested?
interpretation: This verse highlights that merely professing faith is not enough; true faith is tested through trials and tribulations. It signifies that the declaration of faith must be accompanied by the resilience to face challenges, indicating that faith is not just a verbal affirmation but a steadfast commitment that withstands adversity.

translation: And We have certainly tested those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.
interpretation: This verse signifies that God tests His servants through various trials to distinguish between those who are truthful in their faith and those who are false. It implies that the trials and tribulations faced by the believers are a means to purify them and to reveal their true character, and that God is all-knowing and will ultimately distinguish between the sincere and the insincere.

translation: Do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us? How bad is their judgment!
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who commit evil deeds, suggesting that they think they can outrun or escape Allah's punishment. The phrase 'ساء ما يحكمون' (how bad is their judgment) indicates that their belief that they can outsmart or evade divine retribution is a grave misjudgment, highlighting the folly of their actions and the certainty of their accountability before Allah.

translation: Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, then indeed the term decreed by Allah is coming. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is encouraging believers to maintain their faith and good deeds, as they are working towards a meeting with Allah, which is inevitable. It implies that one should live their life with the awareness that they will be held accountable for their actions in the hereafter, and thus, should strive to be righteous and obedient to Allah's commands. The verse also reassures that Allah is all-hearing and all-knowing, suggesting that He is fully aware of one's intentions and actions, and will judge accordingly.

translation: And whoever strives, only strives for their own soul. Indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the effort or struggle (jihad) one undertakes is ultimately for their own benefit. It signifies that the actions and endeavors of an individual, particularly in the context of striving for righteousness or against evil, are for their own spiritual growth and salvation. The verse also underscores the self-sufficiency of God, stating that He is in no need of the worlds, implying that the purpose and outcome of human actions are primarily related to the individuals themselves rather than affecting God's state or needs.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely absolve them of their misdeeds and will reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's justice and mercy. It indicates that those who have faith and perform good deeds will have their bad deeds forgiven and will be rewarded with the best outcome for their good actions, emphasizing the idea that God's reward is always better than what humans can achieve through their deeds.

translation: And We have commanded humans to treat their parents with kindness. But if they strive against you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the delicate balance between the obligation to be kind to one's parents and the imperative to maintain one's faith and not succumb to actions that contradict it, even if such actions are advocated by one's parents. It underscores the principle that one's ultimate allegiance is to God and that one should not obey parents if they attempt to lead one astray from the path of righteousness, particularly in matters of associating partners with God without having any knowledge or evidence to support such actions. The verse serves as a reminder that all actions will be accounted for in the hereafter, emphasizing the importance of making decisions based on faith and knowledge rather than blind obedience to parental authority.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely include them among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's promise to include believers who perform righteous deeds among the righteous, suggesting that their actions will be recognized and rewarded, and they will be considered part of a larger community of virtuous individuals.

translation: And of the people is he who says, 'We believe in Allah'; but when he is harmed because of Allah, he considers the trial of the people as [if it were] the punishment of Allah. And if there comes victory from your Lord, they say, 'Indeed, we were with you.' Is not Allah more knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the hypocrisy of certain individuals who claim to have faith in Allah but when faced with persecution or hardship because of their claimed faith, they waver and prioritize avoiding the affliction of people over standing firm in their faith, equating the people's persecution with Allah's punishment. It further points out their opportunistic nature by stating that if they were to receive victory or support from Allah, they would claim to have been on the side of the believers all along. The verse concludes by rhetorically asking if Allah is not more aware of what is truly in the hearts of all people, implying that such hypocrisy is not hidden from Allah.

translation: And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omniscience and His ability to distinguish between true believers and hypocrites. It suggests that through trials and experiences, the true nature of individuals will be revealed, allowing God to manifest the reality of their faith or hypocrisy. It underscores the theme that God is all-knowing and that He will make evident the sincerity or lack thereof of those who claim faith.

translation: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will carry your sins." But they will not carry any of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deception and false promise of the disbelievers towards the believers, where they ask the believers to follow their path and claim they will bear the sins of the believers. However, this is a lie as they will not be able to carry any of the believers' sins. It underscores the accountability of individuals for their actions and the futility of relying on others to absolve one's sins.

translation: And they will surely bear their own burdens, and burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate.
interpretation: This verse is warning that those who mislead others will not only bear the burden of their own sins, but also the burden of the sins of those they misled. On the Day of Judgment, they will be questioned about the falsehoods they fabricated, indicating that they will be held accountable for their actions and the harm they caused to others through their deception.

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, then the flood overtook them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the prolonged period of Prophet Noah's preaching to his people, emphasizing the patience and perseverance required in conveying God's message. The fact that despite 950 years of effort, the people remained unjust and were eventually punished by the flood, underscores the severity of their wrongdoing and the inevitability of divine justice when people persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing.

translation: So We saved him and those with the ship, and We made it a sign for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse signifies God's power and mercy in saving Prophet Noah and those with him on the ark, making it a symbol or lesson for all people, emphasizing the consequences of disobedience and the reward for faithfulness.

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said to his people, "Worship Allah and fear Him. That is best for you, if you should know."
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental message that Prophet Ibrahim conveyed to his people, emphasizing the importance of worshiping Allah alone and being mindful of Him. The phrase 'ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون' (that is better for you, if you only knew) suggests that the true benefit of worshiping and fearing Allah is not immediately apparent to those who are not guided or knowledgeable. It implies that there is a deeper, perhaps unseen, advantage to following this path, which is only appreciated by those with true understanding or faith. This reflects a broader Qur'anic theme that true knowledge and faith lead to recognizing what is genuinely beneficial and good.

translation: You only worship, besides God, idols, and you produce a falsehood. Indeed, those you worship besides God do not possess for you [the power of] provision. So seek from God your provision and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse critiques the practice of idol worship and the fabrication of false beliefs about these idols. It asserts that the idols worshipped alongside or instead of God do not have the capacity to provide sustenance or any material benefit to their worshippers. Instead, it directs the believers to seek their provision from God alone, to worship Him exclusively, and to be thankful for His blessings. Ultimately, it reminds them that their return is to God, emphasizing the accountability and reckoning that awaits them in the hereafter. The verse thus underscores the monotheistic belief in God's sole authority over provision and the futility of seeking sustenance or salvation from other sources.

translation: And if you deny, already nations before you denied. And not is upon the messenger except [the duty of] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse is a consolation to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the face of rejection by his people. It reminds him that previous nations also denied their messengers, and that his duty is only to convey the message clearly, not to ensure its acceptance. It emphasizes the Prophet's role as a messenger and separates his responsibility from the response of his audience, providing comfort in the knowledge that his task is not to change hearts but to deliver the truth.

translation: Have they not seen how God originates creation, then reproduces it? Indeed, that is easy for God.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting God's power and ability to recreate life after death, just as He originated it in the first place. It is emphasizing that the concept of resurrection is not impossible for God, as He has already demonstrated His power by creating life from nothing. The verse is encouraging people to reflect on the natural world and recognize God's ability to recreate life, making the idea of an afterlife more plausible and reassuring.

translation: Say, "Travel through the land and observe how He began creation. Then, God will produce the final creation. Indeed, God is over all things competent"
interpretation: This verse is encouraging people to reflect on the creation of the universe and the origin of life on Earth. By observing the complexity and diversity of the natural world, one can infer that God is capable of creating and re-creating. The verse is highlighting the idea that if God was able to bring about the initial creation, He is certainly able to bring about a new creation, referring to the afterlife. The verse is emphasizing God's omnipotence and ability to recreate life, serving as a reminder of the possibility of an afterlife and the Day of Judgment.

translation: He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sovereignty and absolute authority of Allah over His creation. It signifies that Allah has the power to punish or reward whomever He wills, based on His divine wisdom and justice. The verse also serves as a reminder of the inevitability of return to Allah, emphasizing accountability for one's deeds in the hereafter. It underscores the concept of divine decree and the futility of human resistance against Allah's will, while also encouraging believers to seek His mercy through righteous actions and repentance.

translation: And you cannot escape in the earth or in the heaven. And you have not, besides Allah , any protector or any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of attempting to evade or defy God's will, whether on earth or in heaven. It underscores the all-encompassing nature of God's power and authority, suggesting that there is no escape or refuge from His judgment or punishment. Furthermore, it highlights the absence of any alternative sources of protection, support, or aid beyond God's sovereignty, reinforcing the idea of total dependence on Him.

translation: And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and the meeting with Him - those have despaired of My mercy, and those for them is a painful punishment
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting God's signs and the hereafter. Those who deny the signs of God and the meeting with Him (i.e., the Day of Judgment and the afterlife) have lost hope in God's mercy. The verse implies that such individuals have severed their connection with the divine and are thus subject to a painful punishment, underscoring the idea that faith and the acknowledgment of the hereafter are essential for receiving God's mercy.

translation: And the answer of his people was not but they said, "Kill him or burn him," but Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's ability to rescue His messengers and believers from the most dire circumstances, emphasizing the power of faith and divine intervention. The narrative of Abraham being saved from the fire serves as a testament to God's capability to deliver His faithful servants from harm, reinforcing the notion that true believers are under God's protection. The verse suggests that such miraculous deliverances are signs or 'ayat' for those who have faith, indicating that these events are not just historical occurrences but hold deeper spiritual significance for those who believe.

translation: And he will say, 'You have taken idols instead of Allah, out of [mutual] affection among you in worldly life. Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will deny others and curse others, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will not have any helpers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony of idol worship and the false sense of camaraderie it fosters among its adherents in worldly life. On the Day of Judgment, however, those who worshipped idols and followed false deities will turn against each other, repudiating and cursing one another as they realize the error of their ways. The verse serves as a warning that the bonds of unity formed around false beliefs are ultimately fragile and will disintegrate when faced with the reality of divine judgment, leaving the idolaters to face the torment of Hell without any helpers or intercessors to save them.

translation: So Lot believed in him [Abraham]. And [Abraham] said, "Indeed, I will emigrate to [the service of] my Lord. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering faith and conviction of Prophet Lut (Lot) in the face of adversity. By declaring his intention to migrate to his Lord, Lut demonstrates his unshakeable trust in Allah's power and wisdom, embodied in the attributes 'Al-'Aziz' (The Almighty) and 'Al-Hakim' (The Wise). This signifies Lut's resolve to seek refuge with Allah, away from the wickedness of his people, and underscores the theme of righteous migration in the pursuit of divine pleasure and protection.

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and We made prophethood and the Book among his descendants, and We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed he is among the righteous in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of prophethood and scripture within the lineage of the prophets, emphasizing that the divine gifts of prophethood and scripture are not limited to an individual but are a legacy that continues through their descendants, underscoring the significance of familial lineage in the transmission of spiritual and religious leadership.

translation: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit the immorality that no one preceded you in [doing] from among the worlds?"   ,
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the severity of the Prophet Lot's people's actions by stating that they were the first to commit such an abhorrent act, implying that their behavior was not only immoral but also unprecedented and thus particularly reprehensible, serving as a critique of their innovation in evil and their lack of precedent in righteousness.

translation: Do you indeed approach men with desire instead of women? Nay, you are a people transgressing beyond bounds. And the answer of his people was not but they said, "Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you should be of the truthful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the societal corruption and moral decay of the people to whom the Prophet Lut was sent. The acts mentioned - approaching men with lust, cutting off the path (likely referring to robbery or banditry), and committing reprehensible acts in their gatherings - signify a deep-seated corruption that pervades their social fabric. The people's response to Lut's condemnation, demanding that he bring upon them the punishment of Allah if he is truthful, demonstrates their defiance and disbelief, showcasing their refusal to heed warnings and correct their ways.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, support me against the corrupting people.'
interpretation: This verse is a supplication from a prophet, likely Noah, as per the context in Surah Al-Mu'minun, to Allah, asking for victory or support against a people described as 'al-mufsidin' (those who cause corruption). The interpretation is that the prophet is seeking divine assistance against those who are spreading evil or corruption, highlighting the struggle between righteousness and unrighteousness, and the reliance on God's power to overcome the forces of corruption.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good news, they said, 'Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this city. Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle that divine punishment is not arbitrary, but is a consequence of the actions of the people. The destruction of a community is justified when its people have crossed the boundaries of justice and righteousness, as indicated by their being described as 'ظالمين' (wrongdoers). It underscores the Qur'anic theme that divine justice is responsive to human actions, and that the fate of communities is tied to their moral and ethical conduct.

translation: He said, "But there is Lut in it." They said, "We are more knowing of who is in it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she is to be among those who remain behind."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice and the fate that awaits those who refuse to heed the warnings of their messengers. The mention of Lot's wife being among those who are to be left behind signifies that faith and righteousness are individual responsibilities, and one's familial ties or social status do not guarantee salvation. It underscores the Qur'anic theme that an individual's destiny is closely tied to their actions and beliefs, emphasizing personal accountability before God.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed by them and felt embarrassed because of them and said, "This is a distressing day." They said, "Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is to be of those who remain behind."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine intervention and protection afforded to the righteous, even in the face of overwhelming adversity and malevolent surroundings. The fact that Lot is assured of his safety and that of his household, with the explicit exception of his wife who is aligned with the disbelieving and wicked people, underscores the principle that salvation is individual and based on one's faith and actions. It suggests that familial ties or social bonds do not guarantee safety or salvation in the face of divine judgment; rather, it is one's personal stance and deeds that determine their fate.

translation: We are about to send down upon the people of this town a punishment from the heaven because of their defiance.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the people of the town (likely Sodom and Gomorrah, known for their corruption) will face divine punishment from above due to their persistent disobedience and corruption, highlighting the consequence of defying God's commands and moral decay.

translation: And We have certainly left it as a clear sign for people who understand.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the remnants or signs left behind by a past event or civilization serve as clear evidence or a lesson for those who possess the faculty of reason and can reflect upon them. It implies that people who are endowed with intellect and can think critically are more likely to derive moral lessons and understand the significance of historical events or the ruins of past civilizations.

translation: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb, and he said, 'O my people, worship Allah and expect the Last Day and do not cause corruption on the earth.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of righteous worship, hope in the Hereafter, and moral responsibility. Prophet Shu'aib's message to his people emphasizes that true faith involves not just worshiping God, but also having a hopeful and accountable outlook towards the afterlife, while also being mindful of one's actions on earth and avoiding corruption.

translation: But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them, and they became lifeless and motionless in their own homes.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting the truth and disobeying God's messengers. The people being referred to were punished with a severe earthquake ("الرَجْفَة") that destroyed them, leaving them lifeless and motionless ("جَاثِمِين") in their own homes, serving as a stark warning to others about the fate that awaits those who deny God's signs and reject His guidance.

translation: And 'Aad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you from their dwellings. And Satan made their deeds appear fair to them and averted them from the path, and they were discerning.
interpretation: This verse is cautioning against the dangers of being misled by Satan. It references the ancient tribes of 'Ad and Thamud, whose ruins serve as a testament to their downfall. The verse suggests that Satan beautified their actions, leading them astray from the right path, despite their having the capacity for insight. The implication is that having the ability to see or understand is not enough; one must also be guided by the truth and resist the deceptive allurements of Satan.

translation: And Korah, and Pharaoh, and Haman. And Moses came to them with clear signs, but they were arrogant in the land, and they were not outstripping.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the theme of arrogance and its consequences. The mention of Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman together serves to illustrate that arrogance can manifest in different forms and among different types of people - wealth (Qarun), political power (Pharaoh), and bureaucratic or ministerial power (Haman). The verse suggests that despite being presented with clear evidence (بينات) by Moses, they refused to humble themselves and instead became even more arrogant. The phrase "وما كانوا سابقين" (and they were not going to escape or outstrip) implies that their arrogance was not only a moral failing but also a futile attempt to evade the consequences of their actions, suggesting that their actions were ultimately futile against the will of God.

translation: So each of them We seized for his sin; and among them were those upon whom We sent a rainstorm of stones, and among them were those who were seized by the blast [of the Thunderstorm], and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned. And Allah would not have wronged them, but it was they who were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the justice of Allah in punishing previous nations for their wrongdoing. It emphasizes that the destruction or punishment inflicted upon them was a consequence of their own actions, not an unjust act by Allah. The various methods of punishment mentioned - such as being hit by a storm, being consumed by a loud cry, being swallowed by the earth, or being drowned - serve as examples of how different communities were held accountable for their sins. The verse underscores the principle that Allah's punishment is a response to the wrongdoing of the people themselves, reinforcing the idea that individuals and communities are responsible for their own fate due to their choices and actions.

translation: The example of those who take protectors other than Allah is like that of the spider who takes a home. And indeed, the weakest of homes is the spider's home, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the futility of seeking protection or support from other than Allah. The example of the spider's web is used to illustrate the weakness and fragility of such attempts. Just as a spider's web is easily destroyed, so too are the alliances and supports that people seek outside of Allah. The verse is cautioning against placing trust in anything or anyone other than Allah, as such trust is ultimately misplaced and will prove to be weak and unreliable.

translation: Indeed, Allah knows whatever they invoke of Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting God's omniscience and omnipotence in relation to the idols or deities that people worship alongside Him. It underscores that God is fully aware of the futility of these other objects of worship and reasserts His unchallengeable might and wise decision-making, suggesting that those who divert their worship to other entities are misguided.

translation: And these examples We set forth for mankind, and none understand them except those who have knowledge.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of wisdom and knowledge in understanding spiritual and moral teachings. It suggests that the deeper meanings and lessons contained within the parables and examples given in the Qur'an are not accessible to everyone, but are reserved for those who possess a certain level of understanding and insight, referred to here as 'the knowledgeable' or 'those who know'. It implies that true comprehension of divine guidance requires not just intellectual knowledge, but also a level of spiritual maturity and awareness.

translation: God created the heavens and the earth in truth. Indeed in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of reflecting on the creation of the heavens and the earth as a sign or evidence ('āyah) for those who have faith (al-mu'minīn). The phrase 'بالحق' (bi'l-haqq) suggests that the creation is not arbitrary or without purpose, but is instead grounded in truth and wisdom, implying a deliberate and meaningful act by God. The interpretation is that the intricate design and order in the universe serve as a testament to God's existence and His purposeful creation, which is particularly significant and convincing for believers as it reinforces their faith.

translation: Recite, [O Muhammad], what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows that which you do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of prayer (salat) in a believer's life as a means to deter them from committing shameful and evil deeds. The remembrance of Allah during prayer is considered the most significant aspect, suggesting that the true power of prayer lies not just in its performance but in the spiritual connection it fosters with Allah. It implies that as one focuses on remembering and glorifying Allah, they are guided away from wrongdoing, indicating a transformative effect of prayer on the individual's moral character.

translation: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them, and say, 'We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you. And our God and your God is one; and we to Him submit.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of engaging with the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) in a manner characterized by the utmost good conduct, except when dealing with those among them who have committed injustice. It advocates for a unified declaration of faith in the revelations received by both parties and acknowledges a shared belief in one God, to whom all submit.

translation: And thus We have revealed to you the Book. Those to whom We gave the Scripture believe in it. And among these [people] are those who believe in it. And none reject Our verses except the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the universal nature of the Qur'an's message and its acceptance by those who are guided by previous scriptures, as well as some among the people to whom it is newly revealed, while emphasizing that it is the disbelievers who reject its signs.

translation: And you did not recite before it any book, nor did you inscribe one with your right hand. In that case, the falsifiers would have doubted.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the miraculous nature of the Prophet Muhammad's receipt of the Quran. It is stating that because the Prophet was illiterate and could not read or write, the fact that he was able to recite the Quran is evidence that it is a divine revelation, and not something he could have come up with on his own. If he had been literate, the hypocrites and those who deny the truth would have had reason to doubt the authenticity of the Quran, but since he was not, their doubts are unfounded.

translation: But it is clear revelations in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge. And none deny Our revelations except the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of knowledge and understanding in recognizing the truth. It suggests that the truth of God's signs (ayat) is not immediately apparent to everyone, but rather it is those who possess knowledge who can truly comprehend and appreciate its significance. The verse also implies that those who reject God's signs are unjust, indicating that their rejection is not due to a lack of understanding, but rather a deliberate choice to ignore or deny the truth.

translation: And they say, 'Why are not signs sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'The signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the challenge faced by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from his detractors who demanded tangible signs or miracles as proof of his prophethood. The response given emphasizes that the authority to send signs or miracles lies solely with Allah, indicating that the Prophet's role is not to perform miracles at will but to clearly warn people of the consequences of their actions. It underscores the Prophet's role as a 'nadhīr mubīn' (clear warner), whose primary responsibility is to convey the message of Allah clearly and warn people about the path they are on, rather than to provide miraculous proofs. This distinction is crucial as it shifts the focus from the demand for miracles to the response to the message itself, emphasizing the importance of faith and obedience over the desire for supernatural validation.

translation: Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down upon you the Book (Qur'an) that is recited to them? Indeed, in that is a mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and mercy for those who have faith. The revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet is not just a miracle or a sign of his prophethood, but a blessing and a reminder for the believers. It implies that the Qur'an is not just a scripture to be revered, but a living guidance that is to be recited, reflected upon, and implemented in one's life. The verse suggests that the true beneficiaries of the Qur'an are those who have faith, as they are able to derive spiritual nourishment and guidance from it.

translation: Say, 'Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you. He is Knower of what is in the heavens and the earth. And they who have believed in falsehood and disbelieved in Allah - it is those who are the losers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the all-encompassing knowledge of God, who is aware of everything in the heavens and the earth, and serves as a witness between the Prophet and his detractors. It highlights the stark contrast between those who have faith in falsehood and reject the truth of God, ultimately leading to their downfall. The verse underscores the notion that true faith is in God alone, and that associating falsehood with Him or rejecting His truth results in loss, both spiritually and ultimately.

translation: And they ask you to hasten on the punishment! And had it not been for a term appointed, the punishment would certainly have come to them. And it will certainly come upon them suddenly, when they shall not perceive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and impatience of those who reject the truth, as they demand that the punishment they are being warned about be brought upon them immediately. The verse serves as a warning that the punishment will indeed come, but on a date predetermined by Allah, and it will arrive suddenly when they are least expecting it, underscoring the theme of divine justice and the inevitability of accountability for one's actions.

translation: They ask you to hasten the punishment. And indeed, Hell is surrounding the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the inevitability and imminence of punishment for those who reject faith. The disbelievers are impatiently demanding that the punishment be hastened, yet the verse asserts that Hell is already encompassing them, suggesting that their doom is certain and inescapable, even if it is not immediately apparent. The verse serves as a warning that the consequences of disbelief are not just future threats, but are already a present reality that surrounds those who reject the truth.

translation: The Day when the punishment will cover them from above them and from under their feet, and He will say, Taste what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, the punishment will encompass the disbelievers from all directions, above and below them, leaving them no escape or respite. The phrase 'from above them and from under their feet' is a metaphorical expression indicating a comprehensive and inescapable punishment. The statement 'Taste what you used to do' serves as a rebuke, linking their suffering directly to their past actions, emphasizing the justice in the punishment they receive for their deeds.

translation: O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship only Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vastness of Allah's creation and provision for His servants, encouraging believers to remain steadfast in their worship of Him alone, even when faced with persecution or hardship that might force them to migrate or flee. It underscores the message that Allah is not confined to a specific land or territory, and that His worship is not restricted by geographical boundaries, thus urging believers to prioritize their faith and continue worshiping Him wherever they may be.

translation: Every soul will taste death. Then to Us will you be returned.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability and universality of death, emphasizing that every soul will experience it. It then shifts the focus from the mortal nature of human existence to the afterlife, indicating that after death, all individuals will return to God, suggesting a reckoning or judgment. It underscores the belief in an afterlife and the accountability of one's deeds in this life before God.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely give them lodgings in Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. Excellent is the reward of the [righteous] workers
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for those who have faith and perform righteous deeds, indicating that they will be given elevated abodes in Paradise, symbolizing a high status and closeness to Allah. The ever-flowing rivers beneath these abodes signify abundance and the continuous nature of the blessings they receive. The verse emphasizes that this reward is eternal, stressing the permanence of the bliss in the afterlife for those who have demonstrated their faith through their actions. It serves as an encouragement for believers to maintain their faith and continue performing good deeds, promising them a noble and lasting recompense.

translation: Those who are patient and upon their Lord rely
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of believers who are steadfast in their faith. The phrase 'those who are patient' refers to individuals who endure hardships and difficulties with perseverance, without complaint or despair. The additional phrase 'and put their trust in their Lord' indicates that these patient individuals also have faith in their Lord's plan and wisdom, relying on Him for guidance and support. This trust is not just a passive state, but an active decision to surrender their affairs to Allah, demonstrating a deep-seated conviction in His mercy, justice, and providence. Together, patience and trust in Allah form a powerful combination that enables believers to navigate life's challenges with resilience and hope.

translation: And how many a creature that carries not its provision! God provides for it and for you. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's all-encompassing provision and care for all creatures. It emphasizes that just as God provides for the sustenance of creatures that are incapable of storing or securing their own provisions, He will also provide for the believers. The verse serves as a reassurance to the faithful that their sustenance is in God's hands, and they should trust in His wisdom and benevolence. The attributes of God mentioned at the end of the verse, 'السميع العليم' (the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing), underscore that God's provision is not blind or arbitrary but is guided by His complete knowledge and awareness of the needs of all His creatures.

translation: And if you were to ask them: "Who created the heavens and the earth, and subjected the sun and the moon?" They would certainly say, "God." So, how are they deluded (away from the truth)?
interpretation: This verse highlights the innate, intuitive knowledge of God's existence and creative power that is present within human beings. Despite this inherent understanding, many people still turn away from the truth and succumb to falsehood, indicating a disconnect between their innate knowledge and their actions or beliefs. The verse suggests that the natural world serves as a clear indicator of God's existence and sovereignty, yet humans often fail to align their understanding with this reality, instead being swayed by misguided beliefs or practices.

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts for him. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sovereignty of Allah over the distribution of sustenance among His servants. It signifies that Allah alone has the authority to decide who receives abundance in provision and who faces scarcity, based on His wisdom. The phrase 'ويقدر له' (and restricts for him) underscores the divine decree that governs the allocation of resources, emphasizing that both expansion and limitation of provision are within Allah's control. The verse concludes with 'إن الله بكل شيء عليم' (Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things), reinforcing the idea that Allah's decisions regarding the distribution of sustenance are guided by His all-encompassing knowledge. This interpretation encourages believers to trust in Allah's wisdom and to understand that the variations in provision are part of a larger divine plan, rather than being random or arbitrary.

translation: And if you ask them, "Who sends down water from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness?" They will surely say, "Allah." Say, "Praise to Allah ." But most of them do not reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony that despite witnessing the revival of the earth through rainfall, a manifestation of God's power, many people fail to attribute this miracle to divine intervention, instead, they acknowledge it, yet their acknowledgment is superficial, lacking in true understanding or rational contemplation, underscoring a disconnect between their verbal affirmation of God's power and a deeper, intellectually grounded faith.

translation: And this worldly life is not but amusement and play, and indeed the home of the Hereafter - that is the [eternal] life, if only they knew
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the stark contrast between the fleeting nature of worldly life and the eternal reality of the Hereafter. It is cautioning that those who are preoccupied with the transient pleasures of this world are missing out on the true and everlasting life that awaits them in the Hereafter, implying a call to prioritize the eternal over the ephemeral.

translation: And when they ride in the ships, they invoke Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him
interpretation: This verse highlights the inconsistency of human behavior in the face of adversity and prosperity. When people are in distress, such as being at sea and facing the risk of drowning, they turn to Allah with sincerity, dedicating their worship and supplication solely to Him. However, once they are rescued and reach the safety of land, they revert to their previous state of associating partners with Allah, indicating a lack of consistent devotion and gratitude.

translation: So that they may deny what We have given them, and that they may take their ease; but they will soon come to know.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who are given blessings and provisions by Allah but respond by being ungrateful and disbelieving. It suggests that despite being given these gifts, they will continue to revel in their worldly life, ignoring the consequences of their actions. The verse ultimately serves as a caution that they will come to realize the error of their ways, but only after facing the repercussions of their disbelief and ingratitude.

translation: Have they not seen that We have made a sacred sanctuary, while people are being snatched away from all around them? Will they then believe in falsehood and deny the favour of Allah?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the stark contrast between the peace and security enjoyed by the people within the sacred precincts (likely referring to the Kaaba in Mecca) and the insecurity and violence faced by those outside it. It questions the moral and spiritual sensibilities of those who, despite witnessing this divine blessing of safety and peace, still choose to reject the truth and deny the favors of God, instead opting to believe in falsehood.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of fabricating lies against Allah or denying the truth when it is presented. It serves as a warning that those who engage in such actions will face severe consequences, with Hell being their ultimate abode. The verse underscores the principle that justice will be served, and the truth will prevail, emphasizing the accountability of individuals for their actions and beliefs regarding Allah and His message.

translation: And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse suggests that those who strive and struggle in the path of Allah, seeking to please Him and follow His guidance, will be rewarded by being shown the correct paths to follow. It implies that the effort to do good and to follow Allah's commandments is met with divine guidance, making it easier for the individual to continue on the right path. Furthermore, it reassures that Allah is with those who do good, indicating His support and companionship for those who act righteously.

translation: In the name of Allah, the most Compassionate, the most Merciful, Alif Lam Mim.
interpretation: These are disjointed letters known as 'muqatta'at' that appear at the beginning of some chapters in the Qur'an. The interpretation of 'Alif-Lam-Mim' is that it signifies the beginning of a new chapter and serves as a challenge to the Arabs, who were masters of language and literature, to comprehend the Qur'an, despite being made up of the same letters they used in their own speech. It is also a demonstration of the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, as it is composed of the same letters that the Arabs were familiar with, yet it conveys a message that is beyond their ability to replicate.

translation: The Romans have been defeated.
interpretation: This verse signifies the defeat of the Byzantine Empire (referred to as 'Rūm' in Arabic) at the hands of the Persians. The context of this verse is crucial as it is part of a larger narrative in Sūrat ar-Rūm, which not only mentions the defeat of the Romans but also predicts their subsequent victory within a few years. The verse is often seen as a sign of the truthfulness of the Qur'an and the prophethood of Muhammad, as it was revealed at a time when the Muslims were in a minority and the outcome of the war between the Persians and the Romans was still unfolding. The interpretation extends to understanding it as a demonstration of divine knowledge and the unfolding of future events as foretold by the Qur'an, reinforcing the faith of the believers.

translation: In the nearest land. And they, after their defeat, will be victorious.
interpretation: This verse is referring to a future event where a group of people, likely the Romans, will be victorious over their enemies in a nearby land, but then will themselves be defeated shortly after. The verse is highlighting the changing fortunes of war and the fleeting nature of power, serving as a reminder to not become too arrogant or complacent in one's successes.

translation: Within a few years. To Allah belongs the command before and after, and on that day the believers will rejoice
interpretation: This verse is referring to a future event that will occur within a few years, likely related to a battle or conflict between the Romans and another party, with the Romans ultimately emerging victorious. The phrase 'For Allah is the command before and after' signifies Allah's sovereignty over all events, past, present, and future. It highlights that the outcome of events is determined by Allah. The verse concludes with 'And on that day the believers will rejoice,' indicating that the believers will be happy at the victory of the Romans, possibly because it aligns with their own values or because it signifies a broader divine plan unfolding. This joy among believers is tied to their faith in Allah's ultimate control and the unfolding of events according to His will.

translation: With the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful
interpretation: This verse highlights God's sovereignty and mercy in granting victory. It signifies that God's assistance is not limited by human constraints or preconceptions; rather, it is bestowed upon whom He wills, based on His divine wisdom and justice. The attributes of being 'Al-Aziz' (the Mighty) and 'Ar-Rahim' (the Merciful) underscore that God's power is coupled with mercy, suggesting that His decision to grant victory is both an expression of His strength and a manifestation of His compassion towards those He chooses to aid.

translation: God has made a promise. God does not break His promise, but most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reliability and faithfulness of God's promises. It emphasizes that God's commitments are unwavering and will be fulfilled, but notes that many people are unaware of or do not understand this aspect of God's nature, underscoring a disconnect between divine promise and human perception or understanding.

translation: They know an outer [i.e., superficial] aspect of the life of this world, but they are heedless of the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony of human knowledge and priorities. While people may possess knowledge about the superficial aspects of worldly life, they remain oblivious to the more profound and significant aspects of the afterlife. It suggests that their focus is skewed, prioritizing the fleeting and material over the eternal and spiritual. This skewed focus is a result of their heedlessness towards the hereafter, indicating a lack of awareness or concern for the ultimate consequences of their actions in the life to come.

translation: Have they not pondered about themselves? Allah has not created the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for a specified term. And indeed, many of the people are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse is urging people to reflect on themselves and the world around them. It suggests that the intricate creation of the universe and the complexity of human beings themselves are evidence of a purposeful and deliberate act of creation, rather than a random or meaningless event. The verse is emphasizing that the existence of the universe and human life has a specific purpose and a limited duration, and that many people, despite this evidence, are in denial of the Day of Judgment and the accountability before their Lord.

translation: Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were stronger than them in power, and they tilled the earth and populated it more than they have populated it, and their messengers came to them with clear signs. And Allah would not wrong them, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: The verse is highlighting the cyclical nature of history and the consequences of rejecting divine guidance. It suggests that previous civilizations, despite being more powerful and having achieved greater accomplishments, were ultimately destroyed because they rejected the clear signs and messages brought by their prophets. The verse implies that their downfall was not due to any injustice on God's part, but rather their own self-destructive actions, indicating a pattern where human actions, particularly the rejection of divine guidance, lead to their own downfall.

translation: Then the end of those who did evil was the worst [consequence] because they denied the signs of Allah and used to ridicule them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of those who have chosen a path of evil, which ultimately leads to their downfall due to their rejection and mockery of the signs of God, indicating a divine pattern where those who persist in wrongdoing and disbelieve in God's messages are met with severe consequences.

translation: God originates creation, then repeats it, then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse highlights the cyclical nature of existence as understood in Islamic theology, where God is the initiator of creation, its repeater or reviver, and the ultimate destination for all return. It underscores the belief in the afterlife and the accountability of human actions before God, emphasizing the omnipotence and sovereignty of God over creation and its destiny.

translation: And the Day the Hour appears the criminals will be in despair
interpretation: On the Day when the Hour will be established, the criminals will be in despair, overwhelmed by their realization of the consequences of their actions and the futility of their previous denials and disobedience.

translation: And they will have no intercessors among their [alleged] partners, and they will [then] be disbelievers in their [alleged] partners.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of idol worship and the false hope of intercession. On the Day of Judgment, those who associated others with God (idolaters) will find that their 'partners' or idols will not be able to intercede on their behalf. Moreover, it indicates that the idolaters will have turned against their idols, rejecting them as they realize the idols' inability to provide any benefit or salvation.

translation: And on the Day when the Hour will be established, that Day shall they be separated (into their categories)
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that on the Day of Judgment, people's alliances, friendships, and familial ties will be rendered meaningless as they will be held individually accountable for their actions. The unity and cohesion that characterized their worldly relationships will give way to separation and divergence, as the righteous and the wicked will be distinguished and sorted out according to their deeds.

translation: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a garden delighted
interpretation: This verse indicates that those who have faith and do righteous deeds will be in a state of joy and delight in Paradise, where they will be treated with honor and made happy, suggesting a life of bliss and contentment in the afterlife.

translation: And as for those who disbelieve and deny Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, those will be brought into the torment [i.e., punishment].
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting faith and the hereafter, indicating that those who deny the signs of God and the accountability of the afterlife will be perpetually ensnared in suffering, with the torment being ever-present for them.

translation: So glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of glorifying God at the beginning and end of the day. The phrase 'when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning' signifies the transition from day to night and night to day, marking the cyclical nature of time.
