translation: And when a party of them said, "O people of Yathrib, there is no stand for you [here], so return [to your homes]." And a faction of them ask the Prophet to excuse them, saying, "Our homes are exposed (unprotected)," though they were not exposed. They did not intend except to flee.
interpretation: This verse critiques the hypocrisy of certain individuals among the Muslims during the time of the Prophet Muhammad, particularly during the Battle of the Trench. It highlights their lack of commitment to the cause and their pretense of having legitimate reasons to stay back or leave. The phrase 'إن بيوتنا عورة' (our homes are exposed/unprotected) is used by some as an excuse to seek permission from the Prophet to leave, claiming their homes were vulnerable to attack. However, the verse clarifies that their homes were not actually exposed or in danger ('وما هي بعورة'), indicating that their true intention was not to protect their homes but to flee from the battle ('إن يريدون إلا فرارا'). This reveals the underlying cowardice and lack of sincerity among these individuals, showcasing the tension between true believers and hypocrites within the early Muslim community.

translation: And if they (the hypocrites) were entered upon from all its sides and then they were asked to commit apostasy (or fitnah), they would have done it and would have lingered in it only a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and lack of resolve of those who claim to be believers but are not truly committed to their faith. It indicates that if the disbelievers were to launch a decisive attack from all sides and the hypocrites were then tempted or pressured into apostasy or rebellion, they would readily succumb to such temptation and not hesitate for long before giving in, showing their true lack of conviction and faith.

translation: And they had already covenanted with Allah before not to turn their backs. And ever is the covenant with Allah [that] He will be asked about it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contradiction between the past commitments and the present actions of the hypocrites. It indicates that they had previously made a covenant with Allah not to turn their backs in times of hardship or battle, but they failed to uphold this promise. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah will hold them accountable for their broken vows, emphasizing the importance of fulfilling one's commitments to Him.

translation: Say, Never will you benefit from fleeing, if you should flee from death or killing; and then [if you did], you would not be given enjoyment [of life] except for a little.
interpretation: This verse is cautioning against fleeing from battle or danger, indicating that such an action will not provide any benefit or protection from death or being killed. It emphasizes that even if one manages to escape temporarily, their enjoyment or pleasure in life will be short-lived, implying that death is inevitable and that one should stand firm against adversity rather than trying to flee from it.

translation: Say, "Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends harm for you or intends mercy for you?" And they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute authority and power of Allah, emphasizing that no one can protect or save individuals from His will, whether it be harm or mercy. It underscores the futility of seeking guardians or helpers other than Allah, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid (the oneness of God) and the dependence of all creation on Him alone.

translation: Allah may well know those of you who are keeping others back, and those who are saying to their brethren, "Come along to us"; and they come not to the battle except a little.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing those who are hindering others from participating in jihad or other communal efforts for the cause of Allah, and those who invite their brothers to join them in their inaction or lack of effort, indicating that they are not genuinely committed to the cause and only show up or make an effort when there is little to no actual hardship or danger.

translation: Covetous against you. And when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one fainting from death. But when the fear is gone, they slash at you with sharp tongues, covetous of the good. Those have not believed, so God has made their deeds worthless. And that is easy for God.
interpretation: This verse critiques the hypocrites among the Muslims who, despite their outward show of faith, are inwardly stingy and unwilling to spend in the cause of Allah or support their fellow Muslims. When faced with danger or hardship, they look to the Prophet for leadership and guidance, indicating a level of dependency on him, but their eyes glaze over as if they are about to faint, showing their lack of resolve or courage. Once the danger passes, they turn on the believers with harsh words, still being miserly with regard to doing good. The verse concludes that such individuals have not truly believed, and as a result, Allah has rendered their deeds worthless. This outcome is considered easy for Allah, highlighting His power and authority over the affairs of His creation.

translation: They think that the confederates have not withdrawn; and if the confederates should come [again], they would wish that they were in the desert among the Bedouin, inquiring [from afar] about your news. And if they were among you, they would not fight except a little.
interpretation: The verse critiques the hypocrites who, despite their claims of faith, were fearful of the confederate tribes (Al-Ahzab) that had gathered against the Muslims. It highlights their deep-seated lack of commitment to the cause of Islam, suggesting that even if the confederates were to return, these hypocrites would wish they were among the Bedouins, far from the conflict, merely receiving news about the Muslims rather than being actively involved. Furthermore, it underscores their reluctance to engage in fighting, indicating that even if they were present among the Muslims, they would not contribute significantly to the battle, fighting little or not at all.

translation: There is certainly for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent model for anyone whose hope is in Allah and the Last Day and [who] remembers Allah often.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the example of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for those who have faith in Allah and the Day of Judgment, and who frequently remember Allah. It suggests that the Prophet's life and actions serve as a model for believers to emulate, particularly in their devotion to Allah and their preparation for the afterlife. By following the Prophet's example, believers can cultivate a strong and righteous character, and attain a deeper connection with Allah.

translation: And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger told the truth." And it increased them not except in faith and in submission.
interpretation: This verse highlights the believers' unwavering faith and conviction in the face of adversity. When they saw the confederate forces gathered against them, they recognized it as the fulfillment of Allah's and His Messenger's promise, thereby affirming the truthfulness of both. Instead of causing doubt or fear, this trial strengthened their belief and submission to Allah's will, demonstrating their unshakeable trust in divine providence.

translation: Among the believers are men who have been true to their covenant with Allah; of them some have fulfilled their vow by [martyrdom], and some of them are still waiting; and they have not altered [their determination] in the least;
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering commitment and loyalty of certain believers who have fulfilled their covenant with Allah, demonstrating their sincerity and dedication to their faith. It distinguishes between those who have already fulfilled their obligation, potentially through martyrdom, and those who remain steadfast, awaiting their turn, without wavering in their resolve. The verse underscores the unshakeable nature of their faith, emphasizing that they have not altered their stance or compromised their commitment, thereby exemplifying the true essence of faithfulness and perseverance.

translation: That Allah may reward the truthful for their truth and punish the hypocrites if He wills or accept their repentance. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's ability to discern the true intentions of individuals, rewarding the sincere (الصادقين) for their truthfulness and dealing with the hypocrites (المنافقين) according to His will, either by punishing them or forgiving them, showcasing His attributes of being forgiving (غفورا) and merciful (رحيما).

translation: God turned back the disbelievers in their rage, they gained no good. And God spared the believers fighting. And God is Strong, Mighty.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's intervention on behalf of the believers, indicating that He saved them from the harm intended by their enemies. The phrase 'لم ينالوا خيرا' (they gained no good) suggests that the disbelievers' efforts against the believers were not only unsuccessful but also ultimately counterproductive, as their actions were driven by 'غيظهم' (their rage or anger), implying a deep-seated hostility. The verse reassures the believers of God's sufficiency in protecting them, emphasizing His attributes of being 'قويا' (Strong) and 'عزيزا' (Mighty), thus reinforcing the idea that God's power is more than enough to safeguard the believers against their adversaries.

translation: And those who backed them from among the People of the Scripture, He brought them down from their strongholds and cast terror into their hearts, some you killed, and you took captive some.
interpretation: This verse refers to the event where the Muslims, led by the Prophet Muhammad, besieged and defeated the Banu Qurayza, a Jewish tribe in Medina that had allied itself with the Meccan pagans against the Muslims. The phrase 'وأنزل الذين ظاهروهم من أهل الكتاب من صياصيهم' indicates that the Banu Qurayza were brought down from their fortified strongholds. The phrase 'وقذف في قلوبهم الرعب' suggests that fear was instilled in their hearts, leading to their defeat. The outcome was that some of them were killed and others were taken captive, signifying the consequences of their betrayal and alliance with the enemies of the Muslims. This event is seen as a demonstration of God's support for the Muslims and a punishment for the Banu Qurayza's treachery.

translation: And He caused you to inherit their land and their homes and their wealth, and a land which you have not trodden. And ever is Allah, over all things, competent.
interpretation: This verse signifies the omnipotence of Allah in granting Muslims the inheritance of the lands, homes, and wealth of those they conquered, as well as promising future conquests of territories they had not yet entered. It underscores the limitless capability of Allah to fulfill His promises to the believers, highlighting His power over all things.

translation: O Prophet, say to your wives, "If you should desire the life of the world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and give you a gracious release.
interpretation: This verse highlights the different priorities and values between the life of this world and the hereafter, presenting the Prophet's wives with a choice that reflects the broader Islamic ethical dilemma between worldly desires and spiritual or religious commitment. It suggests that if they were to prioritize worldly gains and pleasures, they would be given provisions and released in a gracious manner, implying a separation or a different arrangement. The verse underscores the idea that the Prophet's wives, as role models for the Muslim community, are expected to embody certain values and commitments that may not align with the pursuit of worldly life and its adornments. It invites reflection on the nature of true fulfillment and the values that are considered important in Islam.

translation: And if you want Allah and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter, then indeed Allah has prepared for the doers of good among you a great reward.
interpretation: This verse signifies that for those women who prioritize their relationship with Allah and His Messenger, and who are striving for the rewards of the Hereafter, Allah has prepared a great recompense. It highlights the importance of having the right intentions and motivations in one's actions, and assures that those who act with righteousness and sincerity will be richly rewarded.

translation: O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you should commit a clear indecency - the punishment would be doubled for her; and that, for Allah, is easy.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that they are held to a higher standard of moral conduct due to their unique position in the Muslim community. The consequence of committing a clear indecency is a doubled punishment, emphasizing the gravity of their responsibility as role models. The verse underscores the ease with which Allah can accomplish this, highlighting His omnipotence and the inevitability of His justice.

translation: And whoever of you devoutly obeys Allah and His Messenger and does righteousness - We will give her her reward twice; and We have prepared for her a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special reward for women who are obedient to Allah and His Messenger, and who do righteous deeds. The double reward indicates a special honor and recognition for their efforts and commitment to faith, suggesting that their challenges and responsibilities are acknowledged and valued by Allah. The 'noble provision' prepared for them signifies a generous and honorable sustenance, likely referring to Paradise or a blessed life in the Hereafter.

translation: O wives of the Prophet! You are not like anyone among women. If you fear Allah , then do not be soft in speech [to men], lest he in whose heart is disease should covet, but speak with established speech.
interpretation: This verse is cautioning the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to be mindful of their speech and behavior, as they are role models for the rest of the Muslim women. It advises them to avoid being overly soft or flirtatious in their speech, lest it encourages those with weak faith or impure intentions. Instead, they should maintain a dignified and respectful tone in their communication, setting a good example for others to follow.

translation: And stay in your houses and do not display yourselves like the display of the former times of ignorance; and establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity [of sin], O people of the [Prophet's] household, and to purify you with [extensive] purification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the purification and protection of the Prophet's household (Ahl al-Bayt) and instructs them, particularly the wives of the Prophet, to maintain their dignity and modesty within their homes, avoid displaying themselves like they used to during the pre-Islamic era of ignorance, and to be obedient to Allah and His Messenger by performing their religious duties such as prayer and charity. The ultimate goal, as stated, is for Allah to remove all impurity and sin from them and to purify them thoroughly, highlighting their special status and role in the Islamic community.

translation: And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted [with all things].
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the importance of the knowledge and wisdom that the Prophet's wives have been privileged to receive, and are expected to reflect upon and act accordingly. It is suggesting that they should be mindful of the divine revelations and the wisdom that is being shared within their homes, and that they should be aware of the subtle and profound nature of God's actions and plans.

translation: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the obedient men and obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humble men and humble women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who do so, and the men who remember Allah often and the women who do so - for them Allah has prepared forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive nature of faith and righteous actions in Islam, emphasizing that both men and women are equally valued in their devotion to God. It lists various qualities and acts of worship that are characteristic of true believers, such as sincerity, patience, humility, charity, fasting, chastity, and the remembrance of God. The verse underscores that these qualities are not limited to one gender but are expected from both men and women equally. By doing so, it establishes a sense of spiritual equality and mutual responsibility between Muslim men and women. The reward promised for embodying these qualities is forgiveness and a great reward, indicating that the cultivation of these virtues leads to both the pardon of past mistakes and a significant recompense in the hereafter. This verse serves as an encouragement for believers to embody these characteristics, promising a profound spiritual and eschatological reward.

translation: It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should [thereafter] have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of submitting to the will of Allah and His Messenger. It signifies that once a decision is made by Allah and His Messenger, believers should not have any reservations or alternatives; they should wholeheartedly accept and comply with the decision. The verse warns that disobeying Allah and His Messenger leads to clear deviation, implying a significant straying from the right path. It underscores the principle of obedience and surrender to divine guidance as a fundamental aspect of faith.

translation: And [remember, O Muhammad], when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor and you bestowed favor, "Keep your wife and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to make manifest, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you in order that there not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they no longer have need of them. And ever is the command of Allah accomplished.
interpretation: This verse highlights the societal and psychological challenges faced by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in his personal life, particularly in relation to his adoption of Zayd ibn Harithah and Zayd's subsequent divorce from Zaynab bint Jahsh. The verse touches upon the pre-Islamic societal norms regarding adopted sons and their wives, and how Islam aimed to reform these customs. The Prophet was initially hesitant to marry Zaynab after her divorce from Zayd due to societal perceptions and the lingering pre-Islamic practice of considering adopted sons as 'real' sons, thereby making their wives akin to 'mothers-in-law'. The verse signifies a turning point where Islamic law supersedes such societal norms, establishing that adopted sons are not legally considered 'sons', thus allowing the Prophet to marry Zaynab. This act was not just a personal event but a legislative move to abolish the pre-Islamic custom, thereby easing the social and legal constraints for believers regarding the marriages of adopted sons' ex-wives. The verse underscores God's authority over societal norms and the inevitability of His decrees.

translation: It is not for the Prophet to feel constrained regarding what Allah has ordained for him. ˹Such was˺ the practice ˹of Allah˺ with those who have passed away before ˹him˺. And the command of Allah is a ˹pre˺determined decree.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine decree and predestination that governs the lives of prophets and righteous individuals. It signifies that the rules and regulations set by Allah for His Prophet Muhammad are part of a larger, timeless tradition that has been in place since the times of previous prophets and righteous people. The verse underscores the idea that the commandments and fate ordained by Allah are not only preordained but also inevitable, emphasizing the concept of divine destiny and the acceptance of it as part of faith.

translation: Those who convey the messages of God and fear Him and fear none but God. And sufficient is God as a Reckoner.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of those who are entrusted with conveying God's messages. It emphasizes their fear of God and their reliance on Him as the ultimate reckoner, indicating that their accountability is solely to Him. The verse suggests that true messengers of God's word are not swayed by the fear of human reprisal, but instead, are driven by a profound reverence for God, and it is this reverence that grants them the courage to fulfill their duty without being intimidated by others. The phrase 'وكفى بالله حسيبا' (and sufficient is God as a Reckoner) underscores the idea that God is the ultimate judge and accountant of one's actions, implying that those who convey His messages are ultimately answerable to Him alone.

translation: Muhammad is not the father of [any] one of your men, but [he is] the Messenger of Allah and last of the prophets. And ever is Allah, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the finality of Prophet Muhammad's prophethood, clarifying that he is not the father of any man among the believers, but rather is the Messenger of Allah and the last of the prophets. It underscores the uniqueness of his role and the completeness of the prophetic message with him, highlighting Allah's all-encompassing knowledge.

translation: O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong and constant connection with Allah through remembrance, suggesting that believers should frequently engage in acts that bring them closer to Allah, such as prayer, supplication, and reflection on His attributes and blessings, to cultivate a deep sense of spirituality and guidance in their lives.

translation: And glorify Him morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and glorifying Allah throughout the day, specifically during the morning and evening. It signifies that believers should maintain a consistent connection with their Creator, expressing gratitude and praise at the beginning and end of each day. The act of glorifying Allah during these times is not just a ritual but a means of spiritual rejuvenation and a reminder of one's faith and responsibilities.

translation: It is He who confers blessings upon you, and His angels (ask for your well-being), that He may bring you out from the darkness into the light; and He is Merciful to the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and benevolence of Allah towards the believers. The phrase 'He it is Who sends salutations upon you, and His angels (too)' signifies the special care and blessings that Allah bestows upon the believers, and the angels' supplication for them is a testament to their elevated status. The ultimate purpose of this divine favor is to guide the believers out of the darkness of ignorance, disbelief, and sin, and into the light of faith, knowledge, and righteousness. The verse concludes by characterizing Allah as merciful to the believers, underscoring the boundless compassion and kindness that He has for those who have faith in Him.

translation: Their greeting on the Day they will meet Him will be
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, believers will be greeted with peace, indicating a state of serenity and safety. The 'noble reward' prepared for them underscores the generosity and honor bestowed upon the righteous by Allah, highlighting the virtues of faith and good deeds.

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse signifies the multifaceted role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in Islam. He is described as a 'witness' (shahid), indicating his role as a witness to the actions and beliefs of his community and to the truth of God's message. As a 'bearer of glad tidings' (mubashshir), he brings good news to believers of their reward in the hereafter. Lastly, as a 'warner' (nadhir), he cautions those who disbelieve or disobey God's commandments of the consequences they will face. This verse underscores the Prophet's comprehensive mission to guide humanity to the right path through both encouragement and warning.

translation: And as a caller to Allah, by His permission, and as a lamp spreading light.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not only a messenger delivering the message of Allah but is also an exemplary figure whose life and character illuminate the path for believers, guiding them towards righteousness and the worship of one God.

translation: And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty.
interpretation: This verse is an instruction to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to convey the glad news to the believers that they are recipients of Allah's abundant grace and favor. The 'great bounty' refers to the reward that Allah has prepared for the believers in the hereafter, which is a manifestation of His mercy and generosity towards those who have faith and do righteous deeds. It serves as a motivation for the believers to remain steadfast in their faith and to continue doing good, with the promise of a grand reward awaiting them.

translation: And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm, and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and by extension, all believers, to remain steadfast in their faith despite the harm and opposition they face from disbelievers and hypocrites. It emphasizes the importance of relying solely on Allah for protection and support, as He is sufficient to deal with the harm caused by others. The verse encourages believers to adopt a stance of trust and reliance on Allah, rather than being swayed or intimidated by the actions of their detractors.

translation: O you who have believed, if you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, you have no 'iddah (waiting period) to count in respect of them. So give them a provision and release them in a kind manner.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of treating women with kindness and respect, even in situations where a marriage is dissolved before consummation. It underscores the principle of fairness and generosity towards women, emphasizing that they should be provided for and released in a gracious manner, reflecting the Islamic values of compassion and justice.

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their due compensation and those your right hand possesses whom Allah has granted you as a result of war, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts, who emigrated with you, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet [and] if the Prophet wishes to marry her, [this is] exclusively for you, not for the believers [in general] - We have already known what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives and those their right hands possess, [but this is for you] in order that there will be upon you no constraint. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines specific rulings for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding his marriages, distinguishing his circumstances from those of other believers. It permits him to marry certain categories of women, including those who have migrated with him and a believing woman who offers herself to him. The verse emphasizes the unique position of the Prophet, highlighting that these permissions are exclusive to him and are intended to ease his circumstances without causing hardship. It underscores God's knowledge of the obligations He has placed upon the believers and His accommodation of the Prophet's situation, reflecting His attributes of forgiveness and mercy.

translation: You may put off whom you will of them and take to yourself whom you will; and if you desire one you have set aside, there is no blame on you. That is more proper, so that their eyes may be cool and they may not grieve, and that they may be pleased, all of them, with what you give them. God knows what is in your hearts; God is All-knowing, All-clement.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of treating wives with kindness and fairness, suggesting that a husband should manage his relationships with his wives in a way that brings comfort and satisfaction to all of them, thereby minimizing hurt and discontent. It implies that a husband has the flexibility to manage his relationships with his wives in a manner that is considerate of their feelings, and that doing so is a sign of a wise and knowledgeable person, as it requires understanding the complexities of human emotions and being patient and gentle in handling them.

translation: It is not lawful for you (to marry other) women after this, nor to change them for (other) wives, even though their beauty attract you, except any (captives or slaves) that your right hands possess. And Allah is Ever a Watcher over all things.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not allowed to marry any more women after the wives he already had, nor was he permitted to divorce any of them and take others in their place, regardless of how beautiful or attractive they might be. The exception 'except what your right hands possess' refers to the slaves or captives that were under his control, indicating a different ruling for them. The verse emphasizes God's watchfulness over all things, suggesting that He is fully aware of the actions and intentions of His servants, and will hold them accountable accordingly.

translation: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet except when you are permitted for a meal, without awaiting its readiness. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for conversation. Indeed, that was troubling the Prophet, and he is shy of [dismissing] you. But Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask [his wives] for something, ask them from behind a partition. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not [conceivable or lawful] for you to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of Allah an enormity.
interpretation: This verse establishes rules for interacting with the Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing respect for his privacy and the sanctity of his household. It highlights the importance of seeking permission before entering his home and not lingering after meals. It also introduces the concept of hijab for the Prophet's wives, indicating a separation between the public and private spheres to maintain purity of heart for both the believers and the Prophet's wives. Furthermore, it underscores the prohibition against marrying the Prophet's wives after his death, signifying their unique status and the reverence due to them and the Prophet. The verse conveys that certain actions are considered significant in the eyes of God, emphasizing the need for believers to be mindful of their behavior towards the Prophet and his family.

translation: If you manifest something or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever, concerning all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, emphasizing that nothing is hidden from Him, whether it is openly manifested or concealed. It underscores the futility of attempting to hide one's actions or intentions from Allah, as He is omniscient and aware of all things.

translation: There is no blame upon them [wives] with regard to their fathers, nor their sons, nor their brothers, nor their brothers’ sons, nor their sisters’ sons, nor their women, nor what their right hands possess. And be conscious of God. Indeed God is ever, over all things, a Witness.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the importance of modesty and proper conduct for believing women, particularly in relation to their interactions with certain male relatives and others. It is indicating that certain categories of men are considered 'mahram' (those in whose presence a woman is not required to observe the full veil or modesty rules because they are closely related and marriage is prohibited between them), and thus there is no blame on women for not observing the same level of modesty in front of them as they would with non-mahram men. The verse then reminds them to remain mindful of God's watchfulness over all their actions, reinforcing the idea that while certain relaxations are allowed in the presence of mahram relatives, they should still be conscious of their overall behavior and conduct.

translation: Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and salute him with a proper salutation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of showing reverence and respect to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It begins by stating that Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet, establishing a divine precedent. The verse then addresses the believers, instructing them to follow this example by sending their own blessings and salutations upon the Prophet. The use of 'صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما' (send blessings upon him and salute him with a proper salutation) underscores the importance of invoking peace and blessings upon the Prophet as a way of demonstrating devotion and respect. The verse can be seen as fostering a sense of community and unity among believers by encouraging a shared practice that connects them directly to the Prophet and, by extension, to Allah. It also emphasizes the Prophet's central role in Islam, not just as a messenger but as a figure around whom the community rallies in reverence and devotion. By invoking blessings upon the Prophet, believers are participating in a ritual that reinforces their faith and their bond with the divine.

translation: Indeed, those who cause harm to Allah and His Messenger - Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who cause harm or distress to Allah and His Messenger, indicating that such actions are not taken lightly by Allah. It signifies that those who engage in such behavior are subject to Allah's curse both in this life and the hereafter, and that a humiliating punishment is prepared for them. The harm or distress referred to here is likely to be understood as verbal abuse, disobedience, or any form of disrespect towards Allah and His Messenger. The verse underscores the gravity of offending or disobeying Allah and His Messenger, emphasizing the severe consequences that follow such actions in both the worldly life and the hereafter.

translation: And those who harm believing men and believing women for [something] other than what they have earned, have certainly borne upon themselves a calumny and a manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against harming or slandering believers without just cause. It emphasizes that those who wrongfully cause pain or distress to the faithful, whether men or women, by accusing them of something they have not done, are guilty of bearing a false and manifest sin. The verse underscores the gravity of such actions, highlighting the importance of treating believers with respect and kindness, and the severe consequences of failing to do so.

translation: O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of modesty for the believing women. The command to draw their outer garments (jalabib) over themselves is to distinguish them as respectable and chaste women, so they are not harassed or molested. The underlying message is that a society's moral fabric is preserved when its women are treated with dignity and respect, and this is achieved through the practice of modesty.

translation: If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease and those who spread false news in Al-Madinah do not cease, We shall certainly let you overpower them, then they will not be able to stay in it as your neighbours but a little while
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the hypocrites, those with diseased hearts, and the spreaders of false rumors in Medina, indicating that if they do not cease their actions, they will be dealt with firmly by the Prophet and the believers, and their presence in Medina will be short-lived, suggesting a divine plan to cleanse the community of such harmful elements.

translation: Cursed, wherever they are found, they are seized and slaughtered relentlessly
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences faced by those who are cursed or rejected by Allah. The phrase 'wherever they are found, they are seized and slaughtered' signifies the relentless pursuit and eradication of such individuals, indicating a state of being utterly forsaken and relentlessly persecuted.

translation: The tradition of Allah in those who passed away before. And you will not find a change in the tradition of Allah.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the laws and patterns that Allah has set in motion for previous nations will continue unchanged, implying a sense of continuity and consistency in divine justice and response to human actions. It underscores that the consequences of one's deeds, whether good or bad, are part of an unalterable divine tradition that has been in place since the beginning.

translation: People ask you about the Hour. Say, 'Knowledge of it is only with Allah. And what can make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of human knowledge, emphasizing that the timing of the Hour (or Judgment Day) is known only to Allah. It also serves as a warning that the Hour could arrive unexpectedly, at any moment, underscoring the importance of being prepared for it by living a righteous life.

translation: Indeed, God has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who reject faith are not only cursed by God, but also face a severe punishment in the afterlife, underscoring the gravity of their spiritual state and the consequences of their disbelief.

translation: Abiding therein eternally; they will not find a guardian or a helper.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who have earned the wrath of Allah and have been condemned to Hellfire will be eternally trapped, with no escape or respite. The phrase 'they will not find a guardian nor a helper' underscores their utter helplessness and isolation, implying that they will be unable to secure any form of intercession, protection, or salvation from their torment, highlighting the irreversible nature of their punishment.

translation: The Day when their faces will be turned over in the Fire, they will say: 'Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger (Muhammad SAW).'
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and remorse that individuals will experience on the Day of Judgment when they are thrown into Hellfire, realizing too late that their disobedience to God's commands and the teachings of His Messenger was a grave mistake. It underscores the importance of obedience to divine guidance in this life to avoid suffering in the hereafter.

translation: And they will say, "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our dignitaries, and they misled us from the [right] path."
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of blind following and the accountability of individuals for their actions. The people referred to in the verse are acknowledging that they followed their leaders and elders without questioning, and as a result, they were misled from the right path. The verse suggests that the misguided individuals are not absolving themselves of responsibility, but rather, they are acknowledging the role that their leaders played in leading them astray. It emphasizes the importance of personal responsibility and critical thinking, as individuals are held accountable for their choices, even if they were influenced by others.

translation: Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse.
interpretation: This verse is a supplication against those who have disbelieved and wronged. The phrase 'double the torment' signifies an intensified punishment for their disbelief and wrongdoing, suggesting a severe and compounded retribution. The subsequent curse invoked upon them underscores the gravity of their transgression and the severity of their punishment in the hereafter, highlighting the Quranic theme of accountability for one's actions and the consequences of rejecting faith and committing injustice.

translation: O you who have believed, do not be like those who annoyed Moses, then Allah cleared him of what they said. And he was highly honored with Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the believers not to behave like those who harmed Moses by their accusations and slander. It highlights the importance of treating prophets and righteous individuals with respect and dignity. The phrase 'فبرأه الله مما قالوا' (and Allah cleared him of what they said) demonstrates Allah's power to vindicate His messengers and uphold their honor against false accusations. The statement 'وكان عند الله وجيها' (and he was highly honored with Allah) underscores Moses' esteemed position in the eyes of Allah, emphasizing that despite the harm caused by others, Moses' status remained unimpeached. This verse encourages believers to reflect on their behavior towards righteous individuals and prophets, and to avoid causing them harm or distress, as Allah will ultimately vindicate and honor those who are faithful and righteous.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate righteousness.
interpretation: This verse is urging believers to be mindful of their duty to God and to speak truthfully and sincerely. The phrase 'قولوا قولا سديدا' (speak a straight word) implies that one's words should be honest, accurate, and to the point, without deviation or distortion. This is not just a call to truthfulness, but also to integrity in speech, suggesting that believers should be careful in their communication to avoid causing harm or confusion. By doing so, they demonstrate their fear of God and their commitment to righteousness.

translation: He will make your deeds acceptable to you and forgive your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that obedience to Allah and His Messenger is the key to achieving great success, as it leads to the rectification of one's deeds and the forgiveness of one's sins, thereby granting the individual a profound and ultimate triumph.

translation: Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it; but man [undertook to] bear it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense responsibility that comes with being entrusted with the 'amanah' (trust), which can be understood as the moral and spiritual responsibility given to humans. The fact that the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, which are inanimate objects or entities without free will, were unwilling to bear this trust and felt a deep sense of fear towards it, underscores the weight and gravity of this responsibility. In contrast, humans, despite being warned, took on this responsibility. The verse then critiques human nature by describing humans as 'zaluman jahula', meaning they are prone to being unjust to themselves and others and are often ignorant of the consequences of their actions. This suggests that humans, while capable of shouldering great moral and spiritual responsibilities, are also inherently flawed and prone to making grave mistakes, highlighting the need for guidance and self-reflection.

translation: That God may punish the hypocrites, men and women, and the men and women who associate partners with God, and that God may accept the repentance of the believers, men and women. And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's dual treatment of different groups based on their faith and actions. It indicates that God will punish the hypocrites (both men and women) and those who associate partners with God (also both men and women), while showing mercy and accepting the repentance of believers (again, both men and women). The underlying message is one of justice and mercy, where the faith and actions of individuals determine their fate. The verse concludes by affirming God's forgiving and merciful nature, suggesting that His mercy encompasses those who are sincere in their faith.

translation: Praise be to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. To Him belongs praise in the Hereafter, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse highlights the all-encompassing sovereignty and praise of Allah, emphasizing that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. The verse also underscores Allah's wisdom and His all-encompassing knowledge, suggesting that His dominion and praise are not limited to the worldly life but extend into the Hereafter. It implies that Allah's governance is characterized by wisdom and that He is fully aware of all things, thereby establishing a foundation for trust and reverence in His absolute authority and judgment.

translation: He knows what penetrates into the earth and what emerges from it and what descends from the heaven and what ascends therein. And He is the Merciful, the Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's all-encompassing knowledge, emphasizing that He is aware of everything that enters the earth (such as rain, seeds, or buried objects), everything that exits from it (like plants, minerals, or hidden treasures), everything that descends from the heavens (for example, rain, snow, or divine decrees), and everything that ascends to the heavens (such as prayers, souls, or angels). The verse concludes by describing God as 'the Merciful, the Forgiving,' indicating that His comprehensive knowledge is coupled with mercy and forgiveness, suggesting that His awareness of all things is not merely for judgment but also for showing compassion and pardoning His creation.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will most certainly come to you. [He is] the Knower of the unseen." Not absent from Him is an atom's weight in the heavens or in the earth or [what is] smaller than that or greater, except that it is in a clear register
interpretation: This verse highlights the certainty of the Day of Judgment, which the disbelievers deny. The verse asserts that the Day of Judgment is inevitable and that Allah, being the Knower of the unseen, has complete knowledge of everything in the heavens and the earth, no matter how small or large. The verse implies that the occurrence of the Day of Judgment is predestined and recorded in the 'Preserved Tablet' or 'the Clear Book', emphasizing the idea of divine omniscience and the inevitability of the hereafter. It serves as a warning to those who deny the hereafter, affirming that their denial will not avert its arrival.

translation: That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds. Those will have forgiveness and noble provision.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for those who have faith and perform good deeds. The 'magnificent provision' refers to the blessings and rewards in the hereafter, while 'forgiveness' signifies the pardon of their sins. It emphasizes that faith and righteous actions are prerequisites for receiving these divine rewards, underscoring the importance of living a virtuous life according to God's guidance.

translation: And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to thwart them - for them is a painful punishment of abasement.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who strive to undermine or invalidate the signs of Allah, suggesting that their efforts to disbelieve or disobey will ultimately lead to a painful and humiliating punishment.

translation: And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth and it guides to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who possess knowledge and those who do not, in terms of their response to the revelation. It suggests that true knowledge is not just about accumulating information, but about recognizing the truth and being guided by it. The verse implies that the Qur'an is not just a source of information, but a guide that leads to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, indicating that the ultimate goal of the revelation is not just to impart knowledge, but to guide humanity towards a righteous path that is in accordance with the attributes of God, namely 'Aziz (Almighty) and Hamid (Praiseworthy). This interpretation underscores the importance of knowledge in understanding and living by the divine guidance.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Shall we show you a man who will inform you [that] when you have disintegrated in complete disintegration, you will [then] be [recreated] in a new creation?"
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the disbelievers' skepticism and mockery towards the idea of resurrection. They are questioning the possibility of being recreated after being completely torn apart and dispersed. The verse is pointing to the disbelievers' inability to comprehend the power of Allah and their lack of faith in the afterlife, as they are challenging the notion that they can be reassembled and recreated anew.

translation: Do you falsely attribute to God [something] or are you afflicted with madness?  Nay, but those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in the punishment and in the far error.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the consequences of disbelieving in the Hereafter. It suggests that those who do not believe in the afterlife are not only deserving of punishment but are also far astray from the right path, implying a deep-seated spiritual and moral deviation.

translation: Have they not considered what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and earth? If We willed, We could cause the earth to swallow them or cause a piece of the sky to fall upon them. Indeed in that is a sign for every servant turning back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who deny the truth and are obstinate in their disbelief. It signifies that Allah has the power to punish them in various ways, either by causing the earth to swallow them or by sending a piece of the sky upon them. The verse is indicating that the natural world, the heavens and the earth, are under Allah's control and can be used as a means of punishment or as a sign for those who are willing to turn back to Him in repentance and submission.

translation: And We certainly gave David grace from Us: 'O mountains and birds, repeat with him [in praise]!' And We made soft for him iron.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special favor granted to Prophet David by God, where not only he, but also the natural world around him, including mountains and birds, were made to glorify and worship God in harmony with him. Furthermore, it signifies the miraculous ability given to David to manipulate iron as if it were soft, a reference to his skill in crafting armor and other iron works without the need for fire or hammering, symbolizing his prophetic miracle and the divine blessings he received.

translation: “Make coats of mail, balancing well the rings, and do righteous deeds; indeed, I am Seeing of what you do.” (Qur'an 34:11)
interpretation: This verse is instructing Prophet Dawud (David) to perfect his craftsmanship in making coats of mail and to measure the links carefully. The verse is not just about the technical skill of making armor, but is also a reminder to Dawud and his people to do righteous deeds, as God is watchful over their actions. The making of coats of mail is symbolic of preparation for the challenges of life, and the verse is emphasizing the importance of diligence and righteousness in one's endeavors.

translation: And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind - its morning [journey] was a month and its evening [journey] was a month, and We caused to flow for him a spring of [liquid] copper. And among the jinn were those who worked for him by the permission of his Lord. And whoever deviated among them from Our command - We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extraordinary favors bestowed upon Prophet Solomon, including the subjugation of the wind and the jinn to his will. The verse demonstrates God's immense power and ability to subject even the most powerful forces in nature to the will of His messengers. The jinn, who are often associated with darkness and chaos, are here depicted as being harnessed by Solomon to carry out tasks, illustrating the triumph of divine order over chaos. The verse also serves as a warning to those who deviate from God's command, as they will face the punishment of the blazing fire, underscoring the importance of obedience to divine authority.

translation: They worked for him what he willed of chambers and statues and basins like reservoirs, and cauldrons firmly fixed. 'Work, family of David, in gratitude.' And few of My servants are grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and the rarity of true thankfulness among God's servants. The verse begins by describing the blessings bestowed upon the family of David, where they are gifted with the ability to create magnificent works such as statues, large basins, and firmly fixed cauldrons. However, the crux of the verse lies in God's command to the family of David to 'work gratefully.' The phrase 'and few of My servants are grateful' underscores the scarcity of those who truly appreciate and acknowledge God's blessings. It suggests that despite being endowed with numerous favors, most people fail to express genuine gratitude, making the family of David's situation a rare instance of being reminded to be thankful.

translation: But when We decreed death upon him [Solomon], nothing indicated to them [the jinn] his death except a creature of the earth that ate his staff. And when he fell, it became clear to the jinn that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating torment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ignorance and misconception of the jinn about their knowledge of the unseen. It is stated that when Prophet Solomon died, the jinn continued their labor, unaware of his demise, until a creature of the earth (likely a termite or woodworm) ate through his staff, causing him to fall. This event revealed to the jinn that they did not possess knowledge of the unseen; otherwise, they would not have remained in a state of humiliating toil for so long. The verse serves as a correction to the belief that the jinn have access to hidden knowledge, emphasizing that their understanding is limited and that they are subject to the same lack of knowledge as humans when it comes to the unseen.

translation: There was certainly a sign for Saba' in their dwelling place - two gardens on the right and on the left. [They were told], "Eat from the provisions of your Lord and be grateful to Him. A good land [have you], and a Lord competent to forgive."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and the reciprocal relationship between divine blessings and human acknowledgment. The people of Sheba were blessed with a bountiful land and abundant provisions, yet the verse emphasizes that such blessings are not merely ends in themselves but are contingent upon the people's expression of gratitude to their Lord. The phrase 'and be grateful to Him' underscores the Qur'anic theme that divine favor is often conditional upon human response, suggesting that the continuity of blessings depends on the acknowledgment and appreciation of those blessings. The description of the land as 'good' and the Lord as 'Oft-Forgiving' further reinforces the idea that the divine provision is not just material but also encompasses a moral and spiritual dimension, inviting a response that is both practical and devotional.

translation: But they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of the dam, and We replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk trees, and a few lote trees.
interpretation: This verse is a lesson in the consequences of ingratitude and disobedience. The people being referred to were blessed with two gardens, symbolizing a life of ease and plenty. However, upon turning away from God's commands and blessings, they were punished with a great flood (sayl al-'arim), and their bountiful gardens were replaced with ones that produced bitter and useless fruit, signifying a life of hardship and scarcity. This transformation serves as a metaphor for how divine blessings can be withdrawn and replaced with hardship as a result of human disobedience and lack of gratitude.

translation: That is how We requite them for their disbelief. And do We requite anyone except the ungrateful?
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of divine justice, where those who reject faith are met with consequences befitting their actions. It underscores the idea that ingratitude and disbelief lead to punishment, serving as a warning to those who refuse to acknowledge and obey God's commands.

translation: And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed [other] towns easy to be seen and [We] made the journey between them easy. [Saying], 'Travel between them by nights and days safe.'
interpretation: This verse highlights God's wisdom in arranging the geographical layout of the land to facilitate safe travel for the people. The 'blessed towns' refer to the region of Syria and Palestine, which were prosperous and significant in trade and commerce. The verse suggests that God made the journey between these blessed towns and other areas straightforward by placing visible and notable towns in between, making it easier for travelers to navigate. The command to travel 'securely by night and by day' underscores the idea that the route was not only straightforward but also safe, emphasizing God's providence in ensuring the security of travelers.

translation: And they said, 'Our Lord, make the distances between our journeys [longer],' and they wronged themselves, so We made them stories and dispersed them with a total dispersion. Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful [person].
interpretation: This verse is a commentary on the consequences of ingratitude and injustice. The people being referred to were given blessings and opportunities, but instead of being thankful, they complained about the distances they had to travel for trade, indicating their discontent with the provisions they had been given. Their ingratitude and self-injustice led to their downfall and dispersion. The verse suggests that their story serves as a lesson for those who are patient and grateful, implying that patience and gratitude are key virtues that can prevent a similar downfall. It highlights the importance of appreciating the blessings one has and being content with one's circumstances, as a means to avoid suffering a similar fate.

translation: And indeed, Satan proved true his thought about them, and they followed him, except for a party of the believers
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological aspect of Satan's influence on humans. It suggests that Satan's ability to mislead people is closely tied to their own predispositions and inclinations. The fact that Satan's assumption about humans was proven correct implies that humans have a certain vulnerability to his whispers and temptations. However, the exception of 'a group of believers' indicates that faith serves as a protective barrier against Satan's influence, enabling some individuals to resist his temptations and remain steadfast on the right path.

translation: And he had no authority over them, except that We might know him who believes in the Hereafter from him who is in doubt about it. And your Lord is, over all things, Guardian.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omniscience and His ability to keep track of all things, emphasizing that even when Satan or other forces seem to have influence, it is actually within God's knowledge and control, and is used to test the faith of individuals, distinguishing between those who have firm belief in the Hereafter and those who are doubtful about it.

translation: Say, 'Call those you claim besides Allah. They do not possess [even] the weight of a speck in the heavens or on the earth, and they have no partnership in either, nor is there among them any assistant to Him.'
interpretation: This verse is a rebuke to those who associate partners with Allah. It challenges them to call upon these supposed deities to demonstrate their power. The verse asserts that these false gods have no control or influence over anything in the heavens or the earth, not even to the extent of the weight of a tiny atom (ذرة). It further emphasizes that they have no share or partnership in the creation or governance of the universe, nor do they have any support or assistance to offer to Allah. The verse is highlighting the futility and powerlessness of idolatry and polytheism, underscoring the uniqueness and sovereignty of Allah.

translation: And intercession does not benefit with Him except for one whom He permits, until when fear is removed from their hearts, they say, 'What is it that your Lord has said?' They say, 'The truth.' And He is the Most High, the Grand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hierarchy and authority in the divine realm, emphasizing that intercession is only effective with Allah's permission. It underscores the awe and reverence with which the angels regard Allah, as they are only able to speak after their fear has subsided, and when they do, they affirm the truth and majesty of Allah's words, reinforcing His supreme authority and greatness.

translation: Say, "Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?" Say, "Allah." And indeed, we or you are either upon guidance or in clear error."
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the fact that both the Muslims and their opponents (likely the polytheists or disbelievers) claim to be on the right path. The verse is challenging the opponents to reflect on who provides for them from the heavens and the earth, and the answer is given that it is Allah. The underlying message is that the one who acknowledges and is grateful for Allah's provision is more likely to be on the right guidance, implying that the Muslims, who worship and acknowledge Allah as their provider, are on the correct path, while their opponents are in manifest error.

translation: Say, 'You will not be asked about what we committed, and we will not be asked about what you do.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that the disbelievers and the believers are on two separate paths, and that the accountability for their actions will be individual. The verse is indicating that the disbelievers should not expect to be questioned about the actions of the believers, and vice versa. It signifies a separation between the two groups and emphasizes that each group will be judged based on their own deeds.

translation: Say, 'Our Lord will bring us together; then He will judge between us in truth. And He is the best judge, the Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate reckoning and judgment that will take place on the Day of Judgment, where Allah will gather all parties involved in disputes and controversies, and then render a just and truthful verdict, highlighting His attributes as the opener of doors to justice and the all-knowing.

translation: Say, "Show me those whom you have ascribed to Him as partners. No, for He is Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical rebuke to those who associate partners with Allah. It challenges them to provide evidence or justification for their claims, implying that their assertions are baseless. The response 'No, it is Allah who is the Almighty, the All-Wise' underscores the futility of their claims and reaffirms Allah's sovereignty and wisdom, suggesting that the attribution of partners to Him is unfounded and contradicts the reality of His all-encompassing power and wisdom.

translation: And We have not sent you (O Prophet) except comprehensively to mankind as a bearer of good news and a warner, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the universal nature of the Prophet Muhammad's mission, emphasizing that he was sent as a bearer of good news and a warner to all of humanity, not just to a specific group or community. The phrase 'but most people do not know' suggests that despite the universal scope of the Prophet's message, many people remain unaware of or do not understand its significance and relevance to their lives.

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and mockery of those who deny the truth, challenging the believers to bring about the Day of Judgment if they are indeed truthful in their claims, thus underscoring the tension between faith and disbelief.

translation: Say to them, "There is an appointed Day for you, which you cannot delay by a single hour, nor can you bring it forward."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and the precise timing of the Day of Judgment, indicating that it will occur exactly as foretold without any delay or advance, stressing the certainty and the punctuality of the divine plan.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'We will never believe in this Qur'an nor in that which came before it.' If you could but see when the wrongdoers will be made to stand before their Lord, throwing back at one another the blame; those who were regarded as weak will say to those who were arrogant, 'If not for you, we would have been believers'.
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and blame-shifting that will occur among the disbelievers and the oppressors on the Day of Judgment. The weak and oppressed will blame the powerful and arrogant leaders for their disbelief, suggesting that if it weren't for their influence, they would have believed. This verse underscores the complex dynamics of influence and responsibility, pointing to the fact that the leaders and the misguided followers will be held accountable for their actions, and that the excuses made on that Day will be too late to alter their fate.

translation: Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, "Did we keep you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogant and oppressive behavior of those who held power over the weak and oppressed. The leaders or the arrogant ones are denying responsibility for misleading the weak, instead, they are accusing the weak of being criminals, suggesting that their downfall was a result of their own actions, not the guidance or leadership they received.

translation: And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, 'Rather, it was your plotting by night and day, when you were telling us to disbelieve in Allah and make for Him rivals.' And they will [secretly] conceal their remorse when they see the punishment; and We will put the shackles upon the necks of those who disbelieved. Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony of the oppressors' and the oppressed's situations in this life and the hereafter. The weak, who were oppressed, will hold the oppressors accountable for misleading them into disbelief and polytheism. The oppressors, upon seeing the punishment, will be filled with regret, but it will be too late. The verse emphasizes that the punishment is a direct consequence of their actions, and they will be held accountable for their deeds. The chains that will be put around the necks of the disbelievers symbolize the inescapable nature of their punishment, underscoring the principle of justice that underlies the divine plan.

translation: And We did not send a warner to a town, but its affluent ones said, 'Indeed, we are disbelievers in what you have been sent with.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern of arrogance and dismissal exhibited by the affluent and influential individuals within societies towards divine messengers and their messages. It underscores the tendency of those who are privileged and comfortable to reject the call to righteousness and moral accountability, often due to their entrenched worldly interests and complacency.

translation: And they say, 'We are more in wealth and children, and we will not be punished.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance of those who reject faith, boasting of their material wealth and children as if these were signs of divine favor or protection. The verse critiques the misguided belief that worldly possessions and progeny are indicators of divine approval or immunity from divine retribution, underscoring the disconnect between material wealth and spiritual righteousness.

translation: Say, 'My Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it], but most of mankind do not know.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the sovereignty of Allah in distributing sustenance among His creatures. It indicates that Allah alone has the authority to decide who receives abundance and who faces scarcity, based on His wisdom. The verse also touches on human ignorance, suggesting that many people fail to understand or acknowledge this divine prerogative, possibly leading to dissatisfaction or discontent with their circumstances.

translation: And it is not your wealth nor your children that bring you near to Us in station, except for he who believes and does righteous deeds; so it is they who will have a multiplied reward for what they have done, and they are in the upper chambers, secure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true proximity to Allah is not achieved through material wealth or family ties, but rather through faith and righteous deeds. It highlights that those who possess these qualities will be rewarded manifold for their actions and will dwell securely in the highest stations of Paradise, free from fear or harm.

translation: And those who strive against Our signs to thwart them - those are brought to the punishment.
interpretation: This verse is warning those who strive to undermine or invalidate the signs of Allah, suggesting that such individuals will be brought forth or made to face the punishment, implying a severe reckoning for their actions against the divine message.

translation: Say, "My Lord extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts [it] for him. But whatever thing you spend [in His cause] - He will compensate it; and He is the best of providers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine providence and the futility of worrying about material sustenance. It reassures believers that Allah is the ultimate provider and that He has the power to both grant abundance and impose scarcity upon whom He wills. The act of spending in the cause of Allah or for the benefit of others is encouraged, with the promise that Allah will replace what has been spent. This underscores the idea that true reliance should be on Allah, and that acts of charity and generosity are not merely altruistic but are also a means of participating in the divine economy of provision and replenishment. The verse concludes by affirming Allah as the best of providers, emphasizing the superiority of divine provision over any human means of sustenance or support.

translation: And [mention] the Day when He will gather them all and then say to the angels, "Did these [people] used to worship you?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony and the folly of idolatrous worship. On the Day of Judgment, God will gather all beings together and ask the angels if the people who worshipped them were actually worshipping them. The implication is that the angels, being aware of their own servitude to God and their inability to benefit or harm those who worshipped them, will likely respond in the negative, underscoring the misguided nature of the worship directed towards them.

translation: They said, 'Exalted are You; You, [You are] our wali other than them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them'.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reality that many people unknowingly follow and obey satanic influences, thinking they are following something or someone else. It indicates that the majority of those who were considered to be worshiping or following other entities were, in fact, under the influence of jinn, suggesting a form of spiritual or unseen allegiance that was not immediately apparent to them. It underscores the idea that true allegiance and worship can sometimes be misdirected or misunderstood, and that the actual object of one's devotion or obedience may not be as it seems.

translation: So today you do not own for each other [the power to] profit or harm, and We will say to those who wronged, Taste the punishment of the Fire, which you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, the power dynamics will be drastically different from those on earth. Those who were once in positions of power or influence will find themselves powerless to help or harm one another. It highlights the futility of worldly alliances and the reality of individual accountability before God. The verse also serves as a stern warning to those who have committed injustice, indicating that they will be held accountable for their actions and will face the punishment they had previously denied or mocked.

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidence, those who disbelieve say, 'This is not but a man who wants to deter you from what your fathers were worshipping.' And they say, 'This is not but a lie he has invented.' And those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, 'This is not but obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the truth. Despite being presented with clear evidence and signs from Allah, they attribute the Prophet's message to his personal motives and accuse him of fabricating lies. They cling to the traditions of their forefathers, refusing to accept the truth even when it is manifestly clear. The verse underscores the tendency of those who are entrenched in their disbelief to label the truth as magic, demonstrating their inability to distinguish between right and wrong, and their determination to reject the guidance that is offered to them.

translation: And We had not given them any scriptures which they could study, and We had not sent to them, before you, any warner.
interpretation: The verse highlights that the people being addressed had not been given any scripture or warning before the Prophet, emphasizing their lack of prior knowledge or caution regarding their actions and the consequences thereof, thus underscoring the fairness and justice in holding them accountable for their deeds.

translation: And those before them denied, and they have not attained a tenth of what We gave them, but they denied My messengers, so how was My rejection?
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by highlighting the severe consequences faced by previous nations who also denied their respective prophets. It emphasizes that despite being endowed with greater resources and capabilities than the current disbelievers, those past nations were still punished severely for their disbelief. The verse implies that the current disbelievers, having been given fewer blessings and yet still rejecting the truth, should expect an even more severe retribution. It underscores the principle that the punishment is not just commensurate with the sin but is also relative to the blessings and opportunities one has been given, making the rejection of divine guidance all the more egregious.

translation: Say, “I only advise you of one [thing]: that you stand for Allah in pairs and individually, and then reflect. Your companion is not possessed; he is only a warner to you before a severe punishment.”
interpretation: This verse is advising the people to reflect on their beliefs and actions by standing before God, either individually or in groups, and contemplating. It emphasizes that the Prophet is not possessed or mad, but rather a warner sent to caution them about an impending severe punishment, urging them to take heed and change their ways.

translation: Say, "I do not ask you for this message any payment [i.e., reward]; my payment is only from Allah. And He is, over all things, Witness."
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's (peace be upon him) sincerity and detachment from worldly gains. It emphasizes that his mission is not driven by a desire for personal benefit or reward from his people, but rather his accountability and reward are solely with Allah, who is witness to all things.
