interpretation: This verse is advising the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to turn away from those who are obstinate in their disbelief and rejection of the message, and to be patient with them for a time, indicating that their punishment or reckoning will come at its appointed hour.

translation: And let them see, for they will soon see.
interpretation: This verse is a warning and a threat to those who are in denial or opposition. It implies that the truth will become evident to them, and they will realize their mistakes, but it might be too late for them to benefit from this realization. The verse suggests that there will be a reckoning or a moment of clarity when the reality of their actions and the truth they denied will become apparent to them.

translation: Is it then Our punishment (that) they are impatient for?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the impatience and lack of faith of those who are being warned of the impending punishment. It is a rhetorical question that underscores the astonishment and incredulity at the eagerness with which people are seeking the very punishment they are being warned against, rather than heeding the warning and changing their ways. It suggests that their disbelief and disobedience are driven by a hasty and unreflective attitude, rather than a considered and thoughtful one.

translation: And when it (the punishment) descended upon their courtyard, evil was the morning of those who were warned!
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability and severity of God's punishment for those who have been warned but still refuse to heed the warning. The phrase 'evil was the morning of those who were warned' underscores the idea that the consequences of ignoring divine warnings are dire and that the punishment, when it comes, is inescapable and calamitous, marking the beginning of a terrible day for those who were supposed to have taken heed.

translation: And turn away from them until a time
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to turn away from those who reject his message, not to be disheartened by their rejection, and to wait for a while, as the divine plan will unfold and justice will be served.

translation: And see, for they will soon see
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the inevitability of accountability and reckoning. It suggests that those who are currently blind to the truth or are not seeing the consequences of their actions will soon be made to see, implying a future reckoning or judgment where their deeds will be revealed and they will be held accountable.

translation: Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Glory, above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence and purity of God, affirming that He is far exalted above the false and unbefitting descriptions attributed to Him by those who deny the truth or hold misconceptions about His nature. It serves as a declaration of God's absolute glory and majesty, underscoring the reverence and awe due to Him as the Lord of all might and honor.

translation: And peace be upon the messengers.
interpretation: This verse signifies the culmination of divine mercy and acknowledgment upon the prophets and messengers who were sent by God to guide humanity, emphasizing their role in conveying God's message and their ultimate success in their mission despite the challenges they faced.

translation: And all praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse signifies the acknowledgment of Allah's supremacy and sovereignty over all existence, emphasizing that all praise is due to Him as the Sustainer of all worlds, encompassing both the seen and unseen realms, and highlighting the monotheistic belief in His singular lordship over everything.

translation: Saad. By the Qur'an containing the reminder.
interpretation: This verse is an oath sworn by Allah using the letters 'Saad' and the Qur'an, emphasizing the Qur'an's role as a reminder to humanity. It signifies the importance and the weight of the message that is to follow, highlighting the Qur'an's status as a source of guidance and remembrance.

translation: But those who disbelieve are in pride and dissension.
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy and arrogance of those who reject faith. The phrase 'عزة' (izzah) implies a sense of pride and haughtiness, while 'شقاق' (shiqaq) refers to discord, opposition, or hostility. Together, they suggest that those who disbelieve are characterized by a stubborn and prideful resistance to the truth, refusing to submit to it due to their arrogance and enmity towards it.

translation: How many a generation We destroyed before them! Then they cried out when it was no longer a time for escape!
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth, highlighting that previous generations who were similarly obstinate in their disbelief were ultimately destroyed. It emphasizes that once the divine decree for punishment is executed, it is too late for repentance or escape, underscoring the inevitability of God's judgment.

translation: And they wonder that there has come to them a warner from among themselves. And the disbelievers say, "This is a magician, a liar."
interpretation: The verse highlights the irony and stubbornness of the disbelievers who, despite being warned by a messenger from among their own people, reject the message and label the messenger as a deceitful magician. This reaction underscores their disbelief and resistance to the truth, as they are astonished that a warner would come from among themselves, indicating their preconceived notions and biases against accepting the message.

translation: Have I made the gods [into] one God? Indeed, this is a wondrous thing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the astonishment and incredulity that people felt when faced with the idea of monotheism, as preached by the prophets. The speaker is expressing the notion that reducing multiple deities to a single one is considered a wondrous or astonishing claim, underscoring the radical departure from the polytheistic beliefs that were prevalent. It reflects the challenge that monotheistic messages faced in being accepted by societies accustomed to worshipping multiple gods.

translation: And the leaders among them went about [saying], "Continue, and be patient over your gods. Indeed, this is a thing intended."
interpretation: The verse highlights the obstinacy and misguided leadership of the disbelievers, who, instead of reflecting on the truth, encourage each other to remain steadfast in their false beliefs and idolatrous practices, suspecting that there is an ulterior motive or plot behind the call to monotheism.

translation: We never heard of this in the latest religion; this is not but a fabrication.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and close-mindedness of those who reject the truth, as they dismiss the Prophet Muhammad's message as mere fabrication, simply because it does not conform to the traditions and beliefs they inherited from their forefathers.

translation: Is it upon him that the Reminder is sent down among us? Rather, they are in doubt about My Reminder. Rather, they have not yet tasted the punishment.
interpretation: The verse is highlighting the skepticism and doubt of the disbelievers regarding the revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The phrase 'بل هم في شك من ذكري' (Rather, they are in doubt about My Reminder) suggests that their skepticism stems from a deeper issue - a lack of faith in the divine message itself. The verse is implying that their doubt is not just about the Prophet or the revelation, but about the very fabric of the divine guidance. The latter part of the verse 'بل لما يذوقوا عذاب' (Rather, they have not yet tasted the punishment) is indicating that their skepticism will be addressed when they experience the consequences of their disbelief, implying that the truth of the divine message will be made manifest to them through the punishment they will face.

translation: Or do they have the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord, the Exalted in Might, the Bestower?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the absurdity of the disbelievers' claims and attitudes by rhetorically asking if they possess the treasuries of their Lord's mercy. The verse is emphasizing that the distribution of Allah's mercy and bounty is solely in His hands, and that He is the One who decides to whom and when to give it. The verse is also pointing to the attributes of Allah as 'Al-'Aziz' (the Mighty) and 'Al-Wahhab' (the Bestower), indicating that His giving is not out of need or compulsion but out of His own will and generosity, thus underscoring the futility of human claims to control or distribute divine mercy.

translation: Or do they own the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend through [all] means.
interpretation: The verse is highlighting the absurdity of the disbelievers' claims and challenging their supposed authority over the heavens and the earth. It is emphasizing that they do not possess any dominion or control over the universe, and therefore, they should strive to ascend through the means or ways (الأسباب) to attain such a position, if they are truthful in their claims. However, it is implying that it is impossible for them to do so, as they lack the capability and the authority to ascend to such heights. The verse is, in essence, ridiculing their pretensions and emphasizing the futility of their endeavors.

translation: The hosts there will be defeated, among the parties.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the defeat of the confederate tribes that had allied themselves against the Prophet Muhammad and the Muslims in Medina. The phrase 'جند ما هنالك' (the hosts there) refers to these confederate tribes, and 'مهزوم من الأحزاب' (the defeated of the parties) signifies their ultimate failure in their attempt to besiege and destroy the Muslim community. The verse is highlighting the inevitability of defeat for those who band together against the truth and the believers, underscoring the divine support for the latter.

translation: Before them the people of Noah, 'Ad, and Pharaoh, the man of stakes, denied (the messengers)
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the historical pattern of denial and rejection by previous nations of their respective prophets. The mention of 'Pharaoh, the man of stakes' is particularly noteworthy as it not only refers to Pharaoh's power and might but also possibly alludes to his method of punishment or his grandiose building projects, thereby underscoring the magnitude of his tyranny and the severity of his denial of the truth.

translation: And (the people of) Thamud, and the people of Lot, and the Companions of the Wood; these were the (different) parties.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the diversity of nations and communities that rejected the prophets and were subsequently punished. The mention of various groups, such as Thamud, Lot, and the Companions of the Wood, serves to illustrate that the pattern of rejection and punishment is not limited to a specific people or time, but is a recurring theme throughout history, emphasizing the universal nature of God's justice and the consequences of disobedience.

translation: Not one [of the prophets] but was denied by the messengers, and then My punishment was justified.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern of prophetic missions throughout history, where every prophet sent by God was met with denial and rejection by their people. The verse underscores the inevitability and justice of God's punishment for those who refuse to heed the warnings and messages brought by His prophets, emphasizing that such punishment is not arbitrary but a justified response to the persistent rejection of divine guidance.

translation: And these people are not waiting for aught but a single blast; there will be no pause for them.
interpretation: The verse is warning that the disbelievers are not awaiting anything but a sudden and catastrophic event, likely referring to the Day of Judgment or a divine punishment, which will occur without any delay or respite, emphasizing the inevitability and swiftness of the reckoning.

translation: And they say, 'Our Lord, hasten for us our share (of punishment) before the Day of Reckoning'
interpretation: The verse highlights the arrogance and disbelief of those who mock the promise of the Day of Judgment, urging God to hasten their punishment, demonstrating their lack of faith and their misconception that there is no afterlife or accountability for their deeds.

translation: Be patient over what they say and remember Our servant, David, the one with strength. Indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back to God.
interpretation: This verse is urging the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain patient in the face of the hardships and criticisms he is facing from his detractors. It then draws his attention to the story of Prophet Dawud (David), who was known for his strength and power ('ذا الأيد'), but more importantly, for his repentance and turning back to God ('إنه أواب'). The verse is suggesting that just as Dawud was a servant of God who was characterized by his repentance and devotion, the Prophet Muhammad should also remain steadfast and devoted to his Lord, even in the face of adversity. The verse is encouraging the Prophet to draw strength and inspiration from the example of Dawud, and to cultivate a similar spirit of repentance and devotion.

translation: Indeed, We subjected the mountains [to praise] with him, glorifying in the evening and at sunrise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extraordinary favor bestowed upon Prophet David, where even the mountains, typically seen as inanimate objects, are made to glorify and praise Allah alongside him. The phrase 'by the evening and the morning' signifies the consistency and regularity of this glorification, indicating that the natural world is attuned to a rhythm of worship that mirrors the cycles of time itself, underscoring the harmony between the natural order and the divine will.

translation: And the birds are gathered together, all are obedient to Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the state of creatures on the Day of Judgment, where even the birds are gathered and are obedient to God's command, emphasizing the universal submission to God's will on that day.

translation: And We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and decisive speech.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of wisdom and effective communication in leadership. The phrase 'فصل الخطاب' (fateh al-khitab), or 'the ability to decide and articulate one's thoughts clearly,' suggests that true strength and authority come not just from power, but from the ability to make wise decisions and convey them effectively. It implies that a leader's influence is significantly enhanced when they possess both the wisdom to make informed decisions and the skill to communicate those decisions in a clear and compelling manner.

translation: Has the story of the litigants reached you, when they climbed over into the sanctuary?
interpretation: This verse is referring to an event where a dispute or argument (الخصم) reached the Prophet Zakariya (peace be upon him) in a dramatic or unexpected manner, as indicated by 'إذ تسوروا المحراب' (when they climbed over into the sanctuary). The phrase 'المحراب' typically refers to a private chamber or sanctuary, often associated with a place of worship or devotion. The act of 'تسوروا' implies a sense of urgency or secrecy, suggesting that the matter was of great importance or sensitivity. The interpretation here is that this verse is highlighting the intrusion into Zakariya's private devotion or sanctuary by those bringing their dispute, underscoring the significance of the issue they were bringing to his attention, and possibly alluding to the divine intervention or message that follows such an intrusion.

translation: When they entered before David and he was frightened of them, they said, 'Fear not.' [We are] two litigants, one of whom has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth and do not be unjust; and guide us to the sound path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of justice and fairness in resolving disputes. The two disputants, who are described as having wronged one another, come to Prophet David seeking a just verdict. The phrase 'do not be unjust' and 'guide us to the straight path' emphasizes the need for impartiality and righteousness in judgment, underscoring that a just decision is one that is based on truth and equity, rather than personal bias or prejudice.

translation: Indeed, this my brother has ninety-nine ewes and I have one ewe; so he said, 'Entrust her to me,' and he overpowered me in speech.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the psychological manipulation and coercion that can occur in disputes, particularly when there is a significant imbalance of power or resources between the parties involved. The speaker's brother, who has a significant advantage in terms of the number of ewes he owns, uses his persuasive abilities to pressure the speaker into giving up his single ewe, demonstrating how the stronger party can exploit the weaker one through verbal dominance.

translation: He said, "He has certainly wronged you in demanding your ewe [in addition] to his ewes." And indeed, many associates oppress one another, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds - and they are few. And David became certain that We had tested him, so he asked forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing [in prostration] and turned back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of righteous companionship and the rarity of individuals who maintain justice and fairness in their interactions. It suggests that even among those who are closely associated, there is often a tendency towards injustice or exploitation. However, it notes an exception for those who have faith and perform good deeds, indicating that true believers are more likely to uphold justice and fairness. The verse also touches upon the theme of accountability and repentance, as exemplified by Prophet David, who, upon realizing he was being tested, sought forgiveness and turned back to his Lord in humility.

translation: So We forgave him that; and indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and reward that awaits those who are obedient and sincere in their devotion. The phrase 'زلفى' (zulfā) implies a closeness or nearness to Allah, suggesting that the individual has attained a high spiritual rank. 'حسن مآب' (ḥusn ma'āb) refers to a good end or a favorable return, indicating that the person's ultimate fate is secure and commendable. The verse underscores the idea that divine forgiveness paves the way for a special status and a commendable outcome for the individual, emphasizing the benevolent nature of Allah's judgment.

translation: O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow desire, as it will mislead you from the path of God. Indeed, those who mislead from the path of God will have a severe punishment because they forgot the Day of Account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and righteousness in leadership. It warns that following personal whims and desires can lead to deviation from the right path, and that those who deviate from God's guidance will face severe punishment because they have forgotten the Day of Reckoning, implying that accountability for one's actions is a crucial motivator for staying on the right path.

translation: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of disbelievers' skepticism towards the afterlife and the purpose of creation. It underscores that the universe and everything within it were not created without a purpose, contrary to the disbelievers' assumption. The verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith, emphasizing that their disbelief is not only a misguided view of the world's creation but also invites them to face the consequences of their denial in the hereafter, symbolized by the 'Fire'.

translation: Shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like corrupters on earth? Or shall We treat those who are pious like the wicked?
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of justice and differentiation in the treatment of individuals based on their actions and beliefs. It questions the idea of equating those who have faith and perform righteous deeds with those who cause corruption on earth, or comparing the righteous (those who are mindful of God and avoid evil) with the wicked. It underscores the notion that there is a distinction between the two groups in the eyes of God, emphasizing the importance of accountability and the consequences of one's actions. It suggests that a just system, such as the one God intends, does not treat the righteous and the wicked equally, reflecting the divine justice that is a recurring theme in the Qur'an.

translation: A Book which We have revealed unto you, full of blessings that they may ponder its verses, and that men of understanding may remember.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of reflection and contemplation in understanding the Quran. The phrase 'ليدبروا آياته' (that they may reflect upon its verses) indicates that the Quran is not meant to be merely recited, but rather its verses should be thoroughly pondered upon to grasp their deeper meaning and significance. The phrase 'وليتذكر أولو الألباب' (and that those endowed with understanding may take heed) suggests that the Quran is particularly meant for those who possess intellectual faculties and are capable of deriving lessons and guidance from its verses, implying that the Quran's true understanding is reserved for those who are intellectually equipped and spiritually inclined.

translation: And We gave to David, Solomon. An excellent servant! Indeed, he was one who turned to Allah (in repentance)
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character of Prophet Solomon, son of Prophet David. The phrase 'نعم العبد' (an excellent servant) signifies his righteousness and servitude to Allah. The term 'أواب' (one who turns to Allah in repentance) indicates his propensity for seeking forgiveness and turning back to Allah, demonstrating a high level of spiritual consciousness and humility.

translation: When there were displayed before him, in the afternoon, steeds of the highest breed.
interpretation: This verse refers to a test or trial that Prophet Solomon was faced with, where he was distracted by beautiful horses, symbolizing worldly allurements, and was thus made to forget his remembrance of God, highlighting the tension between worldly desires and spiritual obligations.

translation: And he said, "I love the love of good because of the remembrance of my Lord until it (the sun) was hidden by the veil (of night)."
interpretation: The verse is highlighting the psychological state where one's love for something good or beneficial can become so overwhelming that it distracts them from remembering their Lord. The phrase 'until the sun was hidden by the veil (of night)' is a metaphor for how intense this distraction can be, suggesting that the distraction lasted until the end of the day, emphasizing the strength of the distraction caused by the love for good.

translation: Bring them back to me,' and [he] began to slash [their] legs and necks.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the intense love and attachment Prophet Solomon had for horses, to the extent that when he was busy reviewing his horses and lost track of the time for prayer, he ordered them to be brought back to him and then proceeded to slaughter them as an act of atonement for his distraction from his religious duty, demonstrating the importance he placed on fulfilling his obligations to Allah.

translation: And We did test Solomon, and We placed upon his throne a body, then he turned (to Us).
interpretation: This verse is referring to a trial or test that Solomon faced. The 'body' on his throne is often interpreted as a lifeless or dummy body, signifying that Solomon was temporarily stripped of his power or kingship. The test was likely related to his humility and reliance on God. The fact that 'he turned (to Us)' indicates that Solomon repented and returned to God, demonstrating his faith and devotion.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and awareness of the transience of worldly power exhibited by Prophet Solomon. Despite being granted immense wealth and authority, he recognizes that true power and kingdom come from Allah and seeks forgiveness, demonstrating his understanding that even his extraordinary gifts are subject to divine will. His request for a kingdom that will not be given to anyone after him is often interpreted as a desire for a unique and enduring legacy that is pleasing to Allah, rather than a mere accumulation of worldly power. This reflects his focus on the hereafter and his acknowledgment of Allah as the ultimate Bestower of all gifts.

translation: So We subjected the wind to him; it flowed gently by his command wherever he directed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extraordinary favor bestowed upon Prophet Solomon, where the wind was subjugated to his will, serving as a manifestation of divine power and a demonstration of Solomon's unique status as a prophet and ruler, emphasizing the idea that true authority lies not in human might but in divine decree.

translation: And the devils, every builder and diver
interpretation: This verse highlights the extraordinary abilities and skills that the devils, under the command of Prophet Solomon, possessed. The 'builder' refers to their skill in constructing magnificent structures, possibly referring to the elaborate buildings and monuments Solomon commissioned. The 'diver' likely refers to their ability to dive into the depths of the ocean to retrieve pearls and other precious items, showcasing their supernatural capabilities and Solomon's dominion over both the human and supernatural realms.

translation: And others bound in fetters.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who will be bound together in chains in the hereafter, signifying the ultimate fate of those who have been obstinate in their disbelief and disobedience, highlighting the consequence of their actions and the justice that will be served on the Day of Judgment.

translation: This is Our gift; so give freely or withhold, without (the need for) account.
interpretation: This verse signifies God's generosity and the freedom He grants to individuals regarding their charitable actions. It implies that one's decision to give or withhold should be guided by a sense of accountability to God, even though the verse explicitly mentions 'without account.' The phrase 'without account' suggests that God's bounty is so vast that giving or withholding from it does not diminish or affect His resources in any way. It underscores the idea that generosity or stinginess are human choices that reflect one's character and faith, rather than affecting God's reckoning.

translation: And indeed, for him is a high rank with Us and a good final destination.
interpretation: This verse highlights the elevated status and ultimate good end that awaits a righteous individual. 'Zulfy' implies closeness or a high rank, suggesting a special position of honor or favor. 'Hasan m'ab' or 'good end' refers to a commendable or praiseworthy final destination or outcome, often understood in the context of the hereafter as a place of reward or paradise. The verse thus underscores the idea that the individual being referred to is not only held in high esteem but is also destined for a favorable outcome, reinforcing themes of divine justice and mercy.

translation: And remember Our servant Job when he invoked his Lord [saying], "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment."
interpretation: This verse highlights the human vulnerability to Satan's influence, as even a righteous servant like Job was not immune to Satan's affliction. It suggests that Satan's role is not just to tempt humans, but also to cause them physical and emotional suffering, underscoring the need for believers to seek refuge in God and invoke His help in times of distress.

translation: Strike with thy foot: here is (water) wherein is a cool bath and a drink.
interpretation: This verse is a directive to Prophet Ayub (Job) to strike the ground with his foot, which upon doing so, results in a spring or source of water emerging. The phrase 'this is a cool bath and a drink' signifies that the water from this spring is not only refreshing but also healing, serving both as a means for Prophet Ayub to bathe in and to quench his thirst, symbolizing relief and cure from the afflictions he was suffering.

translation: And We gifted him with his family and the like of them along with them as a mercy from Us and as a reminder for those endowed with understanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's grace and mercy towards the Prophet Job, restoring his family and doubling their number as a blessing. It signifies that such divine favors are not just rewards for the righteous but also serve as a lesson for those who possess understanding, reminding them of God's power and mercy.

translation: And take in your hand a bundle (of grass), and strike (your wife) with it, and do not break your oath. Indeed, We found him patient. An excellent servant. Indeed, he was one who constantly turned (to Allah).
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary patience and faithfulness of Prophet Ayyub (Job) in the face of immense suffering. Despite being afflicted with severe trials, he remained steadfast and committed to his oath, demonstrating unwavering obedience to God's command. The verse suggests that true servitude to God is characterized by patience, loyalty, and a deep-seated connection with the divine, as embodied by Prophet Ayyub.

translation: And remember Our servants, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, men of strength and vision.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary characteristics of the prophets Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Ya'qub, who were endowed with strength (أولي الأيدي) in their resolve and actions, as well as insight (الأبصار) into the truth and the future, serving as role models for believers.

translation: Indeed, We purified them with a sincere remembrance of the Home.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the individuals being referred to have been purified or singled out for a specific noble purpose, which is to be reminded of the Hereafter. The phrase 'بخالصة' (with a sincere or pure intention) indicates that their hearts and actions are dedicated solely to the remembrance and contemplation of the afterlife, free from worldly distractions. It implies a state of spiritual purification where their focus is entirely on the eternal life to come, highlighting the importance of the Hereafter in their beliefs and actions.

translation: And indeed, they are with Us among the chosen and the best.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the individuals being referred to are among those chosen and preferred by Allah, highlighting their elevated status and the special favor they enjoy in His sight. It underscores their distinction among others due to their merits or the role they are destined to fulfill, indicating a level of excellence and righteousness that sets them apart.

translation: And mention Ishmael and Elisha and Dhul-Kifl, all are among the best.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exemplary character of the prophets mentioned, emphasizing their righteousness and virtue as role models for believers. By invoking their names alongside others known for their piety, it underscores the importance of following in the footsteps of those who have demonstrated unwavering commitment to God's will.

translation: This is a reminder. And indeed, for the righteous is a good final destination.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Qur'an is a reminder to people, and for those who are mindful of Allah and follow His guidance, there is a good final destination, implying a promise of a favorable outcome or reward in the hereafter for the righteous.

translation: Gardens of Eden, whose gates are opened for them
interpretation: This verse signifies the honor and ease of entry that the righteous will experience in the afterlife, as the gates of paradise are already open for them, indicating a state of readiness and welcome, free from any hindrance or delay.

translation: Reclining therein, they will call therein for abundant fruit and drink.
interpretation: This verse indicates that in Paradise, believers will be in a state of comfort and relaxation (mutakkin), enjoying abundant fruits and drinks, highlighting the luxurious and pleasurable nature of the afterlife for the righteous.

translation: And with them will be those of modest gaze, companions of equal age.
interpretation: This verse is referring to the companions or spouses that believers will have in Paradise. 'Qasirat al-Tarf' (those who restrain their gaze) implies that they are chaste and modest, looking only at their husbands. 'Atrab' (of equal age) suggests that these companions will be youthful and of the same age, emphasizing the blissful and harmonious nature of the relationships in Paradise, free from the discord and disparity that can be found in worldly life.

translation: This is what you were promised for the Day of Reckoning
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Day of Reckoning is inevitable and is a day when all individuals will be held accountable for their deeds. The phrase 'this is what you were promised' serves as a reminder to people of the warnings they received about the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that it is a reality that they cannot escape or postpone. It underscores the certainty and the significance of the Day of Reckoning, highlighting the importance of being prepared for it by living a righteous life.

translation: Indeed, this is Our provision, it has no exhaustion.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the provision and blessings bestowed by Allah are endless and will never be depleted. The phrase 'ما له من نفاد' (ma lahu min nafād) emphasizes the inexhaustible nature of Allah's bounty, suggesting that His generosity is boundless and perpetual, offering comfort and assurance to believers about the continuity of divine provision.

translation: And indeed, for the transgressors is an evil destination
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who transgress and rebel against the commandments of Allah, indicating that they will have a terrible destination to return to, implying a severe punishment or retribution in the hereafter for their disobedience.

translation: They will burn in Hell, and what a wretched resting place.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Hellfire is not just a temporary abode of punishment but a resting place that is utterly detestable, highlighting the eternal and woeful nature of the fate that awaits those who are condemned to it.

translation: So let them taste it - boiling water and a festering discharge
interpretation: This verse is a severe warning to those who deny the truth and reject the message of the prophets. The phrase 'حميم' (hamim) refers to boiling water and 'غساق' (ghasaq) is a pus-like fluid that flows from the bodies of the inhabitants of Hell. The verse implies that those who are punished in Hell will be forced to endure extreme physical suffering, being given boiling water and pus to drink, emphasizing the horrific nature of their punishment.

translation: And others of similar kind (are paired together)
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that everything in the universe is created in pairs, emphasizing the concept of duality and the interconnectedness of all things. It suggests that this pairing is a universal principle, reflecting the balance and harmony that underlie the creation.

translation: This is a troop rushing in with you. No welcome for them. Indeed, they will burn in the Fire.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the stark contrast between those who are being welcomed into Paradise and those who are being condemned to Hell. The phrase 'a troop rushing in with you' is significant because it indicates that both groups are being judged simultaneously, emphasizing the idea that the fate of the righteous and the wicked is inextricably linked to their actions in this life. The rejection and condemnation of the wicked serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of disobedience and the importance of living a virtuous life.

translation: They will say, 'Nay, you [yourselves]! No welcome to you! You have brought it upon us! So evil is the abode.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Day of Judgment's stark reality, where the misguided followers will turn on their leaders, blaming them for their misfortune. It underscores the theme of accountability and the consequences of blindly following others into disobedience and sin.

translation: They will say, 'Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, add to him double punishment in the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the escalating nature of punishment in the afterlife for those who were leaders or influencers in misguiding others. It suggests that not only will they face the original punishment for their own wrongdoings, but they will also receive an additional, intensified punishment for having led others astray. The doubling of their punishment in the fire reflects the gravity of their responsibility and the compounded consequences of their actions.

translation: And they say: What is the matter with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the wicked.
interpretation: The verse highlights the disbelievers' astonishment and bewilderment at not seeing the people they previously considered to be evil or inferior being punished or destroyed, as they had expected. This reflects their misunderstanding of the nature of divine justice and their misconstrued perceptions of good and evil, indicating a lack of faith in the divine wisdom and justice.

translation: Have we made them an object of ridicule or have the eyes missed them?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the astonishment and bewilderment of the disbelievers who were unable to recognize or appreciate the companions of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and instead mocked or ridiculed them. The verse is questioning whether the disbelievers' inability to see the truth or appreciate the believers was due to their own blindness or whether they were simply being mocked by the believers. It underscores the theme of spiritual blindness and the inability of those who are heedless to perceive the truth.

translation: Indeed, that is the truth - the dispute among the people of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the intense dispute and argument among the inhabitants of Hell is a testament to the reality of their punishment and the truth of their recompense for their deeds in the worldly life. It underscores the inevitability and justice of their fate, as they now argue and blame one another for their misguided paths that led them to this end.

translation: Say, 'I am only a warner, and there is not any deity except Allah, the One, the Prevailing.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness and supremacy of God, highlighting that there is no other deity worthy of worship besides Him. The phrase 'الواحد القهار' (Al-Wahid Al-Qahhar) underscores God's uniqueness and His overwhelming power over all creation, reinforcing the central Islamic belief in Tawhid (the oneness of God). The speaker, likely the Prophet Muhammad, is reminded that his role is merely to warn people of the consequences of not believing in this fundamental principle, thereby stressing the importance of monotheism.

translation: The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, the Exalted in Might, the Ever-Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence and mercy of Allah. 'The Exalted in Might' signifies Allah's supreme power and authority over all creation, while 'the Ever-Forgiving' highlights His merciful nature, indicating that despite His immense power, He is also forgiving towards His servants, showing that His justice is balanced with mercy.

translation: Say, 'It is a great announcement'
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance and gravity of the message being conveyed, emphasizing that it is a momentous announcement that holds great significance and consequence, underscoring the weight and seriousness of the news or revelation being communicated.

translation: You are turning away from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to turn away from the truth or the message being conveyed, indicating a state of heedlessness or aversion towards guidance or admonition.

translation: I had no knowledge of the highest assembly when they were disputing
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not privy to the knowledge of the heavenly realm or the arguments and debates that took place among the angels or other celestial beings before he received revelation. It underscores the idea that his knowledge of such matters was not acquired through prior awareness or insight but was rather revealed to him by Allah. It emphasizes the prophetic role as one of receiving and conveying divine revelation rather than possessing inherent knowledge of the unseen.

translation: It is revealed to me only that I am a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse signifies the Prophet's role as a clear warner, emphasizing that his function is solely to convey the message of Allah, without any personal authority or divine claim beyond being a messenger, thus underscoring the clarity and transparency of his warning to those who are heedless of the divine message.

translation: When your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being out of clay"
interpretation: This verse signifies the commencement of humanity's creation, highlighting God's omnipotence and deliberate planning in creating humans from clay, a base material, underscoring the notion that human existence is a result of a deliberate and purposeful act of creation rather than a random or accidental event.

translation: So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse highlights the honor and distinction bestowed upon humanity by Allah, as He breathes His spirit into Adam, signifying a special connection between the Creator and human beings. The command for the angels to prostrate before Adam underscores the elevated status of humanity in the cosmic hierarchy, emphasizing the reverence and obedience due to the divine creation.

translation: So the angels prostrated themselves, all of them together.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unity and obedience of the angels, as they collectively prostrated to Adam upon God's command, demonstrating their unwavering submission to divine will and their recognition of the special status God had conferred upon Adam.

translation: Except Iblis (Satan), he was too proud and became one of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the nature of pride and its consequences. Iblis's refusal to prostrate to Adam was not just a simple act of disobedience, but a manifestation of his deep-seated pride and arrogance. By refusing to submit to God's command, Iblis demonstrated that he was more concerned with his own status and ego than with obeying God's will. This verse serves as a warning that pride can lead individuals to reject the truth and ultimately become disbelievers, as it blinds them to the reality of their own limitations and the greatness of God.

translation: He said: 'O Iblis! What prevented you from prostrating to that which I have created with My Hands? Were you proud or were you [already] of those exalted?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of pride and arrogance as the root of disobedience. By questioning whether Iblis was too proud or considered himself among the exalted ones, it underscores that Iblis's refusal to prostrate was not due to a lack of ability or understanding of the command, but rather due to an inflated sense of self-importance. This interpretation suggests that the verse is cautioning against the dangers of arrogance, illustrating how it can lead individuals to defy divine commands and ultimately result in their downfall.

translation: He said: "I am better than he. You created me from fire, and You created him from clay."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and pride of Iblis (Satan) when he refused to prostrate to Adam. Iblis based his superiority on the material from which he was created, considering fire to be nobler than clay. This reflects a flawed understanding of worth, as true worth is not determined by material origin but by one's character and obedience to God's commands. Iblis's response demonstrates how pride and a sense of superiority can lead to disobedience and ultimately to being cursed by God.

translation: He said: 'Then get out of it, for you are accursed'
interpretation: This verse signifies the expulsion of Satan (Iblis) from the heavens or the Garden of Eden due to his disobedience to God's command to prostrate before Adam. The term 'رجيم' (rajim) means 'stoned' or 'cursed', indicating that Satan is not only expelled but also condemned and subject to divine wrath. This event marks the beginning of Satan's enmity towards humanity, as he vows to mislead them. The verse underscores the consequences of disobedience and the nature of Satan's role as a tempter and adversary to humans.

translation: And indeed, My curse is upon you until the Day of Recompense.
interpretation: This verse signifies a severe warning and condemnation, indicating that the person or group it is addressed to is under divine curse until the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the gravity of their actions or beliefs that have incurred such a fate.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected'
interpretation: This verse is a request by Iblis (Satan) to Allah to grant him respite until the Day of Judgment, indicating his intention to continue misleading humans until the end of time, highlighting the ongoing spiritual struggle between good and evil.

translation: He said, 'Then indeed, you are of those reprieved.'
interpretation: This verse signifies a reprieve or a postponement of punishment, indicating that the individual being addressed is granted a temporary reprieve from the consequences of their actions, serving as a test of their resolve and faith.

translation: Until the day of the known time
interpretation: This verse refers to a specific time appointed by Allah, which is known to Him and will come to pass. The phrase 'the known time' signifies a predetermined moment for a particular event or reckoning, emphasizing the inevitability and certainty of Allah's plan. It is often associated with the Day of Judgment or a significant eschatological event, underscoring the theme of accountability and the ultimate fulfillment of divine will.

translation: He said, 'By your might, I will surely mislead them all'
interpretation: This verse is part of the narrative about Iblis (Satan) in the Qur'an. Here, Iblis is swearing by the might or power ('izah) of Allah that he will mislead all of humanity. The interpretation is that Iblis is making a solemn vow, leveraging the greatest attribute of Allah, which is His 'Izzah or might, to assert his determination and confidence in his ability to corrupt mankind. It highlights the obstinacy and arrogance of Iblis, as he dares to challenge Allah's creation by pledging to lead them astray, underscoring the intense enmity between Iblis and humanity as well as the spiritual struggle that humanity faces.

translation: Except Your chosen servants among them
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of sincere devotion and exclusivity in worship. The phrase 'except Your chosen servants among them' suggests that even among those who may be generally misguided or disobedient, there are individuals who have dedicated themselves genuinely to the worship and service of God alone. It underscores the idea that true faith and devotion can exist even within a broader context of disobedience or error, emphasizing the importance of individual sincerity and the special status of those who are truly devoted to God.

translation: He said, 'And the truth, I say the truth'
interpretation: This verse signifies an affirmation and reaffirmation of the truth. The speaker is emphasizing their commitment to speaking the truth, reinforcing their statement with a solemn oath or pledge, underscoring the certainty and authenticity of their claim.

translation: I will surely fill Hell with you and those of them that follow you all together.
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability and completeness of punishment for those who follow the path of disobedience and rebellion against God's commandments, led by Satan. It highlights the consequence of choosing to follow the misleading path laid out by Satan, indicating that both he and his followers will be held accountable and punished in the hereafter, filling the Hellfire completely.

translation: Say, I do not ask you for any reward for it, and I am not one of the pretentious.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sincerity and humility of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in his mission to convey the message of Islam. It emphasizes that he is not seeking any material reward or personal gain from his people for delivering the message, and that his role is not one of pretension or artificiality, but rather a genuine and heartfelt endeavor to guide them to the truth.

translation: It is not except a reminder for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a universal message intended for all of humanity, not limited to a specific group or individual. It underscores the global and inclusive nature of the Qur'an's guidance and wisdom.

translation: And you will surely know its news after a while
interpretation: This verse is indicating that the truth about a particular matter or event will become clear and known at a later time, suggesting that patience and waiting are required to understand its full significance or consequences.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse signifies the origin and authority of the Qur'an, emphasizing that it is a divine revelation from God, who is both Almighty and Wise. The attribute 'Al-'Aziz' (the Exalted in Might) underscores God's power and ability to enforce His will, while 'Al-Hakim' (the Wise) highlights His wisdom in creating and governing the universe, as well as in guiding humanity through the scripture. It establishes the Qur'an as a source of guidance that is backed by divine authority and wisdom.

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book in truth. So worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity in worship. The phrase 'مخلصا له الدين' (sincerely for Him the religion) indicates that one's devotion and obedience should be purely for the sake of Allah, without any intention of showing off or seeking worldly gain. It highlights that the purpose of revealing the scripture is to guide people towards a genuine and unadulterated form of worship, dedicated solely to Allah.

translation: Unquestionably, for Allah is the pure religion. And those who take protectors besides Him [say], 'We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position.' Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide he who is a liar and [confirmed] disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse highlights the issue of associating intermediaries with God, where people worship others besides God, believing that these intermediaries will bring them closer to God. The verse asserts that God will judge between those who disagree on this matter, and emphasizes that God does not guide those who are liars and ungrateful, implying that the act of associating intermediaries is a form of lying against God and ingratitude towards His blessings.

translation: If Allah had willed to have a son, He could have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Glory be to Him; He is Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse is a refutation of the idea that God has a son or offspring. It asserts that if God had wanted to have a child, He would have chosen one from among His creations as He sees fit. The verse emphasizes God's absolute power and sovereignty, highlighting that He is the One who creates and chooses as He pleases. The phrase 'سبحانه' (Glory be to Him) serves to underscore God's transcendence and purity from any such attribution. The verse concludes by affirming God's uniqueness and irresistible power, described as 'الواحد القهار' (The One, The Omnipotent), reinforcing the notion that God is not in need of or diminished by having a child, and that His will is executed without any constraint.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omnipotence and authority over the universe, demonstrated through the creation of the heavens and earth, the alternation of day and night, and the subjugation of celestial bodies like the sun and moon. The phrase 'كل يجري لأجل مسمى' (each running for a named term) underscores the idea that everything operates within a predetermined timeframe set by God, emphasizing a sense of divine control and order. The attributes 'العزيز' (the Almighty) and 'الغفار' (the Forgiving) suggest that despite His immense power, God is also merciful and capable of forgiveness, pointing to a balance between divine justice and mercy.

translation: He created you from one soul, then made from it its mate, and He has provided for you eight heads of cattle in pairs. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in triple darkness. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you diverted?
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and monotheistic nature of God by detailing the intricate process of human creation and the provision of livestock for humanity. It emphasizes that God is the sole creator and owner of all things, and that humans should not be diverted from worshipping Him alone. The 'triple darkness' refers to the layers of the abdominal wall, the uterus, and the amniotic sac, signifying the complexity and mystery of human creation. The verse serves as a reminder to acknowledge God's sovereignty and to refrain from polytheism or diverting one's devotion away from Him.

translation: If you disbelieve, then indeed, Allah is Rich beyond needing you; and He does not approve for His servants disbelief. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you; and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse highlights the complex relationship between human actions and God's response. On one hand, it underscores God's independence from human actions, emphasizing that disbelief does not harm Him. On the other hand, it reveals God's displeasure with disbelief, indicating a moral and relational dimension to His interaction with humanity. The verse suggests that gratitude is a path to divine satisfaction, implying that human acknowledgment and appreciation of God's blessings can lead to a positive divine response. Furthermore, it emphasizes individual accountability, stating that one person cannot bear the burden of another's wrongdoing, reinforcing the concept of personal responsibility. Ultimately, it points to the inevitability of return to God, where individuals will be informed about their deeds, and underscores God's omniscience, particularly His knowledge of the innermost thoughts and intentions of individuals.

translation: And when affliction touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning in repentance to Him. Then when He bestows upon him a blessing from Himself, he forgets that for which he had called upon Him before, and he makes for Allah equals that he may mislead [people] from His way. Say, 'Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the human tendency to forget God's blessings and turn to polytheism when one's prayers are answered. It suggests that humans often return to their old ways, creating equals for God and straying from the right path after being granted a blessing, indicating a lack of true faith and gratitude.

translation: Is one who is devout in the hours of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, [like one who does not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only they will remember [who are] people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who possess knowledge and those who do not, emphasizing that true understanding and remembrance are exclusive to individuals endowed with intellect and wisdom. It contrasts the devoted individual who engages in nocturnal prayers, demonstrating fear of the hereafter and hope for divine mercy, with others who lack such devotion and insight. The rhetorical question posed underscores the inequality between the knowledgeable and the ignorant, suggesting that only those with sound minds and intellectual faculties are capable of deriving moral lessons and benefiting from spiritual practices.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world is good, and the earth of Allah is spacious. Indeed, the steadfast will be given their reward without account.'
interpretation: This verse is encouraging believers to remain steadfast in their faith even when faced with persecution or hardship, suggesting that they should migrate to another land if necessary, as the earth is spacious and God will provide for them. The verse promises that those who are patient and persevering will be rewarded abundantly by God without measure or limit.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "I have been commanded to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity in worship, indicating that true devotion to Allah requires dedicating one's actions and intentions solely to Him, free from any form of polytheism or hypocrisy. It underscores the concept of 'ikhlas' (sincerity), which is a fundamental principle in Islam, highlighting that one's faith and deeds should be genuinely for the sake of Allah alone.

translation: And I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit (to Allah).
interpretation: This verse signifies the importance of leading by example in submitting to the will of Allah. The speaker, who is Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as understood from the context of the Qur'an, is being commanded to be among the first to submit completely to Allah's will, setting a precedent for others to follow. It underscores the virtue of taking the initiative in faith and obedience, demonstrating that true leadership in faith involves being at the forefront of surrendering one's will to Allah's commandments.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the individual's awareness of their accountability to God and their fear of the consequences of disobedience. It signifies the importance of obedience to God's commands to avoid the severe punishment on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing a personal and direct relationship between the individual and their Creator.

translation: Say, 'Allah [alone] do I worship, sincere to Him in my religion'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity in worship and devotion. It instructs the believer to declare that they worship Allah alone, with their religion and faith being purely dedicated to Him, free from any form of polytheism or hypocrisy. The verse underscores the concept of 'ikhlas' (sincerity), which is a central theme in Islamic theology, highlighting that true worship is that which is done with the intention of pleasing Allah alone.

translation: So worship what you will besides Him. Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who will have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection." Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject the message of monotheism and worship other than Allah. It emphasizes that the true losers are those who, on the Day of Judgment, will not only suffer their own loss but also that of their families, implying that their misguidance has led their loved ones astray as well. The verse underscores the catastrophic nature of this loss, describing it as 'the obvious loss,' highlighting the eternal consequences of misguided beliefs and actions in this life.

translation: They will have layers of fire above them and layers below them. That is what God warns His servants with. 'O My servants, then fear Me'.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning to those who disregard God's commands and indulge in sinful behavior, cautioning them that they will be enveloped by the torment of Hell from all directions - above and below them. The purpose of this vivid depiction of punishment is to instill fear in the hearts of God's servants, prompting them to adopt a righteous path and maintain their devotion to Him, thereby avoiding such a dire fate.

translation: And those who avoided the false deities, lest they worship them, and turned to God in repentance, for them is good news. So give good news to My servants
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of rejecting false objects of worship and turning sincerely to God. It suggests that those who avoid worshiping or following false authorities (taghut) and instead turn to God with sincerity are deserving of good news or glad tidings, likely referring to spiritual reward or salvation. The verse then addresses the Prophet, instructing him to convey this glad news to his followers, emphasizing the role of the Prophet as a bringer of good tidings to the righteous.

translation: Those who listen to the speech and follow the best of it. Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the ones endowed with understanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of discernment and critical thinking in accepting guidance. It suggests that those who are guided by Allah are not merely passive recipients of information, but rather, they actively engage with what they hear, evaluating and distinguishing between different viewpoints to follow the best course. The phrase 'أولو الألباب' (those endowed with understanding) indicates that such individuals possess a level of intellectual and spiritual maturity that enables them to make informed decisions and navigate complex situations effectively.

translation: Is he, then, on whom the word of punishment is justly due [to be helped by you]? Can you, then, rescue him who is in the Fire [of Hell]?
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of attempting to save or guide those who have been decreed by Allah to face punishment due to their persistent disbelief and wrongdoing. It underscores the concept of divine justice and the inevitability of Allah's judgment, suggesting that even the Prophet (peace be upon him) cannot rescue or alter the fate of those destined for the Fire. It emphasizes the limits of human or prophetic intervention in the face of divine decree, pointing to the importance of accepting and submitting to Allah's will.

translation: But those who are mindful of their Lord will have lofty chambers, with chambers built above them, beneath which rivers flow. [This is] the promise of Allah. And Allah does not fail in [His] promise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that the reward for the righteous is not just a simple or singular blessing, but rather a multifaceted and layered one. The 'rooms built above rooms' signify a state of spiritual elevation and a paradise that is rich in its rewards, emphasizing the idea that the blessings of the hereafter are far more complex and superior to what one might expect. It underscores God's promise-keeping nature, reassuring believers of the certainty of their reward.

translation: Do you not see that God sends down water from the sky and causes it to penetrate the earth as springs, and then produces thereby crops of varying hues, and then it withers and you see it turning yellow, and then He makes it crumble. Indeed, in that is a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse is an invitation to reflect on the signs of God's power and wisdom in the natural world. The cycle of water, from its descent from the sky to its role in bringing forth vegetation, which then withers and decays, is a metaphor for the cycle of life and death, and serves as a reminder to those endowed with understanding (أولي الألباب) of the transience of worldly things and the power of God to create, sustain, and transform.

translation: Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam, so that he is on a light from his Lord (as the hard-hearted)? So, woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah! They are in a manifest error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those whose hearts have been opened to Islam by God and those whose hearts have been hardened against the remembrance of God. The former are guided by the light from their Lord, implying a state of spiritual enlightenment and understanding. The latter, with hearts hardened, are in a state of clear deviation, indicating a profound spiritual and moral misguidance. The verse suggests that the receptivity to God's guidance is a divine gift, and those who are not receptive are in a state of spiritual peril.

translation: Allah has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book wherein is reiteration. The skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts relax at the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills. And whoever is misguided by Allah - for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound impact of the Quran on those who are mindful of Allah. The 'best statement' refers to the Quran, described as 'mutashabiha mathani', indicating its cohesive and reiterative nature, reinforcing key messages throughout. The initial reaction of fear, followed by a softening of hearts and skins towards Allah's remembrance, signifies a transformative spiritual journey. It underscores the dual effect of the Quran: it first instills fear of Allah in those who are receptive, and then nurtures a deeper, softer connection with the divine. The verse concludes by emphasizing Allah's sovereignty over guidance, indicating that while He guides whom He wills through the Quran, those whom He allows to stray will not find guidance elsewhere.

translation: Is he who falls on his face (on the Day of Judgement) the worse off, or he who comes secure on that Day? And it will be said to the wrong-doers, 'Taste what you used to earn.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the believer who is protected from the torment on the Day of Judgment and the wrongdoer who will be exposed to it. It emphasizes that the wrongdoer's actions will be the source of their suffering, as they will be made to 'taste' the consequences of their deeds. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in wrongdoing, cautioning them that their actions will have severe repercussions in the Hereafter.

translation: Those before them belied, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth, indicating that divine punishment can come unexpectedly and from unforeseen directions, emphasizing the importance of being mindful of one's actions and the consequences of disbelief.

translation: So God made them taste the disgrace in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater. If they knew
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and engage in sinful behavior, indicating that they will face humiliation and punishment not only in the hereafter but also in this life. It suggests that worldly consequences can be a foretaste of the greater punishment that awaits in the afterlife, implying that if people had foresight or understanding, they would avoid actions that lead to such outcomes.

translation: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example that they might remember.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive nature of the Qur'an, suggesting that it contains a wide variety of examples and parables that cater to different aspects of human life and understanding, aiming to prompt reflection and remembrance among people.

translation: An Arabic Qur'an, without any crookedness, so that they may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of the clarity and straightforwardness of the Qur'an's message, emphasizing that it is free from any distortion or deviation, and is presented in a clear and eloquent Arabic language, with the ultimate goal of guiding people to righteousness and piety.

translation: Allah puts forward an example of a man who is owned by partners in dispute, and a man wholly owned by one man. Are the two alike in condition? All praise is due to Allah. But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the stark contrast between a life of discord and one of peace and harmony. The man with 'partners who dispute' symbolizes a life entangled in conflict and division, likely representing polytheism or the association of others with God, where the individual's allegiance and priorities are fragmented and contentious. On the other hand, the 'man wholly owned by one man' represents a life of unity and singular devotion, symbolizing the tranquility and stability that comes from dedicating oneself fully to one Lord, Allah. The rhetorical question, 'Are the two alike in example?' drives home the idea that these two states cannot be equivalent in value or outcome. The verse concludes with 'Praise be to Allah,' underscoring the divine wisdom in such comparisons, and notes that 'most of them do not know,' indicating a lack of understanding among people about the true nature of their choices and the consequences of their beliefs and actions.

translation: Indeed, you are to die and indeed, they are to die.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability and universality of death, emphasizing that both the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his detractors are subject to the same mortal fate, thereby underscoring the futility of their opposition and the transience of earthly life.

translation: Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, will dispute.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate accountability of human beings before God. It signifies that the disputes and disagreements people have in this life will be brought to a final reckoning on the Day of Judgment. On that day, individuals will stand before their Lord, and their differences will be resolved, underscoring the inevitability of divine justice and the futility of earthly disputes in the face of eternal judgment.

translation: And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of denying the truth when it is presented. It suggests that those who reject the truth and attribute falsehood to God are committing a grave injustice. The verse implies that such individuals will face severe consequences, with Hell being their ultimate abode, underscoring the idea that rejecting the truth has profound and dire repercussions in the hereafter.

translation: And the one who has brought the truth and [they who] believed in it - those are the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights that true righteousness is not just about believing in a message, but also about the one who brings that message. It emphasizes the importance of both the messenger and the believers being on the same path of truth, and that together they constitute the righteous or the 'muttaqun', who are mindful of Allah and avoid evil.

translation: They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the righteous individuals will be granted their desires in the hereafter, not because they had wished for those things in this world, but because their desires in the hereafter will be in accordance with what is good and pleasing to Allah, reflecting the perfection of their spiritual state and the completeness of their joy in the hereafter.

translation: That Allah may expiate for them the worst of what they did and give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's justice and mercy. It indicates that Allah will not only forgive the worst of their deeds but also reward them based on their best actions, showcasing the generous nature of divine justice where the reward exceeds the punishment in magnitude and goodness.

translation: Is not God sufficient for His servant? Yet they try to frighten you with those besides Him. And he whom God leaves to stray, there is not for him any guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of fearing others besides God, as God is sufficient to protect and guide His servant. It emphasizes that those who are misled by God, due to their own rejection of guidance, will not find any other guide to lead them to the right path. The verse serves as a reassurance to the Prophet and, by extension, to believers, that they should not be intimidated by the threats of those who worship or fear others alongside or instead of God. It underscores the omnipotence of God and the inefficacy of other entities or beings in providing guidance or protection.

translation: And whomsoever Allah guides, there will be none to lead him astray. Is not Allah All-Mighty, Possessor of Retribution?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the omnipotence of Allah's guidance and the inevitability of His justice. It suggests that once Allah guides an individual, there is no force or entity capable of leading them astray. The verse underscores the dual attributes of Allah: His 'izzah (might or power) and His capacity for 'intiqam (recompense or retribution). It implies that Allah's guidance is not only unerring but also backed by His omnipotence, and that those who reject guidance will face His justice. It serves as a reassurance to the believers of the security and strength provided by Allah's guidance, while cautioning others about the consequences of straying from the path He has laid out.

translation: And if you ask them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they will surely say, 'God.' Say, 'Then have you considered what you invoke besides God? If God intended for me any harm, are they removers of His harm; or if He intended for me mercy, are they withholders of His mercy?' Say, 'Sufficient for me is God; upon Him [alone] rely the reliant.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of associating partners with God and underscores the sufficiency of relying solely on Him. It demonstrates that even those who claim to worship other deities acknowledge God's role as the Creator, yet they still invoke others alongside Him. The verse challenges the efficacy of these associated deities in either alleviating harm or withholding mercy, concluding that true reliance should be placed on God alone, as He is sufficient for the believer's needs.

translation: Say, O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. Soon you will know.
interpretation: This verse is a call to patience and perseverance in the face of adversity, as the Prophet is instructed to tell his people to continue on their path while he continues on his, implying a forthcoming reckoning where the truth will become apparent.

translation: Who will be visited by a punishment that will disgrace him and on whom will settle a lasting punishment.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the consequences for those who reject the truth and engage in wrongdoing. The 'punishment that will disgrace him' refers to a humiliating and shameful retribution that will befall the individual, likely in this life or on the Day of Judgment. The phrase 'and on him will settle a lasting punishment' suggests that in addition to the initial shameful punishment, a more enduring and perpetual form of suffering will afflict the person, underscoring the severity and permanence of the divine retribution for those who persist in their wrongdoing.

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book for the people in truth. So whoever is guided is for his own soul, and whoever goes astray only goes astray to its detriment. And you are not over them a guardian.
interpretation: This verse highlights the personal responsibility that comes with guidance. It emphasizes that the Prophet's role is to deliver the message, and the consequences of accepting or rejecting it rest solely on the individual. The verse underscores the theme of individual accountability, suggesting that guidance or misguidance is ultimately for the benefit or detriment of the individual themselves, not the Prophet or others.

translation: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die [He takes] during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has ordained death and releases the others until an appointed term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
