interpretation: This verse highlights the sovereignty of Allah over life and death, illustrating that He has complete control over the souls of all living beings, whether they are taken at the time of death or during sleep, and that this should prompt people to reflect on the power and wisdom of Allah.

translation: Or have they taken intercessors with God besides Him? Say, 'Even if they have power over nothing and have no understanding?'
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the practice of polytheistic Arabs who took intercessors other than Allah. It questions the validity of their belief by pointing out that these intercessors have no power or understanding, rendering their intercession useless. The verse highlights the futility of seeking help or mediation from entities that are incapable of benefiting or harming anyone, emphasizing the oneness and uniqueness of Allah as the only true source of power and wisdom.

translation: Say, "To Allah belongs all intercession. His is the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all the power to intercede belongs to Allah alone, and that He has complete dominion over the heavens and the earth. The verse is highlighting the futility of seeking intercession from others, as all intercession is ultimately subject to Allah's will and permission. It serves as a warning against shirk (polytheism) and encourages the believers to direct their worship and supplications solely to Allah, as they will ultimately return to Him for judgment.

translation: And when God is mentioned alone, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink with aversion, but when those other than Him are mentioned, they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the reactions of believers and non-believers when God is mentioned versus when other deities or objects of worship are mentioned. The aversion felt by non-believers towards the mention of God alone signifies their disdain for monotheism and their preference for polytheism or associating other entities with God. Their rejoicing at the mention of other deities indicates their comfort and affinity with beliefs that diverge from the oneness of God, underscoring their lack of faith in the Hereafter as a motivating factor for their worldview and behavior.

translation: Say, O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You will judge between Your servants regarding that in which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the role of Allah as the ultimate arbiter and judge among His servants regarding the matters in which they differ. It highlights Allah's omniscience as the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and His authority as the Creator of the heavens and the earth. The verse is an affirmation of the Islamic belief in the sovereignty of Allah and His decisive judgment in all disputes and differences among people.

translation: If those who have wronged had everything that is in the earth, and as much again with it, they would certainly offer it as a ransom to escape the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will become manifest to them from God what they had not been reckoning.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of the punishment on the Day of Judgment for those who have committed wrongdoing. It suggests that if the wrongdoers were given the opportunity to ransom themselves from the torment by offering everything on earth and an equivalent amount in addition, they would eagerly do so. However, it also indicates that the reality of God's reckoning and punishment will be far more severe and unexpected than they had anticipated, revealing to them aspects of God's justice and wrath that they had not considered or prepared for.

translation: And the evil of what they had done will become evident to them, and the very thing they used to mock at will encompass them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept that the consequences of one's actions will inevitably manifest, and those who mocked or belittled the warnings or punishments will be surrounded by the very thing they once ridiculed, signifying a divine justice where the mockers are ensnared by their own disbelief or wrongdoing.

translation: And when affliction touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a blessing from Us, he says, "I have been given it only because of [my] knowledge." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the human tendency to turn to God in times of hardship, but to forget Him when prosperity returns. It suggests that people's faith is often tested by their circumstances, and that many fail to recognize that the blessings they receive are a test from God, rather than a reward for their own knowledge or abilities. The verse implies that true understanding and recognition of God's role in one's life is lacking in most people.

translation: Those before them indeed said it, but their earnings availed them not.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of relying solely on material wealth and worldly accomplishments for salvation. It suggests that true success lies not in what one accumulates, but in righteous deeds and faith, implying that the disbelievers' rejection of truth and their accumulation of wealth will not protect them from the consequences of their actions.

translation: So the evil consequences of what they had earned struck them. And those who have done wrong from among these people, the evil consequences of what they have earned will strike them, and they will not be able to escape.
interpretation: This verse highlights the universal principle of justice that is at the core of the Qur'anic worldview. It suggests that the consequences of one's actions are inescapable, regardless of one's identity or status. The phrase 'سيئات ما كسبوا' (the evil consequences of their deeds) implies that the suffering or hardship that befalls individuals or communities is a direct result of their own actions. The verse is emphasizing that those who have committed wrongdoing will inevitably face the negative repercussions of their actions, and that no one can evade or escape the consequences of their deeds. This interpretation underscores the importance of personal responsibility and accountability in the Qur'anic perspective, emphasizing that justice is not limited to specific groups or individuals but is a universal principle that applies to all.

translation: Do they not know that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts [it]? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the misconception of those who attribute their prosperity or lack thereof to their own abilities or circumstances, rather than recognizing it as a test from Allah. It emphasizes that Allah is the sole controller of provision, and that He grants it to whom He wills, in abundance or scarcity, as a means to test faith. The verse suggests that true believers will recognize these variations in provision as signs from Allah, demonstrating His power and wisdom, and will accordingly adjust their understanding and behavior.

translation: Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah . Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless nature of Allah's mercy and forgiveness, encouraging even those who have committed grave sins to seek repentance, as Allah is capable of forgiving all sins, no matter their magnitude, provided one turns to Him sincerely.

translation: And return to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you; then you will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who are in a state of disobedience and arrogance, urging them to turn back to their Lord in repentance and submit to His will before the punishment comes upon them, at which point it will be too late for them to receive help or salvation. It emphasizes the urgency of returning to God and surrendering to His command before facing an inevitable and unmitigated consequence of their actions.

translation: And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes to you suddenly while you are not aware.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to heed the best of the revelations sent down from Allah, emphasizing the importance of adhering to the most righteous and virtuous guidance provided by the divine message before the onset of unforeseen punishment. It underscores the necessity of being mindful and responsive to divine guidance to avoid sudden and unanticipated chastisement, highlighting the importance of spiritual vigilance and adherence to the truth.

translation: Lest a soul should say, 'Oh [how great is] my regret over what I neglected in regard to God and that I was among those who took things lightly'
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret that individuals will feel on the Day of Judgment for having neglected their religious duties and mocked those who were devout. It underscores the importance of taking one's faith seriously and not belittling the remembrance of God and righteous deeds, as such negligence and mockery will lead to profound remorse in the hereafter.

translation: Or you say, 'If only God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of individuals to attribute their misguided actions or beliefs to the will of God, suggesting that if God had willed otherwise, they would have been among the righteous. It underscores the human inclination to deflect personal responsibility by invoking divine decree, and serves as a critique of such rationalization, pointing to the importance of personal agency and accountability in one's actions and beliefs.

translation: Or you will say when you see the punishment, "If only I had a return [to former life] I would be among the doers of good."
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and remorse that individuals will experience in the afterlife when they witness the punishment for their wrongdoings. It underscores the human tendency to wish for a second chance to rectify past mistakes and behave righteously, illustrating the consequences of not following a virtuous path in life.

translation: Nay! Indeed, My verses had come to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the individual's rejection of the truth was not due to a lack of evidence or proof, but rather a result of their pride and arrogance, as they had received clear signs (آياتي) but chose to deny them, demonstrating a deliberate and willful rejection of the truth.

translation: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against Allah, their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell a home for the arrogant?
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who attribute falsehoods to Allah, indicating that their actions will result in a severe and humiliating punishment on the Day of Judgment, symbolized by their blackened faces. It underscores the notion that arrogance, coupled with lying about Allah, will lead to a terrible abode in Hell, emphasizing the gravity of such actions and the importance of truthfulness and humility in one's faith.

translation: And Allah will save those who have been conscious of Him, by their triumph; no evil will touch them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that those who are mindful of God and live righteously will be saved and attain success. The phrase 'بمفازتهم' (with their triumph) suggests that they will achieve their goals and attain a state of triumph. The verse also reassures that they will not be touched by evil or experience sorrow, indicating a state of complete spiritual and emotional well-being. The interpretation is that the righteous will be delivered from harm and distress, and will experience joy and triumph in the hereafter.

translation: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the Disposer of all affairs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and all-encompassing authority of Allah, emphasizing that He is not only the creator of everything but also the one who manages and oversees all affairs, indicating a profound level of control and providence over the universe.

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. And those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah - it is those who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah, emphasizing that He has complete control over the heavens and the earth. The phrase 'مقاليد السماوات والأرض' (the keys of the heavens and the earth) signifies Allah's absolute authority and dominion over the universe. The second part of the verse serves as a warning to those who reject Allah's signs and messages, indicating that such disbelief leads to loss, not just in the hereafter but potentially in this life as well, due to the rejection of guidance and truth. It underscores the consequence of denying the divine signs and the importance of faith in achieving success and salvation.

translation: Say, 'Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the absurdity of being commanded to worship others besides Allah, emphasizing that such a directive comes from a place of ignorance, as true knowledge and guidance are derived from Allah alone.

translation: And it was already revealed to you and to those before you that if you should associate [anything] with Allah, your work would surely become worthless, and you would surely be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and, by extension, to all believers, emphasizing the gravity of associating partners with Allah (shirk). It underscores the principle that any act of worship or good deed is rendered null and void if performed with the intention of associating others with Allah. The verse highlights the exclusivity of worship due to Allah, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid (the oneness of God) that is central to Islamic faith. It implies that the acceptance of one's deeds by Allah is contingent upon the sincerity and purity of one's belief, free from any form of polytheism or idolatry. The consequence of shirk is not just the invalidation of one's actions but also being among the losers, indicating a profound loss in both this life and the hereafter.

translation: So worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, and be among the thankful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of dedicating one's worship solely to Allah, highlighting the monotheistic nature of Islam. The command to be among the grateful (شاكرين) suggests that true worship is not just about performing rituals, but also about acknowledging and appreciating the blessings and favors one has received from Allah, thus fostering a deep sense of gratitude and humility.

translation: And they have not appraised Allah with true appraisal. And the earth entirely will be [within] His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disparity between the reverence and awe that Allah deserves and the limited perception of Him held by those who associate partners with Him. It signifies that on the Day of Resurrection, Allah's absolute power and control over all creation will be manifest, demonstrating the futility of associating other entities with Him in worship or attributing to them qualities that are exclusively His.

translation: And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall down dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.
interpretation: This verse signifies the end of the world as we know it and the Day of Judgment. The first blowing of the Trumpet (صور) will cause the death of all beings in the heavens and on earth, except those whom Allah wills to be exempt. The second blowing will signal the resurrection, whereupon all will be brought back to life and stand, awaiting judgment. The verse underscores the absolute power of Allah over life and death and the inevitability of the Hereafter.

translation: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord (God); and the Book will be placed (before the people to be examined); and the Prophets and the witnesses will be brought (to testify); and judgment will be passed between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate triumph of divine justice on the Day of Judgment. The 'earth shining with the light of its Lord' symbolizes the illumination of truth and justice, dispelling all darkness and obscurity. The 'book being laid open' refers to the record of deeds, where every individual's actions are documented. The prophets and witnesses being brought forth underscores the accountability of all before God, with the prophets serving as witnesses to their communities and the martyrs (or witnesses) testifying to their own righteous conduct. The judgment being carried out 'with truth' and without injustice highlights God's perfect justice, where every soul is held accountable for its deeds without being wronged or deprived of its rights.

translation: And every soul will be fully recompensed for what it did and He is most knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, every individual will be recompensed according to their deeds, and it emphasizes God's omniscience regarding the actions of all beings, suggesting that His judgment is based on complete knowledge and justice.

translation: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, 'Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?' They will say, 'Yes, [messengers did come].' But the word of punishment has been justified against the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability of those who rejected faith. Upon arriving at Hell, they are confronted by its guardians, who remind them that messengers had come to warn them about the consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment. The disbelievers acknowledge the messengers' warnings but are still punished because their rejection of faith had predetermined their fate according to God's decree. It underscores the idea that the disbelievers' punishment is not a result of the messengers' failure to warn them, but rather their own rejection of the message, which fulfilled the condition for the punishment as decreed by God.

translation: It will be said, 'Enter the gates of Hell to abide therein eternally.' And wretched is the abode of the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who embody arrogance and pride, indicating that their ultimate destination will be Hell, where they will reside eternally. It underscores the notion that arrogance is not merely a personal trait but a spiritual affliction that leads to severe consequences in the afterlife. The verse emphasizes the idea that the arrogant individual's refusal to humble themselves before the truth and their tendency to look down upon others will be met with divine justice, resulting in their eternal dwelling in a place of suffering and torment. It highlights the moral and spiritual lesson that humility is a virtue highly valued in the eyes of God, while arrogance is vehemently disapproved.

translation: And those who feared their Lord will be led to the Garden in groups until, when they arrive there, and its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them, 'Peace be upon you; you have become pure; so enter it to dwell.'
interpretation: This verse signifies that the righteous individuals will be escorted to Paradise in groups, and upon their arrival, the gates of Paradise will be opened for them. The guardians of Paradise will greet them with peace and welcome them, indicating that they have been purified and are now entitled to enter and reside in Paradise eternally. The verse highlights the honor and reverence with which the righteous will be received in the afterlife, underscoring the idea that their piety and good deeds have earned them a noble and eternal reward.

translation: And they say, "Praise to Allah, who has fulfilled for us His promise and made us inherit the earth [so] we may settle in Paradise wherever we will. And excellent is the reward of [righteous] workers."
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate reward for the righteous who have endured trials and remained steadfast in their faith. Upon entering Paradise, they express gratitude to Allah for fulfilling His promise of a heavenly abode, where they are free to dwell as they please, highlighting the excellence of the recompense for those who toiled in obedience to God's commands.

translation: And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, exalting [Allah] with praise of their Lord. And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said, "Praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate triumph of justice and truth on the Day of Judgment. The angels surrounding the Throne of Allah, glorifying Him, symbolize the acknowledgment of His supreme authority and justice. The decision made among people according to the truth underscores the accountability of individuals for their deeds. The declaration that all praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the universe, highlights His sovereignty and the futility of associating partners with Him, emphasizing the monotheistic belief that underpins the Islamic faith.

translation: Ha-Mim
interpretation: This verse is one of the Muqatta'at, letters or combinations of letters that appear at the beginning of certain surahs in the Qur'an. The interpretation of these letters is subject to various understandings among scholars. One interpretation is that these letters serve as a challenge to the Arabs, who were masters of language and poetry, to produce something similar to the Qur'an, thus affirming its divine origin and the prophethood of Muhammad. The letters are seen as a form of divine authentication, signifying that the Qur'an is a book of divine revelation, not human composition.

translation: The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse signifies the authority and knowledge of God, emphasizing that the revelation of the Book (Qur'an) is from a source that is both almighty and all-knowing, thus establishing its divine origin and the credibility of its message.

translation: The Forgiver of sin, the Accepter of repentance, severe in punishment, the Owner of bounty. There is no god but He; to Him is the final return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of Allah's justice and mercy. On one hand, Allah is described as 'Ghafir al-Dhanb' (The Forgiver of sin) and 'Qabil al-Tawb' (The Accepter of repentance), indicating His willingness to pardon those who turn to Him in repentance. On the other hand, He is also 'Shadid al-'Iqab' (Severe in punishment), underscoring the severity of His justice for those who persist in wrongdoing. The attribute 'Dhu al-Tawl' (The Owner of bounty) suggests that His mercy and justice are both manifestations of His sovereignty and generosity. The verse concludes by reaffirming the monotheistic belief that 'La ilaha illa Huwa' (There is no god but He), and that 'Ilayhi al-Maseer' (To Him is the final return), emphasizing that all accountability and judgment rest with Allah alone. This interpretation underscores the importance of balancing the hope for divine mercy with the fear of divine justice, encouraging believers to lead a righteous life.

translation: No one argues about the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so be not deceived by their roaming in the land.
interpretation: This verse is warning against being swayed by the apparent success and freedom of those who reject the truth. It suggests that their ability to move about and prosper in the world should not be taken as a sign of divine approval or as evidence that the message of the prophets is false. Rather, it is a test of patience and faith for believers, who should not be distracted by the superficial prosperity of the disbelievers from their own commitment to the truth.

translation: Before them the people of Noah and the parties after them denied [the prophets], and every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him, and they disputed with falsehood to refute thereby the truth. So I seized them, and how [terrible] was My punishment.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the historical pattern of nations rejecting their prophets and attempting to suppress the truth. The phrase 'كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح والأحزاب من بعدهم' (Before them, the people of Noah and the parties after them denied) sets the stage by referencing previous instances of rejection. The actions described, such as plotting to seize the prophets ('وهمت كل أمة برسولهم ليأخذوه') and arguing with falsehood to undermine the truth ('وجادلوا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق'), demonstrate the consistent resistance to divine guidance across different communities. The consequence of these actions is severe, as indicated by 'فأخذتهم' (so I seized them), suggesting a divine retribution. The verse concludes with 'فكيف كان عقاب' (and how was My punishment?), which serves as a rhetorical question to emphasize the severity and impact of divine punishment on those who reject the truth and persecute their prophets. This interpretation underscores the Qur'an's warning to its readers about the consequences of disbelief and the importance of heeding the message of the prophets.

translation: And thus the word of your Lord has come into effect upon those who disbelieved, that they are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the decree of Allah has been justified upon those who have rejected faith, that they will be the inhabitants of Hellfire, implying an inevitable consequence of their disbelief and a manifestation of Allah's justice in response to their actions.

translation: Those who carry the Throne and those around it exalt [Allah] with praise of their Lord and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who have believed, [saying], 'Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire
interpretation: This verse highlights the intercession of the angels on behalf of believers, showcasing their role in seeking forgiveness for those who have turned to God in repentance and followed His path. It underscores the mercy and knowledge of God that encompasses all things, emphasizing the importance of repentance and righteous living to avoid the punishment of Hellfire.

translation: Our Lord! And admit them to gardens of perpetual abode which You have promised them, and to the righteous among their fathers, and their wives, and their offspring! Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and justice of Allah, where He not only promises to admit the believers to the Gardens of Eden, but also includes their righteous family members, emphasizing the importance of familial ties and righteousness in the hereafter. It signifies that the reward in the hereafter is not limited to the individual believer, but extends to their family, provided they are righteous, thus underscoring the value of family unity and righteousness in Islam.

translation: And guard them from the evil deeds; and he whom You guard from evil deeds on that Day, You will have surely given him mercy, and that is the grand achievement.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine protection from evil deeds. It suggests that being shielded from committing wrongdoings is a manifestation of Allah's mercy. The achievement mentioned is not just about avoiding punishment but is a grand success because it signifies being under Allah's mercy, which is the ultimate goal for believers.

translation: Those who disbelieve are called out, 'God's hatred towards you is greater than your hatred towards yourselves, when you were being invited to faith but you disbelieved.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony that those who reject faith are more intensely detesting themselves than they detest others, as their rejection of faith leads to their own spiritual downfall. The verse suggests that when they are invited to faith, their refusal not only distances them from divine mercy but also fosters a deep-seated self-aversion, stemming from their own actions against their true interests. It underscores the self-destructive nature of disbelief.

translation: They will say, "Our Lord, You have made us lifeless twice and given us life twice, and we have confessed our sins. So is there to an exit any way?"
interpretation: This verse is referring to the people of Hell who will acknowledge their wrongdoing and the justice of their punishment. They will say that they have experienced two deaths and two lives. The two deaths refer to their original non-existence and then their spiritual death in this life due to their disbelief and sins. The two lives refer to their worldly life and the life they had before their creation in the realm of spirits (alast). They will admit to their sins and ask if there is any way to escape their punishment, indicating their desperation and hopelessness.

translation: That is because when God is invoked alone, you disbelieve; but if others are associated with Him, you believe. So the judgment is for God, the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This is because when God alone is invoked, you disbelieve, but when others are associated with Him, you believe. The judgment is thus for God, the Most High, the Most Great, indicating that the criterion of truth is not in the multitude or diversity of beliefs, but in the singular truth of God's oneness, and that He is the ultimate authority who will judge between the truth and falsehood.

translation: It is He who shows you His signs and sends down for you provision from the sky. And none will remember except those who turn [in repentance].
interpretation: This verse highlights God's role in guiding individuals towards faith and providing for their material needs. The ability to reflect and be reminded of God's signs is reserved for those who turn to Him in repentance and obedience, suggesting that a receptive and submissive heart is necessary for true understanding and appreciation of divine guidance.

translation: So invoke Allah, making your religion pure for Him (alone) even though the disbelievers dislike (it).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity in worship and devotion. It encourages believers to call upon Allah with pure intentions, dedicating their faith and actions solely to Him, regardless of the disapproval or opposition they may face from those who reject faith. It underscores the principle that the acceptance of one's supplication is dependent on the sincerity of one's faith and the purity of one's intentions, and that external opposition or disdain from unbelievers should not deter one from maintaining a genuine and exclusive devotion to Allah.

translation: The Exalter of Ranks, Owner of the Throne; He places the inspiration (al-Rūḥ) from His command upon whom He wills of His servants, that they may warn of the Day of Meeting.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's sovereignty and authority, as He is the one who elevates certain individuals to high ranks and possesses the throne of dominion. The 'inspiration' (al-Rūḥ) refers to the revelation or guidance that God sends to His chosen messengers, empowering them to warn people of the Day of Judgment, when all individuals will meet their Lord and be held accountable for their deeds. The verse underscores the idea that God's messengers are not self-appointed, but rather, they are selected by God to fulfill this critical role, and that their warnings are a manifestation of God's mercy and justice.

translation: The Day when they will emerge [from the graves] - nothing concerning them is hidden from Allah. To whom belongs the dominion this Day? To Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability and the absolute power of Allah on the Day of Judgment. It highlights that on that day, all individuals will be resurrected and brought before Allah, with nothing about them being hidden. The rhetorical question 'To whom belongs the dominion this Day?' emphasizes the sole and uncontested authority of Allah, underscoring His uniqueness and supremacy over all creation. It serves as a reminder of the accountability of humans for their deeds and the futility of attempting to hide or deny one's actions on that day.

translation: This day every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. No injustice today! Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, every individual will be held accountable for their actions, and they will be recompensed accordingly. The phrase 'لا ظلم اليوم' (no injustice today) underscores the absolute justice that will be meted out, implying that no one will be wronged or unfairly treated. The statement 'إن الله سريع الحساب' (indeed Allah is swift in reckoning) highlights the efficiency and swiftness of God's judgment, suggesting that the reckoning will be done with utmost speed and precision, leaving no room for delay or error.

translation: And warn them, [O Muhammad], of the Approaching Day, when hearts will be at the throats, [filled with distress]. For the wrongdoers there will be no devoted friend and no intercessor [who is] obeyed.
interpretation: This verse is warning people of the Day of Judgment, a day when hearts will be filled with anxiety and fear, 'lurking in the throats'. On this day, wrongdoers will be isolated and alone; they will have no close friend or intercessor to help them, and even if they did, their intercession would not be heeded. The verse highlights the gravity of the situation on the Day of Judgment and serves as a warning to those who are unjust, emphasizing their isolation and helplessness.

translation: He knows the stealthy glance and that which the breasts conceal.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's all-encompassing knowledge, suggesting that He is aware not only of outward actions but also of the subtlest inner thoughts and intentions, including those that are hidden or deceitful.

translation: And Allah judges with the truth, while those they invoke besides Him do not judge with anything. Indeed, Allah - He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the omnipotent and just judgment of Allah and the utter inability of other deities or objects of worship to render any judgment whatsoever. It underscores the Islamic belief in the oneness of God (Tawhid) by affirming that Allah alone possesses the attributes of omniscience and justice, symbolized by being 'the Hearing' and 'the Seeing'. This emphasizes the futility of seeking judgment or intercession from other entities, as they lack the capacity to do so, thereby reinforcing the central Islamic tenet that Allah is the sole authority and arbiter in all matters.

translation: Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those who were before them? They were stronger than them in power and [left] more traces in the earth, but Allah seized them for their sins, and they had not from Allah [any] protector.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth and are arrogant. It reminds them that previous nations, who were more powerful and left more lasting legacies, were destroyed by Allah due to their sins. The verse implies that the current disbelievers, despite being weaker in comparison, are equally or even more deserving of punishment if they persist in their wrongdoing. It emphasizes Allah's justice and the inevitability of His punishment for those who commit sins and reject faith.

translation: That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear evidences, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Powerful and severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting the clear signs and messages brought by the prophets. It signifies that those who deny the truth, despite being presented with clear evidence, will face severe punishment from Allah, who is not only powerful but also stern in His retribution. The verse serves as a warning about the outcome of disbelief and obstinacy in the face of divine guidance.

translation: And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority
interpretation: This verse highlights the clear and undeniable evidence that was given to Moses to prove his prophethood and the truth of his message. The phrase 'ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين' (And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority) emphasizes the strength and clarity of the proof that was provided to Moses, indicating that his mission was not based on vague or ambiguous claims, but rather on manifest and convincing signs that left no room for doubt.

translation: To Pharaoh and Haman and Korah, but they said, "[He is] a magician and a liar"
interpretation: This verse highlights the reaction of the disbelievers, represented by Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah, towards the Prophet Moses. They labeled him a magician and a liar, demonstrating their refusal to accept the truth and their tendency to malign the prophets. This reaction is a classic example of how the disbelievers throughout history have responded to the messengers of God, using derogatory labels to discredit them rather than engaging with the substance of their message.

translation: When he came to them with the truth from Us, they said, 'Kill the sons of those who believe with him and let their women live.' But the plotting of the disbelievers is not except in error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extreme measures taken by those who reject the truth when faced with it. The plot to kill the sons of believers and spare their daughters signifies a deep-seated malice and a desperate attempt to undermine the faith. It illustrates that the schemes devised by those who disbelieve are ultimately futile and misguided, leading them further astray.

translation: And Pharaoh said, "Let me kill Moses and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption in the land."
interpretation: This verse highlights the tyrannical and oppressive nature of Pharaoh, who, upon perceiving a threat to his rule from Moses, seeks to eliminate him. It illustrates the fear of those in power when faced with the prospect of change or challenge to their authority, and how they may resort to extreme measures to maintain their status quo. The mention of Moses calling upon his Lord signifies the contrast between the reliance on divine support by the righteous and the reliance on brute force by the oppressors. Pharaoh's concern that Moses might change their religion or cause corruption in the land reflects his own insecurity and the illegitimacy of his rule, as he equates the call to monotheism and righteousness with corruption.

translation: And Moses said, 'I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account.'
interpretation: Moses is highlighting the stark contrast between his own humility and the arrogance of Pharaoh, emphasizing that his trust lies in God, the Lord of all, and that he seeks protection from those who are proud and do not believe in the accountability of their actions on the Day of Judgment, indicating a deep faith in the afterlife and the consequences of one's deeds.

translation: And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh who concealed his faith said, 'Do you kill a man [merely] because he says, "My Lord is Allah" and he has brought you clear evidence from your Lord? And if he should be lying, then upon him is [the consequence of] his lie; but if he should be truthful, there will strike you some of that which he promises you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tension between faith and outward actions, as the believer from Pharaoh's family is concealing his faith due to the societal pressures and dangers associated with openly professing belief in Allah. The verse underscores the principle that one should not be judged solely on their claims but rather on the evidence they bring forth, and that the consequences of false claims rest on the claimant. It also warns against the dangers of ignoring truthful warnings from others, suggesting that heeding such warnings is crucial for avoiding divine retribution. The characterization of Allah as one who does not guide the transgressor and liar serves to emphasize the moral and spiritual consequences of such behavior, implying that those who embody these traits are inherently at odds with divine guidance.

translation: O my people, yours is the dominion this day, [your being] apparent in the land. But who will protect us from the punishment of Allah if it came to us?' Pharaoh said, 'I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the path of rectitude.'
interpretation: In this verse, Pharaoh is shown to be in a state of denial and delusion, where despite being aware of the impending doom, he continues to assert his dominance and tries to mislead his people by presenting his own flawed understanding as the correct path, thereby exemplifying the tactics of a tyrannical leader who uses persuasion and misinformation to maintain control over his followers.

translation: And he who believed said, "O my people, indeed I fear for you [a fate] like the day of the companies
interpretation: The believer is warning his people that they are in danger of suffering a fate similar to that of previous communities who were destroyed when they rejected the messengers sent to them, and that they should take heed from the lessons of history to avoid a similar punishment.

translation: The example of the deeds of the people of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud, and those after them. And Allah does not will injustice to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the messengers and disobey God's commands, drawing a parallel between the fate of past nations who suffered due to their disobedience and the potential fate of those in the present. It underscores God's justice, asserting that He does not will injustice towards His servants, implying that the destruction of these nations was a consequence of their own actions, not an arbitrary act of God.

translation: And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling
interpretation: The verse is warning the people that the Prophet is fearful for them on the Day of Mutual Calling, which signifies a day when people will be calling out to one another in distress and panic, highlighting the gravity of the situation on the Day of Judgment and the importance of heeding the Prophet's warning and guidance to avoid such a dire fate.

translation: The Day you will turn about fleeing; you will not have for yourselves against Allah any protector. And whoever Allah sends astray - there is not for him any guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of God's judgment and the futility of attempting to escape it. On the Day of Judgment, individuals will turn their backs in flight, but they will find no protection or refuge from God's reckoning. The verse also underscores the theme of divine guidance and misguidance, suggesting that those whom God allows to go astray will not find a guide to lead them aright, emphasizing the sovereignty of God over human affairs.

translation: And Joseph had already come to you before with clear signs, but you remained in doubt about what he brought to you, until when he died, you said, 'God will never send a messenger after him.' Thus God leaves to stray he who is a transgressor and sceptic.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the tendency of humans to be ungrateful and dismissive of divine guidance. The example of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) is used to illustrate how people tend to doubt and question the messengers sent by God, and once they pass away, they assume that God will not send another messenger. This verse suggests that such an attitude is a manifestation of a deeper issue - a lack of faith and an inclination towards transgression and doubt, which ultimately leads to being misled by God.

translation: Those who dispute about the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them - great is hatred (in the sight) of Allah and of those who believe. Thus does Allah seal up the heart of every arrogant, tyrannical person.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences of disputing or arguing against the signs and revelations of Allah without having a valid authority or evidence to support one's claims. It warns that such behavior is detestable to both Allah and the believers, and results in Allah sealing the heart of the individual, rendering them incapable of accepting the truth due to their arrogance and tyrannical nature.

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the ways,
interpretation: This verse highlights Pharaoh's arrogance and his attempt to defy the natural order by seeking to ascend to the heavens, demonstrating his refusal to accept the message of Moses and his desire to prove his own divinity.

translation: And the supports (or stairs or paths) of the heavens; then I shall mount up to the God of Moses, and verily, I think him a liar. And thus was made fair-seeming to Pharaoh the evil of his deed, and he was turned away from the path. And the plot of Pharaoh ended in naught but ruin.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and pride of Pharaoh, who not only claimed divinity but also sought to challenge the fundamental beliefs of the people by ascending to the heavens to verify the existence of Moses' God. The verse suggests that Pharaoh's actions were a manifestation of his ego and his attempt to justify his own false beliefs. The phrase 'and thus was made fair-seeming to Pharaoh the evil of his deed' indicates that Pharaoh's own perception of his actions was distorted, making him believe that his evil deeds were justified. This distortion ultimately led him astray from the right path, resulting in his downfall, as indicated by 'the plot of Pharaoh ended in naught but ruin'. The verse serves as a warning against the dangers of unchecked ego and the consequences of deviating from the truth.

translation: And he who believed said, "O my people, follow me, I will guide you to the path of rectitude."
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of a believer as a guide and leader among their community, emphasizing the responsibility to lead others to the right path through their own example and guidance, as exemplified by the believer's call to his people.

translation: O people, this worldly life is only a temporary enjoyment, and the Hereafter is the abode of permanence.
interpretation: This verse is a reminder to the believers that the life of this world is transient and ephemeral, and that the true and lasting abode is the Hereafter. It is a call to prioritize the eternal life over the fleeting pleasures of the world, and to make decisions and choices that are guided by the promise of the Hereafter, rather than being swayed by the temporary allurements of this world.

translation: Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with the like thereof; but whoever does a righteous deed, whether male or female, and is a believer - those will enter Paradise, being given provision therein without reckoning.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of justice in Islam, where individuals are held accountable for their actions. It emphasizes that those who do good deeds and have faith will be rewarded abundantly in Paradise, beyond their expectations or calculations, underscoring the generosity and mercy of God.

translation: And O my people, what is [the matter] with me that I call you to salvation and you call me to the Fire?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the paths chosen by the Prophet and his people. The Prophet is calling his people to salvation, indicating a path of righteousness and virtue, while they, in a state of misguidance, are urging him towards the fire, symbolizing a path of sin and destruction. It underscores the theme of the righteous being led astray by the misguided and the struggle between truth and falsehood.

translation: You invite me to disbelieve in Allah and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, and I invite you to the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the call to polytheism and the call to the monotheistic worship of Allah, emphasizing the rational basis of faith in the one God who is both Almighty and Merciful, and thus, worthy of worship and forgiveness.

translation: Indeed, what you call me to has no claim in this world or in the Hereafter, and our return is to Allah, and the transgressors will be the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who are being misled by false deities or ideologies. It asserts that the objects or beliefs they are being called to worship or follow have no legitimate claim or authority, neither in this life nor in the hereafter. The verse emphasizes that ultimately, all will return to God, implying a reckoning for one's deeds. It specifically identifies those who transgress the limits set by God (the 'musrifun') as being destined for the Fire, underscoring the grave consequences of persisting in such misguidance.

translation: And you will remember what I am telling you. And I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.
interpretation: The verse indicates that those who are being warned will eventually recall the warning given to them, and the speaker, having done his duty, leaves his cause to Allah, who is all-aware of the actions and intentions of His servants, implying a sense of trust and reliance on divine justice and providence.

translation: And God saved him from the evils of what they plotted, and the evil punishment encompassed the people of Pharaoh.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's protection of the believers from the evil consequences of the plots devised against them by their enemies. It also serves as a warning to those who persecute and oppress the righteous, as the punishment that befell Pharaoh's people will similarly befall those who follow in their footsteps.

translation: The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening. And the Day the Hour appears [it will be said], 'Cause Pharaoh's people to enter the severest punishment.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuous suffering of Pharaoh's people, both in the grave and on the Day of Judgment. The exposure to the Fire 'morning and evening' is a torment that they endure even before the final reckoning, serving as a prelude to their ultimate punishment. The verse underscores the severity of their fate, emphasizing that their punishment will be intensified upon the arrival of the Hour, indicating a worsening of their condition from a state of suffering to an even more severe one.

translation: And when they dispute with one another in the Fire, the weak say to those who were arrogant, 'Indeed, we were followers to you, so can you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of accountability and the consequences of one's actions in the afterlife. The weak and the oppressed will hold the leaders and the oppressors accountable for their role in leading them astray and contributing to their downfall. It emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, those who were led astray will seek relief from their leaders, but the leaders will be unable to provide any solace or salvation, underscoring the personal responsibility of each individual for their deeds.

translation: Those who were arrogant will say, "Indeed, all [of us] are in it. Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants."
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of God's judgment and the accountability of human actions. The arrogant ones, who previously denied the truth and oppressed others, will be forced to acknowledge their fate and the justice of God's verdict, realizing that their pride and defiance were futile in the face of divine judgment.

translation: And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, 'Pray to your Lord to lighten for us one day of the punishment.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the desperation and realization of those in Hellfire as they beg the guardians of Hell to intercede on their behalf to ease their suffering, even if only for a day. It underscores the unbearable nature of their punishment and their acknowledgment of their dire situation, illustrating the severe consequences of rejecting faith and righteous deeds in the worldly life.

translation: They will say, 'Did not our messengers come to you with the clear signs?' They will say, 'Yes.' They will say, 'Then supplicate.' But the supplication of the disbelievers is not except in error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of the disbelievers' supplications when faced with the reality of their wrongdoing. It suggests that their prayers or calls for help or salvation are misguided and ineffective because they are rooted in disbelief and a refusal to acknowledge the truth that has been clearly presented to them through the messengers. The verse underscores the theme that those who reject the signs and messages brought by the prophets are ultimately lost and their attempts to seek redress or salvation are in vain.

translation: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in this world's life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah's support and victory are not limited to the hereafter, but are also present in this worldly life for both the messengers and the believers. The phrase 'يوم يقوم الأشهاد' (the Day when the witnesses stand up) refers to the Day of Judgment, indicating that the believers will be vindicated and their truth will be manifest not just in this life but also on the Day of Reckoning, underscoring the certainty of divine justice and the triumph of faith.

translation: The Day when their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode.
interpretation: This verse signifies that on the Day of Judgment, those who have committed wrongdoing will not benefit from attempting to justify or excuse their actions. Instead, they will be met with divine curse and will be destined for a terrible abode, signifying the severe consequences of their wrongdoing in the hereafter.

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the guidance, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the guidance given to Moses was not limited to his lifetime, but was passed down to the Children of Israel through the scripture that was bestowed upon them, emphasizing the continuity and legacy of divine guidance.

translation: Guidance and a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Qur'an serves as a source of guidance and reminder for those endowed with intellect and understanding, implying that its true benefits are realized by individuals who possess the capacity for rational thought and reflection.

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad]. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And ask forgiveness for your sin and exalt [ Allah ] with praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of adversity, reassuring the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that God's promise is true and will be fulfilled. It also instructs him to seek forgiveness for his sins and to glorify God with praise, both in the evening and in the morning, highlighting the significance of maintaining a consistent and sincere connection with God through worship and remembrance.

translation: Those who dispute about the signs of God without authority having come to them - there is nothing in their breasts but (the quest for) greatness, which they will never attain. So seek refuge in God. Verily, it is He who is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who argue about the signs of God without having any valid authority or evidence. It suggests that their argumentation is driven by pride and arrogance, and that they will not succeed in their endeavors. The verse advises the believer to seek refuge in God, who is all-hearing and all-seeing, implying that true understanding and justice come from Him, and that one should turn to Him for protection against the arrogant and the unjust.

translation: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disparity between the grandeur of the universe, represented by the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the relatively lesser significance of human creation. It underscores a profound truth that many people fail to grasp or appreciate, emphasizing a lack of awareness or understanding among the majority of humanity regarding the magnitude and complexity of the universe in comparison to human existence.

translation: And not are equal the blind and the seeing, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the wrongdoer. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent inequality between those who are spiritually blind and those who possess spiritual insight. It draws a parallel between physical sight and spiritual awareness, suggesting that just as the blind and the sighted are not equal, those who have faith and perform good deeds are not equal to those who do wrong. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of reflecting on one's actions and turning towards righteousness, yet it notes that people rarely take heed of such reminders.

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming - no doubt about it - but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to people that the Day of Judgment is inevitable and will occur without a doubt. The phrase 'but most people do not believe' suggests that despite the certainty of this event, many individuals remain unprepared and lack faith, highlighting a disconnect between the conviction in the heart and the reality of the impending judgment.

translation: And your Lord says, 'Invoke Me; I will respond to you.' Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of humility and sincerity in worship. It suggests that those who pride themselves on their status or power and refuse to submit to God's will by invoking Him will be humbled in the afterlife, entering Hell in a state of utter disgrace and subjugation.

translation: It is God Who made for you the night that you may rest therein, and the day giving sight. Verily, God is full of Bounty to mankind, but most men are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's benevolence towards humanity by creating a natural rhythm of rest and activity through the alternation of night and day. The night is for rest and tranquility, while the day is illuminated, allowing people to go about their daily lives. Despite this clear display of divine favor, most people fail to acknowledge and appreciate God's blessings, demonstrating a widespread lack of gratitude.

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, Creator of all things; there is no god except Him; so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the oneness and uniqueness of Allah as the sole creator of everything, and questioning how people can be diverted from worshiping Him alone despite the overwhelming evidence of His existence and creative power. It suggests that the deviation from the truth is a result of a deep-seated issue, perhaps a willful ignorance or a strong inclination towards falsehood, rather than a lack of evidence or proof.

translation: Thus were turned away those who used to deny the signs of Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of those who reject the signs of God to be misled or distracted from the truth, indicating a pattern of behavior where denial of divine evidence leads to being turned away from the right path.

translation: God is the One Who made the earth a resting place for you, and the sky a canopy, and formed you, and perfected your forms, and provided you with good things. That is God, your Lord; so blessed is God, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omnipotence and benevolence towards humanity. It signifies that God is the creator who has made the earth stable for human habitation, constructed the heavens, and crafted humans in the most excellent form. Furthermore, God provides sustenance from good and pure things. The verse concludes by affirming that God is the Lord of all, and thus, He is exalted and blessed. The interpretation of this verse underscores the monotheistic belief in Islam, emphasizing God's role as the sole creator and sustainer of the universe, and it invites believers to acknowledge and glorify God's blessings and attributes.

translation: He is the Living, there is no deity except Him; so invoke Him making your worship sincere to Him (alone). All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity in worship, directing believers to call upon Allah alone, as He is the only true deity worthy of worship, and to dedicate their worship to Him with pure intentions, free from any form of polytheism or hypocrisy.

translation: Say, 'I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah once the clear signs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) affirmation of his monotheistic faith and his rejection of polytheism. The 'clear signs' from his Lord refer to the revelations and miracles that confirmed the truth of his message, compelling him to worship none but Allah, the Lord of all creation. It highlights the central theme of Islam: submission to the will of one God, underscoring the Prophet's role as a recipient and conveyor of divine guidance.

translation: He it is Who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then He brings you forth as a child, then [He develops you] that you may reach your age of full strength, and then that you may become old - though some of you may die before - and that you may reach a term appointed, and that you may understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stages of human development from creation to death, emphasizing God's omnipotence and the transience of human life. It invites reflection on the purpose of life and the inevitability of mortality, encouraging humans to use their intellect to understand the wisdom behind their creation and the stages they go through.

translation: It is He who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's absolute power and authority over existence. The phrase 'He gives life and causes death' underscores His control over the fundamental aspects of life. The subsequent statement about decreeing a matter and it coming into being simply by His command 'Be' emphasizes the effortless and instantaneous nature of His creative power, suggesting that His will is not hindered by any constraints or limitations.

translation: Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah, how they are turned away (from the truth)?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the stubbornness and obstinacy of those who argue against the signs of Allah, indicating that despite being presented with clear evidence, they deliberately turn away from the truth, suggesting a deep-seated resistance to accepting the guidance offered by divine revelation.

translation: Those who deny the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers - soon they will know
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who have rejected the message of the Qur'an and the prophets who came before it. It implies that their denial is not just a simple mistake, but a deliberate rejection of the truth. The verse suggests that those who have rejected the message will eventually face the consequences of their actions and come to understand the gravity of their denial, likely on the Day of Judgment.

translation: When the shackles are around their necks and the chains, they are dragged
interpretation: This verse is describing the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, where they will be dragged into Hell with chains and shackles around their necks, signifying their utter humiliation and inability to escape their punishment, serving as a stark warning to those who reject faith and persist in their disobedience.

translation: Then in the boiling water they will be ignited
interpretation: This verse is referring to the punishment that awaits those who have disbelieved and committed wrongdoings. The phrase 'في الحميم' indicates that they will be immersed in extremely hot water, and 'ثم في النار يسجرون' suggests that afterwards, they will be thrown into the fire, which will be intensely fueled, signifying a severe and unrelenting punishment.

translation: Then it will be said to them, "Where are those you used to associate [with Him in worship]?
interpretation: This verse signifies the Day of Judgment when the polytheists will be questioned about the false deities they used to worship, highlighting their accountability for their actions and the futility of their beliefs.

translation: Other than Allah. They will say, ‘They have abandoned us. Rather, we did not used to invoke anything before.’ Thus Allah leads the disbelievers astray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the theme of misguided intercession on the Day of Judgment. The disbelievers will realize that their supposed intercessors, whom they invoked alongside Allah in the worldly life, have abandoned them. The verse underscores the fact that these intercessors were not genuinely invoked or worshipped by the disbelievers in the first place, indicating a lack of genuine faith or conviction in their supposed deities. The verse ultimately serves as a warning, illustrating how Allah lets the disbelievers go astray, depriving them of guidance and leaving them to face the consequences of their own misguided actions.

translation: This is because of what you exulted in the earth without right and because of what you were arrogant.
interpretation: This verse is a reprimand from Allah to those who were rejoicing and being arrogant on earth without any justification or right, indicating that their past actions and behavior were among the reasons for their current punishment or regret. It highlights the consequence of being excessively joyful and proud without being grounded in righteousness or truth, suggesting that such behavior is not pleasing to Allah and may lead to adverse outcomes.

translation: Enter the gates of Hell, to dwell therein. And wretched is the abode of the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who exhibit arrogance and pride will face eternal damnation in Hell, highlighting the severe consequences of such an attitude, which is considered a major moral failing in Islam. The verse serves as a warning against the dangers of pride and arrogance, emphasizing that such behavior is not only displeasing to Allah but also leads to a terrible abode in the afterlife.

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad], for indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And whether We show you some of what We have promised them or We take you in death, to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the Prophet Muhammad to remain steadfast and patient in the face of adversity and persecution. It reassures him that Allah's promise of ultimate victory and justice is true and will be fulfilled, regardless of whether he lives to see it or is taken in death before it comes to pass. The verse underscores the inevitability of accountability before Allah, emphasizing that all individuals, including those who have opposed or persecuted the Prophet and his followers, will ultimately return to Allah and face judgment for their actions.

translation: And We have already sent messengers before you, [O Muhammad]; among them are those We have related to you their story, and among them are those We have not related to you their story. And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign [or miracle] except by permission of Allah . So, when the command of Allah came, the truth was adjudicated, and those who fabricated [the lie] were the losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sovereignty of God in the process of prophethood and the revelation of miracles. It underscores that prophets can only perform miracles or bring signs with God's permission, emphasizing divine authority and control over such events. The verse also touches upon the ultimate triumph of truth and the downfall of falsehood when God's decree is fulfilled, indicating a teleological perspective where truth is destined to prevail.

translation: God is the one who made for you the livestock so that you may ride some of them and from them you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's provision and blessings to humanity through the creation of livestock, emphasizing the dual benefits humans derive from them - using them as a means of transportation and as a source of food, thus underscoring the theme of divine benevolence and the interconnectedness of human life with the natural world created by God.

translation: And for you in them (the animals) are benefits, that you may reach through them a need that is in your breasts (hearts), and upon them and upon ships you are carried.
interpretation: This verse highlights the multifaceted benefits that humans derive from animals, not just physical benefits like transportation and labor, but also emotional and psychological comfort. The phrase 'a need that is in your breasts' suggests that the presence and utility of these animals fulfill deep-seated desires or needs within humans, possibly referring to the companionship, solace, or sense of security they provide. The comparison with ships further emphasizes the significant role these animals play in human life, akin to how ships are vital for sea travel and trade, indicating that just as ships are crucial for traversing seas, animals are indispensable for traversing land and fulfilling various human needs.

translation: And He shows you His signs, so which of the signs of Allah do you deny?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the tendency of humans to deny or reject the signs and manifestations of God's power and wisdom, despite being exposed to them. It is a rhetorical question that emphasizes the inconsistency in human behavior, where they witness the signs of God but still refuse to acknowledge or appreciate them.

translation: Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them and greater in strength and [left] more traces in the land, but what they used to earn did not avail them.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who deny the truth and reject the message of the prophets. It invites them to reflect on the fate of previous nations who were more powerful and left a greater legacy, but were ultimately destroyed because of their wrongdoing. The verse suggests that material achievements and accomplishments are of no avail when one is disobedient to God, and that true success lies in righteousness and obedience to God's commands. It encourages self-reflection and consideration of the lessons from history to avoid a similar downfall.

translation: But when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what they had of knowledge, and there surrounded them that which they used to mock.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and complacency of those who possess knowledge or worldly advantages, yet reject the truth when it is presented to them through prophets and messengers. Their 'rejoicing in what they had of knowledge' indicates a sense of superiority and self-sufficiency that blinds them to the message of the prophets. The consequence is that they are eventually enveloped by the very punishment or consequences they used to mock, signifying that their dismissal of the divine message was not only misguided but also led to their downfall.

translation: But when they saw Our punishment, they said, 'We believe in Allah ˹alone˺ and reject the ˹false gods˺ we used to associate with Him.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inconsistency and lack of sincerity in the faith of those who only turn to God when faced with hardship or punishment. It suggests that true faith is not merely a response to adversity, but a consistent and genuine commitment to one's beliefs. The verse implies that the faith professed under duress is not necessarily a reflection of a deep-seated conviction, but rather a pragmatic response to circumstances. It underscores the idea that true faith should be characterized by steadfastness and conviction, rather than being swayed by external circumstances.

translation: But their faith did not benefit them once they saw Our punishment. (This is) the law of God that has preceded among His servants. And thereupon the disbelievers lost (everything).
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of God's law (sunnat Allah) that when people witness the consequences of their actions, their faith is no longer accepted if it comes after they have seen the punishment. It underscores the idea that faith must be accompanied by righteous actions before the onset of punishment, and that once the punishment is manifest, it is too late for faith to be of benefit. The verse serves as a warning that those who reject faith will ultimately suffer loss when they face the consequences of their disbelief.

translation: In the name of Allah, the most Compassionate, the most Merciful. Ha-Mim.
interpretation: This verse is one of the Muqatta'at, letters or combinations of letters that appear at the beginning of certain chapters in the Qur'an. The meaning of these letters is not explicitly stated in the Qur'an, but one interpretation is that they serve as a challenge to the Arabs, who were known for their eloquence and mastery of language, to create something similar to the Qur'an, thus proving its divine origin. The appearance of 'Ha-Mim' at the start of several chapters may also signify a thematic connection between these chapters, with 'Ha-Mim' acting as a marker or a mnemonic device to highlight their relatedness or to categorize them in some way.

translation: A revelation from the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, who is not only merciful (Rahman) in this life but also continually merciful (Rahim) in the hereafter, emphasizing the divine origin and the merciful nature of the revelation.

translation: A Book whose verses have been detailed, a Quran in Arabic for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the clarity and precision of the Quran's message, emphasizing that its Arabic language is a facilitator of understanding for those who possess knowledge, suggesting that the Quran's effectiveness in conveying its message is closely tied to the audience's ability to comprehend its linguistic nuances.

translation: (And We have sent you only as) a bearer of good tidings and a warner; but most of them turn away, so they do not hear.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unfortunate reality that many people reject the message of the Prophet, despite being warned of the consequences of their actions and being given the good news of the rewards for the righteous. The phrase 'they do not hear' is not meant to be taken literally, as they are physically capable of hearing the message. Rather, it means that they do not heed or respond to the message, indicating a spiritual deafness that prevents them from understanding and benefiting from the guidance being offered to them.

translation: And they say, "Our hearts are within coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a screen, so work; indeed, we are working."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the call to faith. They claim that their hearts are shielded or veiled from the message, that they are unable to hear it properly, and that there is a barrier between them and the messenger. In essence, they are making excuses for their refusal to accept the truth, and challenging the messenger to continue his efforts, as they too will continue on their path, implying a sense of defiance and competition.

translation: Say, "I am only a man like you, it is revealed to me that your god is one God; so be upright to Him and ask His forgiveness. And woe to the polytheists."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet's humanity and the unity of God, directing the believers to maintain their devotion and seek forgiveness while warning those who associate partners with God of a dire fate.

translation: Those who do not give zakah and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intrinsic link between the act of giving zakah (charity) and belief in the Hereafter. It suggests that failing to give zakah is not just a financial or social failing, but a spiritual one, indicating a lack of faith in the Hereafter. The refusal to give zakah implies a focus on material wealth and a lack of concern for the welfare of others, which is seen as a manifestation of disbelief in the accountability of the Hereafter. Essentially, it underscores that true faith is demonstrated not just by professing belief, but by acting upon it, and giving zakah is one of the practical manifestations of that faith.
