translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - they will have a reward uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the reward of believers who performed righteous deeds will be continuous and uninterrupted in the hereafter, emphasizing the eternal nature of paradise and its blessings.

translation: Say, 'Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two Days and you set up rivals for Him? That is the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the inconsistency in the beliefs of those who deny the oneness of God. It questions how they can reject the Creator of the earth, who has demonstrated immense power by creating it in just two days, yet still attribute partners or equals to Him. The verse underscores the notion that the being capable of such a feat is undoubtedly the Lord of all worlds, deserving of worship and acknowledgment of His uniqueness.

translation: And He placed therein mountains above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, alike for those who ask.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's meticulous planning and provision for the inhabitants of the Earth. The phrase 'for those who ask' suggests that the sustenance and resources provided are not just a random act of creation, but a deliberate and thoughtful provision made with the needs of the inhabitants in mind, indicating a deep consideration for the well-being of those who will live on Earth.

translation: Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, 'Come both of you, willingly or unwillingly.' They both said, 'We come, willingly.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the absolute power and authority of Allah over all creation. The fact that the heaven and earth obeyed His command, despite being given the choice to comply willingly or under compulsion, highlights their inherent subservience to His will. It underscores the idea that everything in the universe is under Allah's control and operates according to His decree, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid (the oneness of God) and the omnipotence of Allah.

translation: And He completed them as seven heavens within two days and inspired in each heaven its command, and We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omnipotence and meticulous planning in creating the universe. The creation of the seven heavens in two days signifies a deliberate and measured approach to creation. The revelation of a specific purpose or 'amr' to each heaven suggests that each level of the heavens has a distinct role or function within the cosmic order. The adornment of the lowest heaven with 'masabih' (often interpreted as stars or celestial bodies) not only signifies aesthetic beauty but also serves a protective function, as indicated by the term 'hifza' (preservation or protection). This protection could be understood as safeguarding the heavens and, by extension, the earth from potential harm or disorder. The verse concludes by attributing this precise and majestic creation to 'al-'aziz al-'alim' (the Almighty, the All-Knowing), emphasizing that the creation is a manifestation of God's power and wisdom. This interpretation underscores the Islamic concept of a universe created with purpose, order, and beauty, reflecting the attributes of its Creator.

translation: But if they turn away, then say, "I have warned you of a thunderbolt, like the thunderbolt [that struck] 'Aad and Thamud."
interpretation: This verse is a warning from Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to convey to the disbelievers that if they turn away from the truth, they will face a punishment similar to that which befell the ancient nations of 'Aad and Thamud, emphasizing the severity and swiftness of divine retribution for those who reject faith and disobey Allah's commands.

translation: When their messengers came to them from before them and behind them, [saying], 'Worship none but Allah,' they said, 'If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels, so indeed we are, with that with which you have been sent, disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy and arrogance of those who reject the message of the prophets. The prophets came to them with a clear and consistent message from God, warning them and guiding them to the right path. However, instead of accepting this message, they responded with a demand that reflects their disbelief and stubbornness, suggesting that if God truly wanted to communicate with them, He would have sent angels as messengers. This response indicates their refusal to accept the truth brought by human prophets, demonstrating their deep-seated rejection of the monotheistic faith and their insistence on tangible, visible proof, rather than accepting the guidance offered through human messengers.

translation: As for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the land without right, and they said, "Who is more powerful than us?" Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is more powerful than them? And they used to deny Our signs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dangers of arrogance and the rejection of divine signs. The people of 'Ad became arrogant and proud of their physical strength, forgetting that the Creator who gave them this strength is even more powerful. Their rejection of God's signs (ayat) indicates a willful blindness to the truth, demonstrating that their arrogance was not just a matter of pride, but also a deliberate refusal to acknowledge the divine authority that governs their existence.

translation: So We sent upon them a screaming wind in days of misfortune to make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth and are arrogant towards the signs of Allah. It highlights the consequences of such behavior, both in this life and the hereafter. The 'wind' sent upon them is symbolic of divine retribution that can manifest in various forms, serving as a tangible example of the consequences of disobedience. The distinction between the humiliation in this life and the greater humiliation in the hereafter underscores the belief in an afterlife where justice is fully realized, and wrongdoing is ultimately punished. The verse emphasizes the idea that worldly punishment is only a precursor to a more severe and lasting consequence, reinforcing the notion that true accountability lies beyond this mortal existence.

translation: And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance, so the lightning bolt of humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept that guidance is not just about being shown the right path, but also about having the will to follow it. The people of Thamud were given guidance, but they chose to reject it and preferred to remain in their state of ignorance and disbelief. Their rejection of guidance and their persistence in wrongdoing led to their downfall, as they were struck by a devastating punishment. The verse serves as a warning that divine guidance is not a guarantee of salvation; rather, it is the individual's response to that guidance that ultimately determines their fate.

translation: And We saved those who believed and used to fear God
interpretation: This verse highlights God's practice of rescuing believers who are characterized by their piety. The term 'muttaqoon' (those who are pious or God-conscious) implies individuals who are mindful of their actions and their consequences in the sight of God, adhering to His commands and avoiding what He has forbidden. The verse suggests that faith accompanied by righteous conduct is a means to salvation, underscoring the importance of both belief and ethical behavior in achieving divine deliverance.

translation: And the Day when the enemies of Allah will be gathered to the Fire, then they will be assembled in ranks.
interpretation: This verse highlights the scene of judgment where the enemies of God are gathered and driven towards the fire of Hell, indicating their accountability for their actions and the consequences of their rejection of faith and disobedience.

translation: Until when they come to it, their hearing and their eyes and their skins will testify against them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive nature of accountability on the Day of Judgment, where not only will individuals be held accountable for their actions, but even their own faculties - their senses and bodies - will testify against them, bearing witness to the deeds they committed in life, underscoring the inescapable nature of divine justice.

translation: And they will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "God has caused us to speak, as He causes all things to speak, and He is the One who created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned."
interpretation: This verse highlights the all-encompassing nature of God's knowledge and power, suggesting that on the Day of Judgment, even the parts of the human body will bear witness against the individual, and that God has the power to make all things speak and testify. It underscores the idea that humans are accountable for their actions and that their bodies, which were created by God, will serve as witnesses against them if they have committed wrongdoing. The verse emphasizes the inevitability of return to God and the reckoning that awaits, reinforcing the concept of accountability in the afterlife.

translation: And you did not conceal yourselves, lest your hearing, and your sight, and your skins testify against you, but you assumed that Allah does not know much of what you do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of attempting to hide one's actions from Allah, emphasizing that even the most intimate aspects of an individual's being, such as their senses and bodily parts, will ultimately testify against them on the Day of Judgment, contradicting the false assumption that Allah is unaware of their deeds.

translation: And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord. It has brought you to destruction, and you have become of the losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of having a negative perception or assumption about Allah. It suggests that the people's misconceptions or false beliefs about their Lord led to their downfall, resulting in them becoming among the losers. It implies that one's beliefs and assumptions have a significant impact on their fate, and having incorrect or negative assumptions can lead to spiritual and moral loss.

translation: If they are patient, their abode is still the Fire. And if they ask to appease [Allah ], they will not be of those who are appeased.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of seeking forgiveness or appeasement after having persisted in disbelief and wrongdoing. It underscores that those who have hardened their hearts against faith and continued on the path of disobedience will ultimately face the consequences of their actions, and their attempts to make amends will be rejected.

translation: And We have assigned for them companions, who have made alluring to them what is before them and what is behind them; and the word (of doom) proved true against them among the nations of the jinn and mankind that had passed away before them. Indeed, they were the losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept that the company one keeps can significantly influence their worldview and actions. It suggests that for those who have gone astray, their companions or peers (referred to as 'قرناء' or 'companions/peers') have played a role in making their misguided path appear appealing, both in terms of their current actions and their past decisions. The verse implies a divine justice where the fate of previous nations, both from among the jinn and humans, who followed a similar path serves as a precedent, underscoring the notion that deviation from the right path leads to loss and that this loss is not arbitrary but a consequence of their choices and the influences they were under.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, 'Do not listen to this Qur'an and make noise during [the recitation of] it that perhaps you will overcome.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tactics employed by those who reject the truth to undermine the impact of the Qur'an. By instructing their followers not to listen to the Qur'an and to create a commotion during its recitation, they hoped to drown out its message and gain an upper hand. This reveals the desperation and fear of those who oppose the truth, as they resort to such measures to prevent the Qur'an's message from being heard and understood.

translation: We will surely make those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment and We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting faith and engaging in evil deeds. It signifies that those who deny the truth and persist in their disbelief will face a severe punishment in this life and the next, and will be recompensed for their worst actions, indicating that their deeds will be judged based on their most evil aspects, rather than being forgiven or mitigated.

translation: That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah - the Fire. For them therein will be the [eternal] home as recompense because they used to deny Our verses.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the ultimate recompense for those who have taken a stance of enmity against God is the fire of Hell, where they will reside eternally. The eternal abode in the fire is a direct consequence of their persistent rejection of God's signs and revelations, indicating a profound spiritual obstinacy and denial of the truth.

translation: And those who disbelieved will say, 'Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and men that we may put them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability and justice on the Day of Judgment, where the disbelievers will be given the opportunity to confront those who misled them, and in their desperation, they will wish to humiliate their misleaders by placing them under their feet, symbolizing the ultimate degradation and punishment for those who led others astray.

translation: Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allah ", and then remained on a right course - the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith. Those who affirm their belief in God and remain committed to their faith are reassured by the angels at the time of their death, alleviating their fears and sorrows, and are given the glad tidings of Paradise, which they were promised during their lifetime.

translation: We are your guardians in this world and in the Hereafter; and you will have therein whatever your souls desire, and you will have therein whatever you call for.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah is assuring the believers that He is their guardian and protector both in this life and the hereafter. The phrase 'ولكم فيها ما تشتهي أنفسكم ولكم فيها ما تدعون' suggests that in the hereafter, the believers will be granted whatever their souls desire and whatever they call for, indicating a state of ultimate satisfaction and fulfillment in paradise. It highlights the boundless generosity and grace of Allah towards the believers, where their deepest desires are met, and their prayers are answered, reflecting the blissful nature of the afterlife for those who are righteous.

translation: As a hospitality from Allah, the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This phrase signifies that the reward or hospitality being referred to is not just a mundane or worldly gesture, but is instead an expression of Allah's mercy and forgiveness towards the believers. It underscores the idea that Allah's generosity and benevolence towards His servants are rooted in His essential attributes of being Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful, implying that the believers are recipients of a gracious and merciful treatment from Allah.

translation: And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah and does righteous deeds and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of a true believer and a righteous individual. It emphasizes that the best person is one who not only believes in Allah but also actively invites others to the path of righteousness, performs good deeds, and openly declares their submission to Allah. The verse suggests that true faith is not just about personal conviction but also about actively promoting the message of Islam and living a virtuous life, thereby setting a good example for others to follow.

translation: And not equal are the good and the evil. Repel [evil] with what is best, and lo, he between whom and you was enmity would become as if he were a close friend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of responding to evil with good. It suggests that when faced with hostility or enmity, one should react with kindness and compassion, rather than retaliating with malice. By doing so, the adversary may transform into a close and affectionate friend, illustrating the transformative power of benevolence in reconciling differences and fostering harmony.

translation: And none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except the owner of a great portion [of good].
interpretation: This verse highlights that the ability to persevere and be patient is a rare quality, and those who possess it are truly blessed. It suggests that the trials and challenges of life can only be endured by individuals who have cultivated the virtue of patience, and that such individuals are endowed with a great share of good fortune or spiritual wealth.

translation: And if an incitement from Satan incites you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse is instructing the believer to seek refuge in Allah when faced with the whispers or temptations of Satan. It signifies that whenever a person feels the influence or prompting of Satan, they should immediately turn to Allah for protection. The verse underscores Allah's attributes as the All-Hearing and the All-Knowing, implying that Allah is fully aware of the whispers of Satan and the believer's plea for refuge, and is capable of providing the necessary protection. It emphasizes the importance of relying on Allah's power and knowledge to counteract the evil suggestions of Satan, thereby highlighting the believer's dependence on divine guidance and support in the face of temptation or adversity.

translation: And of His signs are the night and day and the sun and moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him that you should be worshipping.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning against the worship of celestial bodies, emphasizing that true worship is due to Allah alone, the Creator of these bodies. It underscores the monotheistic belief that the objects of creation, no matter how magnificent, are not worthy of worship; rather, it is the Creator who deserves devotion. The act of prostrating (sajda) is used here not just as a physical act of worship but as a symbol of ultimate submission and reverence, directing it solely to Allah indicates the exclusivity of worship due to Him.

translation: But if they are too proud, (then still) those with your Lord exalt Him by night and by day, and they do not tire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to those who show arrogance towards the worship and remembrance of Allah, that there are those in the heavens who are constantly engaged in the glorification of Allah, day and night, without ever tiring or feeling weary. It highlights the contrast between the attitude of the arrogant and that of the angels or other beings who are devoted to the worship of Allah, emphasizing the importance of humility and persistence in devotion.

translation: And of His signs is that you see the earth stilled, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and grows. Indeed, He who has given it life is the Giver of Life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent
interpretation: This verse is pointing to the power of Allah in reviving the dead. The example given is of the earth which appears barren and lifeless, but upon receiving rain, it is revitalized and brings forth life. This is used as a metaphor to convey that just as Allah can bring life to the lifeless earth, He is equally capable of reviving the dead. The verse aims to instill faith in the resurrection and the omnipotence of Allah.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses - We will drive them into a Fire. Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who distort or deny the signs of Allah, indicating that their actions are not hidden from Him and that they will face severe punishment in the afterlife. The rhetorical question posed in the verse emphasizes the stark contrast between the fate of the disbelievers, who will be cast into the Fire, and those who come secure and safe on the Day of Judgment. It underscores the notion that the consequences of one's actions are directly tied to their beliefs and deeds, and that Allah is fully aware of all that they do, thus encouraging individuals to be mindful of their actions and to adhere to the path of righteousness.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the message when it came to them; and indeed, it is a mighty Book.
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy and resistance of those who reject the truth when it is presented to them. The term 'الذكر' (al-dhikr) refers to the Qur'an, which is described as 'كتاب عزيز' (kitabun 'aziz), a noble or mighty book. The description of the Qur'an as 'عزيز' signifies its power, honor, and the impossibility of being defeated or altered. The rejection of such a noble and powerful scripture by those who disbelieve underscores their stubbornness and refusal to acknowledge the truth, despite its evident nobility and authority.

translation: Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Qur'an is completely protected from falsehood and corruption, whether it be in the form of additions, subtractions, or alterations. The phrase 'from between its hands' refers to the past, indicating that the Qur'an has not been corrupted or altered from its original form since its revelation. Similarly, 'from behind it' refers to the future, signifying that it will remain uncorrupted and unchanged until the end of time. The verse attributes the Qur'an's preservation to its origin, stating that it is a revelation from the All-Wise (حكيم), who possesses perfect wisdom in His actions and decrees, and the Praiseworthy (حميد), who is deserving of all praise for His perfect attributes and actions. Thus, the verse underscores the divine origin and the inimitable nature of the Qur'an, guaranteeing its authenticity and timeless relevance.

translation: Nothing is said to you, [O Muhammad], except what was already said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is a possessor of forgiveness and a possessor of painful penalty.
interpretation: This verse is a message of reassurance to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he is not alone in facing rejection and hardship. It reminds him that previous prophets also faced similar challenges, and that his Lord has the power to forgive those who repent and to punish those who persist in their wrongdoing. The verse is meant to comfort the Prophet and the believers, and to encourage them to remain steadfast in the face of adversity, knowing that their Lord is capable of both mercy and justice.

translation: And if We had made it a Qur'an in a foreign language, they would have said, "Why are its verses not clearly explained? Is it a foreign language and [yet] an Arab [messenger]?" Say, "It is, for those who believe, a guidance and a healing. And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is upon them blindness. Those are being called from a distant place."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of the disbelievers. Even if the Qur'an were revealed in a foreign language, they would still find fault with it, demanding that its verses be clarified. The verse contrasts the response of believers, for whom the Qur'an is a source of guidance and healing, with that of disbelievers, who are unreceptive to its message, as if it were being spoken from a distant place, beyond their comprehension or concern. It underscores the spiritual blindness of those who reject faith, implying that their inability to understand or appreciate the Qur'an stems from their own spiritual state rather than any inherent flaw in the revelation itself.

translation: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, but it came under disagreement. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed they are, concerning it, in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of human discord and skepticism despite being given clear guidance. It implies that if not for God's predetermined will to delay judgment, the differences among people, such as those who received the scripture given to Moses, would have been resolved conclusively. The verse underscores the pervasive nature of doubt among those who receive divine guidance, suggesting that skepticism is a fundamental challenge that faces those given revelation.

translation: Whoever does righteousness - it is for his [own] soul; and whoever does evil [does so] against it. And your Lord is not unjust to the servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of individual responsibility and justice in Islam. It signifies that every individual is accountable for their actions, and the consequences of those actions will be borne by them alone. The phrase "من عمل صالحا فلنفسه" (Whoever does good, it is for his own soul) indicates that the benefits of righteous deeds are for the individual who performs them. Conversely, "ومن أساء فعليها" (and whoever does evil, it is against his own soul) shows that the harm caused by evil deeds is also borne by the individual responsible. The verse concludes with "وما ربك بظلام للعبيد" (And your Lord is not in the least unjust to the servants), emphasizing God's justice and fairness in dealing with His creation. It reassures that God does not wrong His servants by holding them accountable for actions they did not commit or by denying them the reward for their good deeds. This verse underscores the Islamic belief in the justice of God and the personal responsibility of individuals for their actions, reinforcing the concept that one's deeds have direct consequences on their own soul.

translation: To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour. And no fruits come out of their coverings, nor does a female conceive or give birth, except with His knowledge. And on the Day when He will call out to them, 'Where are My partners?' they will say, 'We declare to You that none of us is a witness [to any partners].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute knowledge and sovereignty of Allah over all aspects of existence, including the timing of the Hour, the natural cycles of growth and reproduction, and the accountability of those who have attributed partners to Him. It underscores that on the Day of Judgment, those who claimed other deities alongside Allah will deny their past assertions, acknowledging their lack of evidence or witnesses to support their claims of associating others with Allah's divinity.

translation: And lost from them will be what they were invoking before, and they will be certain that they have no way to escape.
interpretation: This verse indicates that on the Day of Judgment, the disbelievers will realize that their false deities and objects of worship, which they invoked in the worldly life, have abandoned them and provided no benefit. Furthermore, they will understand that there is no escape or refuge for them from the punishment that awaits, signifying the hopelessness and despair that will befall them.

translation: Man never tires of praying for good, and if evil touches him, he is hopeless, despairing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the duality of human nature in the face of fortune and adversity. When faced with good, humans tend to be insatiably optimistic and continually pray for more. However, when hardship befalls them, they quickly succumb to despair and lose hope, demonstrating a lack of resilience and faith in the face of adversity. This verse serves as a commentary on the human tendency to be shortsighted and lacking in steadfastness during times of hardship.

translation: And if We give him a taste of Our mercy after some adversity that has befallen him, he says, "This is [due] to me, and I do not think the Hour will occur; and [even] if I should be returned to my Lord, I will surely have with Him the best." But We will surely inform those who disbelieved about what they did, and We will surely cause them to taste of a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to forget the trials they faced and the blessings they received when they are in a state of comfort and prosperity. It warns that when people are given respite and blessings after facing hardships, they often become complacent and attribute their success to their own merits, forgetting the divine hand that has guided them. The verse serves as a caution against the arrogance that can arise from prosperity and the forgetfulness of one's accountability to God, emphasizing that those who deny the truth will be held accountable for their actions and will face severe punishment.

translation: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and becomes remote on his side (instead of coming to Us), and when evil touches him, then he is full of lengthy supplication.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inconsistency and ingratitude of human nature. When Allah bestows blessings upon a person, they become arrogant, turn away from Allah, and become self-sufficient, forgetting the source of their blessings. However, when hardship befalls them, they become desperate and turn to Allah with lengthy and fervent supplications, indicating a stark contrast between their behavior during times of ease and hardship.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if it is from Allah and you disbelieved in it, who is more astray than one who is in an extreme schism?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of rejecting the truth after being convinced of its divine origin. It implies that those who knowingly deny the message from God are further astray than those who are simply in a state of disagreement or opposition, indicating a deeper level of misguidance associated with willful rejection of the truth.

translation: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. But is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?
interpretation: This verse signifies that God's existence and authority are evident in the universe and within human beings themselves. The phrase 'until it is clear to them that it is the truth' indicates that the signs or evidence (ayat) will continue to be revealed until the truth of God's existence and authority is undeniable. The rhetorical question 'Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?' underscores the idea that God's all-encompassing awareness and witness to everything is sufficient testimony to His existence and power, rendering additional proof somewhat redundant for those with faith.

translation: Unquestionably, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. Unquestionably He is, of all things, encompassing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the all-encompassing nature of God's knowledge and awareness, suggesting that those who doubt the meeting with their Lord are unaware that He is fully aware of everything, including their doubts and actions.

translation: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha-Mim.
interpretation: This verse is one of the Muqatta'at, letters or combinations of letters that appear at the beginning of certain chapters in the Qur'an. The meaning of these letters is known only to Allah. One interpretation is that they serve as a challenge to the Arabs, who were known for their eloquence and mastery of the language, to create something similar to the Qur'an, as it is composed of the same letters they used in their own speech and poetry.

translation: Alif Lam Mim Sad is not the exact translation here as the given verse is 'عسق'. The translation is simply: 'Alif Sad Ha Mim Ain Qaf' or 'Haqq' or simply the letters as they are: 'Ain Sad Qaf'
interpretation: This verse is one of the Muqatta'at, a set of disjointed letters that appear at the beginning of some chapters in the Qur'an. The interpretation of 'عسق' is subject to various understandings among scholars. One interpretation is that these letters are a form of divine mystery, and their meaning is known only to Allah. They may serve as a challenge to the disbelievers, or as a sign of the Qur'an's divine origin and a test of faith for the believers.

translation: Thus God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, inspires you (Muhammad) and those before you.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity and consistency of God's method of revelation to prophets throughout history, emphasizing God's authority and wisdom in guiding His messengers, suggesting that the revelation received by the Prophet Muhammad is part of a larger tradition of divine guidance.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And indeed, He is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and supremacy of Allah over all creation, indicating that everything in the heavens and on earth is under His ownership and control, and that He is exalted above all else in status and greatness.

translation: The heavens are almost torn apart from above them, and the angels glorify the praise of their Lord and seek forgiveness for those on earth. Indeed, God is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immense mercy of God and the interconnectedness of the heavens and earth. The angels, who are often seen as distant beings, are actively seeking forgiveness for humanity, demonstrating God's compassion and the angels' role as intercessors. The verse suggests that God's forgiveness and mercy are not limited to the righteous, but are available to all, emphasizing the universal nature of His benevolence.

translation: And those who take guardians besides Him - God is a guardian over them, and you are not a guardian over them.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the distinction between guardianship and accountability. It is stating that those who take other guardians besides God are still under God's watch and protection, even if they are not following Him exclusively. The verse is emphasizing that God is aware of and has oversight over all individuals, regardless of their allegiances or actions. It is also clarifying the role of the Prophet, indicating that he is not responsible for managing or being the guardian (wakil) over those who have chosen other guardians; his role is to convey the message, not to be accountable for their actions or destinies.

translation: And thus We have revealed to you a Qur'an in Arabic that you may warn the Mother of the Cities [i.e., Makkah] and those around it and warn of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt. A party will be in Paradise and a party in the Blazing Fire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the universal purpose of the Qur'an, which is to warn people of the consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment. The mention of 'the Mother of the Cities' signifies the central role of Makkah in Islam, and 'those around it' indicates that the message is not limited to the inhabitants of Makkah but extends to all surrounding regions and, by extension, to the world. The verse underscores the inevitability and certainty of the Day of Judgment, where people will be divided based on their deeds into those who will be rewarded with Paradise and those who will be punished with Hellfire. It serves as a call to righteousness and a reminder of the accountability that awaits every individual.

translation: And if God had willed, He would have made you one community, but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you; so, race to [all that is] good. To God is your return all together, and He will [then] inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind the diversity among people. It suggests that despite having the power to unify humanity under one belief or path, God has chosen not to, instead allowing diversity to exist. The verse then points to God's mercy as a guiding principle, indicating that those who are guided are those whom God has chosen to receive His mercy. For those who have wronged themselves (the الظالمون, or wrongdoers), the verse underscores their isolation from divine support and guidance, emphasizing that they lack a guardian or helper to rescue or guide them.

translation: Or have they taken protectors other than Him? But it is Allah who is the Protector, and it is He who gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the sovereignty and power of Allah, stating that He is the only true guardian and supporter, and that He has the power to give life to the dead and is capable of doing anything. It is a rebuke to those who seek protection or support from others besides Allah, implying that such actions are misguided as true authority and capability rest solely with Allah.

translation: And in anything over which you differ, its ruling is [to be referred] to Allah. [Say], 'That is Allah, my Lord; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of referring all disputes and differences to Allah's judgment, indicating that when there is a disagreement, the final authority should be the divine guidance as revealed in the Qur'an and through the Prophet's teachings, rather than human opinions or whims, thus reinforcing trust and reliance on Allah.

translation: The Originator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you pairs from among yourselves, and pairs among the cattle. He multiplies you thereby. There is nothing like Him; and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unique creative power of Allah, who not only created the universe but also established a system of pairing within creation, such as between humans and within cattle, illustrating a profound aspect of His design for reproduction and multiplication, and emphasizing His incomparability and omniscience.

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth; He unfolds provision for whomsoever He wills, and straitens it. Verily, He is the Knower of all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's absolute sovereignty and control over the universe, emphasizing that He is the sole dispenser of provision and sustenance. The phrase 'He unfolds provision for whomsoever He wills, and straitens it' suggests that God's distribution of resources is not based on human merit or worthiness but rather on His divine wisdom and purpose. The verse underscores the idea that God's knowledge encompasses all things, and His decisions regarding provision are guided by an all-encompassing understanding of the needs and circumstances of His creation.

translation: He has ordained for you the same religion that He enjoined on Noah, and which We have revealed to you, and which We enjoined on Abraham, Moses and Jesus, (enjoining on them) 'Establish the faith and do not split up regarding it.' What you call upon the pagans to (accept) is hard on them. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills, and guides to Himself the one who turns (to Him).
interpretation: This verse underscores the unity and continuity of the divine message across different prophets and times, emphasizing that the core of the religion ordained by Allah remains the same. It highlights the importance of unity among believers by establishing the faith and avoiding division, while also noting that guidance is a divine prerogative, granted to those whom Allah chooses and to those who sincerely turn to Him.

translation: And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them - out of [mutual] jealousy. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord [postponing judgment] until a specified term, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, those who were made to inherit the Scripture after them are in lingering doubt about it.
interpretation: This verse highlights that divisions and sects among people often arise not due to a lack of knowledge, but rather due to arrogance, pride, and a desire to surpass one another, even when the truth is clear to them. It also warns that those who inherit sacred knowledge or scripture after the initial recipients can sometimes be left in a state of doubt or skepticism about the truth, indicating a need for continuous guidance and reflection.

translation: So to that (faith) you invite ˹people˺ ˹O Prophet˺ and remain steadfast as you have been commanded. Do not follow their ˹own˺ desires, but say, “I believe in whatever Book Allah has sent down, and I have been commanded to be just among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. To us are our deeds, and to you are your deeds. There is no ˹need for˺ dispute between us and you. Allah will bring us all together, and to Him is the ˹final˺ destination.”
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and justice in one's faith and actions. It instructs the believer to continue calling people to the truth and to remain firm on the path as commanded by God, without being swayed by the desires or opinions of others. The verse also highlights the principle of accountability, where each individual is responsible for their own deeds. It concludes by affirming that God will ultimately bring all people together and that the final destination for all is to return to Him.

translation: And those who dispute concerning Allah after He has been responded to [i.e., accepted] - their argument is invalid with their Lord, and upon them is [His] wrath, and for them is a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the futility and consequences of arguing against the truth after it has been established and accepted. The phrase 'من بعد ما استجيب له' suggests that the truth has been acknowledged and responded to, yet some individuals continue to dispute and argue against it. The verse indicates that such arguments are rendered invalid and 'داحضة' (futile or vain) in the sight of their Lord. Furthermore, it warns that these individuals will incur divine wrath 'وعليهم غضب' and face severe punishment 'ولهم عذاب شديد'. The underlying message is that obstinacy in the face of acknowledged truth is not only futile but also invites divine displeasure and punishment.

translation: It is God who has sent down the Book with the truth and the Balance. And what will make you know that perhaps the Hour is near?
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the inevitability and the proximity of the Day of Judgment. The mention of God having sent down the Scripture and the balance (or scale) with truth serves as a prelude to the statement about the Hour (Day of Judgment), suggesting that just as God's revelation and the principle of justice (represented by the balance) are realities, so too is the reality of the Hour. The verse is cautioning that the Hour might be nearer than people think, underscoring the importance of being prepared for it by living righteously according to the guidance provided by the Scripture.

translation: Those who do not believe in it (the Hour) seek to hasten it, but those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in extreme error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the attitudes of believers and non-believers towards the Hour (the Day of Judgment). While non-believers mockingly demand its immediate arrival, believers are filled with a sense of awe and reverence, knowing it to be an inevitable reality. The verse serves as a warning to those who engage in debates and disputes about the Hour, indicating that such skepticism stems from a profound deviation from the truth, underscoring the gravity of their error.

translation: Allah is gentle with His servants; He gives provisions to whom He wills, and He is the Strong, the Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's subtle and gentle care for His creation, indicating that His provision and sustenance are not limited by human perceptions of worthiness or capability. It underscores the idea that Allah's power and might are exercised with gentleness and that His decisions regarding provision are based on His wisdom, not on human criteria. It encourages believers to trust in Allah's wisdom and to recognize that His strength and might are the foundation of His gentle care for them.

translation: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We increase for him in his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world - We give him thereof, but he will not have in the Hereafter any share.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who prioritize worldly gains and those who focus on the hereafter. It suggests that the efforts of individuals are directed towards either the material rewards of this world or the spiritual rewards of the hereafter. Those who genuinely strive for the hereafter will have their efforts augmented, implying a multiplication of their good deeds. In contrast, those who are solely focused on worldly gains may receive some of what they seek, but they will be devoid of any share or reward in the hereafter, underscoring the idea that a singular focus on material wealth and status comes at the cost of spiritual fulfillment and eternal reward.

translation: Or have they partners who have prescribed for them a religion that Allah has not allowed? Had it not been for the Decree of Distinction, the matter would have been settled between them. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse critiques those who follow religious practices or laws not sanctioned by Allah, suggesting that their 'partners' or deities have legislated for them a religion that Allah has not authorized. It underscores the inevitability of judgment and the painful punishment awaiting those who engage in such unjust practices, were it not for the predetermined Word of Decree that has set a time for judgment.

translation: You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, and it will [certainly] befall them. And those who have believed and done righteous deeds will be in lush [and verdant] gardens of the Gardens, having whatever they will with their Lord. That is the great bounty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the fate of the unjust and the righteous on the Day of Judgment. The unjust, despite being apprehensive about the consequences of their actions, will inevitably face the reality of their wrongdoings. On the other hand, believers who have performed righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise, enjoying the fulfillment of their desires at the pleasure of their Lord. This distinction underscores the great bounty that Allah has reserved for the righteous, emphasizing the magnitude of His reward as a manifestation of His immense grace.

translation: That is [the bounty] whereof Allah gives good tidings unto His servants who believe and do righteous good deeds. Say (O Muhammad): "I ask of you no reward for it save the love among relatives." And whosoever earns a good deed, We shall give him an increase in good for it. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Responsive to gratitude.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining kinship ties with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a means of expressing gratitude for his guidance and message. The phrase 'except for the love of my kin' indicates that the reward for the Prophet's efforts is not monetary but rather the affection and loyalty towards his family. This highlights the significance of the bond between the Prophet and his relatives, suggesting that their well-being and respect are intertwined with the acceptance and appreciation of his prophetic mission.

translation: Or do they say, "He has invented about Allah a lie"? But if Allah should will (to seal your heart), He would seal it. And Allah eliminates falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the consequences of denying the truth and attributing falsehood to Allah. It suggests that if the Prophet were to fabricate lies against Allah, Allah would seal his heart, indicating a severe punishment for such an act. However, the verse also reassures that Allah will eradicate falsehood and establish the truth through His words, demonstrating His power to distinguish between truth and falsehood. The verse concludes by affirming Allah's omniscience, emphasizing that He has complete knowledge of the innermost thoughts and intentions of individuals, thus underscoring the futility of attempting to conceal or deny the truth.

translation: And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons their evil deeds, and He knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's merciful and forgiving nature towards His servants. It signifies that God is always ready to accept repentance from those who turn to Him, forgiving their past wrongdoings and having knowledge of their actions, thus encouraging believers to seek forgiveness and live righteously.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - He will give them their rewards and increase them of His bounty. And the disbelievers will have a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the believers who perform good deeds and the disbelievers. The believers are responsive to the call of faith and are rewarded with an increase in God's bounty, indicating a continuous and expanding grace upon them. On the other hand, those who reject faith are met with a severe punishment, underscoring the gravity of their denial and the serious consequences that follow. It suggests that faith and righteous actions are not only a means to salvation but also to an ever-increasing divine favor, while disbelief leads to a dire outcome.

translation: And if Allah were to enlarge the provision for His servants they would surely transgress in the earth; but He sends down by measure as He wills. Surely He is Aware of, and Sees, His servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the delicate balance that Allah maintains in providing sustenance to His creatures. It suggests that if Allah were to abundantly provide for all without any limitation, it would lead to excesses and unrighteous behavior among humans, as they would become complacent and arrogant. Instead, Allah provides sustenance in measured quantities, tailored to the needs and circumstances of each individual. This reflects Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and watchful eye over His creation, as He is fully aware of what is beneficial for each of His servants.

translation: And it is He who sends down the rain after they had lost hope and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's mercy and benevolence towards His creation, as He sends down rain after people have lost hope, reviving the earth and bringing life to it. It signifies that despite despair, God's mercy can bring about renewal and rejuvenation, emphasizing His role as a guardian and protector who is worthy of praise.

translation: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and what He has dispersed throughout them of creatures. And it is within His right to gather them when He wills.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence of Allah by pointing to the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diverse creatures that inhabit them. It underscores that just as Allah has the power to create such vast and varied life, He also has the capability to gather all these creatures together whenever He wishes, emphasizing His absolute power and control over all creation.

translation: And whatever misfortune befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and [yet] He pardons much.
interpretation: This verse highlights the direct relationship between human actions and the consequences they face. It suggests that hardships and misfortunes are a result of the wrongdoings and sins committed by individuals. However, it also underscores God's mercy and forgiveness, indicating that not all wrongdoings are punished, as He pardons many transgressions. This serves as a call to self-reflection and accountability for one's actions, while also comforting believers with the knowledge of God's clemency.

translation: And you cannot escape on earth. And you will not have other than Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who deny the truth and reject the message of Allah, emphasizing their utter helplessness and lack of protection against Allah's will. It signifies that no individual can evade or outrun Allah's judgment, and that without His mercy and guidance, they are devoid of any guardian or helper who could save them from His reckoning. The verse underscores the omnipotence of Allah and the futility of human attempts to defy or escape His authority, reinforcing the concept of accountability and the inevitability of facing divine judgment for one's deeds.

translation: And among His signs are the ships, like mountains, in the sea.
interpretation: This verse highlights the majesty and power of Allah's creation, using the imagery of massive ships sailing through the sea to illustrate His ability to create and control the vast and powerful forces of nature, inspiring awe and gratitude in those who witness them.

translation: If He wills, He can still the wind, so that they (the ships) remain motionless on its (the sea's) surface. Indeed, in that are signs for everyone who is patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the omnipotence of Allah over the natural world, using the control of the winds as a metaphor for His power over all creation. It suggests that a person who is patient (صبار) and grateful (شكور) can derive lessons and signs (آيات) from observing the workings of the natural world, and thus, cultivate a deeper understanding and appreciation of Allah's majesty and providence.

translation: Or He could destroy them because of what they have earned, but He pardons much.
interpretation: This verse highlights the delicate balance between divine justice and mercy. It suggests that while individuals are accountable for their actions and could face the consequences of their wrongdoings, God's mercy prevails, and He chooses to pardon many of their transgressions rather than punishing them. It underscores the concept that God's forgiveness is a dominant aspect of His nature, encouraging hope and redemption for those who have erred.

translation: And those who dispute concerning Our signs/verses know they will have no escape/way out.
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who dispute or argue against the signs of Allah, indicating that they have no escape or refuge from the consequences of their actions. It signifies that those who engage in such disputes are ultimately trapped in their own stubbornness and will face the repercussions of their denial or rejection of Allah's signs.

translation: And whatever you have been given is but a provision of the present life. But what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who have believed and rely upon their Lord
interpretation: This verse highlights the transience of worldly possessions and the enduring value of spiritual rewards. It suggests that true and lasting goodness is reserved for those who have faith and trust in their Lord, implying that a life of faith and reliance on God is more valuable than the fleeting pleasures and material gains of this world.

translation: And those who avoid the major sins and indecencies and, when they are angry, they forgive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of the righteous servants of Allah, who not only avoid major sins and indecencies but also possess the quality of forgiveness when they are wronged or provoked. It signifies that true piety is not just about abstaining from wrongdoing, but also about showing restraint and mercy when faced with situations that might provoke anger, thereby demonstrating a high level of moral and spiritual maturity.

translation: And those who have responded to their lord and established prayer, their affair is [determined by] consultation among themselves, and from what We have provided them, they spend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the characteristics of believers who are successful in their faith. It emphasizes the importance of responding to God's call, establishing regular prayer, making decisions through mutual consultation, and spending in charity from the provisions God has granted them. The verse underscores the values of communal decision-making and social responsibility, suggesting that a community guided by these principles is one that is pleasing to God.

translation: And those who, when an outrage is committed against them, defend themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of standing up against injustice and oppression. It emphasizes that believers should not be passive in the face of aggression, but rather take action to defend themselves and assert their rights. The verse is encouraging a sense of self-respect and dignity, while also implying that such self-defense should be carried out in a just and reasonable manner.

translation: The recompense for an injury is an injury equal thereto (in degree): but if a person forgives and makes reconciliation, his reward is due from Allah: for Allah loveth not those who do wrong.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of justice and retaliation in Islam, stating that the punishment for a wrongdoing should be proportionate to the wrongdoing itself. However, it also encourages forgiveness and reconciliation, indicating that those who choose to forgive and make amends will be rewarded by God. The verse concludes by emphasizing God's disapproval of injustice, underscoring the importance of fairness and righteousness in all interactions.

translation: And whoever avenges himself after having been wronged, those have not upon them any blame.
interpretation: This verse indicates that a person who has been wronged is allowed to retaliate against the one who wronged them, and they will not be held accountable for doing so, as long as their retaliation is proportionate to the initial wrongdoing.

translation: The blame is only against those who oppress people and wrongfully spread corruption upon the earth. For them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that accountability and blame fall squarely on those who commit injustices against others and cause disorder on earth without any legitimate justification. It underscores the principle that such wrongful actions will be met with severe consequences, highlighting the importance of justice and righteousness in societal interactions.

translation: And whoever is patient and forgives, indeed, that is a matter of great resolve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and forgiveness in the face of adversity, suggesting that these virtues require a strong will and determination, and are thus among the most noble and commendable of character traits.

translation: And he whom Allah sends astray, there is no guardian for him thereafter. And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying, 'Is there for return any way?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of being led astray by Allah, implying a divine justice where those who have willfully ignored guidance are left without support or intercession when facing the consequences of their actions. The verse also underscores the desperation and realization of the wrongdoers when they witness the punishment, acknowledging too late their inability to escape or reverse their fate, and their belated quest for a way to return or be redeemed.

translation: And you will see them being exposed to it [i.e., the Fire] humbled from humiliation, looking from behind a thin veil. And those who had believed will say, "Indeed, the losers are the ones who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in an enduring punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the fate of the righteous and the wicked on the Day of Judgment. The wicked, having been led astray by their own actions and desires, will be humbled and ashamed as they are exposed to the Hellfire. Their glances, filled with fear and despair, will be furtive, indicating their reluctance to confront the reality of their punishment. In contrast, the believers will recognize the true losers to be those who have not only lost their own souls but also their families, implying a loss of both individual salvation and the bonds of familial love and support. The verse concludes by affirming that the unjust will endure an enduring punishment, underscoring the permanence and severity of their loss.

translation: And they have no allies who would help them in place of Allah. And whoever is misled by Allah - for him there is no way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of relying on false deities or intermediaries for salvation. It underscores the Islamic concept of Tawhid (the oneness of God), emphasizing that Allah's decree is absolute and that no one can escape His will or alter it. The verse suggests that those who are misled by Allah, due to their own rejection of guidance, are left without any means of rectification or salvation, reinforcing the idea that true guidance and succor come solely from Allah.

translation: Respond to your Lord before there comes a Day which there is no turning back from Allah; you will have no refuge on that Day, nor will you have any ability to deny (your deeds).
interpretation: This verse is urging people to respond to their Lord's call before the Day of Judgment arrives, a day that is inevitable and cannot be averted. On that day, people will have no refuge or escape from God's reckoning, and they will be unable to deny or dispute their deeds. The verse is emphasizing the importance of being responsive to God's guidance and commands in this life, as it will be too late to do so on the Day of Judgment.

translation: But if they turn away, We have not sent you as a guardian over them. Your duty is only to convey (the message). And indeed, when We give man a taste of Mercy from Us, he rejoices in it; but if an evil befalls them due to what their hands have sent forth, then indeed man is ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's role as a messenger and not a guardian over people. It emphasizes that his responsibility is to convey the message, not to ensure its acceptance or to be accountable for people's actions. The verse also touches upon human nature, noting that people tend to be ungrateful and forget the blessings they receive, attributing their successes to their own efforts rather than acknowledging the divine favor. It suggests that humans are prone to forgetfulness and ingratitude when they are in a state of comfort but tend to complain when faced with adversity, which is often a consequence of their own deeds.

translation: To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He creates what He wills. He gives to whom He wills female [children], and He gives to whom He wills males
interpretation: This verse highlights God's absolute sovereignty and authority over the heavens and the earth, emphasizing His power to create as He wills. It underscores the idea that God's granting of children, whether male or female, is entirely within His discretion, and that His decisions are not bound by human preferences or expectations. The verse serves as a reminder of God's omnipotence and the futility of human attempts to dictate or limit His actions. It invites believers to acknowledge and submit to God's will, recognizing that His wisdom and purpose are beyond human comprehension.

translation: or He couples them, males and females, and He makes whoever He wills barren. Indeed, He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's absolute sovereignty and power over creation, particularly in the context of human reproduction. It underscores that God is the one who decides the gender and number of children a person has, and that He can render someone sterile if He so wishes. The verse is emphasizing God's omnipotence and omniscience, suggesting that His decisions in such matters are not subject to human influence or understanding, but are rather part of His all-encompassing plan.

translation: And it is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil or that He sends a messenger to reveal, by His permission, what He wills. Indeed, He is Most High and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the various ways in which Allah communicates with humans, emphasizing that such communication is always initiated and controlled by Allah. It underscores the transcendence and wisdom of Allah, indicating that any form of divine revelation or communication is a manifestation of His sovereignty and wisdom, and is not something that can be claimed or achieved by human effort or desire alone.

translation: And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor [what was] faith, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed, you guide to a straight path
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin and purpose of the Qur'an, emphasizing that it is a source of guidance bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad by Allah. The phrase 'روحا من أمرنا' (a spirit from Our command) underscores the Qur'an's role as a life-giving and guiding force. The verse also stresses the Prophet's initial ignorance of the scripture and faith, underscoring that his knowledge and understanding were a result of divine revelation. The Qur'an is described as a 'نورا' (light) that guides those whom Allah wills among His servants, indicating its function as a source of illumination and direction. Ultimately, the verse affirms the Prophet's role in guiding people to the 'صراط مستقيم' (straight path), which is a metaphor for the righteous and virtuous path in life.

translation: The path of God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. Unquestionably, to God all matters are returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that all affairs and matters ultimately return to God, underscoring His sovereignty and control over everything in the heavens and the earth. It suggests that the path or way (sirāt) that is being referred to is aligned with God's will and dominion, implying a call to align one's life and actions with the divine order and purpose. It highlights the central Islamic belief in God's omnipotence and the inevitability of all things returning to Him for judgment or resolution.

translation: In the name of Allah, the most compassionate, the most merciful. Ha-Mim.
interpretation: This verse is part of the Muqatta'at, a set of disjointed letters that appear at the beginning of several surahs in the Qur'an. The meaning of these letters is not explicitly stated in the Qur'an, but one interpretation is that they serve as a challenge to the Arabs, who were known for their eloquence and mastery of the language, to produce a similar work. The use of these letters may be seen as a way of asserting the divine origin of the Qur'an, as they are not a coherent word or phrase, but rather a collection of letters that are nonetheless considered to be a meaningful and powerful part of the revelation.

translation: By the clear Book
interpretation: This verse signifies the clarity and manifest nature of the Qur'an as a source of guidance. The term 'al-Kitab al-Mubin' emphasizes that the Qur'an is a clear and unambiguous scripture that elucidates the truth, leaving no room for confusion or doubt regarding the message it conveys. It is a declaration that the Qur'an is a lucid and transparent guide for humanity, providing clear instructions and explanations necessary for righteous living and spiritual growth.

translation: Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic language so that people could understand its message and wisdom. The use of Arabic, a language familiar to the people at the time of its revelation, was intended to facilitate comprehension and reflection upon its teachings, thus enabling them to derive guidance and benefit from it.

translation: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted, full of wisdom.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance and origin of the Qur'an, stating that it is rooted in the 'Mother of the Book' (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), a divine record that is considered the source of all revelation. The description of the Qur'an as 'exalted, full of wisdom' underscores its elevated status and the profound wisdom it contains, suggesting that its teachings are not only of divine origin but also imbued with deep insight and understanding.

translation: Shall We then turn away from you the Reminder altogether because you are a people in excess?
interpretation: This verse suggests that the Quranic message is being withheld or ignored from a people who have transgressed beyond limits, implying a divine decision to turn away from those who have exceeded the boundaries of what is considered acceptable due to their excessive and sinful behavior.

translation: And how many a prophet We sent among the ancients
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity and consistency of God's message throughout history, emphasizing that the prophethood is not a new phenomenon but rather a recurring pattern where numerous prophets were sent to guide previous nations, establishing a precedent for the prophetic mission that continues up to the time of the Prophet Muhammad.

translation: And never did a prophet come to them but they used to ridicule him.
interpretation: This verse highlights a recurring pattern in human history where messengers and prophets sent by God to guide people towards righteousness are met with ridicule and scorn. It underscores the tendency of those who are heedless of God's message to mock and belittle the bearers of that message, indicating a deep-seated resistance to truth and a preference for their own ways over divine guidance.

translation: So We destroyed those who were stronger than they in power, and the example of the previous peoples has already passed.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the message of the prophets, indicating that if they persist in their disbelief and transgression, they will face a fate similar to or worse than that of previous nations who were destroyed for their sins. It underscores the principle that divine punishment is not limited by the strength or power of a people, and that those who are more powerful will face a more severe reckoning if they disobey God's commands.

translation: And if you were to ask them: 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' They would surely say: 'The All-Mighty, the All-Knowing created them.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the innate, intuitive knowledge that humans possess about the existence of a supreme creator who is both all-powerful ('al-'Aziz') and all-knowing ('al-'Alim'). Despite the polytheistic tendencies of the people being addressed, when questioned about the creation of the heavens and the earth, they unanimously attribute this grand act to a singular, omnipotent, and omniscient being. This acknowledgment underscores a deep-seated monotheistic instinct within human nature, suggesting that the complexity and majesty of the universe naturally lead people to recognize the existence of a singular, supremely powerful, and knowledgeable creator.

translation: Who has made for you the earth a bed and has made for you paths therein, that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's benevolence and providence in creating a habitable world for humanity. By making the earth a 'bed' or 'mهد' (mahd), it signifies a place of rest and comfort, indicating the earth's suitability for human life. The creation of 'paths' or 'سبلا' (subulan) within it not only facilitates physical movement and navigation but also metaphorically represents the guidance God provides for humans to navigate through life, morally and spiritually, thereby enabling them to find their way to righteousness and salvation.

translation: And Who sends down from the sky, rain in (due) measure, and We revive therewith a dead land (and you are resurrected in the same way)
interpretation: This verse highlights God's power to revive the dead, using the analogy of rain reviving a lifeless land. It suggests that just as God has the power to bring life to a barren earth through rainfall, He also has the power to resurrect humans after death. The phrase 'بقدر' (biqadar) implies that the rain is sent in a measured quantity, indicating a deliberate and controlled act of God, underscoring the idea that resurrection is a deliberate and controlled act of God as well.

translation: And He who created the pairs, all of them, and made for you from the ships and cattle on which you ride
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omnipotence and benevolence by mentioning His creation of pairs in nature and providing humans with various means of transportation, such as ships and animals, to facilitate their lives and travels. It underscores the idea that God's creation is not only diverse and complex but also purposeful, catering to human needs and enhancing their existence.

translation: That you may ride upon their backs, then remember the favour of your Lord when you are firmly settled thereon, and say: 'Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we were not able to do it by ourselves'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of acknowledging and being grateful for the blessings bestowed upon us by Allah. The act of riding a mount or a means of transportation is used as a metaphor to illustrate the relationship between humans and the favors they receive from Allah. The verse encourages believers to reflect on the blessings they have been given and to express their gratitude by acknowledging Allah's power and control over all things. It also underscores the idea that humans are not capable of harnessing or controlling these blessings on their own, but rather it is Allah who has made them subservient to human needs.

translation: And indeed, to our Lord we will return.
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability and certainty of returning to Allah, emphasizing the accountability and judgment that awaits individuals after their earthly life. It underscores the belief in the afterlife and the notion that one's deeds in this world will be reckoned with in the hereafter, serving as a reminder of the ultimate purpose and destination of human existence.

translation: And they assign to Him a portion from among His servants. Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave injustice of attributing offspring or partners to Allah, emphasizing that such actions stem from a profound ingratitude towards Allah's blessings and a clear manifestation of disbelief, as it distorts the true nature of Allah's uniqueness and sovereignty.

translation: Or has He taken daughters out of what He creates and assigned to you sons?
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the pagan Arabs for their discriminatory and unjust attribution of daughters to Allah while desiring sons for themselves, highlighting their biased and illogical beliefs regarding the gender of Allah's children.

translation: And when one of them is given good tidings of that which he attributes as an example to the Most Merciful, his face becomes dark, and he is distressed.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the intense displeasure and distress that some people experience when they are reminded of or associated with the concept of having a son or daughter for the Most Merciful (Allah), a notion that is contrary to Islamic belief and is considered a grave misattribution to Allah's nature. The reaction is so strong that it is likened to someone being given news that fills their face with darkness and causes them inward pain or grief, indicating a deep-seated aversion to the idea being discussed, likely referring to the attribution of offspring to Allah, a concept rejected in Islamic theology.

translation: Or he who is brought up in adornments (luxury) and is not clear in dispute (argument)
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the contradiction in the character of those who are being criticized. It is saying that the person who is brought up in luxury ('في الحلية') and is therefore presumably used to a life of ease and comfort, is unable to make their argument or point clear ('غير مبين') when it comes to disputes or debates ('في الخصام'). The implication is that such a person's upbringing has not equipped them with the skills or the clarity of thought needed to argue or reason effectively.

translation: And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse is a critique of the polytheistic beliefs prevalent among the pre-Islamic Arabs.
