The phrase 'ولتجزى كل نفس بما كسبت' (that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned) underscores the concept of individual accountability, where each person's actions have consequences in the hereafter. The assurance 'وهم لا يظلمون' (and they will not be wronged) signifies that God's judgment is fair and impartial, devoid of injustice, reinforcing the trust in divine justice.

translation: Have you seen he who has taken his god to be his desire, and God has led him astray knowingly, and sealed his hearing and his heart, and put a covering on his sight? Who then will guide him after God? Will you not then remember?
interpretation: This verse is a severe warning to those who follow their desires blindly, making their whims their guiding principle in life. It signifies that when an individual allows their desires to dictate their actions and decisions without being guided by divine guidance or moral principles, they risk being misled by God as a consequence of their own choices. The verse further elaborates on the state of such a person, indicating that God seals their heart and hearing, and veils their sight, rendering them incapable of perceiving the truth. The rhetorical question that follows underscores the futility of expecting guidance for such an individual from any source other than God, and serves as a reminder to reflect on one's actions and the consequences of being led astray by one's desires.

translation: And they say, "There is not but our worldly life; we die and live, and nothing destroys us except time." And they have of that no knowledge; they are not but assuming.
interpretation: This verse critiques those who believe that life is solely confined to the mortal realm, where people are born, live, and die, with no continuation or accountability beyond this worldly existence. They attribute the cycle of life and death to the passage of time, suggesting a natural, inevitable process devoid of any deeper, divine purpose or intervention. The verse underscores that such beliefs are not grounded in knowledge but are rather speculative, highlighting a lack of understanding or conviction about the true nature of existence and the hereafter.

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidence, their argument is not except that they say, "Bring [back] our forefathers, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the obstinacy and lack of genuine engagement with the truth on the part of those who were presented with clear signs and evidence from the Qur'an. Instead of examining the evidence or considering the message on its own merit, they demanded a proof that was impossible to fulfill - the resurrection of their ancestors. This reaction underscores their refusal to accept the truth based on rational or spiritual grounds, instead relying on a frivolous and unfeasible demand, indicating a deep-seated resistance to faith.

translation: Say, "Allah gives you life, then causes you to die; then He will assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt." But most of the people do not know. (Qur'an 45:26)
interpretation: This verse is emphasizing the inevitability and certainty of the afterlife and the Day of Judgment. It is pointing out that just as people experience a cycle of life and death in this world, they will also be resurrected and gathered on the Day of Judgment, a truth that is undeniable despite many people's lack of understanding or acknowledgment of it.

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And the day when the Hour will be established, on that day the losers will be those who have propagated falsehood.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sovereignty of Allah over the heavens and the earth, emphasizing that true power and dominion belong to Him alone. It then shifts focus to the Day of Judgment, warning that on that day, those who have propagated falsehood and injustice will suffer loss, underscoring the accountability of individuals for their deeds and the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood.

translation: And you will see every nation kneeling. Every nation will be called to its record. Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability of individuals and nations for their actions on the Day of Judgment. It signifies that every nation will be held responsible for its deeds and will be recompensed accordingly, emphasizing the concept of justice and moral responsibility in the hereafter.

translation: This is Our record that speaks about you with truth. Indeed, We were recording what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the idea that every action, whether big or small, is being recorded by Allah, and on the Day of Judgment, this record will be presented to the individual, serving as a truthful testimony of their deeds.

translation: So as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear attainment.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who have faith and perform good deeds will be granted entry into the mercy of their Lord, and this is considered an evident success. It highlights the direct correlation between faith, righteous actions, and the attainment of divine mercy, underscoring the idea that true triumph lies not in worldly achievements but in the spiritual success of being enveloped by God's mercy.

translation: And as for those who disbelieved, did My verses not used to be recited to you? But you were arrogant and were a people of criminals.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the attitude of the disbelievers towards the revelations of Allah. It suggests that their rejection of the faith was not due to a lack of understanding or awareness of the divine message, but rather because of their arrogance and criminal nature, implying that their disbelief was a result of a deliberate choice to reject the truth.

translation: And when it is said that the promise of Allah is true and that the Hour - there is no doubt about it, you say, 'We know not what is the Hour; we suppose but a conjecture and we are not convinced.'
interpretation: This verse critiques those who claim uncertainty about the inevitability and timing of the Day of Judgment despite being told that God's promise is true and that there is no doubt about its occurrence. It suggests that their skepticism stems not from a genuine lack of knowledge, but rather from a failure to have firm conviction, instead relying on speculation. The verse underscores the distinction between having faith based on certainty and merely holding beliefs based on conjecture.

translation: And the evil consequences of what they did will become apparent to them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept that the deeds people consider insignificant or laugh at will ultimately become the very things that bring about their downfall. It signifies that the consequences of one's actions will manifest in a way that is directly related to those actions, often in a manner that is ironic or serves as a form of divine retribution. The 'evil consequences of what they did' becoming apparent to them indicates a realization or reckoning where individuals understand that their past deeds, which they may have trivialized or mocked, have led to their current predicament. It serves as a warning against underestimating the impact of one's actions and the importance of taking one's deeds seriously, as they can culminate in severe repercussions.

translation: And it will be said, 'Today We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours, and your abode is the Fire, and you have not any helpers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the reciprocal nature of forgetfulness and its consequences. On the Day of Judgment, those who had forgotten or neglected the meeting with their Lord and the accountability of their deeds in the worldly life will themselves be forgotten by Allah, in the sense that they will be left to face the consequences of their actions without any support or intercession. The verse serves as a stern warning, emphasizing that neglect of one's spiritual obligations and the hereafter leads to being abandoned in the most critical moment, with Hell being their abode and devoid of any helpers or saviors.

translation: That is because you took the signs of God in mockery, and the life of the world deceived you. So today they will not be taken out from it, nor will they be granted respite.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of belittling the signs of God and being deceived by the fleeting allurements of worldly life. It suggests that those who have made a mockery of divine guidance and been distracted by the transient nature of earthly existence will be denied any opportunity to rectify their wrongdoings or seek pardon on the Day of Judgment, underscoring the irreversible nature of their spiritual downfall.

translation: So to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse signifies the acknowledgment of Allah's sovereignty over all creation, emphasizing His lordship over both the heavens and the earth, and everything within them, thereby affirming His absolute authority and dominion.

translation: And to Him belongs the Majesty in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's supreme authority and dominion over the entire universe, encompassing both the heavens and the earth. The attribute of 'al-Kibriyaa' (glory or majesty) signifies God's unmatched greatness and His rightful claim to be revered and worshiped. The verse further reinforces God's invincibility and wisdom through the descriptors 'al-'Aziz' (the Mighty) and 'al-Hakim' (the Wise). It underscores the idea that God's power is not only unchallenged but also guided by profound wisdom, suggesting that His actions and decrees are purposeful and just. This verse serves to instill in the believer a deep sense of awe and reverence for God, acknowledging His unparalleled sovereignty and the perfection of His governance over creation.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. Ha-Mim.
interpretation: This verse is one of the Muqatta'at, letters or combinations of letters that appear at the beginning of certain chapters in the Qur'an. The meaning of these letters is not explicitly stated in the Qur'an, but they are believed to be a form of divine code that holds spiritual significance. Some scholars interpret these letters as a way of grabbing the reader's attention, emphasizing the importance of the message that follows, or as a challenge to the Arabs who were masters of language and literature, to produce something similar. In the context of this particular surah, the letters 'Ha-Mim' may be seen as an introduction to a series of revelations that emphasize the oneness of God, the inevitability of judgment, and the importance of righteous conduct.

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the Quran is not a product of human ingenuity or Muhammad's own thoughts, but a divine revelation from Allah, who is both Almighty (Al-Aziz) and All-Wise (Al-Hakim). The attribute Al-Aziz underscores Allah's power and ability to enforce His will, while Al-Hakim highlights His wisdom in creating and governing the universe, as well as in guiding humanity through the Quran. It establishes the authority and authenticity of the Quran, setting the tone for its message and themes that follow.

translation: We have not created the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for a specified term. And those who disbelieve, from that which they are warned, are turning away.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purposeful and transient nature of creation. The universe, including the heavens and the earth, was not created idly or for amusement, but with a deliberate purpose and for a limited duration. The 'specified term' refers to the Day of Judgment, when all creation will be held accountable for their deeds. The disbelievers, however, remain heedless and unresponsive to the warnings they receive, indicating their rejection of the truth and their refusal to be guided by it.

translation: Say, "Have you considered that which you invoke besides Allah ? Show me what they have created of the earth; or did they have partnership in [creation of] the heavens? Bring me a scripture [revealed] before this or a [remaining] trace of knowledge, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who associate partners with Allah (idolaters and polytheists) to provide evidence for the legitimacy of their idols or deities. It questions their ability to demonstrate any tangible creation or contribution to the heavens and the earth by these deities. It further demands that they produce a scripture or inherited knowledge predating the Qur'an that supports their claims. The essence of this challenge is to underscore the lack of rational or scriptural basis for polytheistic beliefs, emphasizing the uniqueness of Allah's creative power and authority.

translation: And who is more astray than he who invokes besides Allah those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their invocation, are unaware.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of worshipping or calling upon entities other than Allah, emphasizing that such entities are incapable of responding to the supplications of their worshippers, not just in this life but until the Day of Judgment. It underscores the ignorance or obliviousness of these worshipped entities to the prayers directed towards them, illustrating the misguided nature of those who engage in such practices.

translation: And when people are gathered (on the Day of Judgment), they (the revered or followed ones) will be enemies to them (their followers), and they (the revered or followed ones) will be disbelievers in their worship.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reality that many people who are revered or followed by others will ultimately be revealed to be enemies of their followers on the Day of Judgment. It also underscores that those who were worshipped or revered will disown their worshippers, indicating that their worship was misguided and that they were, in fact, disbelievers in the true nature of their 'worship'.

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, "This is obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and obstinacy of those who reject the truth. Despite being presented with clear and convincing evidence (آياتنا بينات), they dismiss it as 'obvious magic' (سحر مبين), indicating their refusal to acknowledge the truth and their tendency to resort to baseless accusations to discredit it.

translation: Or do they say, "He has invented it?" Say, "If I have invented it, you have no power for me against Allah. He is most knowing of that in which you are involved. Sufficient is He as Witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." (Quran 46:8)
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusations of the disbelievers who claimed that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) fabricated the Quran. The verse challenges them to consider the consequences of their accusations and highlights Allah's omniscience and His role as a witness between the Prophet and his detractors, emphasizing that He is fully aware of their claims and is capable of dealing with them, while also underscoring His attributes of forgiveness and mercy.

translation: Say, 'I am not something novel among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's role as a messenger of Allah, indicating that he is not unique in his prophethood but is part of a long line of messengers sent by Allah. It also highlights his humility and submission to Allah's will, as he does not have knowledge of the future or the consequences of his message. The verse underscores that his duty is solely to convey the message revealed to him by Allah, serving as a clear warner to those who are heedless of Allah's commands.

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if it is from Allah and you disbelieved in it and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to [something] similar and believed while you were arrogant? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the inconsistency and arrogance of those who reject the message of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) despite its similarity to the messages revealed to previous prophets, as attested by a knowledgeable person from among the Children of Israel. It emphasizes that God's guidance is not given to those who are unjust and arrogant.

translation: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "If it were good, they would not have preceded us to it." And when they are not guided by it, they will say, "This is an old lie."
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological mechanism used by those who reject the truth. When they see others embracing a new belief or idea before they do, they dismiss its value by suggesting that if it were truly good or beneficial, they would have been the first to adopt it. Furthermore, when they fail to understand or find guidance in it, they resort to labeling it as an 'old lie', indicating their tendency to reject what they do not comprehend or what does not align with their preconceived notions, thereby showcasing their stubborn resistance to accepting new ideas or beliefs.

translation: And before it was the Book of Moses, a guide and a mercy. And this is a Book confirming, in an Arabic tongue, to warn those who have wronged, and as glad tidings to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity and validation of the divine message across different scriptures and prophets. It establishes the Quran as a confirmer of previous revelations, such as the Torah given to Moses, emphasizing its role in guiding those who have gone astray by warning the wrongdoers and giving glad tidings to the righteous. The use of 'Arabic tongue' underscores the clarity and accessibility of the Quran's message to its initial audience, facilitating understanding and adherence. It signifies that the Quran is not only a continuation but also a clarifier of the divine message, serving as a source of guidance and mercy.

translation: Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allah " and then remained on a right course - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and consistency in one's faith. It suggests that those who affirm their belief in God and then remain committed to their faith will be free from fear and sorrow, indicating a state of spiritual security and peace. The verse implies that the initial declaration of faith is not enough; it must be followed by a consistent and unwavering commitment to the principles of that faith.

translation: Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein as a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who are righteous and do good deeds will be rewarded with eternal paradise as a recompense for their actions, highlighting the justice and mercy of Allah in rewarding believers according to their deeds.

translation: And We have commanded humans to treat their parents with kindness. His mother bore him with difficulty and gave birth to him with difficulty, and his bearing and weaning took thirty months. Until when he reached maturity and reached forty years, he said, 'My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your blessings that You have blessed me and my parents with, and to do righteous deeds that please You, and make my offspring righteous for me. I have repented to You, and I am among those who submit.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of being grateful for the blessings one has received, particularly the blessing of parenthood and the struggles that parents, especially mothers, endure for their children. It encourages individuals to not only be thankful for their own blessings but also for those bestowed upon their parents. The verse suggests that true gratitude is demonstrated through righteous actions that please Allah, and by making a sincere effort to raise one's offspring in a righteous manner. The verse also underscores the significance of repentance and submission to Allah, indicating that a person's maturity and reflection on their life's journey should lead them to a deeper commitment to their faith and to living a virtuous life.

translation: Those are they from whom We shall accept the best of their deeds and pass over their evil deeds. (They shall be) among the Companions of the Garden, the promise of truth which they were promised.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's merciful and just nature. It indicates that those who are righteous will be rewarded not just for their good deeds, but will also be forgiven for their bad ones, thus entering paradise as a fulfillment of the promise made to them, underscoring the truthfulness of God's promise.

translation: And the one who says to his parents, 'Fie on you both! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth [from the earth] when generations have already passed before me?' And they both supplicate Allah [saying], 'Woe to you! Believe! Indeed, the promise of Allah is true.' But he says, 'This is not but legends of the former peoples.'
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the attitude of ingratitude and disobedience some people have towards their parents, despite their parents' supplications and pleas to Allah for their child's guidance. It serves as a warning against rejecting the truth and the promise of Allah, labeling it instead as mere tales of the ancients, thus showing a deep-seated disbelief and arrogance.

translation: Those upon whom the word (of judgment) has been fulfilled, among the nations that have passed away before them, from among the jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were the losers.
interpretation: This verse signifies that those who have been condemned by the divine decree are part of a larger pattern observed throughout history among previous nations, both among the jinn and humans. It underscores the recurring theme of divine judgment upon communities that have strayed, indicating a universal principle of accountability and consequence for one's actions across different civilizations and species, emphasizing the inevitability of loss for those who defy divine guidance.

translation: And for all are degrees from what they have done. And He will give them in full their deeds, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse highlights the justice of Allah, indicating that individuals will be rewarded or punished according to their deeds. The 'degrees' refer to the varying levels of reward or punishment that people will receive based on their actions. The verse reassures that Allah will fully compensate individuals for their deeds without any injustice, emphasizing the principle of accountability and fairness in the Hereafter.

translation: And the Day those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire [it will be said], 'You exhausted your pleasures during your worldly life and enjoyed them, so this Day you will be rewarded with the punishment of humiliation because you were arrogant in the land without right and because you were defiantly disobedient.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of a life lived in arrogance and disobedience. It suggests that the pleasures and comforts enjoyed by those who rejected faith in their worldly lives were not merely innocent indulgences, but were instead part of a broader pattern of behavior characterized by pride and transgression. The punishment they face is not just for their disbelief, but specifically for their arrogant and unrighteous conduct on earth, indicating that their misuse of the blessings they received contributed to their downfall.

translation: And mention the brother of 'Aad, when he warned his people in al-Ahqaaf - and there had already passed warners before him and after him - [saying], 'Do not worship except Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible day.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity and consistency of God's message across different prophets and nations, emphasizing that the core warning against polytheism and the call to worship one God has remained unchanged throughout history. It underscores the idea that previous nations were warned and punished for their disobedience, serving as a lesson for subsequent generations, and that the prophet Hud, sent to the people of 'Ad, was part of this unbroken chain of messengers tasked with delivering the same fundamental message.

translation: They said, 'Have you come to us to delude us from our gods? Then bring us what you promise us, if you are of the truthful.'
interpretation: The verse highlights the psychological and social dynamics at play when people are confronted with a message that challenges their long-held beliefs and practices. The demand to 'bring us what you promise' is not just a request for a miracle or a sign; it's a manifestation of their resistance to change and their attachment to their existing beliefs. The verse suggests that the challenge posed by the Prophet or the messenger is not just about proving the truth of their message but also about overcoming the entrenched convictions and traditions of the people they are addressing.

translation: He said, "The knowledge is only with Allah, and I convey to you that with which I was sent, but I see you [to be] a people behaving ignorantly."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of acknowledging the limitations of one's knowledge and the dangers of acting out of ignorance. The speaker is emphasizing that true knowledge rests with Allah, and they are conveying the message they were sent with, yet the people are behaving ignorantly, suggesting a critique of human behavior when it is not guided by knowledge or divine guidance.

translation: But when they saw it as a cloud advancing towards their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud that will bring us rain!" Nay, it is that (torment) which you were asking to be hastened - a wind wherein is a grievous torment!
interpretation: The verse highlights the theme of divine retribution and the consequences of disbelieving in the warnings given by prophets. It illustrates how the people of 'Ad misinterpreted a natural phenomenon (a cloud) as a blessing (rain) when, in fact, it was a harbinger of their destruction, sent as a punishment for their transgressions and their impatience for the very punishment they were warned about. This serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of skepticism and the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: destroying everything by the command of its Lord, so they became such that nothing was seen except their dwellings. Thus We recompense the guilty people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept that divine punishment is not arbitrary but is a consequence of the actions of those who transgress the laws and commandments set by Allah. The destruction caused by the calamity is a manifestation of Allah's justice, underscoring the principle that those who indulge in wrongdoing and persist in their transgressions will face the consequences of their actions. The verse serves as a warning to those who might be inclined to follow a similar path, emphasizing the importance of righteousness and adherence to divine guidance to avoid such a fate.

translation: And We had certainly established them in such a thing as We have not established you, and We had given them hearing, and sight, and hearts. But their hearing and sight and hearts availed them not from anything when they were rejecting the signs of Allah; and they were enveloped by what they used to deride.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the disbelievers of Mecca were given the same faculties as previous nations that were destroyed, yet these faculties did not benefit them because they rejected the signs of Allah. It serves as a warning to the disbelievers that having the ability to hear, see, and understand is not enough if one is not willing to believe and follow the guidance of Allah. The faculties given to humans are meant to be used to recognize and appreciate the signs of Allah, and their misuse or neglect leads to their downfall.

translation: And We have already destroyed the towns around you and varied the signs, so that they might return.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth, indicating that the destruction of surrounding communities is a consequence of their disobedience, and the varied presentation of signs and revelations is intended to prompt them to reflect and return to the right path.

translation: So why did those they took as gods besides Allah as a means of drawing near [to Him] not help them? Rather, they had strayed from them. And that was their fabrication, and what they were inventing.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the futility of idol worship and the falsehood of the claims made by the polytheists. It is saying that the idols and false gods that people worshipped did not provide them with any help or support. Instead, these idols have actually become lost to them, meaning they are no longer visible or effective. The verse is pointing out that the polytheists' claims about their idols being capable of interceding on their behalf or providing them with benefits are nothing but fabrications and lies.

translation: And [mention] when We sent to you a group of the jinn to listen to the Qur'an. And when they were in its presence, they said, "Listen quietly." And when it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of the jinn as witnesses to the Quran and as warners to their own people. It indicates that the jinn were not only able to listen to the Quran but were also moved to convey its message to others, demonstrating a level of understanding and responsibility. The verse suggests a parallel between the jinn and humans in terms of being addressed by the divine message and being tasked with conveying it to their respective communities. It underscores the universal nature of the Quran's message, intended not just for humans but also for other sentient beings like the jinn.

translation: They said, "O our people, indeed we have heard a scripture revealed after Moses confirming what was before it; it guides to the truth and to a straight path."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of continuity and verification in the chain of divine revelation. The people mentioned here are affirming that they have received a new scripture that follows the legacy of Moses and validates the previous messages, serving as a guide to truth and a straight path, indicating that the new revelation is not a departure from the past but a continuation and confirmation of the divine guidance that has been consistently provided.

translation: O our people, respond to God's caller and believe in Him; He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of responding to the call of the prophets and messengers who invite people to believe in God. It highlights the dual benefits of faith: the forgiveness of sins, which is a spiritual benefit, and protection from a painful punishment, which is a consequence of disbelief. The verse is urging the people to take a decisive step towards faith, promising them that it will not only bring them spiritual relief but also safeguard them against the severe consequences of rejecting God's message.

translation: And whoever does not respond to God's caller, then he is not a miracle worker on earth, and he does not have, besides Him, any guardians. Those are in clear error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that those who refuse to respond to God's call, i.e., to believe and obey Him, are not capable of escaping or thwarting God's plan on earth. Moreover, they will not have any protectors or helpers other than God. The verse concludes by stating that such individuals are in clear error, indicating that their refusal to heed God's call leads them astray from the right path.

translation: Have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth and was not tired by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting God's omnipotence by referencing His creation of the heavens and the earth, emphasizing that if He was capable of creating such vast and complex entities without being exhausted, then reviving the dead is certainly within His power, underscoring the concept of resurrection and the afterlife in Islamic belief.

translation: And the Day those who disbelieved are presented before the Fire [it will be said], 'Is this not the truth?' They will say, 'Yes, by our Lord.' He will say, 'Then taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of accountability for one's actions on the Day of Judgment. The disbelievers, who rejected the truth in their worldly lives, will be confronted with the reality of Hellfire, and their acknowledgment of its truth will come too late to alter their fate. Their affirmation, 'Yes, by our Lord,' underscores the certainty and inescapability of the judgment, as they are forced to acknowledge the truth they previously denied. The verse serves as a stern warning to those who reject faith, emphasizing that their disbelief will lead to a dire consequence, and that the punishment is a direct result of their actions.

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad], as the messengers of determination were patient and do not be impatient for them. It will be - on the Day they see that which they are promised - as though they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of a day. [This is] sufficient notice. And who will be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?
interpretation: This verse is urging the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to be patient in the face of adversity, just as the most resolute and determined of the previous prophets were. It is cautioning him against being hasty in his expectations of punishment or relief for his people. The verse is also conveying that the Day of Judgment will arrive suddenly, and when it does, people will feel as though they had only lingered in this world for a brief moment. The ultimate message is that only those who are rebellious and disobedient to God's command will face destruction, implying that the righteous will be spared.

translation: In the name of God, the most Compassionate, the most Merciful. Those who disbelieve and hinder others from the path of God, He will render their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of not just disbelieving in God, but also actively preventing others from following the path of righteousness. It suggests that such actions not only condemn the individuals themselves but also nullify the value of their good deeds, implying a severe spiritual and moral consequence for those who obstruct others' spiritual journeys.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds and believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad - and it is the truth from their Lord - He will remove from them their misdeeds and amend their condition
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and righteous deeds, emphasizing that those who believe and do good works, and have faith in the revelation sent down to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as being the truth from their Lord, will have their bad deeds expiated and their affairs rectified. It suggests that true faith, coupled with righteous action and acceptance of the Prophet's message, leads to spiritual purification and a life of integrity and righteousness.

translation: That is because those who disbelieved followed falsehood and those who believed followed the truth from their Lord. Thus does Allah present to the people their examples.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between those who reject faith and those who embrace it, illustrating that the former follow falsehood while the latter adhere to the truth emanating from their Lord. It underscores God's method of elucidating parables to humanity, drawing a clear distinction between truth and falsehood, and guiding people towards understanding the consequences of their choices. Essentially, it serves as a reminder that the divergence in human paths is rooted in the fundamental decision to follow either truth or falsehood, with God providing examples to help people discern and make informed choices.

translation: So when you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds, and either [confer] favor afterwards or ransom [them] until the war lays down its burdens. That [is the command]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them [Himself], but [He ordered armed struggle] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah - never will He waste their deeds.
interpretation: This verse outlines the rules of engagement and treatment of prisoners during warfare. It suggests that the primary objective is to establish peace and end the conflict. The verse also highlights God's ability to exact revenge without human agency, but instead, He chooses to test believers through their interactions with others. The latter part of the verse reassures that those who are martyred in the cause of God will not have their deeds rendered futile.

translation: He will guide them and put their affairs into a good condition.
interpretation: This verse indicates that God will guide those who believe and do good deeds to the straight path and will rectify their affairs, bringing them out of darkness into light, and making their hearts tranquil and their lives righteous.

translation: And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah not only promises to admit believers into Paradise but also personally guides them to it, making their entry a matter of both divine grace and personal recognition of a place they have been made familiar with, underscoring the intimate relationship between the divine and the believer in the afterlife.

translation: O you who have believed, if you support God, He will support you and stabilize your feet.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reciprocal nature of support between believers and God. It suggests that when believers stand up for God's cause, uphold His religion, and strive for His sake, God will reciprocate by granting them victory over their adversaries and stabilizing their resolve in the face of challenges, thereby ensuring their steadfastness and triumph.

translation: And those who disbelieve, then wretchedness to them and He will cause their deeds to be lost
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who reject faith, indicating that their disbelief will lead to their downfall and the futility of their deeds. The term 'تعسا' (Ta'isa) is an expression of severe condemnation, implying a state of being utterly wretched or miserable. The phrase 'وأضل أعمالهم' (wa adalla a'malahum) suggests that their actions, despite possibly seeming righteous or purposeful to them, are rendered meaningless and lost due to their lack of faith. It underscores the Islamic belief that faith is a crucial determinant of the value and ultimate outcome of one's actions, implying that without it, even the most seemingly noble deeds are devoid of true purpose or reward in the eyes of God.

translation: That is because they hated what Allah revealed, so He rendered their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting or disliking the guidance and revelation sent by Allah. It signifies that those who harbor aversion towards Allah's revelations will have their deeds rendered null and void, devoid of any spiritual benefit or reward, as their rejection taints their actions with insincerity and misguidance.

translation: Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed them utterly. And for the disbelievers there are similar (punishments).
interpretation: This verse is urging people to reflect on the fate of previous nations that were destroyed by Allah due to their disbelief and disobedience. It implies that those who continue on the path of disbelief will face similar consequences, serving as a warning to heed the lessons from history and avoid a similar downfall.

translation: That is because Allah is the Protector of those who believe, and because the disbelievers have no protector.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the believers and the disbelievers in terms of their ultimate support and protection. The believers have Allah as their guardian and protector (Mawla), indicating that they are under His care and guidance. On the other hand, the disbelievers lack such divine support and protection, signifying their isolation and vulnerability. This distinction underscores the consequences of faith and disbelief, emphasizing that true security and assistance come from Allah's guardianship, which is reserved for those who believe.

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to Gardens beneath which rivers flow. But those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire will be their abode.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the ultimate destinations of the righteous and the unrighteous. The believers who perform good deeds are promised an eternal abode in Gardens where rivers flow beneath them, symbolizing a life of serenity, beauty, and divine reward. On the other hand, those who reject faith are allowed to enjoy the fleeting pleasures of this world, living a life akin to that of beasts, devoid of purpose or spiritual nourishment, and ultimately, they are destined for the Fire, which serves as their final resting place. The comparison to cattle underscores a life driven solely by base instincts, lacking the higher faculties that distinguish humans, such as reason and spiritual aspiration.

translation: And how many a city which was stronger in power than your city (Makkah) that hath driven you out? We have destroyed them, so no helper was there for them.
interpretation: This verse serves as a consolation to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) during his exile from Makkah, reminding him that the Quraysh who persecuted him were not invincible, as many other cities and civilizations that were more powerful than Makkah had been destroyed by Allah for their wrongdoings, implying that the Prophet and his followers would ultimately be vindicated.

translation: Is he who is on clear evidence from his Lord like one to whom the evil of his work is made fair-seeming and they follow their lusts?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between those who are guided by clear evidence from their Lord and those who are misled by their own desires and the embellishment of their evil deeds. It underscores the idea that true guidance comes from knowledge and understanding derived from divine sources, as opposed to being swayed by personal whims or the deceptive allure of wrongdoing. The former represents individuals who are enlightened and grounded in their faith, while the latter symbolizes those who are lost in their own ego and desires, illustrating a fundamental dichotomy between righteousness and misguidance.

translation: The example of the Paradise, which the righteous are promised; there are rivers of water unaltered, rivers of milk the taste of which never changes, rivers of wine delicious to those who drink, and rivers of honey pure and clear. In it they will have all kinds of fruits and forgiveness from their Lord. Is this like being forever in the Fire and being given boiling water to drink so that it cuts up their intestines?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the stark contrast between the reward of the righteous and the punishment of the wicked. The description of Paradise is used to emphasize the unimaginable bliss and delight that awaits those who are pious and God-fearing, while the description of Hell serves as a warning of the terrible fate that awaits those who are disobedient and unrepentant. The verse is not just a comparison between two places, but a comparison between two lifestyles and their consequences, emphasizing that the life of piety and obedience is incomparably better than a life of disobedience and sin.

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, [O Muhammad], until when they depart from you, they say to those who were given knowledge, "What has he said just now?" Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has sealed and who have followed their own desires.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of certain individuals who pretend to be interested in the Prophet's message but lack genuine understanding or commitment. Their inquiry to knowledgeable individuals about the Prophet's words after leaving his presence indicates their superficial engagement and lack of true concern for the message. The verse suggests that their hearts have been sealed by Allah due to their persistence in following their own desires, implying a divine judgment on their spiritual state as a consequence of their own actions and attitudes.

translation: And those who are guided - it increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reciprocal relationship between an individual's actions and God's guidance. It suggests that those who are already on the path of righteousness will receive further guidance from God, and this additional guidance will enable them to cultivate greater piety and righteousness. In essence, it underscores the idea that the more one strives to follow the right path, the more God facilitates their journey by providing them with increased insight and moral fortitude.

translation: Are they waiting for the Hour to come upon them suddenly? But its signs have already come. So what good will their reminder be to them when it has come upon them?
interpretation: The verse is cautioning against the denial of the Hour of Judgment, suggesting that people are waiting for it to arrive suddenly, but in reality, its signs have already appeared. The phrase 'فأنى لهم إذا جاءتهم ذكراهم' indicates that when the Hour actually arrives, it will be too late for people to take heed or benefit from their remembrance or warning, implying a sense of regret and too late realization of the truth.

translation: Know, therefore, that there is no deity save God, and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. God knows your movements and your resting places.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having correct knowledge and belief in the oneness of God (Tawhid), while also acknowledging the need for seeking forgiveness for one's own sins and those of the believing community. It highlights that God is all-knowing and aware of the actions and ultimate resting places of all individuals, serving as a reminder to live righteously and be mindful of one's deeds.

translation: And those who have believed say, "Why has a surah not been revealed?" But when a precise surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is hypocrisy looking at you with a look of one overcome by death. And woe to them"
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological state of hypocrites during the early days of Islam when the Muslims were being asked to fight. When a clear and decisive verse or surah was revealed that mentioned fighting, the hypocrites, who were pretending to be Muslims but had doubts and fears in their hearts, would look at the Prophet with a gaze similar to that of someone who is about to die, indicating their fear and anxiety about the prospect of fighting. The verse is criticizing their lack of courage and faith, suggesting that it would have been better for them to face the reality of their fears rather than pretending to be something they were not.

translation: Obedience and good words. And when the matter is decided, if they were true to Allah, it would be better for them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and truthfulness in one's actions and words, particularly when faced with a decision or a challenge. It suggests that even if one is obedient and speaks good words, if they are not genuine in their commitment to Allah, they will not reap the benefits of their actions. The verse implies that true faith and conviction are essential for one's actions to be meaningful and effective.

translation: So, would you, if you were given authority, cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship?
interpretation: This verse is warning against the consequences of turning away from the guidance and teachings of Allah. It suggests that if those who are being warned were to gain power, they would likely engage in corrupt practices and sever their familial ties, highlighting the destructive nature of ignoring divine guidance.

translation: Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He deafened them and blinded their vision.
interpretation: This verse implies that those who have been cursed by Allah are not only punished but also spiritually incapacitated, unable to hear the truth or see the right path, highlighting the consequences of willful disobedience and rejection of divine guidance.

translation: Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon [their] hearts?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that criticizes those who fail to understand and reflect on the Quran. It implies that the reason for their lack of understanding is not the complexity of the Quran, but rather the fact that their hearts are sealed, suggesting that they are not open to guidance and truth due to their own spiritual condition.

translation: Indeed, those who revert to disbelief after guidance has become clear to them - Satan has made [their misdeeds] appealing to them and has given them false hope.
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the role of Satan in tempting individuals who have previously been guided towards the right path. It suggests that Satan's influence can lead people astray, making them revert to their previous state of misguidance after they had gained clarity on the correct path. The term 'سول لهم' (sawwalahu lahum) implies that Satan made their wrong actions appealing to them, while 'وأملى لهم' (wa amlā lahum) indicates that he gave them a false sense of hope or respite, thereby delaying their reckoning or punishment. This interpretation underscores the psychological and moral manipulation that Satan is believed to exert over those who are susceptible to his influence, leading them away from the guidance they once understood.

translation: That is because they said to those who disliked what Allah revealed, "We will obey you in part of the matter." And Allah knows their secrets.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of certain individuals who claimed to align themselves with those who disliked what Allah had revealed, indicating a willingness to compromise on certain matters. It underscores Allah's all-encompassing knowledge, suggesting that He is aware of their hidden intentions and secrets, thus emphasizing the futility of attempting to conceal one's true allegiances or intentions from Him.

translation: How then, when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?
interpretation: This verse is a warning to those who are hostile to the faith and persecute its adherents. It signifies the dire fate that awaits such individuals at the moment of their death, when the angels of death come to take their souls. The act of the angels striking their faces and backs is symbolic of the severe punishment and humiliation they will suffer. It highlights the Quranic theme of divine justice, where those who turn away from the path of righteousness and indulge in wrongdoing will face a painful reckoning. The verse serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of one's actions in this life and the accountability that awaits in the hereafter.

translation: That is because they followed what angered God and hated what pleased Him, so He rendered their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of deliberately pursuing actions that are displeasing to God while rejecting those that are pleasing to Him. It suggests that such a choice leads to the nullification of one's efforts and deeds, implying a spiritual and moral bankruptcy. The underlying message is that one's actions have consequences in the sight of God, and aligning with God's will is crucial for the validity and worth of one's deeds.

translation: Do those in whose hearts is disease think that God will never expose their malice?
interpretation: This verse is highlighting the misconception of those who harbor malice or hypocrisy in their hearts, believing that God will not expose their inner hatred or resentment. It suggests that God is aware of their inner state and will ultimately reveal their true feelings, implying a warning to those who think they can conceal their malice.

translation: And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would know them by their mark; but you will surely know them by the tone of [their] speech. And Allah knows your deeds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ability of Allah to reveal the true nature of individuals, and how believers can discern hypocrisy or hidden intentions through subtle cues in speech and behavior, while also emphasizing Allah's all-encompassing knowledge of human actions.

translation: And We will surely test you until We make evident those among you who strive and those who are patient, and We will test your circumstances.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the true test of faith lies not in the absence of challenges, but in how believers respond to them. It indicates that Allah's purpose in subjecting believers to trials is to discern the sincerity and strength of their commitment, distinguishing between those who actively strive in His cause and those who remain steadfast under adversity. The testing of 'your circumstances' or 'your news' (أخباركم) suggests that Allah is aware of the internal and external conditions of believers, and these trials serve to reveal their true character and faith to themselves and others.

translation: Those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them - never will they harm Allah at all, and He will render worthless their deeds.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the actions of those who reject faith, obstruct others from the path of Allah, and oppose the Messenger after being clearly guided, will not cause any harm to Allah. Instead, their deeds will be rendered null and void, emphasizing the futility of opposing the divine guidance and the ultimate accountability of human actions.

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds.
interpretation: This verse is warning the believers that their good deeds will be rendered null and void if they disobey Allah and His Messenger. It emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, suggesting that without it, even the most righteous actions lose their value and become futile.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the path of Allah, then die while they are disbelievers - never will Allah forgive them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequence of rejecting faith and actively working against the path of God. It indicates that those who not only disbelieve but also obstruct others from following God's guidance, and persist in their disbelief until death, will not receive God's forgiveness. The verse underscores the gravity of leading others astray and the importance of remaining on the path of righteousness until the end of one's life.

translation: So do not weaken and call for peace while you are the higher ones and Allah is with you and will never deprive you of [the reward of] your deeds.
interpretation: This verse is urging the believers not to lose heart or invite their enemies to a peaceful resolution when they are in a position of superiority. It reassures them that God is on their side and that He will not deprive them of the reward of their deeds, implying that their efforts and sacrifices in the cause of righteousness will be duly acknowledged and compensated.

translation: The life of this world is but play and amusement. And if you believe and fear God, He will give you your rewards and will not ask of you your riches.
interpretation: This verse highlights the true purpose of worldly life and the attitude believers should have towards it. It suggests that the life of this world is fleeting and is characterized by play and amusement, implying that it is not the ultimate reality. The verse then shifts focus to the believers, stating that if they have faith and are mindful of God (through righteous deeds and avoidance of wrongdoing), they will be rewarded with their due recompense. Furthermore, it reassures them that their reward is not contingent upon their material wealth, indicating that God does not require their riches. Instead, the emphasis is on their faith and piety as the criteria for receiving their reward. This interpretation underscores the Islamic principle that true value lies not in material possessions but in one's faith and actions. It encourages believers to prioritize their spiritual growth and moral conduct, promising them a reward that is not dependent on their economic status.

translation: If He asks you for it and presses you, you become stingy, and it exposes your ill-feeling
interpretation: This verse is cautioning against the dangers of being asked to spend in charity or for a good cause, and then being stingy or miserly. It suggests that if people are asked to give generously, their reluctance to do so will reveal the deep-seated grudges or resentments they harbor, implying that their unwillingness to give is not just about being frugal but is rooted in a deeper issue of not wanting to let go of their possessions or resources, possibly due to a lack of trust or faith in the cause or the people asking.

translation: Now, you are those who are called upon to spend in the cause of Allah; yet among you are those who are stingy. And whoever is stingy is stingy against his own self. And Allah is the Free of need, while you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be like you.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the Muslim community that if they fail to live up to their obligations of spending in the cause of Allah, they will be replaced by another people who are more willing to do so. The verse highlights the idea that one's actions, including acts of charity, ultimately benefit or harm oneself, and that Allah is not in need of their charity, but rather it is they who are in need of the blessings and rewards that come from it. The replacement mentioned in the verse implies a loss of privilege and responsibility, suggesting that the Muslims of the time were being given a unique opportunity to demonstrate their commitment to their faith, and that failure to do so would result in others being given the chance to take their place.

translation: Indeed, We have granted you, [O Muhammad], a clear conquest.
interpretation: This verse signifies a declaration of a major victory or triumph granted by Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), likely referring to the Treaty of Hudaybiyah or the conquest of Mecca, which marked a significant turning point in the history of Islam, indicating a clear and manifest success that would pave the way for further advancements and the spread of the faith.

translation: That Allah may forgive for you what preceded of your sin and what will follow and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path
interpretation: This verse signifies the comprehensive nature of God's forgiveness and guidance bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad. It indicates that the Prophet is not only pardoned for his past and future errors, but is also the recipient of the completion of God's blessings and is guided on the straight path. The 'straight path' refers to the path of righteousness and true faith, indicating that the Prophet is firmly established on the correct and unswerving path ordained by God. The verse underscores the Prophet's special status and the perfection of his spiritual state, serving as a reassurance of his prophetic mission and the divine support he receives.

translation: And Allah will help you with a mighty victory
interpretation: This verse signifies that the help or victory that Allah grants is not just any victory, but one that is accompanied by honor, power, and might. It implies that when Allah supports or aids someone, it is not a feeble or weak support, but rather a strong and mighty one that is associated with dignity and prestige. The term 'عزيزا' (Aziza) emphasizes the idea that Allah's help is not only effective but also glorifies and strengthens the one who receives it, making them or their cause respected and formidable.

translation: It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers that they would increase in faith along with their [present] faith. And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of divine tranquility in reinforcing faith. The 'sakina' (tranquility or calm) that Allah sends down into the hearts of believers serves to strengthen and deepen their conviction, illustrating the dynamic and growing nature of faith. It underscores the idea that faith is not static but can be augmented through spiritual reassurance. The reference to 'the soldiers of the heavens and the earth' belonging to Allah emphasizes His omnipotence and control over all creation, reinforcing the notion that the reinforcement of faith is part of a broader divine plan. The characterization of Allah as 'Knowing' and 'Wise' suggests that the distribution of 'sakina' and the management of the universe are guided by profound knowledge and wisdom, implying a purposeful and orderly unfolding of events.

translation: That He may admit the believing men and the believing women to Gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide, and that He may absolve them of their evil deeds - and that is, in the sight of Allah, a mighty triumph.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate goal of the believers' journey, which is to attain eternal bliss in the Gardens of Paradise, where they will be free from the burdens of their past wrongdoings. The verse signifies that the success of believers is not just about achieving a certain status, but about being purified from their past mistakes and being rewarded with an eternal life of bliss, which is considered a great triumph in the sight of God.

translation: And He will punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and the men and women who associate others with Allah in His divinity - those who hold an evil opinion about Allah. For them is an evil turn of fortune, and Allah is angry with them and has cursed them, and has prepared for them Hell - a woeful destination.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of harboring negative thoughts about Allah, indicating that such an attitude is a manifestation of a deeper spiritual issue, such as hypocrisy or polytheism. It suggests that one's beliefs and attitudes towards Allah have a direct impact on their spiritual fate, emphasizing the importance of maintaining a positive and sincere relationship with Allah.

translation: And to Allah belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omnipotence and supreme authority over all creation, indicating that He has at His disposal countless forces and beings in both the heavens and the earth that can be mobilized to achieve His purposes, and underscores that His power is coupled with wisdom, suggesting that His actions are always purposeful and just.

translation: Indeed, We have sent you [O Muhammad] as a witness and a bearer of good tidings and a warner.
interpretation: This verse signifies the multifaceted role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in Islam. The term 'شاهدا' (witness) implies that he is a witness to the actions and deeds of his followers and the people around him, holding him accountable for conveying the message of Allah truthfully. 'مبشرا' (bearer of good tidings) indicates that he brings glad news to those who believe and do good deeds, promising them reward and paradise. 'ونذيرا' (warner) signifies that he warns those who disbelieve or commit evil acts, cautioning them of the consequences of their actions and the punishment that awaits them. This verse underscores the Prophet's role as a guide who not only conveys the message but also serves as a witness to the faith and actions of his community, providing both encouragement for the righteous and warning for those who stray.

translation: That you believe in Allah and His Messenger and honour him and reverence Him and glorify Him morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of having faith in Allah and His Messenger, and it outlines several key actions that believers should take to demonstrate their devotion. 'Ta'uzuruhu' (تعزروه) means to support or assist, implying that believers should stand by the Prophet and his teachings. 'Tuwakkiruhu' (توقروه) signifies reverence or veneration, indicating that believers should hold the Prophet in high esteem. 'Tusabbihuhu bukratan wa asilan' (تسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا) means to glorify Allah in the morning and the evening, highlighting the importance of regular remembrance and glorification of Allah. Together, these actions underscore a comprehensive approach to faith that includes belief, support for the Prophet, reverence for him, and regular worship and glorification of Allah.

translation: Those who pledge allegiance to you (Prophet Muhammad) are, in fact, pledging allegiance to God; God's hand is over their hands. So, whoever breaks this pledge, does so to his own detriment. And whoever fulfills the covenant he has made with God, He will grant him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the significance of the pledge of allegiance given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), indicating that it is, in essence, a pledge to God Himself. It emphasizes that any breach of this pledge is a betrayal of one's own soul, as it is a covenant made with God. Conversely, fulfilling this covenant will be rewarded with a great recompense, underscoring the importance of loyalty and faithfulness in one's commitments, especially those made in the name of faith.

translation: The deserters among the bedouins will say, 'Our wealth and our families occupied us, so ask forgiveness for us.' They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say, 'Who then has any power at all [to intervene] on your behalf with Allah, if His will is to do you harm or to bring you benefit?' Nay, but Allah is aware of what you do.
interpretation: The verse is highlighting the hypocrisy of the Bedouins who stayed behind from joining the Prophet (peace be upon him) in his battles, claiming that their wealth and families kept them occupied. The verse is pointing out that their words are not genuine, and that they are not sincere in their request for forgiveness. It is emphasizing that ultimately, it is Allah who has control over their fate, and that no one can intercede on their behalf if He decides to cause them harm or withhold benefit from them. The verse is also underscoring Allah's all-encompassing knowledge of their actions, implying that their attempts to deceive are futile.

translation: Nay, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and that was made fair-seeming to your hearts, and you did conceive an evil thought, and you were a people ruined.
interpretation: This verse is criticizing the hypocrites who doubted the return of the Prophet and the believers to their families after going out for an expedition. It highlights their negative thinking and lack of faith, suggesting that they were a people destined for destruction due to their corrupt nature. The verse implies that their pessimistic outlook and disbelief in the Prophet's return were a reflection of their inner corruption and lack of trust in God's promise to protect the believers.

translation: And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger, then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the fundamental beliefs of Islam, namely, the oneness of God (Allah) and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). It underscores the severe consequence of such rejection, which is eternal damnation in Hellfire, symbolized here as 'a Blaze' (Saeer). The verse implies that faith in Allah and His Messenger is not merely a matter of personal preference but a critical determinant of one's ultimate fate in the hereafter. The use of 'We have prepared' signifies the inevitability and certainty of this fate for those who disbelieve, emphasizing divine justice and the seriousness with which faith is regarded in Islam.

translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sovereignty of Allah over the heavens and the earth, emphasizing His absolute authority to forgive or punish whomever He wills. It underscores the concept that Allah's mercy and forgiveness are not limited, as He is described as being 'Ghafur' (Forgiving) and 'Rahim' (Merciful). The verse suggests that Allah's decisions regarding forgiveness or punishment are based on His wisdom and justice, which may not be fully comprehensible to humans. It invites believers to trust in Allah's justice and mercy, encouraging a sense of humility and submission to His will.

translation: Those who lagged behind will say, when you set forth to take the spoils, "Let us follow you." They want to change the words of Allah. Say, "You shall not follow us. Thus Allah has said before." Then they will say, "Nay, you envy us." Nay, but they understand not, except a little.
interpretation: The verse critiques the hypocrites who, after the Prophet and the believers have gone out to gain spoils of war, wish to follow them, indicating their desire to change the decree of Allah regarding the distribution of war booty. The response to their request is that they will not be allowed to follow, as Allah has already decreed that only those who were present at the battle would receive the spoils. The hypocrites' excuse is dismissed as they are accused of not understanding the situation properly, suggesting their lack of true faith and comprehension.

translation: Tell those who remained behind of the bedouins, "You will be called to [face] a people of great military might; you will fight them, or they will submit. Then if you obey, Allah will give you a good reward; but if you turn away as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse is addressing the Bedouins who excused themselves from participating in the battle against the powerful tribe, warning them that they will soon be called upon to fight against an even more formidable enemy. It emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah's command and the consequences of disobedience, highlighting that those who comply will be rewarded, while those who turn away will face severe punishment, referencing their past behavior as a precedent for the consequences of their future actions.

translation: There is not upon the blind any guilt or upon the lame any guilt or upon the ill any guilt [for remaining behind]. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever turns away - He will punish him with a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the obligations and prohibitions in Islam are considerate of the individual's physical and health condition. It highlights that those who are blind, lame, or ill are not held accountable for actions they are incapable of performing due to their condition. The verse then shifts to a broader message, encouraging obedience to God and His Messenger, promising that those who comply will be rewarded with Paradise. Conversely, it warns that those who turn away will face a painful punishment. The underlying theme is one of mercy and justice, balancing the call to obedience with an acknowledgment of human limitations, while also underscoring the importance of faith and compliance with divine guidance.

translation: Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you, [O Prophet], under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down serenity upon them and rewarded them with a near conquest.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and the knowledge of Allah about the intentions of His servants. The event being referred to is the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, where the companions pledged their allegiance to the Prophet under a tree. The verse shows that Allah was pleased with their sincerity and loyalty, and as a result, He bestowed upon them tranquility and a near victory, which was a fulfillment of their aspirations and a demonstration of Allah's favor upon them.

translation: And much booty they will take. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse suggests that the believers will be granted victory and abundant spoils of war as a result of their faith and trust in Allah, and that Allah's power and wisdom are evident in His dispensation of these blessings.

translation: Allah has promised you many spoils that you will take, then hastened for you this [victory] and withheld the hands of people from you - that it may be a sign for the believers and to guide you to a straight path
interpretation: This verse signifies that the spoils of war are a divine promise to the believers, and the immediate victory granted to them is a manifestation of God's favor and a test of their faith. The phrase 'and to restrain the hands of people against you' suggests that God's intervention not only brings victory but also ensures the safety and security of the believers by deterring their enemies. The ultimate purpose is to guide the believers on the straight path, indicating that the true objective of these worldly victories is spiritual guidance and righteousness.

translation: And [there is] another [favor] that you were not able to achieve, certainly Allah has encompassed it, and Allah is ever, over all things, competent
interpretation: This verse highlights God's omnipotence and all-encompassing knowledge. It suggests that there are things beyond human capability or understanding, but God is fully aware of them and has the power to accomplish them. It emphasizes the limitless nature of God's power and knowledge, reassuring believers of His ability to fulfill His promises and achieve what may seem impossible to humans.

translation: And if those who disbelieve fight you, they would certainly turn their backs, then they would not find a protector nor a helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of the disbelievers' efforts against the believers, indicating that were they to engage in combat, they would inevitably retreat in defeat, finding themselves bereft of any support or aid, underscoring the ultimate triumph of faith over disbelief.

translation: Such has been the practice (approved) of God already in the past: no change wilt thou find in the practice (approved) of God
interpretation: This verse highlights the unchanging nature of God's laws and patterns that have been established since the past. It implies that the consequences of human actions, whether good or bad, will remain consistent with God's established norms, and that these norms are not subject to alteration. It serves as a warning and a reminder of the inevitability of God's decree, encouraging reflection on past events and their outcomes as a guide to understanding the present and future.

translation: And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah after He had given you victory over them. And ever is Allah , of what you do, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights God's intervention in restraining both the Muslims and their enemies from violence against each other in the valley of Makkah, demonstrating His power and control over events. It signifies a moment of divine restraint and peace, underscoring the idea that even in the midst of conflict, God's will can bring about a cessation of hostilities, and that He is ever watchful over the actions of His servants.

translation: Those who disbelieved and prevented you from al-Masjid al-Haram and the offering (of sacrificial animals) being withheld from reaching its destination. And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know - that you would trample them and there would befall you because of them a problem without knowledge - that Allah might admit to His mercy whom He willed. If they had been apart [from them], We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom behind the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, where the Muslims were prevented from reaching the Kaaba by the disbelievers of Mecca. It touches upon the presence of believing men and women among the Meccans, unknown to the Muslims, and how their existence influenced the decision to avoid conflict, lest the Muslims inadvertently harm them. The verse underscores God's mercy and His ability to include whom He wills within it. It also implies that had the believers been clearly distinguishable from the disbelievers, the latter would have faced severe punishment, indicating a divine principle of justice and mercy intertwined with the complexities of human societies.
